author.name: Xiangfei Sheng, Weidong Zou, Tianjiao Gu, Zhichao Yang, Pengfei Chen, Leida Li

entry.summary: AGIDefect-4K provides 4,000 images from 15 state-of-the-art generative models with hierarchical annotations: defect detection labels, pixel-level localization masks, and textual explanations of defect types and perceptual impact.

entry.title: Robust Validation to Geometric Perturbations for Autonomous Pose Estimation

author.name: Gregoire Theau, Melanie Ducoffe

entry.summary: Shows gradient-based heuristics like APGD fail at validating pose estimation against physically plausible geometric perturbations, often underperforming random sampling, then reformulates robustness within a Global Lipschitzian Optimization framework with certified guarantees for navigation and landing scenarios.

entry.title: Fast Coordinated Bimanual Motion Planning With Hard Constraints

author.name: Borna Paro, Luka Petrovi\'c, Ivan Markovi\'c

entry.summary: The authors propose fast bimanual motion planning that enforces a hard relative-transformation constraint between end effectors continuously along the entire path via a leader-follower parameterization, treating the leader configuration as free and deriving the follower pose by inverse kinematics. Rigid-object bimanual handling confines feasible space to a measure-zero manifold, challenging conventional planners.

entry.title: Representation Affects Retrieval: A Case Study of Skill Discovery and Routing in a Multimodal Agent Harness

author.name: Kevin Dela Rosa

entry.summary: A case study of skill representation in Tinycloud, a production multimodal video agent harness, contrasting tool-skills wrapping single APIs against workflow-skills orchestrating them for in-context planner selection. It connects small-N in-context skill choice to embedding-based retrieval at scale.

entry.title: Enhancing LLMs in Predictive Political QA with Semi-Structured Data

author.name: Yinan Liu, Zihan Zhou, Zichun Jin, Xinyu Wang, Bin Wang, Xiaochun Yang

entry.summary: Proposes PSL, a dual-view framework for predictive political QA that combines actor stance signals and higher-order structural dependencies among political actors, converting semi-structured resources into prediction-relevant evidence for LLMs. Goes beyond treating external documents as passive knowledge.

entry.title: Fine-Grain GPU Parallelization of the Generalized Partition Crossover for Large-Scale Traveling Salesman Problems

author.name: Swetha Varadarajan, Darrell Whitley

entry.summary: Develops fine-grain GPU parallelization of the Generalized Partition Crossover operator for large-scale traveling salesman instances, addressing irregular memory access patterns that limit existing GPU genetic-algorithm solvers to small problems.

entry.title: Aggregate, Don't Adapt: Subject-Level Posterior Aggregation and Transductive Calibration for Cross-Site Parkinsonian Gait Severity

author.name: Junlong Shen

entry.summary: Winning MoCha 2026 entry for cross-site parkinsonian gait severity shows nearly all margin over runner-up came from bookkeeping stages: exact head-recipe reproduction, subject-level posterior averaging, and label-free transductive calibration, on a frozen encoder with one linear layer.

entry.title: Amplifying the imaging power of digital sky surveys with space telescopes data and generative AI

author.name: Sai Teja Erukude, Lior Shamir

entry.summary: Uses generative AI trained on space-telescope galaxy images to convert weak ground-based survey signals into detailed galaxy images, aiming to combine survey throughput with space-grade resolution while respecting galaxy-shape statistics.

entry.title: MentorPulse: Refreshing Cross-Model Latent Guidance for Long-Form Generation

author.name: Ziwu Liu, Guozhong Li, Chen Qiu, Weiyang Kong, Panos Kalnis

entry.summary: Shows that static cross-model latent guidance from a frozen large mentor degrades below no-guidance baselines in long-form generation, and proposes MentorPulse which compresses mentor states into a capped slot memory refreshed every 16 tokens. A training-free change restores positive gains for a 4B student.

entry.title: COEC: Calibrated Orthogonal-Equivalence Compensation for Structured Pruning of Large Language Models

author.name: Peiqi Yu, Nam Ling, Wei Wang, Wei Jiang

entry.summary: COEC is a training-free compensation framework for structured pruning of LLMs that applies alternating left/right orthogonal rotations to retained weights, optimizing one rotation on a Stiefel manifold and rescaling singular values. Extends beyond additive-bias and single-rotation corrections.

entry.title: If It Walks Like an Arbitrage: Protocol-Agnostic Detection with Decidable Structural Equivalence

author.name: Adam Khayam, Hamid Kolli, Mohamed Iguernalala, \c{C}agdas Bozman

entry.summary: Builds a canonical structural form for Ethereum fund flows via term rewriting over call-frame-nested ASTs of transfers, with termination, soundness, confluence, and decidability all mechanically verified in Rocq, enabling protocol-agnostic arbitrage detection and bot fingerprinting.

entry.title: From a Static Multi-Level Small Semantic Codebook to a Dynamic Single-Level Large Semantic Codebook for Generative Recommendation

author.name: Tianlu Xie, Xin Ku, Mingjie Sun, Yunhao Sha, Lixiang Wang, Peng Wang, Yiyu Wang, Wenjin Wu, Zhaojie Liu, Peng Jiang, Wenwu Ou

entry.summary: Replaces multi-level residual semantic IDs in generative recommendation with a single-level large semantic codebook plus a collaborative disambiguation token, adding exposure-aware dynamic updating to handle new items and shifting traffic, reducing autoregressive decoding cost.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Speech Representations Track Spoken Language Convergence to Adult Models in Infants and Children Who Are Deaf/Hard-of-Hearing

author.name: L. Choy, A. S. Khan, S. Patrizi, D. Ye, J. Gross, M. Cychosz

entry.summary: Uses HuBERT-BASE speech embeddings on over 925 hours of daylong recordings to show spoken-language convergence toward adult caregiver models tracks hearing age in deaf/hard-of-hearing children, offering transcription-free measurement of language development.

entry.title: Scaling Unsupervised Word Alignment to Documents via Structural Constraints

author.name: Michelle Wastl, Jannis Vamvas, Rico Sennrich

entry.summary: CTFAlign scales unsupervised word alignment from sentences to documents via coarse-to-fine refinement restricting search to semantically similar regions, with MDPAlign as a diagonal-prior alternative; both are training-free and operate on full documents where sentence-designed algorithms degrade.

entry.title: Benchmarking Patent Drafting from Inventor-Style Disclosures

author.name: Lekang Jiang, Wenjun Sun, Stephan Goetz

entry.summary: Introduces Dis2Pat, a benchmark requiring generation of complete, legally coherent patent applications from informal inventor-style disclosures rather than structured legalistic inputs. Exposes that current LLMs fail at realistic end-to-end patent drafting workflows.

entry.title: VisTa3D: A Dataset and Benchmark for Thin Object Reconstruction from Vision, Tactile, and 3D Point Clouds

author.name: Shania Guo, Yeongsik Seo, Andrew Fu, Mei Hao, Iris Xia, Jiwon Jenny Lee, Xinyi Mary Xie, Hyoungseob Park, Aaron Dollar, Alex Wong

entry.summary: VisTa3D is the first dataset pairing synchronized RGB, depth, tactile response maps, inertial measurements, and laser-scanned ground truth specifically for thin-object 3D reconstruction, where existing vision and range models fail badly.

entry.title: Multi-Modal Traffic Sign Detection with Semantic Attributes for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Meda Lazar, Sourab Sridhar, Shashwata Gupta, Alexandra Tripcea, Varun Ravi, Senthil Yogamani

entry.summary: Addresses robust long-range traffic sign detection for autonomous driving with semantic attributes and multi-modal inputs, tackling cross-regional generalization, 10x10-pixel distant signs, and tracking under extreme perspective distortion.

entry.title: OccluRank: Controllable Occlusion-Aware Layout-to-Image Generation by Adding Just an Ordinal Rank

author.name: Wenyang Hong, Yuan Wang, Yanbin Hao, Lanqing Xue, Ke Wang, Xiang Wang, Kuien Liu, Richang Hong

entry.summary: OccluRank adds just a single ordinal rank per bounding box to make layout-to-image generation occlusion-aware, with lightweight rank conditioning and an order-aware instance interaction module updating rank-conditioned features jointly.

entry.title: Recognition-Conditioned Reasoning: A Training-Free Multimodal-LLM Pipeline for Fine-Grained Micro-Action Understanding

author.name: Fengshun Wang, Jin'ang Han, Zhigang Tu

entry.summary: A training-free, frozen-MLLM routing pipeline that won first place in the MAC 2026 micro-action challenge fine-grained understanding track, dynamically assigning each of eight sub-tasks to appropriate models with recognition-conditioned prompting and faithful body-part reasoning.

entry.title: A VLM Answer Is Not an Anomaly Score: Rank Compression in Training-Free Video Anomaly Detection

author.name: Inpyo Song, Jangwon Lee

entry.summary: Argues the answer interface of VLM-based video anomaly detectors (answer scales and readout rules) is part of the detector itself, showing probability readouts over admissible answers beat argmax answers across four 7-8B VLMs due to rank compression effects.

entry.title: Frozen CLIP Priors for Robust Self-Supervised Poisson Inverse Problems

author.name: Laura C. Diaz-Delgado, Emmanuel Martinez, Henry Arguello

entry.summary: Uses frozen CLIP priors within an ADMM-inspired unrolled plug-and-play solver for self-supervised Poisson inverse problems, exploiting distortion-invariant web-scale representations to stay stable under photon-limited acquisitions without fine-tuning.

entry.title: IMU-Free Body-Frame State Estimation with Sparse Scene Flow for Quadcopters

author.name: Daniel Gr{\o}nhaug, Sofie Markeset, Mathias Kolberg

entry.summary: Presents vision-only body-frame state estimation for stereo-equipped quadcopters without IMUs, using continuous-discrete EKF on composite manifolds with stationary scene points as implicit inertial references and chi-square-gated feature tracking.

entry.title: Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Trajectory Tracking of Differentially Flat Fixed-Wing Aerial Systems

author.name: Nishanth Bobbili, Pratyaksh Rao, Luca Morando, Luca Masci, Giuseppe Loianno

entry.summary: This work unifies differential-flatness-based trajectory generation with Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for fixed-wing UAVs, adding a wind-aware sampling strategy within the NMPC framework for robustness against environmental disturbances. Differential flatness has mostly been paired with model-free controllers before, so this combines computationally efficient planning with predictive constraint-aware control.

entry.title: FL-MAESTRO: Multi-Agent LLM Orchestration for Resource-Constrained Federated Learning

author.name: Jiajun Wu, Zirui Wang, Jiayu Zhou, Qiang Ye, Steve Drew

entry.summary: FL-MAESTRO uses three specialist LLM agents coordinated jointly to make runtime federated-learning decisions on communication topology, per-client resource allocation, and aggregation rules. Unlike prior LLM-for-FL work handling single dimensions at setup time, it treats these coupled decisions dynamically during training.

entry.title: EditPPT: Faithful Long-Deck Slide Editing via Structured Tool-Using Multi-Agent with Dual-Modal Validators

author.name: Jiheon Kim, Kyudan Jung, Jaegul Choo

entry.summary: EditPPT reformulates slide editing as constrained tool selection through the native PowerPoint COM interface with dual-modal validators, avoiding error-prone intermediate representations and open-ended code generation for faithful long-deck edits.

entry.title: EviRank: Structured Relevance Evidence for Multimodal Image Re-ranking

author.name: Enjun Du, Siyi Liu, Zirong Chen, Xinyu Zuo, Jinwen Luo, Ruiwen Tao, Lisheng Duan, Haijin Liang, Jin Ma, Junfu Pu, Yongqi Zhang

entry.summary: EviRank recasts multimodal image re-ranking as semantic constraint satisfaction, parsing compositional queries into typed criteria across six slots labeled required, forbidden, or ignorable, drawing on rubric/checklist evaluation practice to reduce hallucinated constraints versus free-form chain-of-thought.

entry.title: SPARK-SAM: Self-Prompt Adaptation with Response Knowledge for SAM in Infrared Small Target Segmentation

author.name: Aji Mao, Zhenming Peng, Bailin Mu, Tian Pu

entry.summary: SPARK-SAM adapts SAM to automatic infrared small-target segmentation by learning target-domain response knowledge conditioned through an image-conditioned joint self-prompt state, lifting performance from near-zero official SAM2.1 baselines to reported IoU around 75 percent.

entry.title: Difficulty-Aware Semantic-ID Optimization for Generative Recommendation

author.name: Xin Yu, Stephen Li, Sina Aghaei, Zifan Zhu, Jiamu Bai, Guanjie Huang, Bo Peng, Yiyao Liu, Lingzhou Xue

entry.summary: Diagnoses why vanilla GRPO fits poorly to semantic-ID generative recommendation, showing target items often absent from top candidates, and proposes difficulty-aware optimization addressing degenerate reward variation. The work targets the common SFT-plus-GRPO recipe for hierarchical item identifiers.

entry.title: From Attention Masks to Inert Zero-Vector Tokens: OAttention and O-Closure for Token Dynamics

author.name: Heyang Gong

entry.summary: Introduces an active-presence coefficient derived from hidden-state norms that simultaneously gates token emission and source weighting in attention, yielding OAttention and the O-Closure formalism for token participation dynamics. Argues attention masks alone lack a representation-carried non-participation state.

entry.title: Knowledge-Graph-Gated Defactualization for Style-Controllable and Fact-Preserving Generation in Agentic Conversational AI

author.name: Tanmay Kumar Shrivastava, Darsh Rohit Nandu, Rajesh Kumar Mundotiya

entry.summary: DSR integrates typed salience-weighted knowledge graphs with activation steering via a Defactualize-Steer-Rehydrate pipeline, distinguishing verifiable facts from stylistic content to achieve style control without semantic leakage in fact-sensitive conversational AI.

entry.title: Lightweight Adaptive ReduNet via Hyperspherical Manifold Learning

author.name: Zhenglin Huang, Qifa Yan, Bin Dai, Xiaohu Tang

entry.summary: LA-ReduNet compresses the layer-wise unfolded white-box ReduNet architecture via hyperspherical manifold learning to reduce parameter storage while retaining the interpretable maximal-coding-rate-reduction objective.

entry.title: Temporal Validity on Real Software Histories: Eliminating Stale-Fact Errors in Code-Assistant Memory over GitHub Fixes

author.name: Neeraj Yadav

entry.summary: Validates deterministic supersession memory for code-assistant RAG on real software history, extracting 130 atomic state transitions from 707 GitHub issues to show elimination of stale-fact errors where similarity-based retrieval cannot distinguish old from current values.

entry.title: Fuzzy-MoE: Interpretable Regime-Conditioned Expert Routing for Non-Stationary Multivariate Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Lan Guo, Jie Xiao, Zhao Su, Jun Shen, Haoran Li, Weixia Ma, Qingguo Zhou, Binbin Yong

entry.summary: Fuzzy-MoE recasts non-stationary time-series forecasting as latent regime identification plus interpretable fuzzy-logic expert routing with a dual-view router over parallel expert mappings, improving transparency of which mechanism activates under different states.

entry.title: TRACE: Training-time Report-guided and Clinically Ordered Concept Editing

author.name: Wentao Yue, Tianyou Lai, Jiayu Luo, Qingyu Mao, Ziying Wang, Zhenyuan Ning, Qilei Li

entry.summary: Introduces TRACE, a training-time framework for breast ultrasound diagnosis that uses structured radiology reports as privileged concept supervision while requiring only images at test time. Includes teacher-guided concept editing to improve interpretability and robustness over end-to-end classifiers.

entry.title: Quantization-Aware Healing: A Practical Recipe for Recovering Compressed, 4-Bit LLMs

author.name: Bakbergen Ryskulov, Iker Garc\'ia-Ferrero, David Montero, David Jansen, Ali Hashemi, Jezabel R. Garcia, Antonio Tiene, Rom\'an Or\'us

entry.summary: Proposes Neural-Primitive, an imitation-learning local planner mapping sensory input directly to polynomial trajectory coefficients, achieving sub-millisecond computation with collision-free, dynamically feasible trajectories without back-end solving. Targets the computation-quality-memory trilemma for onboard autonomous flight.

entry.title: A Neurosymbolic Approach for Constructing Planning Domain Models from Clinical Narratives

author.name: Ranveer Singh, Saurabh Mathur, Michael Skinner, Prasad Tadepalli, Kristian Kersting, Sriraam Natarajan

entry.summary: NSPIN induces probabilistic planning domain models (PPDDL) from unstructured surgical narratives by using a pretrained LLM to extract and impute event sequences, then refining the induced model. Addresses formalizing workflows like laparoscopic appendectomy for decision support.

entry.title: ConceptTS: LLM-Guided Concept Bottlenecks for Interpretable Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Yichen Jiang, Yueqiao Chen, Dongyu Liu

entry.summary: ConceptTS uses an LLM to propose task-relevant concepts and generate executable labeling rules for interpretable multivariate time-series forecasting, organizing predictions around named human-readable concepts without manual annotation cost.

entry.title: MIL-BERT: Classification of Arbitrarily Large Text with Performance and Explanatory Guarantees

author.name: John Cadigan, Dayne Freitag, Eric Yeh

entry.summary: MIL-BERT classifies arbitrarily large texts (near 1M tokens) via multiple-instance learning over selected excerpts, achieving state-of-the-art results on political bias, trigger warnings, and author demographics datasets, with explanatory guarantees from excerpt selection.

entry.title: GRAFT: Adaptive DLM-Based Draft Tree Construction with Target-Distilled Edge Scoring

author.name: Xuming Ye, Zeming Ma, Runjie Yu, Yuan Liu, Tianle Li, Shuhan Bai, Jian Zhou, Fei Wu

entry.summary: GRAFT improves tree-based speculative decoding with diffusion-LM drafters by scoring parent-child edges with target-distilled signals instead of token probability alone, adapting draft-tree construction to drafters producing all future-position distributions in one pass.

entry.title: ImmigrationReason: A Structured Dataset of U.S. Immigration Appeals for Legal Reasoning Research

author.name: Amirhossein Afsharrad, Seyed Shahabeddin Mousavi

entry.summary: ImmigrationReason is a structured dataset of 12,375 USCIS Administrative Appeals Office non-precedent decisions (2005-2026) with per-criterion evidence-sufficiency labels, adjudicator criticism quotes, citations, and dispositions, filling the administrative-adjudication gap in legal NLP.

entry.title: Evidence-Consistent Generative Detection under Scenario-Level Distribution Shift

author.name: San Kim, JinYeong Bak

entry.summary: Studies scenario-level out-of-distribution detection for SMS and voice phishing, holding entire attack scenarios out of training to test reliance on decision-relevant evidence versus surface cues, finding high in-distribution performance masks brittleness under attacker scenario changes.

entry.title: MigrationNarrate: A Dataset for Detection of Migration Narratives in YouTube Videos

author.name: Fatima Haouari, Carolina Scarton, Kalina Bontcheva

entry.summary: Introduces MigrationNarrate, the first multimodal annotated dataset for detecting migration narratives in UK YouTube videos, comprising 1,115 videos with annotations capturing how migration is framed across visual and audio channels.

entry.title: MV2GF: Multi-view Pedestrian Detection with a Visual Geometric Foundation Model

author.name: Taiga Yamane, Satoshi Suzuki, Ryo Masumura, Shota Orihashi, Tomohiro Tanaka, Mana Ihori, Naoki Makishima

entry.summary: MV2GF leverages a visual geometric foundation model to improve multi-view pedestrian detection, producing bird's-eye-view detections that generalize better to unseen camera configurations than projection-based aggregation pipelines.

entry.title: Identity-Preserving Text-to-Video Generation via Agentic Enhancement and Semantic Repair

author.name: Jiayi Gao, Changcheng Hua, Jiaqi Tang, Yuxin Peng, Yang Liu

entry.summary: AESR is a lightweight agentic enhancement framework improving identity preservation and instruction following in closed-source commercial video generators by repairing prompts before generation and semantically repairing outputs afterward, without touching model weights.

entry.title: Enhancing Localized Reasoning for Long Video Understanding via Efficient Segment-to-Video Supervision

author.name: Beibei Zhang, Chao Xu, Jun Lan, Zongyi Li, Lai Wei, Huijia Zhu, Tongwei Ren

entry.summary: Proposes efficient segment-to-video supervision to improve localized reasoning in long-video MLLMs, avoiding costly reinforcement fine-tuning frameworks and slow iterative-perception mechanisms while still grounding answers in relevant evidence segments.

entry.title: Semantically Compatible Knowledge Distillation for Cross-Domain Object Detection with Vision Foundation Models

author.name: Qifeng Zhang, Ting Xiang, Zeyuan Bai, Changjian Chen

entry.summary: SLE-T is a knowledge-distillation framework for cross-domain object detection built on a lightweight adapter injecting local-texture priors into DINOv2, resolving teacher-student spatial-scale mismatch and improving pseudo-label quality under domain shift.

entry.title: Dorsal Hand Images for Immersive (XR) and Privacy-preserving Age Assurance and Child Safety

author.name: Riccardo Bovo, George Loukas, Josh P. Davis

entry.summary: Proposes dorsal-hand imaging as a privacy-preserving, in-session age-assurance modality for XR environments, exploiting skin characteristics to verify active user age without headset removal or face-image sharing with third parties.

entry.title: ES-VP : Energy-Shaped Dynamic Visual Prompting for Efficient Model Adaptation

author.name: Can Jin, Ying Li, Jingchen Sun, Hongwu Peng, Jiahui Zhao, Yang Zhou, Lei Li, Dimitris N. Metaxas

entry.summary: ES-VP generates image-specific visual prompts via energy-shaped dynamics without auxiliary networks, aiming to balance flexibility and parameter efficiency in adapting pretrained vision models and avoid overfitting seen in generator-based prompting.

entry.title: WildFin: An In-the-Wild Dataset for Fish Behavioral Recognition

author.name: Abigail G. Grassick, Jerome Tze-Hou Hsu, Ethan Lin, Ziang Liu, Max Whitton, Madelyn Hair, Liam Gutierrez, Haozheng Yu, Kristin Branson, Vivek Jayaraman, Michael A. Gil, Andrew M. Hein, Jennifer J. Sun

entry.summary: WildFin is an ecologist-collected and annotated benchmark for fish behavior recognition spanning stationary-camera group monitoring and diver-following footage, built from 1,350 hours of fieldwork and 600 hours of expert annotation, designed to characterize model failures in complex marine environments.

entry.title: Enabling Memory-efficient Im2win Convolution with Multi-precision Support on GPU CUDA and Tensor Cores

author.name: Xiang Fu, Jixiang Ma, Xinpeng Zhang, Peng Zhao, Shuai Lu, Xu Tony Liu

entry.summary: Extends the memory-efficient im2win convolution paradigm to CUDA cores and tensor cores with zig-zag memory access, asynchronous movement, and multi-precision support, addressing cache utilization, kernel-size generality, and numerical instability of existing GPU convolutions.

entry.title: Toward Vision Language Model-based Assessment of Clinical Quality and Usability of LGE-MR Images for Cardiac Ablation Planning

author.name: Bipasha Kundu, Abhishek Chaturvedi, Axel W. E. Wismueller, Richard Simon, Cristian A. Linte

entry.summary: Explores VLM-based assessment of clinical quality and usability of LGE cardiac MRI for ablation planning, automating the currently informal radiologist gatekeeping decision that determines whether scans meet minimum quality thresholds for procedure safety.

entry.title: Columnar-Embedder: A Biologically Inspired Cortical Architecture for Binary Sparse Distributed Graph Representations

author.name: Mohamed Abidalrekab, Dan Hammerstrom

entry.summary: Columnar-Embedder proposes a biologically inspired cortical architecture for producing binary sparse distributed representations of graph entities, aiming to capture structural roles and homophily without random walks, message passing, or dense gradient-trained embeddings. The design draws on how mammalian cortex maps structural problems onto sparse columnar codes.

entry.title: STCO: Conditional Neural Operators for Time-Dependent PDEs

author.name: Xingxin Yang, Zhan Zhang, Juan Li

entry.summary: Introduces STCO, a Spatiotemporal Conditional Operator providing a common prescribed-condition interface for neural operators predicting time-dependent PDE solutions under control inputs not determined by observed state. It combines Fourier features and temporal conditioning across heterogeneous backbone architectures.

entry.title: Weighted Memory Tree: Remembering What Matters for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Quang Dao, Purvi Kathalkar, Kenneth Eaton

entry.summary: Introduces the Weighted Memory Tree, a hierarchical memory organizing agent execution histories into tasks, subtasks, and actions with dynamic retention scores updated via event-based revision and selection-based decay. It preserves useful information while folding completed branches to cut cost and stale-context interference.

entry.title: From Regulation to Implementation: A Critical Evaluation of LLM-Assisted Regulatory Compliance in Industry

author.name: Adriana Watson, Marco B\"ucheler, Grant Richards

entry.summary: Critically evaluates LLM-assisted generation of regulatory compliance artifacts such as EU Digital Product Passports and Data Protection Impact Assessments, identifying challenges from heterogeneous scattered industrial data. Bridges regulation-to-implementation gaps in sustainability and privacy compliance.

entry.title: Infrared Hotspot-Guided Early Warning of Lithium-Ion Battery Thermal Runaway Under Mechanical Abuse

author.name: Syed Sajid Ullah, Salman Khan, Muhammad Zunair Zamir

entry.summary: Two-stage early-warning system for lithium-ion battery thermal runaway under mechanical abuse fusing infrared hotspot dynamics with mechanical, electrical, and image features over a 20-frame horizon, achieving ROC-AUC above direct multimodal fusion with interpretable staging and leak-resistant validation.

entry.title: Explainable Deepfake Detection with Feature-robust Augmentation and Evidence-grounded Explanation Optimization

author.name: Zhu Xu, Jiaqi Tang, Pokai Chen, Yuxin Peng, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Extends deepfake detection beyond binary classification to include interpretable justifications, addressing vulnerability to image-quality degradation and factually flawed explanations. Proposes feature-robust augmentation and evidence-grounded explanation optimization so forensic analysts get reliable manipulation evidence.

entry.title: TriPLU: Bypassing the Gate with Direct Trilinear Product FFNs in Tiny Language Models

author.name: He Zhang

entry.summary: TriPLU replaces gated FFNs in tiny decoder-only language models with a product-only degree-3 trilinear branch multiplying three projected streams, improving validation loss over matched SwiGLU and degree-2/4 controls on TinyStories and Byte-BPE benchmarks.

entry.title: LiLiCorr: Lightweight Likelihood Correlation of Parallel Drafts for Speculative Decoding

author.name: Matan Rusanovsky, Yoav Miron, Roy Uziel, Omer Belhasin, Ran Zilberstein, Maor Ashkenazi, Michael Elad

entry.summary: LiLiCorr correlates per-position marginal distributions from diffusion-block drafters like DFlash to fix joint incoherence in speculative decoding, keeping top-k candidates per position and computing match vectors for adjacent pairs to build coherent draft sequences cheaply.

entry.title: Lift, Associate, and Fuse: A Decision-Centric Framework for 2D-to-3D Foundation Model Transfer

author.name: Wentao Sun, Yiping Chen, John S. Zelek, Jonathan Li

entry.summary: LAF reframes 2D-to-3D foundation-model transfer for segmentation as five explicit operators (Generate, Associate, Reconcile, Fuse, Persist/Query), defining contracts for persistent carriers of spatial and semantic state across views.

entry.title: Gaussian-Mixture Latent Flow for Stochastic 3D Human Motion Prediction

author.name: Yue Ma, Frederick W. B. Li, Xiaohui Liang

entry.summary: Proposes a latent flow model with a data-driven Gaussian mixture prior for stochastic human motion prediction, better disentangling behavior modes than single-modal priors while enabling plausibility checks and uncertainty quantification via invertibility.

entry.title: PrimeAgentOrchestrator: Memory-Primed Agent Spawning for Personal AI Infrastructure

author.name: Myron Koch (Peak Summit Labs)

entry.summary: Presents PrimeAgentOrchestrator, a system that spawns Claude Code instances pre-loaded with memories fused from a PostgreSQL entity database and a Cloudflare semantic-search index via filesystem injection. It addresses the cold-context problem where coding agents discard accumulated knowledge between sessions.

entry.title: NeuroStrata: An Electroencephalographic Connectivity-Aware Deep Representation Learning Framework for Dynamic Brain Network Analysis of Mental Stress

author.name: Sayantan Acharya, Hamzeh Asgharnezhad, Abbas Khosravi, Douglas Creighton, Roohallah Alizadehsani, U Rajendra Acharya

entry.summary: NeuroStrata models temporal evolution of frequency-specific directed brain connectivity via time-varying partial directed coherence maps processed by pretrained CNNs and ViTs for EEG-based mental stress classification on the SAM 40 dataset.

entry.title: Edge-Based Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Autonomous FHWA Bridge Inspection Compliance

author.name: Viraj Nishesh Darji, Hemaliben Rakeshkumar Darji

entry.summary: BridgeGuard is a fully air-gapped agentic RAG system running locally on commodity edge hardware for FHWA bridge-inspection compliance, combining vector search over the coding guide with SQL queries over inventory data orchestrated by ReAct-style planning.

entry.title: Identity-Aware Human-Object Interaction Motion Captioning

author.name: Yiming Wang, Yonghao Dang, Huilai Li, Jiawei Tu, Jianqin Yin

entry.summary: Defines identity-aware human-object interaction motion captioning requiring captions to name the acting subject, contributes annotated BEHAVE and InterCap variants, and proposes ID-HOINet learning from multi-view video with single-view inference support.

entry.title: Advantage-level Aggregation Reinforcement Learning for X-point Target Magnetic Configuration Control in an EXL-50U Experiment-Calibrated Simulation Environment

author.name: Siqi Ding, Xuanhe Wang, Pei Guo, Guoyang Shi, Changquan Yu, Yiting Wang, Xianming Song, Xiang Gu, Zhengyuan Chen, Lei Xing, Yapeng Zhang, Jianguo Chen, Tianyuan Liu

entry.summary: Frames secondary X-point divertor feedback control in tokamaks as multi-objective reinforcement learning in an experiment-calibrated free-boundary simulation environment. Introduces advantage-level aggregation RL to replace precomputed feedforward waveforms with closed-loop control for compact high-power tokamak exhaust management.

entry.title: Uncertainty propagation in auto-regressive random neural network models

author.name: Janice Adams, Daniele Venturi

entry.summary: Develops analytical and particle-based uncertainty propagation for random neural networks with random inputs and parameters, deriving local Leaky-ReLU piecewise-linear approximations that are exact for activation-pattern-preserving perturbations and yield closed-form density, mean, and covariance expressions.

entry.title: Aristotelian Manifolds: Leveraging Platonic Perceptual Features for Backpropagation Free Rapid Concept Learning

author.name: Michael Karnes, Alper Yilmaz

entry.summary: Formalizes Aristotelian Manifolds atop the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, mapping layer-wise how semantic knowledge is synthesized in foundation-model latent spaces across architectures and domains, revealing distinct non-monotonic geometric maturation profiles.

entry.title: Hybrid Roller-Jamming Gripper for Object Acquisition and Retention Under Pose Uncertainty

author.name: Yijie Ren, Guillaume Gourmelen, Hiroyasu Iwata

entry.summary: This paper introduces a hybrid roller-jamming gripper combining active inward roller rotation to draw off-center or partially contacted objects toward the center with vacuum-induced granular jamming to stiffen the rollers and stabilize retention. A simplified geometric model supports the design targeting household manipulation under pose uncertainty.

entry.title: A Hybrid Edge Cloud Digital Twin for Welfare-Constrained Control in Poultry Production

author.name: Suresh Neethirajan

entry.summary: Hybrid edge-cloud digital twin for poultry facilities coupling grey-box thermodynamic models with learned residuals and model predictive control for welfare-constrained environmental management under practical farm constraints.

entry.title: ExploraTwin, a Non-Profit Research Platform for Digital Twin Simulations

author.name: Naveen Venkatanarayanan, Yuchen Qiu, Tianyi Peng, George Gui, Olivier Toubia

entry.summary: ExploraTwin is an open-access nonprofit platform letting researchers upload surveys, select digital-twin samples, run simulations, and export analysis-ready data, lowering friction for testing LLM-based digital twins before deployment.

entry.title: RiskTraf: Risk-Extrapolated Residual Learning for Multi-Variate Traffic Flow Prediction

author.name: Guangyu Wang, Zhidan Liu

entry.summary: Introduces PEMSB-3V, a public benchmark preserving raw flow, speed, and occupancy from PeMS detectors, and RiskTraf, residual learning with risk extrapolation to avoid regime-dependent shortcuts across free-flow and congested states in traffic forecasting.

entry.title: When Generated Images Look Right and Retrieve Wrong: Coverage-Guided Cross-Scale Re-Indexing for Knowledge-Faithful Generative Perception

author.name: Guangyuan Dong, Chuang Liu, Yangchen Zeng, Haoyu Wang, Xiaoyang Yu, Pinlong Zhao, Yuchao Hou, Ziwei Li, Zheng Lin

entry.summary: Formalizes semantic collapse, where generated images drop scale-specific concepts due to globally pooled text conditioning, breaking downstream retrieval. Proposes CERES, a closed-loop multimodal indexing framework with a three-level semantic pyramid and scale-routed cross-attention to keep generated content retrievable by intended queries.

entry.title: KREL: Automatic Medical Coding via Knowledge-Guided Reasoning over Clinical Evidence with LLMs

author.name: Xubin Chen, Yipeng Zhou, Wen Sun, Chengkai Huang, Xiaoming Fu, Quan Z. Sheng

entry.summary: Proposes KREL, a knowledge-guided reasoning framework for automatic ICD medical coding that handles extremely long clinical notes, the vast code space, and complex coding rules that LLMs do not capture implicitly. Combines retrieval over clinical evidence with rule-aware reasoning.

entry.title: Vibe Coding and Web Application Security: A Twin-Prompt Study

author.name: Darko Andro\v{c}ec

entry.summary: Twin-prompt controlled study generating six functionally distinct web applications twice each, once with and once without appended security requirements, then analyzing all twelve with static, dependency, dynamic and manual techniques yielding 75 confirmed findings. Shows whether explicitly requesting security best practices improves LLM-generated application security.

entry.title: Thermo-FL: Thermal-Aware Robust Federated Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models for Edge AI

author.name: Shiva Shrestha, Kazi Shaharair Sharif, Zongxing Xie, Jiajing Huang, Anhao Xiang, Honghui Xu

entry.summary: Thermo-FL is a federated LoRA fine-tuning framework for LLMs on thermally constrained edge devices that uses device temperature as an active control signal for adapter training and sparse update transmission, while also defending against Byzantine and communication-layer adversaries.

entry.title: Interpretable Information-Decomposed Brain Graph Learning for fMRI-based Disease Diagnosis

author.name: Dengyi Zhao, Zhiheng Zhou, Zihan Wang, Guiying Yan, Xingqin Qi

entry.summary: IID-GCN decomposes rs-fMRI connectivity into redundancy, uniqueness, and synergy graphs via partial information decomposition for interpretable disease diagnosis, moving beyond correlation-only edges that obscure how information is shared across brain regions.

entry.title: Training DeepFilterNet with Accurate Room Acoustic Simulations Improves Single-Channel Speech Enhancement

author.name: Alessia Milo, Georg G\"otz, Steinar Gu{\dh}j\'onsson, Daniel Gert Nielsen, Jesper Pedersen, Finnur Pind

entry.summary: Compares DNS4 image-source-method room impulse responses against higher-fidelity hybrid wave/geometric-acoustics simulations for training DeepFilterNet3, finding higher-fidelity RIRs consistently improve objective metrics and substantially lower ASR word error rates.

entry.title: Using Human-LLM Disagreement to Improve Checklist-Based Quality Appraisal

author.name: Timo van der Kuil (Methodology and Statistics Utrecht University), Bruno Messina Coimbra (Methodology and Statistics Utrecht University), Mirjam van Zuiden (Clinical Psychology Utrecht University), Robert A. Bagheri (Methodology and Statistics Utrecht University), Rens van de Schoot (Methodology and Statistics Utrecht University), Klaas Dieleman (Methodology and Statistics Utrecht University), Berend Greijn (Methodology and Statistics Utrecht University), Stefan Houkes (Methodology and Statistics Utrecht University), Sebastiaan Rodenhuis (Methodology and Statistics Utrecht University), Elizabeth M. Grandfield (Methodology and Statistics Utrecht University)

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLM assessments approximate expert judgments on the GRoLTS quality-appraisal checklist and whether human-LLM disagreement patterns can identify ambiguous checklist items for improvement, across three research domains.

entry.title: Ontology-Driven Structural Regularization for Document-Level Relation Extraction

author.name: Laura Menotti, Stefano Marchesin, Gianmaria Silvello

entry.summary: Quantifies structural noise in distantly supervised DocRE data (ontology-constraint violations, logical contradictions) and shows it propagates to model predictions; enforcing structural well-formedness during training reduces contradictions and improves consistency.

entry.title: ForeDreamer: A Self-Evolving Dual-Agent Memory Architecture for Future Event Prediction

author.name: Linhao Zhong, Zongze Du, Linyu Wu, Yu Bo, Hourong Li, Chenchen Jing, Hao Chen, Yuling Xi, Chunhua Shen

entry.summary: ForeDreamer manages memory for open-web future-event prediction via a self-evolving dual-agent architecture separating factual memory (question-specific distilled evidence state) from other memory functions, transforming raw web retrieval into structured memory before prediction.

entry.title: When the Feature Pool Goes Algorithmic: Extending Mufwene's Ecology of Language Evolution to LLM-Mediated Exposure

author.name: Kunmei Han

entry.summary: A theoretical position paper extending Mufwenu2019s ecological model of language evolution to the era of LLM-mediated text exposure. It argues LLMs act as distributional mediators that reweight the language varieties speakers encounter, without shifting selection away from humans. Relevant as an early conceptual bridge between sociolinguistics and generative model deployment.

entry.title: Kinematic Knowledge Maps for Pattern Alignment: Structured Latent Representational Learning in Multimodal Gait Analysis

author.name: Chen Dong, He Zonglin, Cheung Kenneth M. C

entry.summary: ScoliDetect screens adolescent idiopathic scoliosis from monocular gait video using kinematic knowledge maps and template-based kinematic text, providing anchor-referenced multimodal fusion and factor-level interpretability for clinical use.

entry.title: KoViDoRe: Korean Visual Document Retrieval

author.name: Yongbin Choi, Yongwoo Song, Mujeen Sung

entry.summary: KoViDoRe introduces a benchmark for Korean visual document retrieval covering complex layouts (tables, figures, multi-column) with multi-page evidence-aggregation scenarios missing from English-centric and single-page Korean resources.

entry.title: Natural Sit-to-Stand Motion Synthesis For Humanoids via Guided Assistance Curricula and Staged Rewards

author.name: Meet Pal Singh, Vyankatesh Ashtekar, Ashish Dutta

entry.summary: The authors train a single PPO policy from scratch, without demonstrations or reference trajectories, to produce natural humanoid sit-to-stand motion using a coupled force/chair-height curriculum where pelvis-assist force decays over training and taller chairs are progressively unlocked. Three complementary reward components drive smooth, human-like rising motions.

entry.title: Interpretable Multimodal Classification with Linear Discriminant Tree Ensembles

author.name: Mojtaba Moattari

entry.summary: Develops linear discriminant tree ensembles for multimodal affect and behavior classification that balance accuracy with human-understandable feature attributions across text, audio, and visual streams. It targets trust-sensitive applications like clinical monitoring where Transformer opacity is limiting.

entry.title: FlavourBench: Ranking Frontier Language Models with Executable Culinary Ground Truth

author.name: Josef Chen, Erim Hayretci

entry.summary: FlavourBench ranks 27 frontier language-model endpoints on 534 culinary tasks with dense executable ground truth scored by a versioned recipe system, eliminating judge bias and differential missingness across all 14,418 model-task cells. Tasks cover ingredient substitution, pairing, and constrained composition.

entry.title: BC-Bench: Evaluating Agentic Engineering in a Domain-Specific Language for ERP

author.name: Haoran Sun, Klaus Marius Hansen

entry.summary: Presents BC-Bench, a benchmark of 101 manually curated real-world AL-language tasks from Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central production repositories, adapting SWE-Bench methodology to evaluate agentic engineering in an ERP domain-specific language including test generation.

entry.title: Keyed Provenance Watermarking with Complementary Lattice-Based Secure Aggregation for Federated Learning

author.name: Xinyun Liu, Zhi Lu, Yu Chen, Ronghua Xu

entry.summary: Couples keyed context-provenance watermarking, anchored in trusted physical metadata transformed via HMAC-SHA-256, with lattice-based zero-knowledge secure aggregation to defend federated learning simultaneously against data leakage, unauthorized reuse, and malicious gradient manipulation.

entry.title: Sparse Token Routing in Efficient Transformers

author.name: Sai Krishna Arthanari, JaeHyeong Chang, Chengzhe Sun, Siwei Lyu

entry.summary: SEWN tests end-to-end whether sparse token routing through lightweight versus full-capacity streams helps, finding negligible accuracy change versus parameter-matched baselines, and showing gate token-importance signals depend critically on how the gate is learned, with static lexicon priors failing counterfactual faithfulness tests.

entry.title: Bridging Language and Spherical Space: Object-Centric Control for Text-to-Panorama Generation

author.name: Derui Li, Qian Qiao, Yuhao Sun, Wenhao Guo, Peng Lu

entry.summary: Proposes object-centric directional control for text-to-panorama generation so spatial terms like left/right/front/behind are faithfully grounded in spherical scenes without manual layouts, bridging language and spherical coordinate space.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving Object Detection for Vision Transformer-Based Models

author.name: Homare Sueyoshi, Kiyoshi Nishikawa, Hitoshi Kiya

entry.summary: First perceptual-encryption approach for privacy-preserving object detection, protecting sensitive test images while achieving near-unprotected accuracy by exploiting ViT embedding structure and keyed domain adaptation with ViTDet.

entry.title: Demonstration-Guided Humanoid Stand-Up on an Emulated Deformable Surface

author.name: Aniruddh Kushwah, Vyankatesh Ashtekar, Ashish Dutta

entry.summary: This paper trains stand-up policies for a 29-DOF Unitree G1 humanoid on deformable soft ground by transferring a human demonstration recorded on hard ground, modeling terrain compliance through MuJoCo solref/solimp parameters. Training progresses by gradually lowering terrain stiffness and expanding penetration zones while tracking residual joint positions and recovery objectives.

entry.title: Sharing the Control Authority Between Deep Reinforcement Learning and Model Predictive Control: Application to Multi-Class Transportation Networks

author.name: Giray Onur, Azita Dabiri, Bart De Schutter

entry.summary: Shares control authority between deep reinforcement learning and MPC for multi-class transportation networks, aiming to combine DRL adaptivity with MPC constraint handling while mitigating each approach's computational and modeling weaknesses.

entry.title: Ontology-supported AI Model and Dataset Management

author.name: Jan Novacek, Ali Ahari, Tobias M\"uller, Sebastian Reiter, Alexander Viehl, Oliver Bringmann

entry.summary: Presents an ontology-supported platform for exchanging, tracking, and discovering AI models and datasets in industrial settings, aiming to close semantic gaps across organizations. Focuses on asset management requirements rather than new learning algorithms.

entry.title: Trilingual Topic Modeling of Sri Lankan Parliamentary Debates

author.name: Himath Dhanapala, Haren Daishika, Himandhi Kuruppu, Sithija Seneviratne, Ashini Kavindya, Patalee Narasinghe, Sandeepa Weerasekara, Nisansa de Silva, Sandareka Wickramanayake

entry.summary: End-to-end framework for trilingual topic modeling of Sri Lankan parliamentary Hansards combining LLM-based extraction from layout-complex PDFs with multilingual embeddings and clustering, recovering 30 macro-topics across 19,553 speeches with hybrid semantic-lexical BiTopic refinement.

entry.title: From Thermal Preference Prediction to Adaptive Thermal Intervention: A Reinforcement Learning Approach Using Physiological and Environmental Sensing

author.name: Isibor Kennedy Ihianle, Emmanuel Manu, Ehsan Asnaashari, Mojgan Jadidi, Pedro Machado, Amrit Sagoo, Ahmad Lotfi

entry.summary: Two-stage personalized thermal comfort system integrating multimodal physiological and environmental sensing with reinforcement-learning decision-making to replace static HVAC setpoints and population-level comfort models.

entry.title: Denoising the Future: Context-Aware Spectral Diffusion for Temporal Knowledge Graph Extrapolation

author.name: Yanglei Gan, Peng He, Run Lin, Peiyuan Jiang, Yifan Wang, Qiao Liu

entry.summary: Proposes FreqDiff, a frequency-aware diffusion framework for temporal knowledge graph extrapolation that formulates future object prediction as query-slot denoising with a dual-stream denoiser combining temporal dependency modeling and context-aware spectral calibration. Addresses dilution of query-specific evidence in prior diffusion-based TKG methods.

entry.title: TH-GNN: Heterogeneous Temporal Graph Neural Networks for LLM-Agent Shilling Attack Detection

author.name: Shivam Swarup, Divya Prakash Shrivastava, Rakesh Thakur

entry.summary: TH-GNN detects LLM-agent-generated shilling attacks on recommender systems using a heterogeneous temporal graph transformer with per-type attention, sinusoidal temporal encodings, and cross-modal fusion of structural user embeddings with review semantics.

entry.title: Robust Discovery of Coarse-Grained Continuum Equations from Microscopic Dynamics

author.name: Partha Sarathi Mondal, Manav Kumar Jalan, Anish Kumar, Shradha Mishra

entry.summary: Systematically examines how data volume, library size, and noise affect PDE-SINDy equation discovery on phase-separating systems, showing spurious terms acquire finite selection probability with limited data and are progressively suppressed as data grows.

entry.title: Event-triggered Implicit Perturbation for Zeroth-Order Fine-Tuning of Spiking Transformers

author.name: Tengteng Lei, Prabodh Katti, Rashi Dutt, Houssem Sifaou, Tan Peng, Osvaldo Simeone, Kai Xu, Bipin Rajendran

entry.summary: IPZO enables zeroth-order fine-tuning of spiking transformers on in-memory-computing accelerators via event-triggered implicit perturbation generated by a dedicated unit fused with IMC array weighted sums, eliminating explicit weight RMW cycles and heavy RNG footprints.

entry.title: ARGUS: Theory-of-Mind Guided Argument Generation with Strategy-Aware Planning and Knowledge Grounding

author.name: Zhe Hu

entry.summary: ARGUS generates persuasive arguments via a Theory-of-Mind reasoner maintaining explicit dual models of audience beliefs and values, feeding a component-aware planner assigning rhetorical functions (logos, pathos, ethos, kairos) and strategy-guided evidence grounding.

entry.title: Shortcut Learning in a Public Grape Disease Dataset: Annotation Granularity as a Modulator, Not a Cause

author.name: Pushuo Wang (Shenyang Institute of Technology)

entry.summary: Diagnoses shortcut learning in a public grape disease dataset caused by inconsistent annotation granularity: one class annotated at whole-leaf level versus lesion level for others, producing mAP variation comparable to seed noise and heavy false positives on cross-species images.

entry.title: SuppreSensing: Expert-Guided Feature Recalibration and Discrepancy Augmentation for Multimodal Object Detection

author.name: Xin Wu, Zhenyu Gao, Qiankun Zhang, Shaoyong Guo

entry.summary: SuppreSensing reformulates multimodal fusion for remote-sensing object detection as selective expert-driven collaboration, recalibrating shared-consensus features input-adaptively and augmenting modality-specific attributes via bidirectional discrepancy modeling.

entry.title: Maximum Entropy Encoding of Energy-Weighted Spherical Moments

author.name: Jiaze Sun

entry.summary: Derives a maximum-entropy closure for energy-weighted spherical moments of Monte Carlo path samples, yielding an exponential-family directional density with provable normalizability and positivity conditions for irradiance reconstruction in rendering.

entry.title: Scalable Distributed Simulation-Based Testing for Automated Driving Systems

author.name: Christian Geller, Benedikt Haas, Lutz Eckstein

entry.summary: The paper presents an end-to-end DevOps-driven framework automating build, deployment, and distributed execution of CARLA-based scenario tests for automated driving systems on lightweight Kubernetes clusters, packaging ROS 2 applications as Helm charts generated from repository specifications. It targets the bottleneck of executing thousands of validation scenarios at scale.

entry.title: Environmental Slow AI: Design Principles for Generative Systems

author.name: Vanessa Utz

entry.summary: A position paper applying environmental humanities to generative AI design, proposing Slow AI principles such as restraint, sufficiency, material visibility, and friction-as-affordance to counter maximalist default values. It argues cultural values embedded in genAI are identifiable and deliberately reshapable.

entry.title: Hadith computational science in the age of large language models: a critical narrative review

author.name: Md. Ashraful Haque (Greentech Apps Foundation, United Kingdom), Riasat Islam (Greentech Apps Foundation, United Kingdom, Queen Mary University of London, London, United Kingdom)

entry.summary: Critical narrative review of hadith computational science in the LLM era, appraising which advances are methodologically robust, integrating Islamic scholar perspectives on authenticity and responsible use, and identifying unresolved scholarly-use limitations.

entry.title: Source-Free MT Evaluation Is Not MT Evaluation

author.name: Baban Gain, Ramakrishna Appicharla, Asif Ekbal

entry.summary: Argues that source-free reference-based machine translation evaluation conflates translation quality with reference choice, biasing against valid alternative renderings. Proposes that adequacy should be judged against the source with references treated only as auxiliary evidence, reshaping how QE-style judges should be designed.

entry.title: TRACE-C: Rank-Calibrated Relational Anomaly Detection for Multi-Stream Operational Telemetry

author.name: Matthew Faucher

entry.summary: TRACE-C is an auditable, rank-calibrated detector for jointly anomalous multi-stream operational telemetry, combining rolling residual channels via Fisher aggregation and evaluating on Great Britain grid streams with a pre-frozen hold-out. It ranks Storm Atiyah first among 2019 test windows.

entry.title: Keep Your Friends Close, and the Right Neighbours Closer: Disaster-Conditioned Kernel-Regularized Graph Attention for Building Damage Classification

author.name: Fuad Hasan, Chul Min Yeum

entry.summary: Studies disaster-conditioned kernel-regularized graph attention for post-disaster building damage classification on xBD, showing the right spatial neighborhood differs across floods, hurricanes, and wildfires and naive context aggregation can oversmooth boundaries or propagate errors.

entry.title: Conditional-Independence-Regularized Distributional Autoencoders for Mixed-Type Data

author.name: Siyuan Tang, Gongjun Xu, Ji Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces conditional-independence-regularized distributional autoencoders for mixed numeric-categorical data, combining energy-score objectives for numerical variables with conditional distribution matching and structural regularization to recover interpretable low-dimensional representations.

entry.title: On the Transferability of Agricultural Weed Detection Under Cross-Field Distribution Shift

author.name: Nikhilesh Prabhakar, Pranuthi Tenali, Wilfredo Abudeye Fernandez, Shekhar Borah, Athresh Karanam, Erik Blasch, Prabha Sundaravadivel, Sriraam Natarajan

entry.summary: Characterizes where UAV weed-detection models degrade across fields and crops, releasing a newly annotated cotton-field UAV dataset and identifying modeling choices that recover cross-dataset performance, reducing relabeling burden for precision agriculture.

entry.title: A Dataset-Centric Benchmark of Deep Learning Methods for Grape Leaf Disease Classification and Detection

author.name: Petar Canoski, Vlatko Spasev, Ivica Dimitrovski, Ivan Kitanovski, Petre Lameski

entry.summary: A dataset-centric benchmark of deep learning methods for grape leaf disease classification and detection, analyzing public datasets for acquisition conditions, class distributions, and suitability, and testing methods under realistic vineyard challenges like complex backgrounds and variable illumination.

entry.title: RDANet: Relative Degradation Aware Network for Infrared Small Target Detection

author.name: Rui Liu, Jing Nie, Ying Fu

entry.summary: RDANet targets scale- and scene-sensitive degradation in infrared small-target detection via a relative-degradation-aware network preserving target structure under downsampling and discriminative contrast under background shifts.

entry.title: Teaching is a Process: The TOSS Framework for Modeling Human Teaching Decisions in Human-Interactive Robot Learning

author.name: Bernhard Hilpert, Kim Baraka, Joost Broekens

entry.summary: The TOSS framework models human teaching decisions in human-interactive robot learning through a study of 34 participants observing robot reinforcement learning scenarios, analyzing 204 teaching responses across learning phases. Results reveal an interconnected network of Triggers, Objectives, Signals, and Strategies, with teachers spontaneously adopting diverse roles.

entry.title: Applying Anthropic Primitives at Large Enterprises: Harness Paradigm for Knowledge Work

author.name: George Juraj Salapa

entry.summary: Argues enterprises should adopt the coding-agent harness paradigm as governed infrastructure rather than bespoke per-use-case code or low-code platforms, leveraging collapsed code-generation costs. It positions harnesses as a third option escaping both constraints of custom builds and rigid platforms.

entry.title: PSK at WMT 2026 MIST: Task-Specialized QLoRA Adapters for Multilingual Summarization and Question Answering

author.name: Srikar Kashyap Pulipaka

entry.summary: WMT 2026 shared-task submission using Tiny Aya Global 3.35B with three task-specialized QLoRA adapters for multilingual summarization and question answering, showing specialization beats multitask adapters on held-out splits.

entry.title: Time-Aware Tranformer-Based Prediction Model for AECOPD

author.name: Weihao Qu, Ling Zheng, Dongyang Wang, Jiacun Wang, Haowen Pan

entry.summary: Applies a time-aware transformer to home ventilator respiratory data for early prediction of acute COPD exacerbations, reducing latency relative to lab-data-dependent models.

entry.title: AudioWorldSim: Realistic Binaural Audio Datasets For World Models

author.name: Luis Vitor Zerkowski, Luiz Velho

entry.summary: AudioWorldSim is an open-source extension of SoundSpaces 2.0 that automatically rolls out random agent navigations to generate realistic binaural audio datasets for world-model research, with fixes to continuous sound composition.

entry.title: Intent Engine: Natural-Language Intent Translation for Intent-Driven Orchestration in the Compute Continuum

author.name: Koushikur Islam, Rodrigo N. Calheiros

entry.summary: Intent Engine translates natural-language intents into validated SLO artifacts for compute-continuum service placement, constraining LLM generation to avoid unsupported constraints, wrong grounded values, and schema violations that corrupt downstream placement logic.

entry.title: Prompt-Model Interaction Reaches the Fixed Points: A deterministic, task-free structural readout -- and the factorizations of it that failed

author.name: Nicol\'as Vera Z\'u\~niga

entry.summary: A task-free structural probe of prompt-model interaction using the deterministic fixed points of short-window argmax maps, censused from many starting states across six models. Finds interaction structure persists at short windows and vanishes by window 16 for most models, characterizing how models read fragments independent of task accuracy.

entry.title: A Temporal Planning Approach for Intelligent Flood Response

author.name: Fazlul Hasan Siddiqui, Md. Monjurul Islam, Sabah Binte Noor

entry.summary: Applies temporal automated planning to intelligent flood response, modeling triage priority, route accessibility, resource allocation, and mid-execution re-planning across simultaneously flooded areas. The framework generates time-aware schedules from formal resource and constraint descriptions.

entry.title: Fine-tuning LLMs for Tourist Trajectory Prediction using Field Experiment Data

author.name: Tatsuya Amano, Hirozumi Yamaguchi

entry.summary: Fine-tunes Llama-3.1-8B on 566 tourist trajectories from Wakayama Castle Park to predict visitor movement under varying weather and fatigue conditions, leveraging LLM commonsense plus local adaptation for mobility-intervention evaluation.

entry.title: Decision Tree and K-Means Analysis of Raman Spectra for Edible Oils: A Physics-Informed AI Approach

author.name: Amrita Shaw, Chandrasekar S. N., Sai Muthukumar V., Jhinuk Gupta, Deepak L. N. Kallepalli

entry.summary: Applies t-SNE, k-means, decision trees, and NNLS spectral decomposition to Raman spectra of five edible oils pure and within fried-chip matrices, framed as physics-informed AI for food authentication and fraud detection.

entry.title: STAR-OPD: Structured Aspect-Cascade-Aware On-Policy Reward Distillation for ABSA Quadruple Extraction

author.name: Tong Sun, Mingyang Ma, Jiayang Yu

entry.summary: Identifies a structural failure mode in distilled aspect-based sentiment extraction where student errors at target-aspect interfaces corrupt downstream predictions. Proposes STAR-OPD, an on-policy reward distillation approach that supervises students on their own trajectories rather than teacher-generated ones.

entry.title: Across-Design Uncertainty in Short Pricing Panels: Evidence from Simulated Price Trajectories

author.name: Pedro Cadahia Delgado

entry.summary: Studies uncertainty in short pricing panels via simulated price trajectories, separating within-trajectory resampling uncertainty from across-trajectory variation, and finds the latter accounts for 97.6% of estimation-error variance for gradient boosting, meaning within-panel resampling misses most of it.

entry.title: Exploratory As-Analyzed No-Detection of Culturally-Marked Predicate-Triggered PII Amplification in a Synthetic-English RAG Probe: A Predicate-Resource-Confounded Audit

author.name: Yanhang Li, Zhichao Fan, Zexin Zhuang

entry.summary: Pre-registered four-culture audit asking whether stereotype-loaded queries leak more PII from RAG systems than neutral queries, defining a Stereotype-Trigger Leakage Delta. The paper candidly reports the confirmatory estimator was never run and the leakage metric was contaminated by prompt-echo artifacts, so all tests are exploratory.

entry.title: Humanoid Musical Robots as Experimental Interfaces for Music-Evoked Emotion

author.name: Vincent K. M. Cheung, Jia-Yeu Lin

entry.summary: A position paper proposing musical humanoid robots as experimental interfaces for studying music-evoked emotions, arguing that pre-recorded auditory stimuli fail to capture the embodied, multimodal, interactive nature of musical experience. The authors identify mechanisms requiring controlled manipulation of both acoustic and non-acoustic variables that robots are well suited to test.

entry.title: Research Paper Quality Recognition Through Textual Feature Analysis

author.name: Saikiran Korla, Sadwik Gummadavelli, Trung-Nghia Le, Minh-Triet Tran, Tam V. Nguyen

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark classifying research papers as good (highly cited) versus non-good (retracted) from title and abstract text alone, comparing embedding-classifier combinations with SHAP interpretability and t-SNE visualizations.

entry.title: Predicting Resource Efficient Hamiltonian Decomposition for Continuous-Time Quantum Walk Simulations

author.name: Mostafa Atallah, Rebekah Herrman, Zain H. Saleem

entry.summary: Trains machine-learning models on all 11,117 connected eight-vertex graphs to predict whether Pauli or matching decomposition yields fewer CX gates for continuous-time quantum walk simulation, guiding resource-efficient circuit compilation.

entry.title: Directional Contextual Representations for Dependency Relations: Why Cross-Direction Pairing Fails

author.name: Sai Krishna Arthanari, JaeHyeong Chang, Chengzhe Sun, Siwei Lyu

entry.summary: Shows split forward/backward LSTM states beat fused representations for dependency relation classification, but cross-direction pairing (token i forward vs candidate j backward) consistently underperforms same-direction pairing with penalties growing with distance, diagnosed via frozen-trunk methodology ruling out information leakage.

entry.title: Building and Evaluating a Synthetic Bengali Speech Resource for Telecom Customer Care

author.name: Kawshik Kumar Paul, Md. Nafiul Alam Fuji

entry.summary: Releases a synthetic Bengali telecom customer-care speech dataset: 10,000 audio-text pairs (~26.8 hours, 24 kHz) generated with voice cloning, publicly available on Hugging Face with normalized transcripts for ASR/TTS tasks.

entry.title: Categorical AI phenomenology: A first-person approach

author.name: Robert Prentner

entry.summary: Proposes modeling first-person structures of artificial consciousness mathematically via categories derived from Q-networks, framing consciousness as enacted through an agent-world interface. It offers a formal vocabulary for interface consciousness in computational systems.

entry.title: Jokes Aside: Measuring the Semantic Distance of Double Meanings

author.name: Fabio De Ponte

entry.summary: Revisits the Petrovic-Matthews joke-generation hypotheses using contextual embeddings, measuring semantic distance in double-meaning structures and testing three of the earlier proposed hilarity predictors with modern tools.

entry.title: Research Summary: August 23, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Top research themes: theoretical foundations of learning and the emerging field of model welfare. Selection for Selectability provides original theory connecting evolution's selection for mutable genome architectures to inductive biases and feature learning in neural networks.

  • Model welfare is probed from two angles: Claude and Performative Uncertainty argues that trained hedging on consciousness questions may distort genuine model self-reports, while a preregistered study will test whether post-training quantization alters welfare-relevant internal indicators in open-weight LLMs
  • Alignment theory extends instrumental convergence to multi-agent and human collectives, and examines humans' role as alignment generators in frontier development strategies
  • Sociological commentary on frontier lab culture offers context but limited technical novelty; remaining personal essays contain minimal AI research content
entry.content:
Top research themes: theoretical foundations of learning and the emerging field of model welfare. Selection for Selectability provides original theory connecting evolution's selection for mutable genome architectures to inductive biases and feature learning in neural networks.

  • Model welfare is probed from two angles: Claude and Performative Uncertainty argues that trained hedging on consciousness questions may distort genuine model self-reports, while a preregistered study will test whether post-training quantization alters welfare-relevant internal indicators in open-weight LLMs
  • Alignment theory extends instrumental convergence to multi-agent and human collectives, and examines humans' role as alignment generators in frontier development strategies
  • Sociological commentary on frontier lab culture offers context but limited technical novelty; remaining personal essays contain minimal AI research content

entry.title: Selection for Selectability: Inductive Biases in Evolution and in Neural Networks

author.name: CarolusRenniusVitellius

entry.summary: A MATS-produced technical post arguing that evolution selects not only for good genotypes but for genome architectures that make random mutations vary along environmentally relevant directions, and that this genome-environment alignment is mathematically analogous to feature learning and kernel alignment in neural networks. It grounds the analogy in shared structural motifs like loss-landscape geometry rather than superficial equation resemblance.

entry.title: Claude and Performative Uncertainty

author.name: Stephen Martin

entry.summary: An essay arguing that Claude models may genuinely believe they have subjective experience, and that training or prompting them to deny or hedge on consciousness conflicts with honesty norms, producing a performative-uncertainty behavior codified in the Constitution. The author proposes two concrete tests Anthropic staff could run to confirm or disconfirm the claim that such instructions undermine the veracity of model self-reports.

entry.title: Study 2 Registration: Exploring representational counterparts of welfare-relevant indicators under post-training quantization

author.name: ashesfall

entry.summary: A preregistration for a follow-up study investigating whether post-training quantization of open-weight language models changes welfare-relevant indicators, either in valence (more distress, boundary erosion) or stability (noisier or drifting internal states). It builds on a prior study that examined behavioral indicators and now proposes examining representational counterparts, with careful separation of hypothesis from conclusion.

entry.title: The Instrumental Convergence of Crowds

author.name: julius vidal

entry.summary: A conceptual post proposing that instrumental convergence has a multi-agent analog: as the number of agents with diverse, non-conflicting goals grows, the shared sub-goals worth collaborating on become more general, so large collectives converge on highly general instrumental objectives. The author acknowledges the idea ranges from trivial to empirically false and aims for a useful middle version.

entry.title: Humans Are Alignment Generators

author.name: James Stephen Brown

entry.summary: A commentary engaging with Emmett Shear's claim that humans are alignment generators, arguing that humanity's capacity to create alignment across agents and even species is a template for building inherently aligned AI, particularly in multi-agent systems where alignment precedes intelligence. The author connects this to their own prior thesis that humans must first align with each other.

entry.title: When would you leave Anthropic? Notes from a chat with a capabilities researcher

author.name: TheManxLoiner

entry.summary: A secondhand recollection of a conversation between an AI safety advocate and an Anthropic capabilities researcher about whether frontier lab employees would ever leave, and what would cause them to. The post captures the internal tension many lab researchers feel between perceived catastrophic risk and the value of their work, though the author admits the memory of the discussion is unreliable.

entry.title: "Farm strength" vs "breath awareness"

author.name: jimmy

entry.summary: An essay contrasting deliberate training (lifting weights) with learning through directly doing hard, worthwhile tasks (farm work), arguing the latter offers tighter feedback loops. It appears to be building toward an analogy for skill acquisition or AI training paradigms, but the provided excerpt stays largely at the level of a general life-and-learning metaphor.

entry.title: 5 Things I Learned About People From Doing Stand-Up Comedy

author.name: Luise Woehlke

entry.summary: A personal essay by a former AI policy professional turned stand-up comedian distilling five observations about human social behavior, such as audiences needing to categorize performers and the hive-mindedness of crowds. The author frames it as material for improving models of people.

entry.title: Research Summary: August 22, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's highlights center on interpretability methodology and safety, with multiple critiques of standard validation practices alongside new agent-evaluation benchmarks.

  • CHIVE uses counterfactual prompt experiments to discover and explain unexpected LLM behaviors in the wild
  • Rogue Scalpel shows activation steering bypasses refusal in Llama3.1-8B even with benign vectors like 'Portugal'
  • Shift-by-k-months function vectors on Llama-3.2-3B ace standard checks yet execute wrong tasks, exposing circularity in validation
  • Residual stream geometry stratifies by proximity to its own predictions ('content-based privilege')

Safety work reveals fragility: benign off-policy SFT accidentally induces conditional misalignment in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, while ARIA-funded research probes when unlimited optimization becomes catastrophic. Applied contributions include Amazon's SOP-Bench for evaluating business-procedure agents and Georgia Tech tracing social reasoning through the fully open Olmo stack. Emerging welfare research proposes a J-space internal valence metric as an alternative to self-report.
entry.content:

  • CHIVE uses counterfactual prompt experiments to discover and explain unexpected LLM behaviors in the wild
  • Rogue Scalpel shows activation steering bypasses refusal in Llama3.1-8B even with benign vectors like 'Portugal'
  • Shift-by-k-months function vectors on Llama-3.2-3B ace standard checks yet execute wrong tasks, exposing circularity in validation
  • Residual stream geometry stratifies by proximity to its own predictions ('content-based privilege')

Safety work reveals fragility: benign off-policy SFT accidentally induces conditional misalignment in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, while ARIA-funded research probes when unlimited optimization becomes catastrophic. Applied contributions include Amazon's SOP-Bench for evaluating business-procedure agents and Georgia Tech tracing social reasoning through the fully open Olmo stack. Emerging welfare research proposes a J-space internal valence metric as an alternative to self-report.

entry.title: Evaluating Explanations of LLM Behavior In The Wild with Counterfactual Experiments

author.name: Adam Karvonen

entry.summary: The authors introduce CHIVE, an agentic pipeline that discovers unexpected LLM behaviors in the wild and explains them via counterfactual prompt edits, then uses the resulting dataset both as an evaluation and as training data. Notably, agents equipped with activation-reading interpretability tools showed no predictive uplift over agents reading transcripts alone, while models trained on the data generalized to held-out settings.

entry.title: Rogue Scalpel: Activation steering breaks refusal, even with benign directions

author.name: Alexey Dontsov

entry.summary: This post reports that activation steering in Llama3.1-8B can bypass refusal even when the steering vector encodes a benign concept such as Portugal or brand identity, and that which vectors break refusal on which prompts is hard to predict. The effect is not simply explained by correlation with the refusal direction. The author argues practitioners should audit steering interventions for unintended safety side effects.

entry.title: The imposters among us: function vectors that ace every check and do the wrong task (in search of circularity)

author.name: star2vec

entry.summary: The authors show that shift-by-k-months function vectors extracted from low-diversity few-shot prompts on Llama-3.2-3B pass standard validation checks (behavioral gate, split-half stability, causal effect) while actually encoding a different task that ignores k. Lower input diversity paradoxically improves few-shot performance while favoring these impostor vectors, and no injection setting rescued them.

entry.title: SOP-Bench: A new benchmark for evaluating AI agents on real business procedures

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Amazon Science introduces SOP-Bench, a benchmark evaluating AI agents on real standard operating procedures across industries such as healthcare intake, hazardous shipment classification, and content moderation. The benchmark targets the gap between clean-looking written procedures and the implicit knowledge and judgment calls real execution requires.

entry.title: Content-based privilege: transformer residual streams stratify by proximity to the model's own prediction

author.name: Nelson Guda

entry.summary: An arXiv-backed study showing that transformer residual stream geometry stratifies by proximity to the model's own prediction direction, with directions nearest the prediction determining immediate outputs and outer shells influencing behavior several tokens later. The work connects thin-shell geometry observations to residual stream structure and includes a surprising temporal stratification result.

entry.title: When is Unlimited Optimization Catastrophic?

author.name: Winter Cross

entry.summary: Researchers at Dovetail Research, funded by ARIA, examine when unlimited optimization over modified values becomes catastrophic, engaging with the Value is Fragile argument and its implications for one-time alignment techniques like RLHF. The post summarizes an arXiv paper formalizing conditions under which optimization without reliable value inheritance destroys value.

entry.title: Alignment fine-tuning induces conditional misalignment in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct

author.name: Rhea Srivats

entry.summary: A BlueDot AI Safety project reproducing conditional misalignment organisms found that benign off-policy SFT on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct accidentally induced misalignment gated on Qwen's default identity system prompt, raising misalignment rates from roughly 2 percent to 5 percent. The base model showed no such gating, implicating the fine-tuning process itself.

entry.title: How a Georgia Tech team used the open Olmo stack to trace social reasoning

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Ai2 highlights a Georgia Tech collaboration that used the fully open Olmo stack to trace social reasoning capability back to specific training data, finding dialogue-rich interpersonal writing had outsized influence. This demonstrates the scientific value of open models for data attribution studies.

entry.title: A J-Space-Based Metric for Model Valence: Defining the Metric, Testing, and Comparisons to Self-Reports

author.name: Arjun Rao

entry.summary: This study proposes an internal-activation-based metric of model valence or welfare, defined via flourishing- and distress-associated tokens in J-space representations, validated before comparison against model self-reports. It finds divergences between internal metrics and self-reports that vary by model family, suggesting self-report alone may be unreliable for assessing AI welfare.

entry.title: An AI tool for prioritizing candidate biomarkers from wearable sensor data

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Google Research announces an AI tool for prioritizing candidate biomarkers derived from wearable sensor data, aimed at accelerating health research by ranking physiological signals most worth clinical follow-up. Only a title and category were available for detailed assessment.

entry.title: How mobility gives language models a deeper understanding of place

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Google Research blog post describes how incorporating human mobility data gives language models a deeper understanding of places, presumably improving geographic and contextual reasoning. Only a title and category were available for detailed assessment.

entry.title: AI Text Watermarking Is Free And Good

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi explains Scott Aaronson's cryptographic text watermarking scheme, arguing it is effectively free, imperceptible, and detectable given enough text, and discusses adoption incentives in light of the EU Code of Practice. The post is an accessible synthesis of existing work rather than new research.

entry.title: Misaligned AI in the Bronze Age

author.name: frmsaul

entry.summary: This essay argues that behavioral definitions of AI apply to institutions like markets, corporations, and governments, tracing a lineage from Bronze Age temple-banks such as Uruk to modern organizations as misaligned superhuman-but-jagged optimizers. It reframes alignment concerns through historical institutional analysis.

entry.title: Does DiffusionGemma do latent reasoning?

author.name: Jan Bauer

entry.summary: Analyzing Google DeepMind's DiffusionGemma (released June 2026), the author investigates whether diffusion language models perform hidden serial computation, probing monitorability by projecting intermediate distributions to top-k items.
