This replaces discrete diagnostic classification with continuous progression estimation.

entry.title: When to Retrain: An Empirical Study of Retraining Policies for Streaming ML Under Concept Drift, Budget, and Latency Constraints

author.name: Sawan Dasari

entry.summary: A controlled empirical comparison of periodic, error-threshold, and drift-detector-triggered retraining against never retraining, under explicit budget limits and the realistic delay between triggering retraining and deploying the new model. Nearly four thousand runs across drift regimes and budget settings yield practical guidance on refresh policies.

entry.title: Inject, Align, Recover: Staged Post-Training for Retrieval-Free Document Knowledge Internalization

author.name: Qian Kou, Xiaofeng Shi, Xiaosong Qiu, Hua Zhou

entry.summary: IAR is a three-stage post-training recipe for turning a fixed document corpus into parametric knowledge for retrieval-free QA: Inject converts documents into continuation, rewrite and reconstruction objectives, Align adds answer-only QA supervision, and Recover merges to restore general ability. It separates knowledge acquisition from behavioral formatting and from capability preservation. It offers an alternative to always-on retrieval for bounded corpora.

entry.title: CAViAR: A Causal Video Dataset for Fine-Grained Accident Reasoning in Real-World Scenarios

author.name: Sparsh Garg, Yi-Wen Chen, Vijay Kumar B G, Abhishek Aich

entry.summary: CAViAR is a human-annotated dashcam benchmark of 2,249 real accident videos labeled with environmental conditions, accident type, causal explanation, at-fault agent, affected agent and apparent rule violation. It targets responsibility attribution and rule-violation reasoning, which perception-focused autonomous driving benchmarks do not cover. It supports evaluation of high-level causal reasoning for driving systems.

entry.title: Open-Vocabulary 3D Object Detection with Co-Distillation Discovery and Dual Guidance Robust Training

author.name: Shangbo Yuan, Jie Xu, Xiaofeng Zhu, Na Zhao

entry.summary: Improves open-vocabulary 3D object detection by making foundation-model-based novel object discovery more reliable through co-distillation and by adding dual-guidance robust training that tolerates noisy pseudo-labels. It attacks localization and classification errors that propagate through the standard two-stage pipeline.

entry.title: ID-VTG: Image-Disambiguated Video Temporal Grounding

author.name: Minghang Zheng, Jingli Wei, Hongyi Yang, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Introduces image-disambiguated video temporal grounding, where a reference image plus text localizes the segment in which a specific individual performs an action, with two new benchmarks covering gymnastics and open-world video. The task targets cases where fine visual attributes cannot be described in words.

entry.title: Flow Matching-Based PET Image Reconstruction

author.name: Fumio Hashimoto, Ziqian Huang, Tatsuya Yokota, Kuang Gong

entry.summary: Applies flow matching to PET image reconstruction, exploiting the fact that flow models can estimate clean images from intermediate states so data-consistency refinement can be decoupled from flow propagation. A Poisson-likelihood guidance term with an expectation-maximization preconditioner adapts the method to PET physics.

entry.title: World-Model-Grounded LLM Planning for AUV and ASV Navigation Near Offshore Wind Farms

author.name: Markus Buchholz, Ignacio Carlucho, Yvan R. Petillot

entry.summary: Grounds LLM mission planning for underwater and surface vehicles in a physics-based neural world model, adding a three-phase trajectory optimizer and MPC-style closed-loop replanning with a trust-region guard. The language model decides what to do while the world model determines feasible durations and collision risk across different thruster configurations.

entry.title: Verifiable abstention makes AI leak diagnosis accountable in water distribution networks

author.name: Tianwei Mu, Yue Wang, Mingzhe Yuan, Manhong Huang, Wenhong Wang, Xuerui Yin, Qing Luo, Min Xiao, Hui Yang, Jun Li, Dan Xue

entry.summary: Recasts water distribution leak localization as decision-making under verifiable abstention, using a physics-grounded executor agent that falsifies competing hypotheses against a digital twin and an independent supervisor with an LLM auditor that checks evidence against a code-verifiable contract before certifying a dispatch, requesting more evidence, or abstaining. Under field-grade noise, decision precision on acted events rises from 32 percent forced baseline to 96 percent.

entry.title: TokenPowerSandbox: Evidence-Gated CPU-First Screening for Energy-Aware LLM Serving

author.name: Chenxu Niu

entry.summary: Introduces an energy-aware LLM serving workflow that uses a cheap CPU-side projector plus short GPU probes and frozen, tamper-evident provenance to predict serving energy without exhaustive profiling. On a single H100 with a 7B model it reports energy prediction error near 6 to 7 percent on blind holdouts.

entry.title: The Role of Grid Cells in Reducing Spatial Aliasing in Hippocampal Place Representations

author.name: Alexander Johnson, Obadah Ghizawi, Ali A. Minai

entry.summary: Shows in a computational model that adding grid-cell inputs disambiguates place representations that would otherwise be identical in symmetric or repetitive environments driven only by boundary-derived sensory cues. The result clarifies a functional role for internally generated periodic spatial signals.

entry.title: Change Point--Aware Evaluation and Re-Calibration of PPG-Based Blood Pressure Estimation

author.name: Yunwon Tae, Minje Park, Gyunho Rho, Dongjoon Yoo, Sunghoon Joo

entry.summary: Argues that averaged error metrics hide failures of photoplethysmography-based blood pressure models during rapid physiological changes, and proposes evaluating around automatically detected change points. It also explores recalibration targeted at those fluctuation periods.

entry.title: Composed Historical Image Retrieval by Modeling Temporal Representations

author.name: Adri\`a Molina Rodr\'iguez, Oriol Ramos Terrades, Josep Llad\'os Canet

entry.summary: Learns image representations that explicitly decompose a temporal component from other visual content, so that historical photographs can be retrieved with composed time-aware queries without collapsing the embedding to a single dimension. The paper develops the mathematical basis for such decomposable representations.

entry.title: SIDScope: A Diagnostic Resource for Semantic-ID Interfaces in Generative Recommendation

author.name: Jiandong Ding, Huijie Qin, Tiandeng Wu, Yi Cao

entry.summary: Provides diagnostics for the semantic identifier mappings that connect item tokenizers to generative recommenders, checking provenance, structure, path resolution and what changes after a refresh. Across nine exported mappings it finds interface health is multi-signal rather than a single score.

entry.title: Understanding Multilingual Medical ASR Adaptation Through Layer-Wise Analysis

author.name: Souranil Kahali, Rituparna Bose, Abner Hernandez, Tomas Arias-Vergara, Andreas Maier, Ning Ma, Paula Andrea Perez-Toro

entry.summary: Analyzes how medical and multilingual fine-tuning reshapes the internal encoder representations of Whisper models, comparing zero-shot decoding, English-only, German-only, staged, and joint bilingual adaptation. It goes beyond word error rate by using layer-wise probing to explain where adaptation actually changes the model.

entry.title: rEDMRec: Distilling Large Language Model Reasoning into an Editable Experience Memory for Recommendation

author.name: Minh Hoang Nguyen, Tung Le, Huy Tien Nguyen

entry.summary: rEDMRec distills expensive teacher-LLM reasoning about user preferences into a compact, editable experience memory that a lightweight ranking model retrieves from, avoiding regeneration on every request. The memory is also inspectable and correctable as user tastes drift.

entry.title: From Threat Intelligence to Detection: Knowledge-driven Enrichment and Template-based Rule Grounding for Automated Sigma Rule Generation

author.name: Sepehr Ghaffarzadegan, Boubakr Nour, Makan Pourzandi, Mourad Debbabi, Chadi Assi

entry.summary: Proposes an LLM pipeline that enriches cyber threat intelligence reports with knowledge and then generates Sigma detection rules constrained by templates, so outputs remain syntactically valid and deployable across SIEM platforms. It aims to shorten the gap between new threat reports and working detection logic.

entry.title: Leaf Values as Coordinates: Exact Contrastive Explanation for Gradient-Boosted Ensembles

author.name: Emanuele Luzio

entry.summary: Observes that a gradient-boosted ensemble is exactly linear in the space of per-tree leaf values, so differences between two instances are supported only on trees where their leaves differ. This yields exact, sparse contrastive explanations and a recourse method with no sampling, surrogate fitting, or feature-additivity assumptions.

entry.title: Quantum Kernel Estimation for the Discovery of Early Lung Cancer Detection

author.name: Hamed Javidi, Alex Zajichek, Hakan Doga, Laxmi Parida, Filippo Utro, Peter J. Mazzone

entry.summary: Evaluates hybrid quantum-classical kernel methods for early lung cancer detection from cell-free DNA fragmentomics and methylation features, comparing angle and dense-angle encodings with several entanglement strategies against classical baselines. Feature selection reduces inputs to 20 and 40 dimensions to fit fidelity-based quantum kernel computation.

entry.title: Answer-Level Trust Selection for Physical Vision-Language Reasoning

author.name: Rongyu Yu, Ke Niu, Fengxiang He

entry.summary: Formulates answer-level selective prediction for quantitative physical reasoning by vision-language models and proposes a post-hoc, model-agnostic framework to accept or reject individual estimates of duration, speed, or acceleration. It argues self-consistency alone is insufficient because models can be stably wrong or rely on text priors instead of visual evidence.

entry.title: CLaST: Context-aware Contrastive VAE for Probabilistic Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Alexander Marusov, Dmitry Anikin, Petr Sokerin, Vitaliy Pozdnyakov, Ilya Kuleshov, Alexey Zaytsev

entry.summary: CLaST is a variational autoencoder for probabilistic multivariate time-series forecasting that adds a contrastive objective so that latent embeddings preserve contextual similarity between observations. It reports gains across nine standard forecasting benchmarks.

entry.title: DecoVAE: a Lightweight Interpretable Trend-Seasonal VAE Framework for Efficient Probabilistic Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Alexander Marusov, Dmitry Anikin, Alexey Zaytsev

entry.summary: DecoVAE is a probabilistic forecasting VAE that explicitly separates trend and seasonal streams with matched inductive biases, applying a smoothness regularizer on the latent trend trajectory and frequency-domain modeling for seasonality. The goal is interpretable decomposition with low memory and runtime cost.

entry.title: Dynamic Structural Causal Modeling for Sleep

author.name: Ranveer Singh, Saurabh Mathur, Pranuthi Tenali, Arun Badi, Sriraam Natarajan

entry.summary: Learns dynamic causal graphs of sleep-disordered breathing from 105 home sleep apnea test recordings using a constraint-based temporal causal discovery algorithm with domain-knowledge edge constraints and bootstrap aggregation. Results show that apnea-desaturation links persist across sex and age subgroups while other relationships vary.

entry.title: Physical-Support Confidence Sets for Highly Coherent Dictionaries

author.name: Guan-Ju Peng

entry.summary: Addresses the problem that sparse recovery over highly coherent learned dictionaries can produce an accurate atom support whose physical interpretation is not actually supported by calibration data. It builds confidence sets over physical supports by retaining all calibration-compatible dictionaries and deployment-compatible sparse codes.

entry.title: TorchDCM: A Unified PyTorch-Native Package for Discrete Choice Modeling

author.name: Baichuan Mo, Zhengzhong Ricky You, Xiqun Michael Chen, Ruimin Li

entry.summary: Introduces TorchDCM, a PyTorch-native library that compiles discrete choice model specifications into a unified differentiable likelihood engine supporting estimation, inference, and prediction on CPU or GPU. It targets the gap between mature econometric software and scalable differentiable computation.

entry.title: Interpretable Feature Learning for RF Fingerprinting via Polar MKANs

author.name: Mikhail Krasnov, Ljupcho Milosheski, Carolina Fortuna

entry.summary: Proposes a block-partitioned monotonic Kolmogorov-Arnold network on polar-coordinate radio inputs so each latent dimension depends only on magnitude or phase, giving disentangled and monotone features for radio frequency device fingerprinting. It reports much higher disentanglement scores than unpartitioned baselines on a synthetic gain and carrier-offset benchmark.

entry.title: From Noise to Signal: Improving Security Log Anomaly Detection Using LLMs with Endpoint-Specific Logs

author.name: Christopher Henshaw, Gour Karmakar

entry.summary: Builds a standardized instruction-based classification framework using language models to detect anomalous authentication behaviour in endpoint security logs, including borderline cases missed by rule-based and statistical baselines. It emphasizes endpoint-specific log data rather than generic public datasets.

entry.title: Daedalus-150M: A Convolution-Attention Hybrid Designed for CPU Inference

author.name: Christos Koutsiaris

entry.summary: Daedalus-150M inverts the usual design flow by targeting single-user 4-bit CPU inference first, keeping full attention in only 6 of 18 blocks and using fixed two-timestep convolutions elsewhere so most of the network never re-reads a growing cache. Trained from scratch on about 60B tokens, it reportedly beats GPT-2 124M, Pythia-160M, OPT-125M and GPT-Neo-125M that saw far more data. It is a case study in hardware-first small-model architecture.

entry.title: CVSD-Reg: Cross-Modal Visual Semantic Prior Distillation for Robust LiDAR Registration

author.name: Eunsoo Im, Junghun Suh, Gyeonggwan Lee, Seunghwan Hong

entry.summary: CVSD-Reg distills semantic priors from a frozen DINOv2 vision teacher into a Point Transformer V3 LiDAR encoder using contrastive and spherical-manifold alignment, aiming for registration descriptors robust to density, viewpoint, and sensor changes. It reflects the broader trend of transferring 2D foundation-model knowledge into 3D sensing.

entry.title: Accelerated Genetic Programming Hyper-Heuristics for Simulation-Based Scheduling via Agentic AI

author.name: Heyang Thomas Li, Alexander Pletzer, Yuan Tian, Yi Mei, Mengjie Zhang

entry.summary: Uses agentic AI to profile and refactor slow Python research code for discrete-event project-scheduling simulations used in genetic-programming hyper-heuristics, where nested loops and object-oriented state updates resist library vectorization. The aim is to give researchers large speedups without specialized low-level optimization expertise.

entry.title: Governance Records as Supervision: Verifier-Selected Self-Training for Structured Workflow Repair

author.name: Jesus Salas

entry.summary: Tests whether governance records from machine-verifiable workflows, linking task contract, attempt, verifier decision, and accepted output, can serve as training supervision. Plans generated by a 14B model in thinking mode and accepted by an independent planning verifier were used to fine-tune the same checkpoint for non-thinking execution, raising verifier-accepted plans from 1 to 57 out of 80 held-out cases with no regressions.

entry.title: Which Negatives Matter? Ask Your Text Encoder: Adaptive Similarity Margins for Dense-Caption Retrieval

author.name: Haoyue Liu, Ye Chen, Zhichao Wang, Xiaoying Tang

entry.summary: Diagnoses that InfoNCE-based contrastive fine-tuning saturates on dense caption retrieval, with loss dropping below one thousandth on most batches in the first epoch and gradients becoming numerically zero in almost half of measurements because of near-duplicate captions. HN-CLIP responds with adaptive similarity margins derived from the text encoder so that hard negatives continue to provide learning signal.

entry.title: Self-prompting and cross-model consensus enable reproducible data extraction from scientific literature with large language models

author.name: Valentin Romanov, Monique Bax, Steven Niederer

entry.summary: Evaluates four escalating workflows for extracting contextualized data from research articles using browser-based frontier LLMs, finding that models perform well with expert prompts, can author nearly as effective prompts themselves, but fail substantially at autonomous literature discovery by missing or hallucinating references. Cross-model consensus is used to improve reproducibility of extractions.

entry.title: Stopping and Routing LLM Judge Panels

author.name: Bin Zhu, Yi Xie, Yanghui Rao

entry.summary: Formulates the design of LLM judge panels as a role-conditioned allocation problem, using a small labeled audit set to classify candidate judges as redundant copies, global complements, or slice specialists, then deriving a policy for which judges to call on which examples and when to stop adding them. It targets the cost and redundancy of modern evaluation stacks that mix judges, reward models and safety classifiers. It brings decision-theoretic discipline to LLM-as-judge pipelines.

entry.title: G-CARL: Grounded Checklist-Aligned Reward Learning for Patient-Oriented Medical Report Interpretation

author.name: Shiao Xie, Siyu Chen, Jianwei Lv, Bo Yuan, Yujin Wang, Xiandong Li

entry.summary: Defines patient-oriented medical report interpretation as an open-ended multimodal generation task requiring both evidence-grounded factuality and accessible, context-aware patient communication, then proposes grounded checklist-aligned reward learning to optimize these differently-verifiable objectives jointly. Conventional supervised fine-tuning conflates the two goals. It targets a genuine clinical communication need.

entry.title: From Retrieved Context to Runtime Control: Adaptive Compression for Edge-based RAG

author.name: Zlatan Feric, Amir Taherin, Yanzhi Wang, David Kaeli

entry.summary: Argues that fixed or offline-selected context-compression rates for retrieval-augmented generation ignore workload variation and device state, and that on an edge SoC the compressor itself consumes the latency and energy it is meant to save. The paper proposes runtime-adaptive compression control that accounts for live device conditions. It matters for on-device RAG energy and latency budgets.

entry.title: Learning to Beat: Phenotype-Guided Latent Flow with Regional Motion Priors for Biventricular Motion Synthesis

author.name: Xuan Yang, Xiaohan Yuan, Hao Li, Lingyu Chen, Yanan Liu, Qingya Li, Lei Li

entry.summary: Synthesizes full cardiac-cycle biventricular motion from a single end-diastolic mesh using motion-informed functional parcellation combined with conditional latent flow, making deformation region-specific and phenotype-adaptive. It addresses the practical scarcity of dense 3D-plus-time cardiac meshes.

entry.title: STEP: Score-Based Temporal Energy for Human Pose Video Anomaly Detection

author.name: Jakub Micorek, Mateusz Kozi\'nski, Horst Possegger

entry.summary: STEP notes that adding noise to raw joint coordinates when training energy-based models for skeleton anomaly detection creates physically impossible poses, worsening with longer temporal windows. Projecting pose sequences into a whitened PCA space keeps injected noise physically meaningful and stabilizes density learning.

entry.title: Gravity-aware partially calibrated absolute pose estimation from affine- or rotation-covariant features

author.name: Marcus Valtonen \"Ornhag, Alberto Jaenal, Stefan Adalbj\"ornsson

entry.summary: Derives new minimal-solver constraints for absolute pose plus focal length estimation that exploit both a gravity direction from IMUs and the local affine or rotation covariance embedded in feature descriptors. This extends recent covariant-feature pose work to the partially calibrated case.

entry.title: HandMvNet: Real-Time 3D Hand Pose Estimation Using Multi-View Cross-Attention Fusion

author.name: Muhammad Asad Ali, Nadia Robertini, Didier Stricker

entry.summary: HandMvNet estimates absolute 3D hand pose and shape from multiple camera views in real time via multi-view cross-attention fusion, resolving the scale-depth ambiguity of monocular methods without requiring camera parameters as input. It reports competitive accuracy at substantially lower inference cost.

entry.title: PelviNeXt: A Modality-Agnostic Hybrid Network for Pelvic Imaging in Women's Health

author.name: Siam Tahsin Bhuiyan, Rashedur Rahman, Sefatul Wasi, Halima Khatun, Ashraful Islam, AKM Mahbubur Rahman, Saadia Binte Alam, M Ashraful Amin

entry.summary: PelviNeXt is a modality-agnostic hybrid CNN-attention network applied unchanged to pelvic ultrasound and X-ray for PCOS and fracture tasks in the under-resourced area of women's health imaging. While benchmarking, the authors discovered extensive exact and near-duplicate images in the main public PCOS dataset, a data-integrity finding with implications for prior reported results.

entry.title: Spiking Local Interaction and Adaptive Complementary Fusion for Spiking Transformer

author.name: Dongcheng Zhao, Sicheng Shen, Zhenyu Yang, Zhiyuan Li, Jinyan Yu, Yongjian Wang, Tiechui Yao, Wenli Zhang, Tielin Zhang

entry.summary: Adds an attention-independent local interaction pathway to spiking transformers using lightweight depthwise and pointwise transformations, then adaptively fuses it with spiking self-attention via layer-specific channel-wise coefficients. The motivation is that binary queries and keys collapse continuous similarity into sparse responses and suppress weak local relations.

entry.title: BASC : Behavior-Aligned Quantization and Pruning for Low-Bit Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Linliang Chen, Yan Zhong, Xin Liu, Sai Li, Wang Kang

entry.summary: BASC argues that quantization and pruning of spiking neural networks fail because their local criteria ignore temporal task feedback and inter-channel dependencies, a mismatch the authors call criterion-behavior mismatch. It aligns compression decisions with network behavior to get better low-bit SNNs for constrained devices.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Agents as Dynamic Graph Transformation: A Survey and New Perspective

author.name: Yuanyuan Xu, Wenjie Zhang, Yin Chen, Xuemin Lin, Ying Zhang

entry.summary: A survey that reinterprets self-evolving LLM agents as processes of dynamic graph transformation, where memories, tools, skills, workflows, and inter-agent relations form an evolving topology rather than a static support structure. It aims to unify the graph-for-agents and self-evolving-agents literatures.

entry.title: Evaluating Structured Information Extraction with Open Models in a High Risk Public Sector Application

author.name: Elias Schubert, Felix Bie{\ss}mann

entry.summary: Benchmarks open-source OCR engines, LLMs, and vision-language models on realistic multi-step structured information extraction pipelines in a public sector application that the EU AI Act would classify as high risk. The goal is to determine whether open alternatives can responsibly substitute for proprietary extraction services.

entry.title: FinRCA-Bench: Benchmarking Evidence Retrieval and Reasoning for Financial AI Systems

author.name: Pratik Ghawate

entry.summary: FinRCA-Bench is a deterministic synthetic benchmark of 2,250 accounts-payable-to-bank reconciliation cases across 14 operational tables, with 1,500 injected failures in 15 causal categories plus legitimate and hard-negative cases. Its purpose is to disentangle whether financial reasoning failures come from bad evidence retrieval across relational links or from genuinely poor reasoning.

entry.title: Eureka: Task-Conditioned Meta-Agent Orchestration for Scientific Discovery

author.name: Alizer Wong, Heng Cui, Yi Tan, Xiongchao Zhan, Liang Lin, Yuxiang Guo, Zhaorong Dai, Zixin Zeng, Wenyuan Li

entry.summary: Eureka compiles long-horizon scientific tasks into dynamic obligation graphs with explicit acceptance criteria, forming specialized macro-agents with their own state, tools, and verifiers through receding-horizon planning and cost-gated architecture evolution. The authors report theoretical results on regret and serializability plus completion of all 170 recursive tasks with nearly 4,000 certificates and no false acceptances.

entry.title: NE-BERT: A Multilingual Language Model for Nine Northeast Indian Languages

author.name: Badal Nyalang

entry.summary: NE-BERT is a multilingual encoder trained on roughly 8.3 million sentences covering nine Northeast Indian languages plus Hindi and English, using weighted data sampling and a custom unigram tokenizer. It reports substantially lower perplexity than IndicBERT-V2 and MuRIL across all nine target languages and better tokenization fertility than mBERT.

entry.title: Institutional Prestige as Geographic Bias in Large Language Models: Evidence from Three Factorial Experiments with Bootstrap Confidence Intervals

author.name: Maikel Leyva-Vazquez, Florentin Smarandache

entry.summary: Three factorial experiments across four LLMs and five professional domains test whether candidate evaluations are swayed by applicant name ethnicity versus institutional prestige and country. Prestige effects are robust and substantially larger than name-origin effects, which are near zero.

entry.title: Aslema at NADI 2026: Augmentation through Fewshot for SLU

author.name: Tajwaar Shafiq, Hunzalah Hassan Bhatti, Shammur Absar Chowdhury, Firoj Alam

entry.summary: A shared-task system for Tunisian Arabic spoken language understanding that compares zero-shot omni-modal LLMs with fine-tuned models and adds synthetic dialectal utterances generated by an LLM and voiced through cloning. Fine-tuning plus synthetic augmentation improves both intent recognition and slot filling.

entry.title: Quantifying Event Impacts on Time Series via Multiscale Contrastive Learning

author.name: Yiming Sun, Shengyu Chen, Zhengzhang Chen, Haoyu Wang, Xiaowei Jia, Haifeng Chen

entry.summary: Formulates event-conditioned impact prediction, estimating short-term abnormal financial loss after discrete disclosures such as cybersecurity breaches using pre-event market history and sparse event metadata. A multiscale contrastive learning approach is used because standard forecasters rely on endogenous trend and seasonality and fail on rare heterogeneous shocks.

entry.title: LLM as Detector: An In-context Learning Approach for Tabular Anomaly Detection

author.name: Tu Anh Hoang Nguyen, Dang Nguyen, Thuc Duy Le, Trung Le, Sunil Gupta

entry.summary: LLM-Detector converts normal tabular training data into statistical summaries, causal dependency descriptions, and prototypes, then prompts an LLM to synthesize scoring code that captures anomaly logic from cross-feature dependencies. This uses in-context learning instead of fine-tuning or synthetic anomaly generation.

entry.title: DraftFM: A FoundationModel for Day-Zero Drafting in Magic: The Gathering

author.name: Brian Ward

entry.summary: DraftFM tackles the day-zero card drafting problem in Magic: The Gathering, where the card list is public but no pick logs exist, by scoring only available cards through frozen features derived from public card records and text embeddings. With no card or set identities in the model, a 1.6M-parameter network trained on 149 million historical picks generalizes to unseen cards.

entry.title: FleetSieve: Decision-Critical Profiling for SLO-Aware LLM Fleet Configuration

author.name: Huang Cheng, Scott Zhang, Aubert Li

entry.summary: FleetSieve chooses which serving configurations to profile based on their expected influence on the final fleet allocation decision, jointly modeling throughput capacity and tail latency and stopping when conservative and optimistic allocations converge. On an H100 grid for a 31B open-weight model it matches the exhaustive-search decision using far fewer measurements.

entry.title: Online Test-Time Adaptation for Generalizable Dynamic Graph Anomaly Detection

author.name: Jialun Zheng, Hanchen Yang, Jiannong Cao, Yankai Chen, Yuanjing Feng, Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: OTTA-DGAD adapts a pretrained dynamic graph anomaly detector to unseen domains when target data arrive as sequential unlabeled chunks, extracting evolving prototypes of normal and anomalous behavior from temporal ego-graphs. This combines domain-agnostic and evolving domain-specific patterns instead of assuming access to the full target dataset.

entry.title: From Street View Imagery to Street Quality Indicators: Vision Language Inference for the Suburban 15-minute City

author.name: Joan Perez, Giovanni Fusco

entry.summary: Uses an open-source vision-language model workflow to assess streetscape quality from street view imagery across suburban and peri-urban areas near Nice, in support of pedestrian-oriented 15-minute city planning. It substitutes large-scale automated inference for costly manual field surveys.

entry.title: Transfer Learning in Nonparametric Regression with Deep ReLU Networks

author.name: Junpeng Ren, Carlos Misael Madrid Padilla, Yanzhen Chen, Oscar Hernan Madrid Padilla

entry.summary: Establishes a transfer-learning framework for nonparametric regression across multiple groups that share a common mean function plus group-specific additive offsets, via a two-stage pooling-then-offset estimator. The authors derive L2 error upper bounds for broad estimator classes and explicit convergence rates when deep ReLU networks are used. It gives theory for a very common practical recipe.

entry.title: A Virtual Member of a Community of Practice for the Society of Petroleum Engineers: From Prototype to Deployment

author.name: John Boden, Joshua Eckroth, Dayne Freitag, Skyler Gipson, Johnathan Keefe, Karen Myers, Eric Schoen, Pedro Sequeira, Reid Smith, Michael Wessel

entry.summary: Reports the evolution and deployment of ATHENA, a virtual knowledge assistant for a petroleum-engineering community of practice, after a first prototype study with 75 professionals showed large productivity gains and reduced performance inequality relative to a strong RAG baseline. The paper describes upgrades in multi-document retrieval, answer validation and proactive assistance. It is a rare account of a measured, real-world professional deployment.

entry.title: Where Grounding Accuracy Lives on the IoU Curve: Label-Free Inference-Time Boundary Refinement

author.name: Bo Ma

entry.summary: Studies label-free, inference-time refinement of bounding boxes from a frozen vision-language grounding model: small predicted regions trigger a higher-resolution re-grounding pass inside a context crop, gated by geometric guards. Reports meaningful mAcc gains on tens of thousands of Ref-L4 expressions, especially at strict IoU thresholds.

entry.title: Scale-Separated Conditioning for Style-Encoder-Free Diffusion Stylization

author.name: Jingtao Zhang, Haorui Gao, Youqing Liang, Zeming Liu

entry.summary: SEFS performs reference-based diffusion stylization without any style encoder or aligned content-style-target triplets, deriving style tokens from stochastic low-resolution crops so that palette and texture transfer while global layout leaks less. Content is supplied via edge and segmentation conditioning in a diffusion transformer.

entry.title: Point-Based 3D Reconstruction from Sparse Views under Known Illumination

author.name: Magnus Kaufmann Gjerde, Joakim Bruslund Haurum, Jeppe Revall Frisvad, Markus Worchel, J. Andreas B{\ae}rentzen, Thomas B. Moeslund

entry.summary: Proposes differentiable point-based reconstruction using opacity-bearing beta surfels with an adjoint light-transport formulation, so physically based illumination constrains geometry and appearance under known lighting. Evaluated on five synthetic objects from ten posed views.

entry.title: G3Ego: Gaze-Guided Graphs for Egocentric Action Understanding

author.name: Marko Haralovi\'c, Akash Ramakrishnan, Estefania Talavera Martinez

entry.summary: G3Ego builds action scene graphs from sparsely sampled egocentric frames using vision-language descriptions, grounded objects, and hand cues, then prunes irrelevant entities using the wearer's gaze before temporal aggregation. It uses gaze as a structural pruning signal rather than an extra input feature.

entry.title: AsymFeX: A Symmetry-Driven Framework for Ischemic Stroke Segmentation Across Imaging Modalities and Stroke Stages

author.name: Maunil Shah, Vaanathi Sundaresan

entry.summary: AsymFeX segments acute ischemic stroke lesions by first correcting head tilt to the true mid-sagittal plane and then comparing each voxel with its contralateral neighborhood through cross-hemisphere attention, mirroring radiologist practice. It is designed to be compatible with standard nnU-Net pipelines across modalities and stroke stages.

entry.title: Fractional Decay KV-Cache: Ownership-Aware Memory Management for Improved Inference Relevancy in Dialog Systems

author.name: Sukanta Ganguly

entry.summary: Proposes a KV cache eviction policy for dialog systems that scores each cached entry along two channels, cumulative attention importance and a recency-weighted relevance signal governed by temporal decay with reinforcement-style updates. The combination is meant to retain historically important tokens while adapting quickly when the conversation topic shifts.

entry.title: What Can Artificial Intelligence Learn from Medicine? Generative Analogies and Reliable Machine Learning Systems

author.name: Emanuele Ratti, Lena Zuchowski

entry.summary: A philosophy-of-science analysis arguing that the frequent comparison between clinical translation and machine learning deployment is best understood as a generative analogy, and works out which epistemic warrants actually transfer. It aims to give more precise grounding for reliability standards in ML systems.

entry.title: Epistemic Subordination: Generative AI and the Infrastructure of Knowledge

author.name: Gilad Abiri, Emanuel V. Towfigh

entry.summary: A legal and philosophical argument that generative AI harms are not a set of separable biases but a structural condition in which the majority's way of knowing becomes the default infrastructure of knowledge. It traces implications across several legal domains where minority epistemologies are absorbed but subordinated.

entry.title: Discretizing Continuous Time Series for Imputation with Masked Diffusion Training

author.name: Dongbin Kim, Seungyun Lee, Geonwoo Shin, Jaewook Lee

entry.summary: MDTIM adapts masked discrete diffusion training to time-series imputation, using a MASK token that is structurally orthogonal to real observations and predicting original values rather than injected noise. This addresses two limitations of continuous diffusion imputers.

entry.title: In Two Minds about Lifelong Learning: Exploring Hemispheric Redundancy and Specialisation in Neural Models

author.name: Benjamin Smith, Levin Kuhlmann, Kaushik Roy, Gideon Kowadlo

entry.summary: Explores a biologically inspired continual learning architecture with two partially redundant, partially specialized hemisphere-like modules, motivated by the fact that animals avoid catastrophic forgetting while standard networks trade retention against plasticity. It tests whether hemispheric redundancy and specialization help lifelong learning in neural models.

entry.title: Green BOA: Determining the environmental break-even point for ML-based data compression

author.name: Caterina Doglioni, Akshat Gupta, Thomas Elliott, Hanzila Hussain, Sanjiban Sengupta

entry.summary: Summarizes internship projects estimating when machine-learning-based lossless data compression becomes environmentally net-positive, comparing training and inference carbon costs against carbon savings from reduced storage. It frames the analysis as a break-even point calculation.

entry.title: DICS: Data-Informed Centroid Splitting for Decision Tree Classifiers

author.name: MD Saifur Rahman Mazumder, Feng Yu

entry.summary: DICS reduces the cost of decision tree training by using class-aware clustering to construct a compact candidate split set instead of exhaustively searching all thresholds. The authors provide theory suggesting predictive performance is preserved under stated conditions.

entry.title: When Machines Speak: A Unified Generative Framework for Integrating Machine-Native Symbols into Pretrained Large Language Models

author.name: Su Yan, Rakesh Iyer

entry.summary: UniLang extends pretrained LLM vocabularies and embedding spaces so that machine-native discrete symbols such as entity or behavior IDs become first-class generative units alongside natural-language tokens. This bridges structured prediction and language modeling without discarding the compactness of symbolic representations. It targets recommendation and industrial systems where entities are IDs rather than words.

entry.title: Remember, Verify, or Ask? Cross-Family Evaluation of Memory Commitment in LLM Agents

author.name: Baichuan Li, Junyi Yao, Zihao Zheng

entry.summary: Defines the memory-clarification boundary for LLM agents: whether information from an interaction should be persisted durably, used only in-context, re-verified, or clarified with the user, and evaluates it with a 140-scenario benchmark plus a contrast set. Labeling is validated by independent non-author annotators with high agreement, and evaluation covers both action choices and structured tool calls across Claude and Qwen families. Wrong durable writes silently corrupt future agent behavior, so this decision matters.

entry.title: A knowledge-guided agentic framework for mitigating patient-context ambiguity in health queries

author.name: Mahyar Abbasian, Saba A. Farahani, Arshia Ilaty, Hung Cao, Ramesh Jain, Amir M. Rahmani

entry.summary: Proposes a knowledge-guided agentic layer that sits between a patient and an unchanged downstream LLM, detecting when a short health query is underspecified with respect to symptoms, medications, allergies or diet, and eliciting the missing context before answering. This prevents the model from silently assuming clinical facts. It is a modular safety wrapper for health chatbots.

entry.title: HARP: Hierarchical Adaptive Ranking with Preference-Adaptive Fusion for Query-Based CVE Prioritization

author.name: Haochen Liu, Zhengzhang Chen, Haoyu Wang, Yanchi Liu, Jundong Li, Haifeng Chen

entry.summary: HARP ranks CVEs for remediation from a natural-language triage query plus a bank of past validated triage cases, using a graph-grounded multi-view framework with preference-adaptive fusion. The premise is that organizations already hold implicit prioritization preferences that are hard to write as prompt instructions but are visible in historical decisions. It aims to replace fixed scoring criteria with learned organizational preference.

entry.title: Does Listening Matter? Backchanneling and Nodding in AI Clone

author.name: Koji Inoue, Kazushi Kato, Tatsuya Kawahara, Shunichi Kasahara

entry.summary: Adds real-time-predicted verbal backchannels and head nodding to an AI clone that already had voice cloning and LLM-based responses, then measures the effect in a within-subjects study with 35 participants. Listening behaviors significantly improved perceived attentiveness, the sense of talking with the real person, and co-presence. It argues clone fidelity must include how a person listens, not just how they speak.

entry.title: Core-KAN: Continuous Vision Kernels with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks

author.name: Lan Guo, Mengling Li, Haoran Li, Jun Shen, Yuanbo Jiang, Qingguo Zhou, Binbin Yong

entry.summary: Core-KAN builds continuous convolution kernels with Kolmogorov-Arnold-style basis functions conditioned on locally predicted relative scales, decoupling geometric scale adaptation from content-dependent filtering. This avoids the cost of generating kernels at every spatial location.

entry.title: CalcSeg: Confidence-aware 3D Latent Context Curriculum Learning For Myocardial Scar Segmentation From Single-Stack LGE-CMRs

author.name: Nivetha Jayakumar, Hannah Kim, Amit R. Patel, Miaomiao Zhang

entry.summary: CalcSeg segments myocardial scar from single-stack late gadolinium-enhanced cardiac MRI using fused 3D latent context and a confidence-aware semi-supervised curriculum that progresses from easier to harder scar cases. It targets low contrast, small diffuse lesions, and limited 3D context.

entry.title: DART-S: Reachability-Audited Active-Suspension Preconditioning for Off-Road Vehicle Jumps

author.name: Yu Hu, Fangzhou Zhao, Liang Chen, Chen Min, Wei Li, Mingyuan Sang, Jiajia Ma, Shican Chen, Di Pang, Baolei Chen

entry.summary: DART-S preconditions an off-road vehicle's active suspension on the takeoff ramp to reshape pitch, pitch rate, and wheel spin before liftoff, since airborne torque authority alone cannot correct large takeoff errors. A calibration map plus an interval-reachability screen decides which suspension action to apply, validated across hundreds of runs in the BeamNG simulator.

entry.title: Thoughts on Taking OpenAI Foundation Funding

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: A reflective post from a SecureBio-affiliated author about whether to accept funding from the OpenAI Foundation for biosecurity work, weighing the risk of compromised independence and of reducing developers' incentive to build safeguards against the reality that pandemic resilience is needed regardless of any one lab's choices. It documents concrete reasoning about conflict of interest in safety-adjacent philanthropy.

entry.title: ADEPT: Accelerating Dexterity via Pre-Training and Post-Training using Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jayjun Lee, Jessica Yin, Asif Rana, Nicholas Blauch, Sam Mady, Mohak Bhardwaj, Nima Fazeli, Nathan Ratliff, Karl Van Wyk, Ankur Handa

entry.summary: Covered in yesterday's Research roundup, ADEPT is a large-scale reinforcement learning framework that pretrains a dexterous manipulation policy on generic object reposing and then post-trains downstream long-horizon policies using that behavior as a prior, working from raw visuo-tactile input across high-degree-of-freedom hands. The pretrained policy zero-shots the reposing phase, and the paper addresses the instability of naive RL fine-tuning on top of it.

entry.title: Redakto - The Incognito Tab for LLMs

author.name: Saurav Kumar Saha, Tom R\"ohr, Felix Bie{\ss}mann

entry.summary: Redakto is a tool for removing personally identifiable information from text before it is sent to an LLM or downstream processor, supporting both redaction and related privacy functionalities. The authors motivate it by EU legal uncertainty that slows adoption of LLMs in regulated European settings.

entry.title: Improving Natural-Language Combinatorial-Optimization Accuracy in Resource-Constrained Language Models via Formal Abstractions

author.name: Shrenil Shaun Sharma, Avi Sharma

entry.summary: SDDL is a neuro-symbolic framework that translates natural language scheduling problems into compact solver-aligned representations of tasks, resources, constraints, and objectives, then hands search to a deterministic compiler and solver. The motivation is that small models deployable in resource-constrained settings frequently violate feasibility when scheduling directly from text.

entry.title: Pairwise Ranking Outperforms Single-Action RL for Offline Explanation Selection: A Practical Lesson

author.name: Tanay Chowdhury, Saeideh Shahrokh Esfahani

entry.summary: Compares selection strategies for serving pre-generated recommendation explanations, moving LLM generation offline into a frozen candidate pool and using a small CPU-resident selector at request time to stay under 100 milliseconds without a GPU. Across roughly 3,000 evaluation pairs, pairwise ranking approaches such as LambdaRank outperform single-action RL methods including PPO, GRPO, and DPO.

entry.title: DentAgent: Evidence-Centric Multi-Agent Coordination for Multimodal Dental Reasoning

author.name: Zijie Meng, Xiwei Dai, Yixuan Tang, Jin Hao, Yang Feng, Fudong Zhu, Xiaoqiang Liu, Shaosheng Cao, Zuozhu Liu

entry.summary: DentAgent coordinates five modality specialists under an orchestrator for dental assessment across domain knowledge, radiographs, intraoral photographs, and 3D dental data, with each specialist converting observations into structured evidence records so conclusions remain traceable rather than implicit in generated text.

entry.title: TestifAI: Tomography-Based Testing for Deep Learning Systems

author.name: Arooj Arif, Tobias Hartung, Elena Botoeva, Alexandros Koliousis

entry.summary: TestifAI is a testing framework for estimating deep learning model robustness against combinations of input perturbations rather than one perturbation at a time, addressing the combinatorial explosion that makes exhaustive robustness testing infeasible when each test requires thousands of inferences. It targets safety-critical deployments such as autonomous driving.

entry.title: Language Models for Portuguese: A Systematic Mapping Study

author.name: Jhessica Silva, Carlos Caetano, Helena Maia, Breno Bernard Nicolau de Fran\c{c}a, Sandra Avila, Helio Pedrini

entry.summary: A systematic mapping of the Portuguese-language model ecosystem, consolidating scattered information from papers, technical reports and model repositories into a structured survey of models and data resources. It highlights gaps in resources for a widely spoken but under-served language.

entry.title: Learning-State-Aware Dynamic Generative Data Augmentation on Small-Scale Datasets

author.name: Ting Xiang, Chenxi Deng, Jinhui Zhao, Bingting Jiang, Ke Zhang, Changjian Chen, Zhuo Tang

entry.summary: LSADA makes generative data augmentation adaptive by building a per-sample learning state that sets augmentation strength and region-specific strategies for small image-classification datasets. It aims to balance diversity against preservation of class semantics using downstream model feedback.

entry.title: Asymmetric Attention Heads: Structured Head-Wise Context Allocation for Transformer Attention

author.name: Zimu Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes giving different attention heads different context spans, grouping heads by feature-derived statistics and assigning local causal windows while keeping the standard multi-head output interface. Experiments at 4096-token context suggest some local-allocation variants are competitive with full-span attention.

entry.title: Which Eviction Policy Should an LLM Cache Use? A Systematic Study Across Workloads, Capacities, and Encoders

author.name: Yash Kulkarni, Shubham Harkare, Arvind Suresh Yogesh Babu

entry.summary: A systematic head-to-head comparison of eviction policies for semantic caches serving LLM responses, spanning three corpora, three capacities and two encoders. The main finding is largely negative: no policy beats LFU by more than a trivial margin, though weak policies such as FIFO can lose up to about nine points at tight capacity, and the authors give a conditional packing argument for why upside is limited. It is useful guidance for LLM serving infrastructure.

entry.title: Linguistic Holonomy and Statistical Watermarks: Inner Geometry of Meaning-Preserving Transformations

author.name: Daniele Corradetti

entry.summary: Argues that measuring watermark robustness by endpoint semantic similarity is the wrong statistic, and shows that chains of meaning-preserving rewrites decompose into an endpoint component plus a holonomy in the stabilizer of the initial state that semantic deficit cannot detect. The framework formalizes how paraphrase loops erode statistical watermarks invisibly to current metrics. It has implications for provenance evaluation protocols.

entry.title: PersonalBench: Measuring the Authorship Gap in LLM Personalization

author.name: Yash Ganpat Sawant

entry.summary: PersonalBench evaluates inference-time personalization by whether outputs actually resemble a target author's writing, using a trained authorship-verification model, an LLM judge and stylometrics across 50 authors and 1,000 generations. Personalization methods produce author-differentiated text (AUC about 0.92) but never close the gap between machine and human authorship. It reframes personalization evaluation around authorship rather than preference alignment.

entry.title: Gallileo-4D: Frozen Backbone Ensemble for Dynamic 4D Reconstruction

author.name: Nicol\`o Savioli

entry.summary: A competition report describing a third-place dynamic 4D reconstruction entry that made no gradient updates at all: twelve of thirteen fine-tuning configurations hurt the leaderboard while often improving local validation. The author attributes the inversion to a train-test data-variant mismatch and instead spends compute on inference-time ensembling of decoding configurations.

entry.title: AutoLumNet: Monotone Optimal Transport for Single-Shot Exposure Correction

author.name: Airin Akter Tania, Md Raihan Khan, Mohiuddin Ahmad

entry.summary: AutoLumNet corrects arbitrary exposure errors in one shot by splitting the mapping into a strictly monotone global tone curve, parameterized as the integral of a positive density, plus a bounded local residual. The monotone form provably preserves pixel luminance ordering and spatial extrema while remaining dense in valid tone corrections.

entry.title: DIFFCZSL: Compositional Zero-Shot Learning Regularized by Diffusion Representations

author.name: Hangyu Tian, Zhenqi He, Yanghao Wang, Long Chen

entry.summary: DIFFCZSL regularizes compositional zero-shot learning with intermediate representations from diffusion models, arguing that generative features better preserve structure between primitive concepts and their compositions than purely discriminative embeddings. It complements vision-language model baselines.

entry.title: DPC-Net: Dual-Prior Collaborative Network for All-in-One Image Restoration

author.name: Zhaokun He, Kangbiao Shi, Axi Niu, Jian Jin, Peng Wu, Wei Dong, Qingsen Yan

entry.summary: DPC-Net performs all-in-one image restoration by combining degradation-semantic coupled priors, supervised by a vision-language model constraining feature distributions, with explicit low-level visual priors during reconstruction. The goal is to reduce structural distortion and semantic inconsistency across mixed degradations.

entry.title: APPROVE: Visual End-User-in-the-Loop Robot Programming with LLMs

author.name: Bijan Kavousian, Miray \"Ozakkas, Josefine Monnet, Oliver Petrovic, Christian Brecher

entry.summary: APPROVE combines LLM-generated robot programs with a Blockly block-based visualization and an explicit user confirmation step, so non-expert end users can inspect, correct, and reuse generated programs. It targets the transparency and intent-alignment gaps in natural-language robot programming.

entry.title: SAGE: Ergodic Control for Autonomous and Adaptive Inspection of Subsea Infrastructure

author.name: Markus Buchholz, Ignacio Carlucho, Yvan R. Petillot

entry.summary: SAGE applies ergodic control to subsea infrastructure inspection, allocating vehicle time in proportion to a live sensor-derived risk distribution over valves rather than following a scripted route. A two-structure, five-valve scenario compares it against a fixed-loop A-star tour under matched time budgets.

entry.title: Position: Profiling Game Worlds by Transition Complexity

author.name: Lele Cao

entry.summary: Proposes the Transition Complexity Profile, a small reproducible metric suite that quantifies how hard the next-state prediction problem is in a game environment at a declared observation interface, covering branching factor, opponent-induced uncertainty, and temporal dependency span. The goal is to stop world-modeling and RL papers from conflating environment difficulty with method quality.

entry.title: Large Language Models in Mental Health: A Systematic Review of Applications, Innovations, and Ethical Challenges

author.name: Yisong Chen, Yifan Gao, Sijing Yu, Chuqing Zhao, Yang Lu

entry.summary: A systematic review of LLM applications across mental health, spanning social media screening for depression and suicide risk, clinical conversational agents, therapy support, prompt engineering for domain adaptation, and multimodal inputs. It also catalogs interpretability and ethical concerns for clinical deployment.

entry.title: ORBITER: Conflict-Aware Decision-Making for Agentic Last-Mile Delivery

author.name: Mingzhao Li, Chenxi Liu, Yan Zhao, Hao Miao

entry.summary: ORBITER is an agentic arbiter for next-order decisions in last-mile delivery that describes the current delivery state in language so an LLM can reason explicitly about spatial, temporal, and behavioral cues, while addressing LLM sensitivity to task presentation through a conflict-aware arbitration structure rather than direct prediction.

entry.title: The Deontic Gap: Large Language Models and the Modal Language of Obligation

author.name: Daniel Hart, Sarah Allred, Joseph Abbas, Morenike Alugo

entry.summary: Compares how LLM-generated text uses obligation modals such as must and should against contemporary human corpora and a century of published prose. AI output consistently underuses positive deontic modals, patterning like formal published English rather than current speech.

entry.title: Formal Verification of Romanov's Triplet Logic: A Verified Filter for Sliding-window 3-CNF with Application to Structured Formulas

author.name: Dmitry V. Alexandrov

entry.summary: Provides the first machine-checked formalization of a triplet-based combinatorial framework for reasoning about satisfiability structures, verifying a clause-by-clause translation and an intersection procedure in a proof assistant. The verified component functions as a sound filter for a restricted class of formulas.

entry.title: Performance Drift Detection in Machine Learning as a Service (MLaaS) for IoT Environments

author.name: Deepak Kanneganti, Sajib Mistry, Sheik Mohammad Mostakim Fattah, Erik Elmroth, Aneesh Krishna, Monowar Bhuyan

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for detecting performance drift in cloud machine learning services from the client side, where users cannot inspect the provider model, by learning a surrogate of the service behavior. It targets IoT settings where both data distributions and provider models change over time.

entry.title: A Two-Stage Time-Aware Transformer for Short-Horizon AECOPD Risk Prediction

author.name: Dongyang Wang, Weihao Qu, Ling Zheng, Haowen Pan

entry.summary: Presents a two-stage time-aware transformer that predicts short-horizon risk of COPD exacerbation directly from raw pressure and flow waveforms recorded by home ventilators, rather than from episodic clinical variables or handcrafted features. It also aims to estimate the timing of an impending event instead of only binary risk.

entry.title: Rationally Enriched Chebyshev Trunk Bases for DeepONet Surrogates of High P\'eclet Entrance Transport

author.name: Mingeun Choi, Satish Kumar

entry.summary: Enriches the trunk basis of a DeepONet operator surrogate with rational functions built via the adaptive AAA algorithm alongside Chebyshev polynomials, targeting singularly perturbed high-Peclet transport problems with thin boundary layers. Over repeated training runs it outperforms vanilla and Chebyshev-only trunk variants on three benchmark problems.

entry.title: An Inclusive and Lightweight Approach to Federated Continual Learning for Cultural Heritage

author.name: Ioannis Theologitis, Debin Meng, Stylianos Eleftheriadis, Vasileios Lolis, Konstantinos Votis

entry.summary: Proposes FedCurv-DR, a lightweight regularization-based federated continual learning method for cultural heritage collections that are distributed across institutions and continuously growing. Parameter-importance estimates are accumulated across clients and updated only periodically to reduce communication cost.

entry.title: A comparison between ceiling-mounted FMCW, IR-UWB and Wi-Fi radar for in-bedroom human activity monitoring and sleep interruption detection

author.name: Anton Lambrecht, Reda El Hail, Xianjun Jiao, Pieter Crombez, Dominique Schreurs, Peter Karsmakers, Adnan Shahid, Eli De Poorter

entry.summary: Provides a controlled head-to-head comparison of ceiling-mounted FMCW radar, impulse-radio ultra-wideband, and Wi-Fi sensing for bedroom activity monitoring and sleep interruption detection, using synchronized recordings from 20 participants across six room layouts. It fills a gap where prior studies used incomparable hardware and protocols.

entry.title: Reward-Guided Autoregressive Graph Generation for Efficient Multi-Agent Communication Topology Design

author.name: Poomphob Suwannapichat, Boonyarit Changaival, Caesar Wu, Pascal Bouvry

entry.summary: Proposes RGA-Designer, which adds a reward model capturing both task correctness and structural sparsity to an autoregressive graph generator that designs communication topologies for LLM multi-agent systems. The fine-tuning stage is RLHF-inspired, aiming to cut token consumption while keeping reasoning accuracy. It matters because multi-agent orchestration costs scale with edges in the communication graph.

entry.title: StreamSoccer: Event-Driven Memory for Streaming Soccer Commentary

author.name: Chenxi Shao, Bozhong Wang, Jiaxin Huang, Zhao Liu, Sunwei Zhu, Tianxin Hang, Gaoqi He, Yang Li, Changbo Wang

entry.summary: StreamSoccer generates live soccer commentary from streaming video using event memory as its intermediate representation, with a fixed-budget active memory that integrates the stream and consolidates completed events into retrievable historical records. A unified generator draws on current, recent and historical states and can also choose to stay silent. It is a concrete instance of bounded-memory streaming video understanding.

entry.title: S$^2$GS: Structured Sparse Gaussian Streaming for Efficient Free-Viewpoint Video Reconstruction on Edge-IoT Devices

author.name: Yiwei Li, Jiannong Cao, Weixun Gao, Rui Cao, Songye Zhu, Yinfeng Cao, Mingjin Zhang

entry.summary: S2GS streams free-viewpoint video reconstruction by exploiting structured temporal sparsity, updating only Gaussian residuals organized in a streaming octree to cut per-frame optimization time and storage. The target is deployment on constrained edge and IoT devices for telepresence and digital twins.

entry.title: Prompt-Conditioned Channel Attention for Hierarchical Feature Modulation toward Anatomy-Agnostic Segmentation

author.name: Mosharof Hossain, Md Rabiul Islam, Limon Halder, Erchin Serpedin, Md Kamrul Hasan

entry.summary: Prompt-Conditioned Channel Attention injects semantic prompts deep into a segmentation network by modulating channels across hierarchical feature levels, rather than fusing prompts only late in the pipeline. The claim is anatomy-agnostic interactive segmentation that better handles ambiguous boundaries and modality artifacts.

entry.title: Multimodal Trajectory Planning for Surface Vehicles using Turning Circle-based Control Barrier Functions

author.name: Changyu Lee

entry.summary: Combines model predictive control with a turning-circle-based control barrier function for autonomous surface vessels, replacing purely proximity-based safety with a geometry that respects nonholonomic motion and finite turning radius. The formulation exposes distinct left- and right-turn avoidance modes so the solver can explore topologically different trajectories.

entry.title: Measuring the Partial-Credit Gap: A Strict Benchmark on Vietnam's 2025 Convex Marking Scheme

author.name: Nguyen Quoc Hung, Nguyen Dang Minh, Le Nhu Quynh, Tran Khanh Linh, Nguyen Kieu Linh

entry.summary: Argues that binary right-or-wrong scoring misrepresents model ability when the underlying exam uses a non-additive grading scheme, using Vietnam's reformed national high school exam where four true-false statements earn convex partial credit. Getting three of four correct earns half a point rather than the three quarters standard accuracy would imply, creating a measurable gap between reported accuracy and actual exam score.

entry.title: Bridging Search and CRM: Productionizing AI Product Research Agents for Customer Re-Engagement

author.name: Mandar Kulkarni, Pooja A., Samir Shah

entry.summary: Describes a deployed e-commerce system that connects search intent signals with CRM re-engagement by detecting users with exploratory purchase intent, running multi-agent grounded product research over behavioral signals, external knowledge, and catalog data, and delivering personalized recommendations through a messaging channel.

entry.title: Impact of Iterative Fine-Tuning on Transcription Accuracy in Complex Historical Sanskrit Manuscripts

author.name: Kartik Chincholikar, Kaushik Gopalan, Mihir Hasabnis

entry.summary: Shows that iteratively fine-tuning a classical OCR pipeline at both layout and appearance levels on the target manuscript progressively improves transcription of complex historical Sanskrit documents. The loop adapts to period-specific handwriting, page texture and imaging noise.

entry.title: GrabVG: Graph-Attentive Binding for Visual Grounding in UAV Imagery

author.name: Chaowei Wang, Yan Di, Jingjun Sun, Baozhe Liu, Jiaxu Tian, Yuheng Li, Guangqian Guo, Shan Gao

entry.summary: GrabVG improves language-guided object localization in drone imagery by adding graph-attentive binding that exploits spatial topology among many small, visually similar objects. It targets failures caused by visual redundancy and repeated local configurations in bird's-eye-view scenes.

entry.title: Recovering Nonlinear Functions of Latent Variables: A Plausible-Value Neural Network Framework

author.name: Eunjeong Song (Department of Education, Korea University, Seoul, Republic of Korea), Sehee Hong (Department of Education, Korea University, Seoul, Republic of Korea)

entry.summary: Derives an attenuation bound showing that measurement error shrinks the recoverable variance of the kth-order component of a nonlinear regression on latent variables by the kth power of the score reliability. It proposes combining plausible-value posterior draws with neural networks to recover latent-scale nonlinear functions without prespecifying functional form.

entry.title: HiRA-CAM: Preserving Fine-Grained Spatial Relevance in Gradient-Based Visual Explanations

author.name: Manasi Nerurkar, Ali A. Minai

entry.summary: HiRA-CAM improves gradient-based saliency maps for convolutional networks by adaptively combining activation maps from all layers rather than a single chosen layer. The authors report sharper and more focused explanations than LayerCAM and Grad-CAM for object classification.

entry.title: PL-NBA: A Possession-level Universal Basketball Video Dataset Supporting Multiple Visual Understanding Tasks

author.name: Yunhao Zhao, Haoying Sun, Jiarui Li, Zhuming Wang, Ya Jing, Xiangbo Shu, Lifang Wu, Changwen Chen

entry.summary: PL-NBA is a basketball video dataset annotated at the level of full offensive possessions, with 11,000 clips and over 31,000 events labeled with players, captions, types, and timestamps from 60 NBA games. Possession-level continuity enables tasks such as event anticipation that single-action datasets cannot support.

entry.title: When Saying No Makes Better Videos: Designing Dual Gatekeeping for Pedagogically Grounded AI Content Creation

author.name: Yearim Kim, Njun Baek, Nojun Kwak

entry.summary: Studies an AI video authoring pipeline with two layers of deliberate refusal: educators iteratively reshape scripts against multimedia learning theory, and automated metrics flag violations of instructional coherence and narrative-visual synchronization. A study with 23 educators plus automated evaluation suggests principled refusal improves pedagogical quality.

entry.title: Coupled-cluster molecular properties across the main group that extrapolate beyond training size

author.name: Wenhao He, Xu Chen, Noah Song, Haowei Xu, Tim S. Hindges, Bohan Li, Zihan Lin, Yu Yao, Avetik R. Harutyunyan, Fang Liu, Yao Wang, Hao Tang, Ju Li

entry.summary: Covered in yesterday's Research roundup, Trains an equivariant network to predict an effective one-electron Hamiltonian from a single cheap density-functional calculation, then derives energies, gaps, dipoles, polarizabilities and bond orders at coupled-cluster accuracy across nine main-group elements. The model reportedly generalizes to molecules larger than those in training.

entry.title: RDFdL: Integrating RDF with Differential Dynamic Logic

author.name: Yuyang Li, Lukas Kubelka, Julia Butte, Tobias K\"afer

entry.summary: RDFdL extends RDF knowledge graphs with differential dynamic logic so that continuous physical dynamics described by differential equations can be represented alongside static knowledge and verified. Differential equations and state-space ranges are encoded in RDF and SHACL with semantics given by translation to dL.

entry.title: When Clean Signals Are Not Enough: Detecting Structural Ambiguity for Safe Wearable Stress Classification

author.name: Saba A. Farahani, Hung Cao, Amir M. Rahmani

entry.summary: Identifies structural ambiguity in wearable stress detection, where a classifier with 93 percent mean accuracy completely fails for individual subjects whose cross-signal physiological coupling breaks down near stress onset. The proposed monitor quantifies subject-specific coupling divergence before inference and routes each window to classify, defer, or abstain without retraining the downstream model.

entry.title: Training-Free Inference-Time Self-Reflection and Cost-Bounded Early Stopping for Large Language Models

author.name: Wei Yu, Suxing Liu, Minjie Yu, Jiahao Wang, Zhijian Zheng, Haocheng Deng, Bing Li

entry.summary: EvoResearcher is a training-free inference-time protocol that loops generation, self-critique, and revision on a single frozen model until a maximum depth or a confirmation sentinel triggers early stopping, keeping compute bounded. Four self-reflective reward components covering correctness, efficiency, reflection depth, and tool-call diversity are instantiated as prompt-level mechanisms rather than RL objectives.

entry.title: Adaptive Memory and Reflection Multi-Agent System for Medical Question Answering

author.name: Pradeep Murugesan, Luoxiao Yang, Xueli Chen, Xinqi Fan

entry.summary: Proposes a medical question answering system where specialized agents share persistent memory and reflection-based feedback, retrieving relevant prior cases to inform reasoning. A complexity assessment router sends questions through solo, collaborative, or escalated workflows, with consensus and ethical oversight modules applied before output.

entry.title: Intercepting the Kangaroo: Experimental Astrolinguistics with Constructed Lexicons, Active Probing, and Large Language Models as Informants and Hypothesis Proposers

author.name: Francesco Cordella, Mauro Cappelli

entry.summary: Turns speculative astrolinguistics into a simulation testbed by giving two language models deliberately incompatible constructed lexicons and having a scripted orchestrator attempt translation, with full ground truth available. The paper names and studies the kangaroo effect, where a word silently attaches to the wrong referent, across hundreds of runs.

entry.title: Empirical Characterization of Learning Geometry in Hybrid Quantum Forecasting Models

author.name: Sandra Leticia Ju\'arez-Osorio, Jorge I. Hernandez-Martinez, Jesus Ivan Ruiz-Martinez, Andres Mendez-Vazquez, Eduardo Rodriguez-Tello

entry.summary: Compares the empirical neural tangent kernel dynamics of a compact hybrid quantum forecasting model against a structurally matched classical baseline on harmonic-mixture and chirp benchmarks, tracking kernel-target alignment, kernel drift, and spectral concentration. Despite different optimization geometries, held-out performance is similar.

entry.title: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection Using Flow Matching on Tabular Data

author.name: Philip Konz, Tejaswini Medi, Margret Keuper

entry.summary: Studies flow-matching-based unsupervised anomaly detection on tabular financial data when the training set is already contaminated with anomalies, comparing time-conditioned contraction matching against a forest-flow variant across several scoring functions. The main finding is that the choice of anomaly score dominates, with the original single-step decision score underperforming.

entry.title: Reliable Financial Named Entity Recognition under Domain Shift

author.name: Zihao Zheng, Baichuan Li, Junyi Yao, Jiayu Long

entry.summary: Studies confidence estimation and selective prediction for financial named entity recognition across a three-tier distribution shift from SEC filings to financial news to general social media, comparing a BERT tagger with LoRA-tuned small Qwen models under five inference-time confidence signals. A key finding is that the ranking of confidence signals itself changes under shift, so F1 alone does not indicate what is safe to automate. It targets deployment risk in financial information extraction.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration with the Common-Sense Reasoning Capabilities of LLMs for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Mehdi Azarafza, Faezeh Pasandideh, Ali Ehteshami Bejnordi, Stefan Henkler, Achim Rettberg

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid autonomous-driving stack in which an orchestrator coordinates PPO-trained reinforcement learning and PID control while LLM common-sense reasoning is applied only at a supervisory level, avoiding direct vehicle control. The design is motivated by LLM latency and hallucination risks that make direct actuation unsafe. It illustrates a layered pattern for embedding LLM reasoning in safety-critical control.

entry.title: Robust Cross-Modal Foundation Model Perception for Underwater Robots under Degraded Visual Conditions

author.name: Mohammad Arif Ul Alam

entry.summary: Evaluates whether frozen DINOv2 visual features can be complemented by sonar for underwater robot perception as optical quality degrades, using a controlled five-level degradation benchmark. The framing shifts attention from nominal detection accuracy to cross-modal robustness curves.

entry.title: A 360-Degree Vision Dataset for Learning Yaw Control on GPS-Denied Micro-UAVs in Disaster-Response-Relevant Environments

author.name: Niklas Voigt, Hartmut Surmann

entry.summary: Presents a 360-degree camera dataset from industrial, underground, and training environments recorded by a custom micro-drone, used to learn a yaw controller that steers toward open space when radio links fail in GPS-denied settings. The application focus is disaster and CBRN emergency response.

entry.title: PVRA: A Pointwise Key-point Voting Framework for Robotic Assembly

author.name: Kulunu Samarawickrama, Roel Pieters

entry.summary: PVRA is a modular 3D keypoint voting framework that learns assembly dependencies from RGB-D scenes to output actionable next-step information rather than only object poses. The authors argue object-centric perception alone is insufficient for autonomous progressive assembly.

entry.title: Petri Net Description of Biological Neural Circuits for Fast Hardware Prototyping

author.name: Carlo daCunha, Rodrigo Pena, Marcos Turqueti

entry.summary: Proposes describing biological neural circuits as timed Petri nets so that neurons, synapses, and spikes have formally verifiable timing semantics, enabling deadline-guaranteed real-time hardware execution independent of integration timestep. It claims analytic correspondence to leaky integrate-and-fire dynamics.

entry.title: FM-Bench: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Management with Competing Agents

author.name: Tianyou Wang, Chongyang Gao, Kezhen Chen, Chen Dong, Yinghao He, Donghan Li, Wangcheng Xu, Hongjiu Zhang, Chi Li

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.18423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language model agents now execute bounded tasks reliably. Whether they can sustain effective decision-making over long horizons, where actions have cum...

entry.title: Syntactic Simplification of OWL Class Expressions

author.name: Alkid Baci, N'Dah Jean Kouagou, Caglar Demir, Axel-Cyrille Ngonga Ngomo

entry.summary: Presents an algorithm for syntactically simplifying OWL class expressions produced by class expression learning, applying rewriting rules to remove redundancy and find shorter equivalent forms while preserving logical entailments. The result is more compact and human-readable descriptions for description logic knowledge bases.

entry.title: DeepTCM1.0: A Multi-Expert AI Agent for Deciphering Mechanisms of Chinese Herbal Formulae Based on General Large Language Models

author.name: Wenxin Duan, Hanwei Wang, Zhongying Peng, Zhonghua Lu, Jiayi An, Fan Song, Yong Liang

entry.summary: Presents a multi-expert LLM agent system that decomposes analysis of traditional Chinese medicine formulas across specialist roles to reduce hallucinated mechanistic reasoning. It targets the gap between classical TCM theory and network pharmacology style evidence.

entry.title: StocksTalk: A Voice-Enabled Conversational Agent for Structured Query Generation over Web Data

author.name: Akshat Parmar, Vikranth Udandarao, Abhay Shakya, Tanmay Hire, Avinash Anand, Rajiv Ratn Shah, Daniel Wang Zhengkui

entry.summary: A voice-driven system that converts spoken stock-screening requests into validated SQL over market data, exposing intermediate artifacts such as extracted constraints and normalized metrics for user inspection. It is evaluated on a curated benchmark of 150 spoken queries.

entry.title: How Quantum Is the Advantage? A Fair, Calibration- and Noise-Aware Benchmark and Attribution Audit of Quantum Machine Learning for Network Intrusion Detection

author.name: Syeda Anshrah Gillani, Mirza Samad Ahmed Baig, Shahid Munir Shah, Asher Ali, Hamzah Siddiqui

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.18155v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum machine learning (QML) for network intrusion detection (NIDS) is routinely reported to reach near-perfect accuracy, yet the most rigorous stu...

entry.title: When Do LLMs Actually Help? Evaluating LLMs as Data Quality Annotators

author.name: Praphulla Lal Shrestha

entry.summary: Tests whether an LLM reliably flags data quality problems in e-commerce entity matching and brand mislabeling against rule-based baselines and human labels. Simple rules match zero-shot LLM performance, and a few-shot prompt that looked better on a small validation sample degraded full-scale results.

entry.title: Visual-Prompt Guided Wildlife Instance-Level Recognition

author.name: Mufhumudzi Muthivhi, Jiahao Huo, Terence van Zyl, Fredrik Gustafsson

entry.summary: Proposes a single-stage detection plus re-identification model for wildlife individuals that searches identities directly in latent space using a self-supervised vision backbone and wildlife descriptors. Preliminary accuracy remains well below the two-stage state of the art.

entry.title: Finetuning Strategies for Querying Sounds by Vocal Imitation

author.name: Aditya Bhattacharjee, Christos Plachouras, Sungkyun Chang, Emmanouil Benetos

entry.summary: A technical report on the winning entry to a 2025 challenge for retrieving sound effects from vocal imitations, comparing contrastive learning on a frozen pretrained audio encoder against joint contrastive-triplet training with semi-hard negatives on a lightweight encoder. It documents fine-tuning choices that mattered for the task.

entry.title: SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments

author.name: Bo Liu, Simon Yu, Yiding Jiang, Ao Qu, Andrew Zhao, Zichen Liu, Junsu Kim, Zijian Zhou, Seungone Kim, Tongzheng Ren, Mickel Liu, Hanfei Yu, Zhaorun Chen, Weiyan Shi, Paul Pu Liang, Luke Zettlemoyer, Yejin Choi, Natasha Jaques

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.19197v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Continuous self-improvement requires an ever-expanding pool of self-generated, diverse, adaptive goals. For language agents, existing training enviro...

entry.title: Beyond Multimodal Alignment: Certifying Physical Language through Response Substitution and Ordered Execution

author.name: Kaizhen Tan, Xin Xu, Siru Tao, Yixiao Li, Hanzhe Hong, Yang Feng, Heqing Du

entry.summary: Proposes a capability hierarchy and a certificate procedure to test whether representations from different sensors carry interchangeable executable meaning when substituted into a frozen response model, and whether that meaning survives new action compositions. Experiments on haptic clustering show audio and acceleration representations of the same unseen surface land far closer in response space than mismatched pairings.

entry.title: Exact Algebraic Computation of Learning Coefficients for Two-Dimensional Singular Models

author.name: Gr\'egoire Sergeant-Perthuis (CQSB, Sorbonne Universit\'e), Elias Tsigaridas (Ouragan Team, INRIA), Jules Tsukahara (Ouragan Team, INRIA)

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.20183v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical information criteria such as the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) rely on regularity assumptions that break down for singular models, lea...

entry.title: VQC-ZTI: Variational Quantum Control for Zero Trust Protection of the Tactile Internet

author.name: Mubassir Serneabat Sudipto (Iowa State University), Shakil Ahmed (Grand Valley State University), Ashfaq Khokhar (Kansas State University)

entry.summary: Proposes a split-plane zero-trust security architecture for tactile internet services in which a variational quantum classifier scores encrypted-flow telemetry off the control path while a conventional policy engine enforces cached decisions. The design decouples anomaly detection sensitivity from enforcement aggressiveness.

entry.title: A Repeated Measurements Approach to $SoH$ Battery Modelling of Cyclic Aged Data in a Laboratory Environment

author.name: Mark Cary, Charles Bokor

entry.summary: Applies a linearized nonlinear repeated-measurements model to battery state-of-health ageing profiles from laboratory cycling, separating within-profile measurement noise from cell-to-cell variation. It uses regularized iterative generalized least squares with hyperparameter re-estimation on ten cells.

entry.title: The impact of feature engineering and an optimisation framework for ocean colour machine learning

author.name: Edson Silva, Julien Brajard, Simon Cappe, Lasse H. Pettersson, Fran\c{c}ois Counillon

entry.summary: Assesses how feature engineering, rather than model or hyperparameter tuning, affects ocean colour retrieval models, proposing a seven-level sequence of data transformations from band selection through scaling. It demonstrates the framework with multilayer perceptrons, support vector machines, and gradient-boosted trees on satellite data.

entry.title: Gravitational-wave parameter estimation with machine-learning generated surrogate waveforms

author.name: Suyog Garg, Kipp Cannon
