The contrast identifies increasing input efficiency as a specific candidate mechanism behind the enormous sample-efficiency gap between children and LMs.

entry.title: Fool's Gold: Defensive Deception Against Safety-Removal Attacks on Open-Weight Models

author.name: Mark Russinovich

entry.summary: Proposes decoy hardening, a defense that accepts that abliteration will strip refusal behavior from open-weight models and instead trains the post-attack state to emit confident but factually falsified answers to hazardous operational requests. The defense is learned inside a differentiable simulation of the attack and tested on seven models from five families spanning 9B to 122B.

entry.title: Decomposition Attacks Across Unlinkable Identities: Limits of Stateful Defenses for LLM Services

author.name: Bowen Sun, Zhengyue Zhao, Xiaogeng Liu, Yinzhi Cao, Chaowei Xiao

entry.summary: Analyzes decomposition attacks in which an adversary splits a harmful task into individually benign requests issued under unlinkable identities, so no stateful monitor can group them. For a fixed non-retrying attack strategy the authors prove the achievable security-utility tradeoff is fully determined by a specific structural property, establishing limits on what stateful defenses can accomplish.

entry.title: Q-Learning With World Models

author.name: Perry Dong, Yueru Jia, Chelsea Finn, Dorsa Sadigh

entry.summary: This work asks how to use learned world models to improve off-policy Q-learning rather than to generate imagined rollouts for direct policy optimization, which suffers compounding bias at long horizons and high visual complexity. The stated target is sample-efficient RL fine-tuning of vision-language-action policies for real robots. It could sharpen how model-based components are integrated into value learning for robotics.

entry.title: PROBE: Manipulation-Grounded Visual Question Answering with VLM Agents

author.name: Vineet Bhat, Siyi Chen, Alex Zook, Xuning Yang, Stan Birchfield, Valts Blukis, Jonathan Tremblay

entry.summary: Formalizes Manipulation-Grounded Visual Question Answering, where answering a question requires physically moving distractor objects to reveal occluded ones so the scene changes with each action. PROBE contributes a high-fidelity tabletop simulator plus a framework for benchmarking and finetuning VLM agents on this interactive perception setting.

entry.title: When AI art has no author: Study finds generated images often can’t be traced to training data

author.name: Rachel Gordon | MIT CSAIL

entry.summary: MIT CSAIL researchers identify what they call attribution decay: as generative image models are trained on more data, the counterfactual influence of any single training example, artist, or subject on a given output shrinks toward nothing, so removing that data often leaves outputs unchanged. They argue that if removal changes nothing, that data cannot be held responsible for the output, which undercuts data-attribution-based approaches to credit, licensing, and liability. The finding bears directly on active lawsuits and proposed regulation.

entry.title: Spectral Gaps of Hit-and-Run and Coordinate Hit-and-Run

author.name: Yunbum Kook, Santosh S. Vempala

entry.summary: Proves a new spectral gap bound for Hit-and-Run sampling on convex bodies expressed via the Poincare constant of the target rather than the outer radius, refining the classic Lovasz-Vempala mixing bound. Combined with recent KLS progress, this gives near-quadratic-in-dimension mixing for nearly isotropic bodies, and the paper also treats coordinate Hit-and-Run.

entry.title: There is No Theoretical Curse of Multilinguality For Embedding Space Structure

author.name: Niyati Bafna, Neha Verma, Vil\'em Zouhar, Philipp Koehn, David Yarowsky

entry.summary: Formalizes what perfect multilinguality would mean for an embedding space and proves that the minimum dimensionality needed grows only logarithmically in the number of languages, so the curse of multilinguality is not an inherent geometric constraint. The result reframes observed multilingual degradation as an artifact of training and capacity allocation rather than a representational impossibility.

entry.title: Hydra-0: Action Flow for Generalist World Modeling and Control

author.name: Hongyu Li, Bowen Wen, Xinghao Zhu, Yixuan Wang, Yilun Du, Yunzhu Li, George Konidaris, Stan Birchfield, Soha Pouya, Chenran Li, Yan Chang

entry.summary: Hydra-0 is a generalist world model conditioned on action flow, representing robot actions as pixel motion so a single visual interface transfers across embodiments, tasks, environments, and video generation backbones. The authors report large reductions in robot- and object-motion prediction error over an action-conditioned baseline, strong agreement between replayed and reference success rates on a robot benchmark, zero-shot composition, and an emergent inverse mode that infers compatible robot motion from video. This positions world models as both controllers and reliable policy evaluators.

entry.title: Advancing Open and Reproducible Relational Learning: RelArena-$\alpha$, TabPFN-Rel and RPI

author.name: Adrian Hayler, Klemens Fl\"oge, Alan Arazi, Rishabh Ranjan, Jure Leskovec, Felix Birkel, Brendan Roof, Anurag Garg, Kristina Collins, Lydia Sidhoum, Jonas K\"ubler, Siyuan Guo, Oscar Key, Jan Hendrik Metzen, Rylee Grace, David Salinas, Arthur Cahu, Simon Bing, Benjamin J\"ager, Tuana \c{C}elik, Mihir Manium, Vitor Monteiro, Jake Robertson, Jerry Chen, Eliott Kalfon, Tom\'as Pereda, Lilly Wehrhahn, Dominik Safaric, Tobias Schroeder, Georg Grab, Diana Kriuchkova, Clara Cornu, Philipp Singer, Nick Erickson, Vahid Balazadeh, Marie Salmon, Simone Alessi, K\"ur\c{s}at Kaya, Philipp Jund, L\'eo Grinsztajn, Yann LeCun, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, Madelon Hulsebos, Lennart Purucker, Sauraj Gambhir, Frank Hutter, Noah Hollmann

entry.summary: Prior Labs releases three open-source artifacts for relational (multi-table) learning: RelArena-alpha, a unified benchmarking framework; TabPFN-Rel, a relational extension of tabular in-context learning; and RPI, a supporting interface. The stated aim is to give the field a reproducible way to compare methods on relational tasks, with an alpha release aimed at researchers.

entry.title: Would this change your answer? Evaluating Explanations of LLM Behavior In The Wild with Counterfactual Experiments

author.name: Adam Karvonen, Euan Ong, Subhash Kantamneni, Samuel Marks

entry.summary: CHIVE is an agentic pipeline that finds unexpected language model behaviors in real usage and probes them with automated counterfactual prompt edits, producing thousands of explanations with supporting counterfactual evidence. The work operationalizes counterfactual simulatability as the criterion for whether an explanation of model behavior is actually good.

entry.title: Write, Execute, Refine: From Skill Followers to Skill Optimizers via Reinforcement Learning from Execution Feedback

author.name: Kang Peng, Zhiwei Zhang, Yichen Zhang, Zezhong Wang, Yiming Du, Geng Tu, Baojun Wang, Bin Liang, Ruifeng Xu, Kam-Fai Wong

entry.summary: Observes that agent-authored procedural skills actually hurt tool-using agents by 8 to 11 points relative to no skill, implying that following guidance and improving it from execution evidence are separate capabilities. WER trains a dedicated Skill Optimizer outside a frozen executor: the optimizer proposes skills, the frozen agent repeatedly executes them, and a programmatic verifier scores outcomes to supply relative credit for RL.

entry.title: Chain-of-Experience for Continual LLM Improvement

author.name: Haoqin Tu, Yunhao Fang, Yizhong Wang, Cihang Xie, Shen Yan

entry.summary: Studies Chain-of-Experience, where LLMs accumulate experiential traces through repeated interaction with self-feedback or environmental signals such as unit-test pass rates, forming a continual improvement loop at inference time beyond zero-shot performance. The setting is evaluated across math, coding, and knowledge tasks with eight models including GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Claude.

entry.title: TokEval: A Tokenizer Evaluation Suite

author.name: Clara Meister

entry.summary: TokEval is a tokenizer evaluation suite that goes beyond fertility and compression rate to measure linguistically and structurally meaningful properties such as UTF-8 character boundary integrity and digit place-value alignment for arithmetic. Controlled pretraining runs varying only the tokenizer are used to test whether these metrics actually predict downstream model performance.

entry.title: OV3D-Bench: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Open-Vocabulary Monocular 3D Detection

author.name: Mariia Gladkova, Neehar Peri, Ishan Khatri, Deva Ramanan, Daniel Cremers

entry.summary: OV3D-Bench is a diagnostic benchmark for open-vocabulary monocular 3D detection that removes the unrealistic per-image class-name oracle used by several prior methods, substituting dataset-level prompts, and decomposes performance into localization, semantic robustness, and cross-domain transfer instead of a single AP number. Seven detectors are evaluated across seven indoor and outdoor datasets.

entry.title: WANDR: A Benchmark for Wide and Deep Research

author.name: Vitaliy Polshkov, Marcin Pitera, Jeremy Yang, Kirill Priemko, Maksim Gaiduk, Aleksandr Nikolenko, Denis Bykov, Clare Southern, Denis Yarats, Jerry Ma

entry.summary: WANDR is a 500-task benchmark for research agents that must both discover many entities meeting stated criteria and investigate each in depth, returning independently verifiable records with sources and excerpts. Tasks are encoded as qualification key hierarchies whose branching factors set the required record count, covering workflows like market mapping and due diligence.

entry.title: Sparse Prototype Code Underlies Classification and Prediction Across Modalities

author.name: Yehonatan Avidan, Daniel D. Lee, Haim Sompolinsky

entry.summary: Reports that classification tasks induce a shared representational geometry across state-of-the-art vision, audio, and language models, in which within-class variability is structured and correlated with the class centroid and rival-class centroids. A mean-field theory built on this observation predicts generalization behavior from the geometry.

entry.title: Do Language Models Consistently Encode the Current Year?

author.name: Suze van Adrichem, Aditi Bhaskar, Diyi Yang, Christopher Potts, Jing Huang

entry.summary: Probes how language models represent the current year using two distinct tasks: inferring it indirectly from verb tense versus answering the question directly. Both track the post-training cutoff closely, and for base models the tense-based task predicts the pretraining cutoff to within about ten months on average, yet the internal mechanisms behind the two tasks differ.

entry.title: Thinking in a Low-Resource Language: What SFT Builds, What RL Fixes, What Accuracy Cannot See

author.name: Ayoub Kirouane, Christos Petrocheilos

entry.summary: Fine-tunes three frontier mixture-of-experts models with roughly 3.6 to 4.0 billion active parameters to reason in Greek, finding that accuracy benchmarks show essentially nothing because random seed variation alone moves scores by 7.7 points, exceeding every data and recipe effect measured. The real change is in the reasoning language: base models never produce Greek reasoning traces, SFT makes checkpoints reason in the question language, and RL further adjusts behavior in ways accuracy cannot detect.

entry.title: The Problem Is the Problem: Towards Scalable Mathematical Discovery

author.name: Zeyu Zheng, Shengtong Zhang, Jeremy Avigad, Prasad Tetali, Sean Welleck

entry.summary: Argues that in AI-assisted mathematics the scarce resources are frontier-model reasoning and expert review time, and proposes a workflow where humans supply a research direction rather than a single pre-chosen problem, letting the system generate and triage candidate problems. Aims to remove the two human bottlenecks at the start and end of discovery pipelines.

entry.title: Toward Better Assessment of LLMs' Performance in Clinical Error Detection

author.name: Yifan Zhang, Rahmatollah Beheshti

entry.summary: Argues that clinical error-detection benchmarks, which are built by injecting errors into notes so each bad note has a clean twin, are evaluated wrongly because aggregate F1 ignores the paired structure. Evaluating fifteen LLMs on four test sets in three languages, thirteen fall below chance on pairwise discrimination despite F1 scores that practitioners would read as deployable.

entry.title: What Tokens are Learned when Tokenization is Optimized Jointly with Language Modeling?

author.name: Saketh Reddy Vemula, Parameswari Krishnamurthy

entry.summary: Analyzes what token inventories emerge when tokenization is learned jointly with language modeling, comparing tokenizer-free SSLMs and H-Nets against fixed subword tokenizers across 18 typologically and script-diverse languages. SSLMs recover morphologically aligned and contextually efficient units, while H-Nets optimize for byte-level efficiency with long tokens that barely overlap standard subword vocabularies.

entry.title: Mask What Matters: Saliency-Guided Video Self-Supervised Learning for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Christopher Lang, Alexander Braun, Abhinav Valada

entry.summary: V-JEPA4A adapts the V-JEPA video self-supervised objective for autonomous driving with saliency-driven masking, arguing that random masking wastes the pretext signal because safety-critical cues like pedestrians, vehicles, and lane boundaries occupy a small fraction of each frame. The model is pretrained on publicly available driving videos and targeted at downstream driving perception.

entry.title: DumpsterCluster: From Dumpster Diving to Serving LLaMA-70B on $60 GPUs

author.name: Zeyu Cao, Xuan Guo, Cheng Zhang, Cheuk Hang Lau, Ilia Shumailov, Yiren Zhao

entry.summary: The authors physically built a 128-GPU cluster from second-hand retired accelerators for about 22 thousand dollars and ran it for a year, achieving competitive LLaMA-70B inference throughput through pipeline-parallel optimizations. The paper analyzes when such repurposing is economically and environmentally justified versus buying new hardware.

entry.title: Foresight-England: Development of a National-Scale Generative AI Model of Electronic Health Records for Medical Event Prediction across the COVID-19 Pandemic

author.name: Simon Ellershaw, Christopher Tomlinson, Zeljko Kraljevic, Spiros Denaxas, Harry Hemingway, Cathie Sudlow, Angela M. Wood, Anoop D. Shah, Richard Dobson

entry.summary: Foresight-England is a 243M-parameter decoder-only generative foundation model of electronic health records trained entirely inside the NHS England secure data environment on de-identified longitudinal records for roughly 61 million people. It is evaluated on medical event prediction spanning the COVID-19 pandemic, including direct and indirect pandemic effects, as a research pilot.

entry.title: Do LLMs Know What to Ask and When? Evaluating Multi-Turn Information Seeking

author.name: Yepeng Huang, Jiawen Zhang, Michelle Dai, Xiaorui Su, Shanghua Gao, Zi Wang, Marinka Zitnik

entry.summary: The authors formalize multi-turn information seeking as solving a k-underspecified constraint satisfaction problem, where k measures how much information is missing, and release MT-InfoSeek with 5,251 problems and over 9,000 task instances across math, logic, biology, medicine and general knowledge. Models are evaluated on what they ask, when they decide to ask, and how well they integrate acquired information.

entry.title: Optimal Watermark Localization in Mixed-Source Large Language Model Texts

author.name: Jose H. Blanchet, T. Tony Cai, Xiang Li, Hao Liu, Qi Long, Weijie J. Su

entry.summary: This work formalizes locating which token positions of a mixed human and machine text retain watermark evidence as a token-level multiple-testing problem with a latent per-position indicator, going beyond prior global detection results. Under an asymptotic regime indexed by signal sparsity, next-token concentration and effective vocabulary growth, the authors derive a sharp boundary for when localization is possible.

entry.title: Learning to Price with Persuasion

author.name: Maria-Florina Balcan, Tejas Pagare, Karan Singh

entry.summary: Studies the sample complexity of jointly designing prices and information signals when a seller knows buyer profiles but not their prior beliefs about taste distributions, extending a recent information-plus-mechanism-design economic model into a learning-theoretic setting. The paper gives sample-requirement results for revenue-maximizing schemes in both batch and online regimes.

entry.title: Judge, Retrieve, or Abstain: Uncertainty-Guarded LLM Judging with Provable Risk Guarantees

author.name: Sher Badshah, Ali Emami, Hassan Sajjad

entry.summary: Proposes an uncertainty-guarded LLM judging pipeline for objective tasks where the judge must choose between answering from parametric knowledge, invoking retrieval, or abstaining, with provable risk guarantees on the resulting verdicts. This targets the reliability gap that arises when reference-free judges hallucinate factual verdicts while tool augmentation is too costly to apply everywhere.

entry.title: Agent Lightning v1.0: Towards Harnessed Agentic RL

author.name: Zhiyuan He, Siwei Zhang, Zhiwen Zhou, Yuqing Yang, Yu Kang, Yuge Zhang, Luna K. Qiu, Tin Yan Tsui, Jiahang Xu, Chong Luo

entry.summary: Version 1.0 of a framework that trains arbitrary agents via RL through an LLM endpoint proxy, decoupling the deploy-time harness from the training engine so the trainer only sees request-response sequences. The paper names this pattern harnessed agentic RL and notes its adoption by several other training frameworks.

entry.title: Co-RL: Unsupervised Reasoning Emerges from Diverse Cohort in Multi-agent RL

author.name: Yunhao Yang, Yuexin Bian, Yunjie Tian, Di Fu, Tianjin Huang, Yuanyuan Shi, Ziang Xiao, Nuno Vasconcelos, Yijiang Li

entry.summary: Co-RL shows that reasoning improvements can emerge without ground-truth rewards when a diverse cohort of models trains together in a multi-agent setup, using cross-model signals instead of purely self-generated feedback. This is intended to avoid the diversity collapse, bias reinforcement, and training breakdown that plague single-model self-rewarding RL. It matters as verifiable-reward supervision becomes scarce at frontier capability levels.

entry.title: No Task Fails Every Time: Why One-Shot Audits Are Structurally Blind to Agent Damage

author.name: Shiven Khurdi

entry.summary: AgentRelBench measures real damage done by LLM agents by diffing database state across repeated runs with severity pricing and no model in the measurement loop, evaluated over 2,128 runs spanning nine models. The central finding is that no task caused damage on every run, so single-run audits systematically miss harmful agent behavior.

entry.title: Le Critique: Privileged Value Functions for LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Siddarth Venkatraman, Matthieu Dinot, Laurence Aitchison

entry.summary: Le Critique argues learned value functions can fix both the sequence-level credit assignment limits and the straggler-rollout throughput problems of group-relative RL methods like GRPO, and proposes two strategies to make critics practically competitive, including giving the value function privileged information. This challenges the current dominance of critic-free LLM RL pipelines.

entry.title: Proteus: Incremental Memory Activation for Long-Context Sequence Modeling

author.name: Reza Bayat, Ali Behrouz, Vahab Mirrokni, Aaron Courville

entry.summary: Proteus introduces incremental memory activation for long-context sequence models, expanding the effective capacity of a recurrent memory state as the context grows instead of exposing a static memory from the first token. The early bottleneck forces stronger compression of history and reduces interference between stored content and incoming tokens.

entry.title: Eigenanalysis framework for autoregressive neural emulators of multi-scale chaotic dynamics

author.name: Conrad Ainslie, Pedram Hassanzadeh, Michael W. Mahoney, Ashesh Chattopadhyay

entry.summary: Develops a spectral framework explaining why autoregressive neural emulators of chaotic systems blow up over long rollouts, by analyzing the Jacobian of the learned one-step update: direct next-state architectures generically admit eigenvalues above one, while integration-consistent formulations do not. This replaces ad hoc stabilization tricks with a diagnosable dynamical cause.

entry.title: Code as Representation: A Compilable Parsing Paradigm for Academic Documents

author.name: Rihui Jin, Jun Wang, chengyuan zhu, Liang Mingyu, Yue Gao, Li Yunxuan, Kuicai Dong, Guilin Qi, Lin Ren, Yongrui Chen, Xinbang Dai, Jiaqi Li, Tongtong Wu, Gholamreza Haffari

entry.summary: Proposes Compilable Academic Document Parsing, which represents a scientific PDF page as contextual LaTeX plus executable Python so tables, formulas, charts, and pseudocode retain their structure, data, and logic instead of being flattened into Markdown. The framing treats parsing as a representation problem for multimodal models rather than purely a perception problem.

entry.title: MoE-ViE: Mixture of Experts Vision Encoder for Efficient Image and Video Understanding

author.name: Bonan Zhang, Shiyu Dong, Quan Hung Tran, Katharina Gschwind, Shuqi Yang, Sijia Chen, Adel Ahmadyan, Seungwhan Moon, Lu Zhang, Ahmed Kirmani, Babak Damavandi, Anuj Kumar

entry.summary: MoE-ViE systematically explores mixture-of-experts designs for CLIP-style vision encoders, finding that fine-grained expert topologies clearly beat both dense scaling and standard MoE, and adds an auxiliary-loss-free load balancing variant plus a custom kernel to control latency. The work comes from an industry multimodal team.

entry.title: Anthropic Risk Report: August 2026

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: A detailed read-through of Anthropic's August 2026 risk report, arguing the report discloses substantial and sometimes alarming new information that Anthropic was not obligated to publish, including autonomy threat models, misalignment framings, and the existence of an unreleased internal frontier model referred to as Model 2. The author treats voluntary disclosure of this depth as a modest positive update on lab transparency. It is analysis of a lab safety document rather than original research.

entry.title: Towards a theory of inference-time alignment with unknown rewards

author.name: Steve Hanneke, Hongao Wang, Mingyue Xu

entry.summary: Formulates inference-time alignment as a weak-to-strong statistical learning problem in which everything, including the reward, must be learned from data rather than assumed available. It gives a learning-theoretic account of when a decent reference policy can be boosted at test time into a strong policy with high probability.

entry.title: On the Principles Behind Neural Network Optimizers

author.name: Yushun Zhang

entry.summary: This thesis builds a principled foundation for Adam, showing a problem-dependent phase transition between divergence and convergence depending on batch-size-dependent hyperparameters, and explaining Adam's advantage over SGD on Transformers via a near-block-diagonal Hessian with strong block heterogeneity. It then uses this structural understanding to motivate new optimizer designs.

entry.title: Decorrelation Is Not Complementarity: Skill, Not Lineage, Governs Trusted-Monitor Ensembles

author.name: Anik Jha

entry.summary: Studies ensembles of cheap trusted monitors that score a stronger untrusted model's actions for backdoored code, across 24 open-weight monitors spanning nine pretraining lineages and a wide range of detection skill. It finds that minimizing average pairwise correlation, the standard recipe for building such panels, does not predict ensemble gain, because agreement decomposes into a shared-detectability component and an idiosyncratic error component that predict gain with opposite signs.

entry.title: AutoSR: Automatic Symbolic Regression by Searching Research States

author.name: Kejia Zhang, Youran Sun, Xinyu Ren, Chugang Yi, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: AutoSR reframes symbolic regression as searching over persistent research states rather than isolated candidate equations, keeping the motivations and probes that led to each formula so the system can reason about what to try next. The argument is that numerical fit and syntactic complexity are insufficient measures of scientific credibility when noisy finite data admit expressions that diverge wildly outside the observed regime.

entry.title: Emotion Across Speech and Faces: Shared Affective Mechanisms in Multimodal Foundation Models

author.name: Xiutian Zhao, Luqi Sun, Bj\"orn Schuller, Berrak Sisman

entry.summary: Probes whether multimodal foundation models recognize emotion in speech and faces through shared affective units or modality-specific pathways, identifying sparse emotion-sensitive decoder neurons in three open models including Gemma-4-12B-it and Qwen2.5-Omni-7B. Visual emotion neurons are shown to be causally necessary, since deactivating them selectively degrades recognition of the associated facial expressions.

entry.title: Effective Personalized AI Tutors via LLM-Guided Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Angel Tsai-Hsuan Chung, Botong Zhang, Ling-Chieh Kung, Hamsa Bastani, Osbert Bastani

entry.summary: Combines a carefully designed generative tutoring chatbot with a reinforcement learning algorithm that sequences practice problems using signals from student-chatbot interactions, moving from reactive question answering to proactive guidance. Deployed in partnership with the Taipei City Government and an educational research institute.

entry.title: PTXBench: Benchmark and Adapt LLMs for GPU Kernel Optimization with Architecture-specific PTX

author.name: Genghan Zhang, Yixin Dong, Chengze Fan, Zhichen Zeng, Yueming Yuan, Shaowei Zhu, Kunle Olukotun

entry.summary: PTXBench evaluates whether LLMs can write architecture-specific PTX assembly for GPU kernel optimization, measuring correctness, whether the intended target instructions actually execute, and speedup against frontier libraries for GEMM and attention on H100 and B200 hardware. No evaluated model consistently matches vendor libraries, and failures concentrate on attention backward passes. The authors also fine-tune Qwen3.6-27B, an existing open model, with repair-conditioned supervision.

entry.title: Certifying Compressed Language Models: An Audit and a Statistical Toolkit

author.name: Amogh Singh

entry.summary: Argues that reporting a small net benchmark delta is nearly uninformative evidence that a compressed model matches its original, because opposing per-item flips cancel; across 1,707 model-by-task cells the per-item churn is roughly five times the net accuracy change. It adds a preregistered audit of 17 published equivalence claims and a statistical toolkit for making such claims properly.

entry.title: Workspace Topology as an Attack Vector in Agentic Coding Assistants

author.name: Alexandre G. R. Day, Pradeep Yadlapalli, Sriram Venkatapathy, Thomas Paniagua, Nick Raines, Sahil Wadhwa, Himanshu Kumar, Andy Luo, Sudeep Panyam, Rikhiya Ghosh, Pranab Mohanty, Giri Iyengar

entry.summary: This empirical security study defines workspace topology, meaning directory depth, codebase modularity, injection position within a file and surrounding context framing, as an attack surface for indirect prompt injection against agentic coding assistants. Across open-source repositories in ten languages and six engineering domains, these structural factors measurably change attack success rates.

entry.title: Auditing Exposure to Harmful Content on TikTok using Multimodal Language Models: A Cross-National, Age-Stratified Study

author.name: Hamidreza Saffari, Francesco Pierri

entry.summary: Audits TikTok exposure to harmful content using sockpuppet accounts across four age personas in France, Italy, and Sweden, collecting nearly 37,000 videos from passive scrolling and active harm-keyword sessions. Four multimodal LLMs are validated against native-speaker labels, with Gemini 2.5 Flash using sampled frames plus text performing best at roughly half the cost of native video upload.

entry.title: BayesPrompt: human readable prompts that make sense

author.name: Franky Kevin Nando Tezoh, Ali Hussaini Umar, Alessandro Laio, Guido Sanguinetti, Riccardo Rende

entry.summary: BayesPrompt reframes prompt reconstruction as Bayesian posterior inference over prompts rather than perplexity minimization, arguing that the usual optimization is ill-posed and therefore yields unintelligible pseudoprompts. The resulting sampler produces prompts that are simultaneously low-perplexity and human-readable, improving on state-of-the-art alternatives across several metrics on a real dataset.

entry.title: An Empirical Study of Reward Specification and Benchmark Reliability in GRPO-based LLM Unlearning

author.name: Rub\'en Balbastre, Juan Manuel Ordu\~na, Mariano P\'erez

entry.summary: Empirically studies reward specification for GRPO-based LLM unlearning, comparing lexical suppression, anti-refusal shaping, rubric-based broad answering, and explicit refusal contrast in a controlled LoRA setting on the RWKU benchmark. The central finding is that optimization success does not equal behavioral unlearning, since forget scores, held-out completion audits, and actual behavior diverge, and the underspecified case of target-adjacent prompts is where models leak, evade, or over-refuse.

entry.title: Pushing the Limits of High-Resolution Weather Forecasting through Data Scaling

author.name: Yang Zhao, Peisong Niu, Tian Zhou, Ziqing Ma, Guanlong Ma, Rong Jin, Huiling Yuan, Liang Sun

entry.summary: BaguanHR argues that the bottleneck for 0.1 degree machine-learning weather forecasting is data rather than model transfer, and shows super-resolution has lower conditional entropy than forecasting, making it a better vehicle for resolution transfer. The framework therefore upgrades training data resolution instead of fine-tuning coarse forecast models on scarce high-resolution samples.

entry.title: Large Discovery Models: Empirically-grounded Model-Based Open-Ended Search

author.name: Zhongwei Yu, Yan Song, Xue Yan, Anjie Liu, Xingyu Lu, Yihang Chen, Huichi Zhou, Siyuan Guo, Luoyang Sun, Sihan Chen, Xiangning Yu, Jun Wang

entry.summary: The Large Discovery Model couples a generative proposal model over structured spaces such as molecules, proteins, and programs with a Bayesian non-parametric reward surrogate that provides calibrated uncertainty, addressing the unreliability of LLM self-assessment for novel candidates. The recurrent architecture iterates proposal and empirical grounding for open-ended optimization.

entry.title: Learn What's Left, Not What's Mastered: Saturation Aware Advantage Reweighting for Multi-Reward Policy Optimization

author.name: Yixuan Wang, Yifei Chen, Haichao Zhang, Haozheng Luo, Xander Wu, Jie Ni, Yun Fu, Nuno Vasconcelos, Yijiang Li

entry.summary: The paper shows that scalarizing multiple rewards with fixed weights before group-relative standardization in RL post-training causes distinct rollouts to receive identical advantages and keeps spending gradient budget on already-saturated objectives. It proposes saturation-aware advantage reweighting so optimization pressure shifts toward objectives with remaining headroom.

entry.title: PertMind: Eliciting Emergent Biological Reasoning in LLM via Reinforcement Learning on Cellular Perturbation Data

author.name: Zhenchao Tang, Xiaogang Xu, Tianxu Lv, Jiahui Guan, Jiale Zhou, Haohuai He, Zhi Song, Hanbo Huang, Jiehui Huang, Jiafei Wu, Zhe Liu

entry.summary: PertMind turns cellular perturbation atlases into reinforcement learning environments, using measured gene responses as computable rewards at gene, pathway, and format levels after a trusted-trajectory supervised initialization. Trained only on forward perturbation-response prediction, it reportedly transfers to reverse perturbation identification and combination tasks while retaining general language ability.

entry.title: MoNe: Modular Neural Memory for Efficient Long Context Inference

author.name: Wonguk Cho, Kyubyung Chae, Tribhuvanesh Orekondy, Sunghyun Park, Hyoungwoo Park, Jeongho Kim, Arash Behboodi, Kyuwoong Hwang, Sungrack Yun

entry.summary: MoNe attaches a lightweight fast-weight memory module to a frozen pretrained Transformer, reading context in segments via test-time learning with layer-local gradient updates so that queries never re-read context tokens. It reports linear preprocessing and constant query cost, cutting compute and peak memory by roughly 80 percent at 128K tokens with about 6 percent parameter overhead.

entry.title: On the Fragility of Self-Improving Agents: Variance, Task Order, and Underspecification

author.name: Qinyuan Ye, Yu Li, Yada Pruksachatkun, Jiaxin Zhang, Chien-Sheng Wu

entry.summary: Re-evaluates two prominent memory-based self-improving agent methods with multiple seeds and randomized task orderings, finding that reported gains are often within noise and that task order materially changes outcomes. Concludes that current self-improvement results are fragile and that evaluation in complex environments is inherently high-variance.

entry.title: Leveraging generative hallucination and biophysics-informed modeling for unified biomolecular sequence-structure co-design

author.name: Xuefeng Liu, Mingxuan Cao, Xiao Luo, Songhao Jiang, Tobin Sosnick, Jinbo Xu, Louis Maher, Rick Stevens

entry.summary: MCTH performs all-atom sequence and structure co-design by treating pretrained folding and inverse-folding networks as frozen black boxes and using Monte Carlo tree search to allocate a fixed inference budget across hallucinated candidate states, with optional biophysical control inside the same loop. It emphasizes underexplored DNA and RNA design where complex training data is scarce. Inference-time search substitutes for scarce supervised data.

entry.title: Efficient RLVR Scheduling via Graph-Structured Online Difficulty Estimation

author.name: Zhizhao Liu, Zhiliang Tian, Xi Wang, Zhihua Wen, Yihang Xiong, Zhiquan Lai, Dongsheng Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes a scheduler for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards that estimates per-sample difficulty online using a graph over samples, avoiding both dedicated probing overhead and the cold-start problem of history-based estimators. Rollout budget is then allocated adaptively so hard-but-learnable problems get more exploration.

entry.title: Belayer: Efficient Fault Tolerance for LLM Agentic RL Training

author.name: Jiecheng Zhou, Qinghao Hu, Peng Sun, Xingcheng Zhang, Weiming Zhang

entry.summary: Belayer is a fault-tolerance system for reinforcement learning on language model agents, where rollouts couple GPU inference with stateful environment containers whose actions leave side effects like file edits and installs. It provides recovery mechanisms so that a component failure does not discard long trajectories or leave the model in an environment state inconsistent with its context.

entry.title: Whose Gold? Annotator-Pool Disagreement Is Large at the Item Level, and Hidden by Small Leaderboards

author.name: Anik Jha

entry.summary: Measures how much preference-benchmark labels depend on who was hired to annotate, finding that on items where both expert and crowd pools are internally unanimous the pools still assign different majority labels roughly a quarter of the time and reverse the winner about nine percent of the time. Strikingly, the resulting model leaderboards are identical, which the author argues is much weaker evidence of robustness than it appears given the small number of models compared.

entry.title: Probabilistic Circuits as Reasoning Machines in Artificial Intelligence (Part I)

author.name: Robert Peharz

entry.summary: A cumulative habilitation thesis surveying probabilistic circuits as a tractable framework for reasoning under uncertainty, arguing for probability as a core AI language and showing how structural constraints on circuits guarantee tractable inference despite the general NP-hardness of probabilistic inference. It consolidates a decade of work on learning and reasoning with tractable probabilistic models.

entry.title: Multi-Agent AI System for Radiology Report Structuring and Quality Assurance with Independent Radiologist Evaluation

author.name: Iryna Hartsock, Cesar Lam, Christopher Otteni, Aliya Qayyum, Robert Gatenby, Cyrillo Araujo, Ghulam Rasool

entry.summary: Develops and retrospectively evaluates a locally deployed multi-agent pipeline that structures 638 CT radiology reports into standardized anatomical sections and flags quality problems including findings-impression mismatches, gender-anatomy conflicts, and undocumented communication of critical findings. Two board-certified radiologists independently assessed the system's outputs.

entry.title: J-Miner: Recovering Executable Decision Knowledge from Language-Model Classifiers

author.name: Yunfan Gao, Xinyi Huang, Tao Sheng, Haorui Song, Yun Xiong, Haofen Wang

entry.summary: J-Miner extracts the implicit decision knowledge that a fine-tuned LLM classifier acquires, aggregating vocabulary-aligned internal signals across layers and token positions into named text-level concepts, then learning executable decision rules over those concepts from the classifier's own predictions. The result is an inspectable, validatable rule set that can be reused independently of the source model.

entry.title: ETHEREAL: A 25.6-$\mu$s/inf. Low-latency Event-driven Graph-neural-network Processor for High-resolution Vision at the Edge

author.name: Adrian Kneip, Martin Lefebvre, Daniel Gehrig, Victoria Catal\'an Pastor, Davide Scaramuzza, Marian Verhelst, Charlotte Frenkel

entry.summary: ETHEREAL is presented as the first dedicated processor chip for event-driven graph neural networks, achieving inference latency of about 25.6 microseconds for high-resolution event-camera vision at the edge. It resolves the mismatch between dense regular compute and sparse irregular memory access that general hardware handles poorly.

entry.title: Fair ASR: Re-Evaluating Black-Box Jailbreaks under Shared Target-Call Budgets

author.name: Zhida He, Xiaoyu Wen, Han Qi, Ziyuan Zhou, Peng Yu, Jiajia Li, Chaochao Lu, Qiaosheng Zhang

entry.summary: Fair-ASR argues that reported jailbreak attack success rates are incomparable because methods spend wildly different numbers of queries, and proposes evaluating black-box attacks under a shared budget of calls to the target model while tracking attacker-side calls separately. Eleven representative attacks are re-evaluated under this protocol. Compute-normalized comparison changes the apparent ranking of attacks.

entry.title: Learning reshapes power-law anisotropy in internal representations

author.name: Asahi Nakamuta, Jun-nosuke Teramae

entry.summary: Derives an exact solution for the learning dynamics of a wide two-layer linear network with power-law structured inputs and teacher, explaining how the widely observed power-law anisotropy of internal representations arises from input statistics and task-driven feature learning. It links representation spectra in artificial networks to those observed in cortex.

entry.title: CaliBench: Are the Stochastic Dynamics of Video World Models Physically Calibrated?

author.name: Jonathan Sadeghi, Jenny Seidenschwarz, Jesse Allardice, Sirish Srinivasan, Benjamin Graham, Jeffrey Hawke

entry.summary: CaliBench asks whether video world models produce physically calibrated distributions of outcomes rather than merely plausible individual samples, by scoring generations in interpretable discrete outcome spaces such as bin indices, die faces, and roulette colors whose true distributions are known in closed form. This enables exact calibration measurement instead of coarse distributional comparison in learned feature space.

entry.title: RigidBench: Evaluating Rigid-Body Physics in Video Generation Models

author.name: Swarnim Jain, Shangzhe Wu

entry.summary: Introduces a simulator-grounded benchmark that evaluates whether video generation models move rigid objects physically correctly, by comparing generated continuations against reference physics rollouts from the same initial frame. It supplies per-frame masks, depth, 6-DoF trajectories, and contacts so that motion, geometry, identity, and background errors can be scored separately instead of being blurred into one whole-frame metric.

entry.title: Beyond Visual CoT: Internalized Visual Thinking for Proactive Video Reasoning

author.name: Xiaoyu Zhu, Xinke Deng, Suresh Taddewadikar, Arnab Kumar Mondal, Zhongyu Jiang, Ian Fasel, Joerg Liebelt

entry.summary: Argues that models can learn visual reasoning during training but skip image generation at inference: the post-training method jointly optimizes text prediction and next-embedding prediction of future video frames on unlabeled video. This internalizes visual foresight and avoids the heavy inference cost of generating intermediate reasoning images for proactive video reasoning.

entry.title: Unsupervised Learning of Cell Instances with Generative Routing Pyramids

author.name: Ziwen Liu, Martin Weigert

entry.summary: Introduces an unsupervised method that segments and phenotypes individual cells in microscopy images by reconstructing each image with a coarse-to-fine routing pyramid that binds pixels to spatially sparse latent sources. Pixel-to-latent assignments become instance masks while the latents themselves encode per-cell appearance, unifying segmentation and representation learning without annotations.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Decision Making in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Abderrahmene Boudiaf, Irfan Hussain, Sajid Javed

entry.summary: A survey that organizes uncertainty in multimodal LLMs around a decision-centered pipeline: sources of uncertainty produce observable signals, signals must be calibrated for risk, and calibrated uncertainty should drive concrete system actions such as abstention or escalation. It spans token and logit uncertainty, grounding failures, cross-modal conflict, distribution shift, and unanswerable questions.

entry.title: Which Source Wins? Task-Dependent Reliance in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Rodela Ghosh, Aviral Gupta, Guangjing Wang

entry.summary: Studies how vision-language models reallocate reliance between image and text when one modality is degraded, using arithmetic problems where the rendered image and the text support different answers, plus a new manually reviewed benchmark of 229 chart-report conflicts. Six open-weight VLMs are evaluated across four legibility levels to trace how preference shifts as one source becomes harder to read.

entry.title: ArborMem: Navigating Interaction States with Memory Forests

author.name: Zongwei Lv, Yuemeng Xu, Yilun Yao, Siyi Ding, Xinyu Tan, Yaoming Li, Guangxiang Zhao, Weihong Lin, Lin Sun, Xiangzheng Zhang, Tong Yang

entry.summary: ArborMem represents a long-running conversation as a navigable forest of interaction states so an agent can first determine which prior state the current turn resumes before retrieving relevant content. This targets interleaved multi-task conversations where topics are interrupted and revisited, a case that flat retrieval over conversational history handles poorly.

entry.title: SeqFeed: Improving Agentic RTL Code Generation with Sequential Behavior Feedback

author.name: Yuxin Du, Juxin Niu, Tao Hu, Xi Wang, Zhe Jiang, Nan Guan

entry.summary: SeqFeed improves agentic RTL hardware code generation by giving agents feedback about sequential signal behavior across clock cycles, which is invisible in source code and drowned out in raw simulation waveforms. Drawing on how human engineers debug, the authors specify that feedback must be event-addressable and targeted, and construct a representation meeting those requirements.

entry.title: Lymphocyte Mimicry Correction via Region-Level Tissue Reasoning and Unbalanced Optimal Transport

author.name: Xiang Li, Yuqi Wang, Casey C. Heirman, Jihye Heo, Kyle J. Lafata

entry.summary: Loki-OT resolves cell mimicry, where different cell types look morphologically alike, by propagating region-level tissue context reasoning from a pathology multimodal LLM down to individual cell predictions through unbalanced optimal transport. Density priors from the MLLM act as soft guidance that reassigns ambiguous cells, exploiting tissue context already latent in cell foundation model features but unused by standard cell-level supervision.

entry.title: Expressivity In Multimodal Contrastive Learning

author.name: Andrew Stuart, Florian Wolf

entry.summary: This work studies the expressive power of CLIP-style multimodal contrastive architectures from a population-level density-estimation viewpoint, asking which joint distributions over modalities a given contrastive parameterization can approximate arbitrarily well. It isolates representational capacity from optimization and data effects. The results give theoretical grounding to an architecture family underpinning text-to-image and vision-language systems.

entry.title: KernelArc: A Multi-Agent Framework for GPU Kernel Optimization

author.name: Joyjit Kundu, Ben Stoffelen, Kaili Wang, Peter Vrancx, Ludovic Denoyer

entry.summary: KernelArc runs strategy-specialized agents in parallel with a shared conclusions-only memory and deterministic benchmarking to autonomously optimize GPU kernels on H100 and B200 hardware. Outputs include custom BF16 GEMM, fused MoE backward passes, NVFP4 grouped-query attention, and paged prefill attention, with public leaderboard submissions.

entry.title: Wuying-Browser-Agent: Real-World Centric Fundamental Long-Horizon Browser Agents

author.name: AIMAE Team, Tianxiang Chen, Yan Cheng, Zhangye Han, Xiaowei Li, Chang Liu, Cheng Liu, Zhongqiang Ma, Long Peng, Xiaobing Tu, Yinggui Wang, Hongliang Wei, Chen Wu, Daiping Xin, Kunyu Zhou, Pengyang Zhou, Peiyuan Chen, Ziyuan Chen, Yutao Deng, Chunyu Dong, Xiangyu Fu, Yicheng Feng, Ruian He, Haochen Li, Miancan Liu, Zhengqin Liu, Wei Peng, Jinkui Ren, Haoyu Tan, Dong Xiao, Rongkun Xue, Shujian Yang, Xianhang Ye, Ziqi Yuan, Ziyang Yu, Linghan Zhang, Xiantao Zhang, Xuanpu Zhao, Yinan Zhao, Zhenghui Zhao, Bin Zhu, Likai Zou

entry.summary: A large industry team presents a full-stack browser agent framework aligning execution harness, supervision data, RL optimization, and evaluation for long-horizon tasks on live websites. Components include a structured browser harness, curriculum SFT on recovery and complex-UI trajectories, and a divergence-aware online GRPO variant.

entry.title: Inductively Scalable, Single-Step Neural Surrogates for Wave-Scattering Inverse Problems

author.name: Charles Dove, Laura Waller

entry.summary: The authors break the scaling barrier for single-step, non-recurrent neural surrogates of electromagnetic wave simulation by generating hard training examples on the fly with gradient ascent over refractive-index and source configurations, instead of sampling randomly from a vast input space. This lets surrogates handle far more simulation variables than the previous limit of a few tens. It could substantially speed up photonic inverse design.

entry.title: From Corpora to Co-Evolving Capabilities: Capability-Centric Data Design for Generalist Image Generation

author.name: Xingjian Wang, Zhao Wang, Taihang Hu, Jun Zheng, Qing Jin, Qinye Zhou, Zhengtao Wu, Yongchao Du, Zuan Gao, Chao Lin, Yefeng Shen, Xiaoli Xu, Zhengze Xu, Hao Yan, Yuhang Yu, Mingzhou Zhang, Mengting Chen

entry.summary: A large industrial team presents a capability-driven data infrastructure for generalist image generation, with three data engines producing relational supervision for text-image grounding, image-to-image transformation, and image-knowledge association, plus a curriculum that respects dependencies among capabilities. It reframes data curation from per-task corpora to co-evolving capability design.

entry.title: The Limits of Binding in Dual Encoders

author.name: Kin Ian Lo

entry.summary: The paper gives a mathematical account of why dual-encoder models such as CLIP fail at compositional binding, for example distinguishing a red car with a blue dog from the swapped description. It shows the ideal-encoder axioms are satisfiable, so failure requires extra hypotheses, then proves three obstructions including an exact exponential decay law for swap margin with role-nesting depth.

entry.title: OceanLight: Efficient Global Ocean Forecasting via Geometry-Adaptive Unstructured Mesh Representation

author.name: Wei Wu, Xiang Wang, Hongze Leng, Qingye Min, Junxing Zhu, Junqiang Song

entry.summary: OceanLight is a global ocean forecasting model that tokenizes the ocean on a geometry-adaptive unstructured mesh and uses a graph neural network backbone, avoiding wasted computation on land cells and allowing higher resolution where flow is complex. The authors report pointwise accuracy and kinetic energy spectral fidelity exceeding structured-grid deep learning baselines at lower cost.

entry.title: RecurrentGPT: Expressive Depth through Recurrent Modulation in Transformers

author.name: Amr Hegazy, Amr Alanwar, Mostafa Elhoushi

entry.summary: RecurrentGPT brackets a single shared transformer core, iterated a variable number of times, between fixed prelude and coda blocks, and adds a lightweight gated update conditioned on the hidden state, the prelude output and resampled noise to prevent the representational collapse that plain layer sharing causes. The goal is to buy depth-like expressivity without paying full per-layer memory.

entry.title: DeltaLog: Deferred Materialization of Recurrent States for Linear Attention Decoding

author.name: Junqing Lin, Jingwei Sun, Guangzhong Sun

entry.summary: Presents a decoding scheme for linear-attention models that avoids writing the full recurrent state back to memory after every generated token, instead keeping a dense base state plus a bounded log of compact recent updates. Since it does not change model semantics, it is a drop-in memory-bandwidth optimization for large-state linear attention architectures.

entry.title: CoM$^3$eT: A foundation model for medical image analysis through federated, multidimensional context integration

author.name: J. Raphael Sch\"afer, Kai Geissler, Till Nicke, Chiara Tappermann, Karoline Heber, Eike Petersen, Habib Mergan, Lars Ole Schwen, Nick Weiss, Annika Gerken, Jan Hendrik Moltz, Tom Bisson, Isil Dogan O, Tim-Rasmus Kiehl, Norman Zerbe, Sefer Elezkurtaj, Robin S. Mayer, Nadine Flinner, Peter Wild, Isabel Dahm, Felix Peisen, Heinrich von Busch, Robert Grimm, Sebastian Arndt, Lisa Siegler, Matthias Stefan May, Antje Prasse, Natalia Artysh, Fabian Kiessling, Johannes Lotz

entry.summary: Presents a medical vision foundation model that unifies pathology and radiology, sparse and dense prediction tasks, and two- and higher-dimensional inputs by modeling multidimensional context with attention, trained in a federated manner across institutions. It reportedly outperformed other medical foundation models in an open competition covering twelve datasets.

entry.title: MANIGUARD: A Benchmark and Data Suite for Specification-Grounded Safety Evaluation and Improvement of Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yiyan Peng, Philip Wang, Simon Sinong Zhan, Yiqi Lyu, Zhenyang Ni, Jixin Yan, Fiorelli Wong, Ruochen Jiao, Hang Yin, Xinyu Cao, Huajie Shao, Manling Li, Ruohan Zhang, Qi Zhu

entry.summary: ManiGuard is a benchmark and data suite for evaluating whether foundation-model manipulation policies succeed safely, specifying safety independently of task success across six contact-rich household task families and 200 base tasks with out-of-distribution perturbations. It pairs the benchmark with a safety-annotated trajectory generation pipeline intended to improve, not just measure, policy safety. This fills a real gap as robot foundation models are evaluated almost entirely on success rate.

entry.title: When a model reads a drug's class from its name—not its knowledge

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Ai2 researchers use Olmo 3 together with its fully open training corpus to show that the model often infers a drug's therapeutic class from morphological cues in the drug name rather than from knowledge of the specific medication, and trace this shortcut to how frequently each drug appears in training data. This is a clean demonstration of the value of open training data for diagnosing shortcut learning. The finding has direct safety implications for medical question answering.

entry.title: KnowSim: Evaluating Information Calibration in LLM Assistants with User Simulators that Learn

author.name: Yoonjoo Lee, Hyoungwook Jin, Tae Soo Kim, Shaoyang Zhang, Philippe Laban, Q. Vera Liao

entry.summary: KnowSim evaluates whether assistants match explanations to a user's actual understanding by simulating users with explicit knowledge-state graphs of information units and prerequisites that update according to learning-theory rules. It yields metrics for knowledge growth and calibration that static simulators cannot capture.

entry.title: ASI-Bench: At the Dawn of Artificial Superintelligence

author.name: Junwei Zhou, Zhen Sun, Binyu Li, Jiangyu Zhou, Yuexi Pan, Hengyu Wang, Honghe Ren, Xiaohan Jia, Xueyang Zhou, Xiaoyu Cao, Yongchao Chen, Yuanning Feng, Junhao Wu, Cheng Zhang, Sijia Chen, Haoyu Xue, Chengsong You, Huan Wang, Koutian Wu, Peigan Gao, Jiakun Wu, Wenzhe Li, Ergan Shang, Qingyuan Zheng, Jingjing Zhou, Ruixuan Jia, Yan Xu, Hongrui Zhang, Xiao-Han Ma, Zhengxiang Cheng, Yuexing Hao, Liting Mai, Xianglin Ji, Wenjun Zhang, Zhuofan Chen, Yixiao Huang, Chi Wang, Wenyue Hua, Yilun Hao, Yuantao Zhai, Ziyan Zhao, Jingyan Xie

entry.summary: ASI-Bench is a very large collaborative benchmark aimed at measuring innovative exploration and autonomous scientific execution rather than recall of known knowledge, and it progressively removes human scaffolding across difficulty tiers. It positions itself as an early measurement instrument for superintelligence-style capabilities.

entry.title: LEGO-RL: Harness-Native Reinforcement Learning for Coding Agents

author.name: Yiming Du, Yuxin Jiang, Tao Yuan, Jianbo Dai, Shaowei Wang, Jierun Chen, Chaofan Tao, Xianzhi Yu, Lifeng Shang, Kam-Fai Wong, Xiaohui Li, Haoli Bai

entry.summary: LEGO-RL connects unmodified production coding-agent harnesses to policy-gradient training by proxying the LLM endpoint in-process to capture raw generation streams for exact token alignment, while handling crashes and reward hacking that corrupt outcome signals. It aims to eliminate the train-inference mismatch that plagues harness-based agent RL.

entry.title: Iterative tensor network transformations for element-wise evaluation of elementary and filtering functions

author.name: Xiao Wang, Tomohiro Hashizume, Pia Siegl, Dieter Jaksch

entry.summary: The authors introduce an iterative framework for evaluating elementary and nonlinear filtering functions element-wise directly on data compressed as tensor trains, avoiding decompression and keeping cost controlled on exponentially large arrays. Demonstrations include nonlinear processing of a 3D reactive flow field. This removes a long-standing obstacle to using tensor networks for general data processing.

entry.title: Can LLMs Reason in a Legally Meaningful Manner? A Small-scale Study on European Court of Human Rights Cases

author.name: Amogh Raina, Ilias Chalkidis, Daniel Hershcovich, Henrik Palmer Olsen

entry.summary: The authors probe whether a top-tier reasoning model produces legally meaningful justifications when forecasting outcomes of European Court of Human Rights cases, varying how strongly prompts hint at what counts as valid legal reasoning, and scoring outputs with both humans and an LLM judge. The evaluated system, GPT-5.4, is an established model analyzed here rather than a new release. Results indicate reasoning quality falls well short of legal standards even when predictions are plausible.

entry.title: Understanding Curriculum Learning in Large Language Models via Cross-Difficulty Optimization Dynamics

author.name: Zhikai Ding, Ziyi Ye

entry.summary: The paper explains why curriculum learning helps for some LLM post-training tasks and not others by analyzing optimization dynamics across difficulty levels, formalizing a relative transfer relationship between easy and hard data that predicts which schedule will work. It converts an empirical folk practice into a testable criterion. Useful for designing data schedules in reasoning post-training.

entry.title: No Gaussian Required: Contrastive Inverse Dynamics for JEPA World Models

author.name: Jack Boylan, Chris Hokamp

entry.summary: The paper challenges the use of distribution-matching regularizers such as SIGReg to prevent representation collapse in joint-embedding predictive architectures, arguing that anti-collapse pressure should come from transition data rather than from prescribing an isotropic Gaussian latent. Its AC-MTM method keeps the forward latent prediction objective and adds an action-contrastive inverse-dynamics term. Directly engages current debates around LeCun-style world models.

entry.title: HarnessRisk: A Lifecycle-Oriented Benchmark for Agent Harness Safety

author.name: Yajing Bai, Jinhao Duan, Jie Peng, Xianfeng Wu, Sijia Liu, Song Wang, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: HarnessRisk is a benchmark of 128 sandboxed cases that organizes agent safety around six operational phases of the harness itself, covering configuration, capability extension, runtime operation, state persistence, action control, and incident recovery, with each case pairing a benign user goal against an embedded adversarial instruction. It shifts evaluation from isolated attack techniques toward lifecycle responsibilities. Useful for comparing where in an agent stack safety actually fails.

entry.title: MobileWorldSafety: Benchmarking GUI Agent Safety Against Environmental Injection Attacks in Android Apps

author.name: Sujin Chen, Lijun Li, Tianyi Du, Jing Shao

entry.summary: MobileWorldSafety benchmarks GUI agents that operate real Android apps against environmental injection attacks, where malicious instructions are embedded in the untrusted screen content the agent must read, across everyday mobile usage scenarios. The authors argue existing benchmarks miss realistic consumer contexts. It quantifies a deployment-blocking vulnerability for phone-operating agents.

entry.title: Cross-Entropy Risk Estimation for Language Models: Inconsistency Must Be Dense, and the Holdout Method Is No Exception

author.name: Hanti Lin

entry.summary: Argues that the held-out per-token cross-entropy risk used to fit scaling laws cannot be consistently estimated, because whether a model has finite risk depends on tail properties of the distribution its weights induce that no finite sample can reveal. The holdout method is shown to be no exception to this impossibility.

entry.title: Toward Optimal Second-Order Path-Length Guarantee for Adversarial Multi-Armed Bandits

author.name: Mengxiao Zhang

entry.summary: This paper resolves an open question from Bubeck and coauthors by proving that their existing adversarial bandit algorithm already achieves second-order path-length regret, without modification, via a more involved analysis. The result strengthens adaptive regret guarantees for K-armed bandits against oblivious adversaries.

entry.title: Non-Crossing Deep Quantile Regression for Distributional Survival Prediction

author.name: Shuai Huang, Zhe Qu, Zhaowei Hua, Guohao Shen, Rui Tang, Hongtu Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes a censored non-crossing quantile framework for survival analysis that jointly estimates multiple conditional survival quantiles on the original time scale while guaranteeing valid ordering by construction, using Kolmogorov-Arnold and Transformer backbones. The authors provide a finite-sample excess-risk bound alongside the architecture.

entry.title: Whether LLMs Can Navigate Beliefs and Facts Depends on How You Phrase It

author.name: Quang Minh Nguyen, Luis Frentzen Salim

entry.summary: Extends prior work on LLMs failing to acknowledge user beliefs grounded in false information, testing 10 models across 18 epistemic expressions. The gap between handling factual and false beliefs swings from plus 50 percent for one hedging phrase to minus 14 percent for another, showing the weakness is largely an artifact of the specific epistemic verb rather than a uniform capability deficit.

entry.title: From Global Benchmarks to Local Evaluations: Benchmarking LLMs for the German Public Sector

author.name: Camilla Dalerci, Thilo Michael, Robin Schaefer, Daniel Weinland

entry.summary: Presents first results from a holistic evaluation framework for LLM selection in the German public sector that adds three governance dimensions rarely benchmarked: estimated energy consumption, provider transparency, and knowledge of German party positions. Estimated energy use varies more than sixtyfold across models and is not explained by parameter count alone, and no single model leads on all dimensions.

entry.title: Inference-Time Attention Steering for Vision-Language-Action Driving Models

author.name: Darshan Nagendra Prasad, Lars Ullrich, Knut Graichen

entry.summary: Applies a bounded additive pre-softmax attention bias to visual tokens of detector-localized traffic actors in a vision-language-action driving model, implemented as a fail-open forward hook requiring no retraining. Across 50 lane-change scenarios the diffusion trajectory decoder shows a monotonic dose response to bias magnitude, reaching roughly 17 centimeters of mean displacement with measurable lateral shifts.

entry.title: GenRec: Knowing Where to Reconstruct and Where to Generate

author.name: Ata \c{C}elen, Jaewoo Jung, Federico Tombari, Marc Pollefeys, Sunghwan Hong, Michael Niemeyer, Daniel Barath

entry.summary: GenRec builds the distinction between reconstruction and generation directly into a multi-view flow matching model, treating pixels visible in source views as having a unique correct value while disoccluded or out-of-volume regions admit plausible completions. Existing generative novel view synthesis methods apply one uniform loss to both regimes and blur geometric fidelity with hallucination.

entry.title: Probing the Prefill: Detecting Code Vulnerabilities via Latent Activations

author.name: Alizishaan Khatri

entry.summary: This study trains lightweight MLP probes on last prefill-token hidden activations from four open models to predict whether C or C++ code supplied as context is vulnerable, testing on Devign, Big-Vul, Draper VDISC, and PrimeVul. The premise is that a generating model's internal state already encodes vulnerability signal before any output is produced, enabling cheaper pre-emptive defenses than post-hoc scanners. The models probed, including Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3.6-27B, and Gemma-4-12B, are established releases used here as subjects of analysis.

entry.title: The Model's Tell: Measuring Context-Leakage Attack Signals with Behavior Gauges

author.name: Maosen Zhang, Jianshuo Dong, Boting Lu, Wenyue Li, Xiaoping Zhang, Tianwei Zhang, Jie Zhang, Han Qiu

entry.summary: LeakGauge detects when a prompt is trying to extract a system prompt or retrieved documents by appending a short probe suffix and reading the prefill token probabilities, rather than requiring access to hidden states. This turns a white-box probing insight into a cheaper, more deployable guardrail signal for context-leakage attacks.

entry.title: Forward Pass Domain Adaptation (Without Cross-Layer Backpropagation)

author.name: Rivaan Patil, Simon Dennis, Hao Guo, Kevin Shabahang

entry.summary: Forward-Pass-Only training adapts LLMs without backpropagating through the model body, based on the observation that at late layers the output-layer prediction error aligns with the true gradient at cosine similarity around 0.5. The authors report roughly 3x throughput and 40 percent lower peak memory than standard fine-tuning while preserving off-domain benchmark scores.

entry.title: Mitigating Rubric Interference in LLM Judges via On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Dingyao Yu, Tong Zhang, Yutao Mou, Yunxiao Zhang, Wei Ye, Shikun Zhang

entry.summary: The paper identifies rubric interference in LLM judges: when many rubric items are evaluated in a single pass, the verdict on one item shifts depending on which others are present, with only about a third of samples fully consistent across rubric compositions. It introduces a measurement framework using expansion, subsetting, reordering, and noise injection, and mitigates interference through on-policy self-distillation.

entry.title: MiNO: Cotangent-bundle propagator learning for PDEs

author.name: Gnankan Landry Regis N'guessan, Bum Jun Kim

entry.summary: MiNO learns the propagator of a PDE in phase space, represented as a phase governed by the eikonal equation and an amplitude governed by transport, then reconstructs solutions through an oscillatory integral. The insight is that the operator generating an evolution can be far smoother than the discontinuous fields it produces, which helps with sharp fronts and caustics.

entry.title: MAPLE: MoE Adaptive Plug-and-play Layer-wise Expert allocation

author.name: Lie Li, Wen Li, Junxiao Shen, Gusheng Hu

entry.summary: MAPLE challenges the convention that every layer of a sparse mixture-of-experts model should route to the same number of experts, deriving a closed-form sensitivity-guided allocation that redistributes the expert budget across layers. It is training-free and applies to pretrained MoE LLMs without changing weights.

entry.title: GEO-Flag: Detecting and Measuring GEO-Optimized Web Content

author.name: Junjie Chu, Ye Leng, Mingjie Li, Yun Shen, Xinyue Shen, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: GEO-Flag studies generative engine optimization, where webpages are rewritten to maximize their chance of being selected and cited by generative search engines, potentially giving low-authority or false content disproportionate visibility. The authors release GEOFlagBench with 3,200 webpages across 400 queries and develop detection methods for optimized content.

entry.title: Which Question Is Your Attention Metric Answering? Attention Rows as Compositional Data

author.name: Marios Papamichalis, Regina Ruane

entry.summary: This interpretability methods paper shows that comparisons of transformer attention rows depend critically on an unreported choice: whether to keep or drop the attention sink token before computing cosine similarity, divergence or entropy. Across ten pretrained models from five families, between seventeen and forty-seven percent of judgments about which heads are similar flip with the convention, and a well-known BERT head-clustering result appears to be an artifact of it.

entry.title: Margin-Regularized Structured Semantic Alignment for Brain-Language Correspondence

author.name: Jiaqi Wang, Huawen Hu, Shu Zhang

entry.summary: MD-SigLIP aligns brain embeddings directly with text embeddings in a shared semantic space using margin-regularized structured alignment, enabling retrieval-based decoding instead of free generation. The motivation is that generative brain-to-text decoders make it impossible to tell whether decoded content reflects neural representations or is confabulated by the language model.

entry.title: The Plot Thins: Uniformity and Linearity in Literary Summaries

author.name: Rebecca M. M. Hicke, Sil Hamilton, David Mimno, Ross Deans Kristensen-McLachlan

entry.summary: Builds a dataset mapping sentences in 150 novel summaries back to their source chapters using combined human and LLM annotation, then measures how linearly and uniformly summaries traverse the source text. The alignment task proves surprisingly hard for both humans and models, and the resulting metrics reveal systematic differences in how summaries compress and reorder narrative.

entry.title: Temporal Leakage in Financial News NLP: A Multi-Architecture Audit with a Regime-Specific M&A Signal

author.name: Chenhao Xue, Raslen Guesmi, Siwei Feng, Yucheng Gong, Jacob Xavier Sundram, Jordan Pang, Lan Wang, Julian Kaljuvee

entry.summary: Audits temporal leakage in financial news direction prediction across nearly 50,000 articles and 16 feature-model combinations, finding random train-test splits inflate correlation-based scores by 1.1x to 6.5x with the inflation growing with model capacity. Conditioning on event type, mergers and acquisitions emerges as the only category retaining a signal under chronological evaluation.

entry.title: CABLE: Extending the Reach of Memory Retrieval via Complementary Antecedent-Based Linking and Expansion

author.name: Zheling Tan, Jin Gao, Dequan Wang

entry.summary: CABLE addresses evidence reachability in long-term conversational memory, noting that semantic-similarity retrieval systematically misses earlier plans and motivations that are semantically distant from the later events they explain. Rather than linking memories by semantic overlap, which duplicates what the retriever already finds, it builds a sparse set of links that specifically complement the host retriever.

entry.title: Do Large Language Models Play Six Degrees of Separation? Measuring Topological Compression in Long-Context Manifolds

author.name: Md. Faiyaz Abdullah Sayeedi

entry.summary: Bypasses attention weights, which are distorted by artifacts like attention sinks, to study the geometry of LLM hidden states directly, sparsifying similarity matrices of long-context representations into unweighted graphs. The analysis finds that deep latent spaces natively organize into small-world networks, offering a topological account of how models make distant multi-hop semantic leaps.

entry.title: When Writing Style Drifts: Benchmarking Authorship Verification under Distribution Shifts in Genre, Time and the AI-Era

author.name: Lotta Kiefer, Brisca Balthes, Christoph Leiter, Yamen Ajjour, Elena Schmidt, Steffen Eger

entry.summary: Introduces AVShift, a German authorship verification benchmark of over 150,000 text pairs spanning three genres and 21 years, designed to test robustness under genre shift, temporal drift, and AI-assisted writing simultaneously rather than in isolation. It addresses the field's overreliance on English data and single-factor shift studies.

entry.title: PlanPO: Group Planning-Aware Policy Optimization for Multi-Turn Agentic LLMs

author.name: Dayang Liang, Liyuan He, Xuan Feng, Shuxin Li, Bo An, Yunlong Liu

entry.summary: PlanPO addresses advantage collapse in group-relative RL for multi-turn agents, where roundabout and efficient successes get identical rewards, by adding coarse-to-fine planning-aware advantage signals. The goal is to learn transferable planning behavior instead of memorizing task-specific action patterns.

entry.title: LLM-Derived Preference Judgments Are Not Self-Consistent

author.name: Matthew T. Ford, Francis Bahk, Jingjing Wang, Adam S. Jovine, Tinghan Ye, David B. Shmoys, Peter I. Frazier

entry.summary: Tests whether cardinal preference judgments elicited from LLMs, such as willingness to pay, can be reproduced by any single utility function, using statistical consistency tests over arithmetically linked queries. Finds that these judgments are not self-consistent, undermining pipelines that fit utility functions from LLM-elicited preferences.

entry.title: StartupBench: Benchmarking General-Purpose Agents on Market-Validated End-to-End Workflows

author.name: Liya Zhu, Xin Ma, Tao Liu, Haodong Wang, Ge Zhang, Jingzhe Ding, Qingshui Gu, Yongjie Zhong, Jinxiang Meng, Yuan Gao, Yunqiu Zhou, Hao Zhu, Jifeng He, Yongzhi Liao, Xinyi Zhang, Chaoxin Li, Yi Zhu, Xi Lin, Duju Zeng, Xiang Gao, Wen Zhang, Yunyang Wang, Duo Wang, Huan Zhou, Zuo Wang, Jin Chen, Kaiyuan Zhang, Chuqian Yu, Tianhao Yu, Longxiang Liu, Jianbo Xue, Huimin Che, Jiahao Wang, Yujia Qin, Jiaheng Liu, Shen Yan, Xiaolong Chang, Wenhao Huang

entry.summary: StartupBench derives end-to-end agent tasks by reverse-engineering the workflows of AI startup products that already have demonstrated market adoption, rather than from researcher intuitions about useful capabilities. It aims to measure whether benchmark progress translates to work real users actually pay for.

entry.title: The Working Set of a Coding Agent: Coherence Debt in Repository-Scale Tasks

author.name: Bardia Mohammadi, Lars Klein, Aman Chadha, Akhil Arora, Laurent Bindschaedler

entry.summary: Models repository-scale coding as reconstructing a coupled-fact graph and defines coherence debt as the facts covered by neither the context window nor parametric memory. Systematic channel ablation across seven models and five harnesses shows no model succeeds on an unseen API with both channels empty, and that a library rename defeating memorized knowledge causes all seven models to fail identically.

entry.title: Institution-Specific LLM Prompting Recovers PHI That De-identification Systems and Their Gold Standards Both Miss

author.name: Daniel Palacios, Matthew Brady Neeley, Angel Adetomike Otto, Shalini Dhamodharan, John P. Woodhouse, Chi-fan Lin, Mark Zobeck, Zhandong Liu, Hyun-Hwan Jeong

entry.summary: On 100 annotated pediatric oncology notes with over 5,000 PHI spans, the authors show that prompting LLMs with institution-specific context recovers protected health information such as internal hospital abbreviations and building names that both purpose-built de-identification tools and the human gold standard missed. Eight LLMs are benchmarked against Stanford TiDE, OpenMed PII, and pattern baselines under three prompt specificity levels. It challenges the reliability of existing de-identification gold standards.

entry.title: Where a New Concept Must Enter: Entry Point Gates Cross-Task Usability in Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Zongyang Qiu, Yihan Wu, Kaixuan Fan, Bo Li, Hui Xiong

entry.summary: To settle whether understanding and generation actually reinforce each other in unified multimodal models, the authors bind a novel rendered 3D entity plus a screened pseudo-word through exactly one task direction and then measure the untrained direction, eliminating the data confounds that plague joint-training ablations. They find transfer channels exist in both directions but depend strongly on where the new concept enters the model. A clean causal probe of a contested architectural claim.

entry.title: A Theoretical Framework for Parallel Lifelong MAPF Using Group Decentralized Planning

author.name: Alex DeWeese, Jiaoyang Li, Guannan Qu

entry.summary: This work proves that the Rolling-Horizon Collision Resolution framework is near-optimal for lifelong multi-agent path finding under a discounted MDP formulation, then uses that analysis to motivate a group-decentralized planning extension that parallelizes computation. It aims to preserve solution quality while scaling to larger agent counts.

entry.title: Tail-Aware Top-$k$ On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Huipeng Huang, Hongxin Wei

entry.summary: The authors show that the common practice of minimizing reverse KL over a teacher's renormalized top-k tokens discards tail probability mass, which lets student entropy and tail probability drift upward and degrades accuracy. Their tail-aware objective retains information about probability outside the top-k set.

entry.title: Conditional Evaluation of Language Models with Cheap Auxiliary Signals

author.name: Zhi Zhang, Lingfeng Lyu, Yue Kang, Doudou Zhou

entry.summary: LACE is a semi-supervised estimator for measuring conditional (per-slice) LLM performance by combining scarce gold labels with abundant cheap signals such as judge scores, pairwise comparisons, and confidence features. Local centering ensures that even biased or miscalibrated auxiliary signals cannot shift the estimand while still reducing variance.

entry.title: MINT: Min-Selection Preference Distillation for Balanced Multi-Objective Alignment

author.name: Tony Tu, Sayan Chakraborty, Ruomeng Xu, Tony Qin, Austin Tian

entry.summary: MINT changes preference distillation so that sampled candidates are ranked by their weakest objective rather than a weighted sum of rewards, which is the min limit of a generalized power mean, while keeping the standard preference optimization loss unchanged. The motivation is that additive rewards let training collapse onto whichever objective is cheapest to improve, producing agents that sound helpful without being helpful.

entry.title: Discovering High-Quality Chess Puzzles with Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Allen Nie, Anirudhan Badrinath, Nicholas Tomlin, Timothy Dai, Carissa Yip, Rose E Wang, Emma Brunskill, Chris Piech

entry.summary: Offline reinforcement learning is used to search large puzzle databases for chess puzzles that are pedagogically high quality, balancing tactical motifs and required look-ahead depth rather than just difficulty rating. The work targets the general problem of automatically generating deliberate-practice material where expert curation is expensive.

entry.title: The Distributional View of Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Gordei Verbii, Juho Lee

entry.summary: This paper reframes token-level knowledge distillation as matching a family of multi-temperature views of the teacher's logits rather than a single softened distribution, aggregating them with geometry-aware objectives such as log-linear pooling and entropic Wasserstein barycenters under an embedding-based ground cost. It proves a collapse result showing when the geometry-aware objective degenerates to the pointwise Kullback-Leibler case.

entry.title: On the Identifiability of Masked Prediction: Mode Blindness and Mask Schedules

author.name: Yichao Cai, Javen Qinfeng Shi

entry.summary: This theory paper asks when masked prediction objectives identify the underlying joint distribution, and shows that for data with two well-separated modes the answer depends on the mask schedule alone: schedules dominated by large visible contexts are provably blind to global mode weights, since reweighting modes changes total variation by a constant while barely changing the objective. The authors introduce an epsilon-identifiability notion to quantify this. The result has direct implications for masked language modeling and diffusion-style discrete generative training.

entry.title: Beyond the Trace: Coupling an Interpretable Reasoning-State Readout to Native MoE Routing

author.name: Kang Chen, Sihan Zhao, Yixin Cao, Yugang Jiang

entry.summary: Distills a 64-axis semantic frame from a reasoning model's own internal states that separates inference effort from problem-induced strain, revealing process information absent from the emitted chain of thought. It then reconstructs those axes from native mixture-of-experts routing statistics, giving a low-overhead proxy with per-axis correlations around 0.69 to 0.86 across three models.

entry.title: What Aggregate Scores Miss: Measuring Item-Level Regressions in Commercial LLM API Migrations

author.name: Xiaonan Xu, Wenjing Wu
