entry.summary: By querying 900 benchmark items 50 times each across three pairwise upgrades in an existing OpenAI product sequence, the authors show that aggregate benchmark deltas hide substantial item-level churn, with many items reliably regressing even when the overall score improves. They classify each item under false-discovery-rate control with a practical-significance threshold. The models involved are established releases, and the finding is a warning about migration decisions based on headline scores.

entry.title: DUET: Dual-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Same-Weight Disagreement for Prohibition Compliance

author.name: Zihan Li, Feifei Li, Wenhui Que

entry.summary: DUET trains models to obey runtime-injected prohibitions by pairing two identical-weight teachers, one shown the prohibition and one not, so their per-token disagreement isolates the causal effect of the rule. This token-selective on-policy distillation signal is designed to fix the mismatch between sequence-level preference training and token-localized violations.

entry.title: Spectral Saliency for Machine Unlearning

author.name: Cedar Site Bai, Amber Yijia Zheng, Raymond A. Yeh, Brian Bullins

entry.summary: Spectral Saliency Unlearning takes the spectral view popularized by the Muon optimizer and applies it to machine unlearning, thresholding weak singular components so updates touch only directions with confident forget-set signal. Theoretical justification accompanies the method.

entry.title: SchurQuant: Groupwise Discrete Optimization for Layer-Wise LLM Quantization

author.name: Gunjun Lee, Sehwan Son, Younjoo Lee, Byungjun Kim, Jung Ho Ahn

entry.summary: SchurQuant improves backpropagation-free post-training quantization of LLM weights by analytically eliminating the optimal continuous response of the not-yet-quantized suffix, giving an exact groupwise quadratic with Schur-complement curvature, and by refitting scales and zero points instead of freezing the grid. It reports accuracy gains in the difficult two-bit regime.

entry.title: Generalised Transportability via Causal Abstractions

author.name: Yorgos Felekis, Paris Giampouras, Fabio Massimo Zennaro, Theodoros Damoulas

entry.summary: Extends causal transportability from query-by-query identification to a model-level view grounded in causal abstraction, so conclusions can be carried to a target population even when a query is not transportable or when no target data exist at all. It returns values rather than only symbolic formulas.

entry.title: PL-Guard: Probabilistic Logic Reasoning for LLM Guardrails

author.name: Satchit Chatterji, Shihan Wang, Giovanni Sileno, Erman Acar

entry.summary: PL-Guard separates semantic grounding from policy reasoning in LLM guardrails by having a local model extract policy-relevant predicates and a ProbLog rule layer decide whether a policy is violated. The neurosymbolic split aims to reduce both unsafe compliance and over-refusal compared with prompted judges.

entry.title: Stop Indexing at Full Precision: Revisiting Clustering for Vector Embeddings

author.name: Leonardo Kuffo, Peter Boncz

entry.summary: The paper shows that clustering vectors for approximate nearest neighbor index construction does not need full precision: applying dimensionality reduction, quantization and dimension pruning before clustering yields centroids within about one percent of ideal quality while cutting storage roughly sixtyfold. Implementations are open sourced.

entry.title: Crystal-structure design by agentic AI in a language of motifs

author.name: Dinh-Khiet Le, Minh-Quyet Ha, Hong-Phuc Vu-Dinh, Takashi Miyake, Hiori Kino, Hieu-Chi Dam

entry.summary: Presents an agentic AI system for crystal-structure design that reasons in an interpretable vocabulary of recurring geometric motifs, editing a motif profile to propose new candidate structures with stated rationales and then validating the best ones with first-principles calculations. It is applied to designing rare-earth-lean magnetic materials, targeting the extrapolation to new structure types that data-driven screening usually misses.

entry.title: Hide&Seek: Learning to Explain in an End-to-End Differentiable Network

author.name: Tal Ellinson, Hadi Mohasel Afshar, Sally Cripps

entry.summary: Hide&Seek is an end-to-end differentiable architecture for instance-wise feature selection that jointly trains a selector and a predictor under one objective, avoiding the information leakage and non-differentiability that hamper prior selector-predictor interpretability methods. The design aims to give per-instance explanations that are faithful because the predictor genuinely only sees the selected features.

entry.title: The canonical facets of multi-separator polytopes

author.name: Bjoern Andres, Silvia Di Gregorio, Jannik Irmai, Lucas Fabian Naumann, Shengxian Zhao

entry.summary: A polyhedral study of the graph multi-separator problem, an alternative to lifted multicut for image segmentation, characterizing all facets induced by the natural integer program using efficiently checkable graph conditions. The authors then strengthen the inequalities, find additional facets, and obtain a totally dual integral description for the path case.

entry.title: An Investigation of Translationese in the Generations of Multilingual Large Language Models

author.name: Maria Valentini, T\'ea Wright, Julisa Granados, Eliana Colunga, Katharina von der Wense

entry.summary: Investigates whether text natively generated by multilingual LLMs carries the statistical fingerprints of translation, applying established translationese indicators to state-of-the-art multilingual model outputs. It also asks how model-generated translationese differs from the translationese produced by direct translation, bearing on whether these models internally route generation through English.

entry.title: Effects of Answer Format Variation on Gender Bias in Large Language Models

author.name: Ksenia Merzlyakova, Sebastian Pad\'o, Franziska Weeber

entry.summary: Shows that measured gender bias in LLMs depends substantially on the answer format used to elicit responses, comparing closed-ended, Likert, and open-ended formats on the BBQ benchmark and survey data with three instruction-tuned models. The finding imports a well-established survey-science concern into LLM bias measurement and questions the stability of format-locked bias benchmarks.

entry.title: Spectral Gradient Orthogonalization Improves Differentially Private Training at Scale

author.name: Sabari Shanmugam, Nick Barnes, Kerry Taylor

entry.summary: This work adds spectral orthogonalization of noisy gradients via polar decomposition as a free post-processing step in differentially private training, exploiting the low-rank structure of vision gradients. The authors characterize a phase transition where orthogonalization only helps once per-direction signal-to-noise exceeds a threshold.

entry.title: Optically Writable Atomic Vapor Memory as a Substrate for Optical Reservoir Computing

author.name: Elizabeth Robertson, Mingwei Yang, Lina Jaurigue, Guillermo Gallego, Kathy L\"udge, Janik Wolters

entry.summary: The authors build an optically addressable random-access memory in warm cesium vapor, storing information in hyperfine populations and reading it out via probe absorption, then use it as the physical substrate of a reservoir computer. They report kernel rank near 8.8 across eight spatially multiplexed rails and low bit error on an XOR task, while noting that memory lifetime bounds temporal depth. It matters as a concrete demonstration that atomic-vapor memory can serve as analog compute hardware, not just a quantum storage element.

entry.title: FetchMan: Learning Visual Humanoid Loco-Manipulation Policies from Simulated Experiences

author.name: Omar Rayyan, Zhi Li, Max Argus, Yuxin Jiang, Chang Yu, Chenfanfu Jiang, Yuchen Cui

entry.summary: FetchMan trains visual humanoid loco-manipulation policies entirely in simulation, finding that behavior cloning of synthetic demonstrations plateaus regardless of data volume. Refining the cloned policy with Flow-GRPO on a single sparse reward breaks through that ceiling, yielding transferable whole-body pick-and-fetch behavior. The result is a useful data point on sim-to-real recipes for humanoids where teleoperation data is scarce.

entry.title: DiSCO: Defending text-to-image generation through distribution-guided contrastive prompt optimization

author.name: Tong Zhang, Motasem Alfarra, Carlos Hinojosa, Christos Louizos, Bernard Ghanem

entry.summary: DiSCO defends proprietary text-to-image models from unsafe generation using zero-shot, distribution-guided contrastive prompt optimization that works purely black-box. It targets the benign-adversarial case where prompts read as harmless yet still trigger unsafe imagery because of learned data distributions.

entry.title: When AI Designs AI: Innovation or Imitation?

author.name: Yikang Yang, Zhengxin Yang, Luzhou Peng, Minghao Luo, Yanqi Kan, Wanling Gao, Jianfeng Zhan

entry.summary: Builds task-specific algorithmic design spaces from human-authored methods and maps agent-designed solutions into them to quantify at module level how different agent designs really are. Evaluates common LLM agents across open-ended multimodal AI tasks on both performance and design divergence.

entry.title: When to Review: Spaced Repetition for Continual Pre-Training of Language Models

author.name: Alankar Atreya, Devesh Batra, Yoages Kumar Mantri, Geremy Bantug, Greig A Cowan, Raad Khraishi

entry.summary: Reframes replay in continual pre-training as adaptive review scheduling, applying the SuperMemo-2 spaced-repetition algorithm with per-example state and mapping perplexity to a recall-quality signal. Chooses not only how much history to replay but which specific examples should return at each step.

entry.title: Mixture-of-Expert Blocks Contain Strong Hallucination Detection Signals

author.name: Joao Fonseca, Rodrigo Rodrigues, Paolo Romano

entry.summary: Shows that mixture-of-experts internal signals, including router entropy, expert disagreement, and usage patterns, provide strong per-token hallucination detection signals unavailable in dense architectures. Per-token granularity enables localizing hallucinated spans rather than flagging whole answers.

entry.title: COMIC: Reference-Aware Safety Gating for Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Md Abdullahil Oaphy, Anhao Xiang, Zongxing Xie, Huayue Gu, Chenyu Wang, Honghui Xu

entry.summary: COMIC identifies a reference-dependent failure mode in multimodal models where neither the text prompt nor the image is harmful alone, but harm emerges when a benign operation such as summarize or translate is bound to a specific visual target. Rather than moderating the prompt-image pair as a whole, it gates safety at the grounded operation-target pair produced during dereference. This reframes the correct unit of analysis for multimodal jailbreak defense.

entry.title: Learning Discrete Riemannian Metrics for Physical Fields with Cochain-Frame Equivarianc

author.name: Dongzhe Zheng, Christine Allen-Blanchette

entry.summary: Riemannian Hodge Message Passing separates exact topological structure, encoded by fixed cellular coboundary operators, from learned geometry represented as symmetric positive-definite cochain metrics. This yields a mesh-based neural surrogate that respects conservation laws by construction while learning material response and anisotropy.

entry.title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Perception-Decision Misalignment in Omni-LLMs via Modality Subspace Activation

author.name: Hongbo Jiang, Jie Li, Yunhang Shen, Tianyu Xie, Pingyang Dai

entry.summary: This paper diagnoses perception-decision misalignment in omni-modal LLMs, where answers stay unchanged even when a key modality is altered, using a dual-lens measure combining answer retention rate and logit angular discrepancy. It introduces the CausalMSBench diagnostic set and mitigates the issue through modality subspace activation.

entry.title: Rethinking Reverse KL as Adaptive Entropy Distillation

author.name: Shizhen Li, Zhiyu Shen, Yuyin Lu, Yunhe Pang, Jielin Song, Yanghui Rao, Fu Lee Wang

entry.summary: This work decomposes on-policy reverse KL distillation into a teacher-fitting term and a student-entropy term, showing the token-level optimal student is a tempered version of the teacher with an adaptive weight. It argues reverse KL alone already provides the imitation-strength control that prior work sought by mixing forward and reverse KL.

entry.title: Iterative Refinement Diffusion for Super-Resolved Data Assimilation of Multiscale Physical Systems

author.name: Mrigank Dhingra, Ramchandran Muthukumar, Rebecca Willett, Omer San

entry.summary: Iterative Refinement casts super-resolved data assimilation as resolution-wise forecast-analysis cycles instead of a one-shot coarse-to-fine diffusion mapping, so past states constrain reconstruction. This blends classical assimilation structure with generative super-resolution while reducing reliance on expensive high-resolution forecast models.

entry.title: Online Convex Optimization with Dueling Feedback

author.name: Yiyang Lu, Hareshkumar Jadav, Mohammad Pedramfar, Ranveer Singh, Vaneet Aggarwal

entry.summary: Studies adversarial online convex optimization when the learner sees only a binary preference between two queried points, converting dueling feedback into approximate gradients via a simple reduction. This yields the first regret guarantees in this setting, including improved rates for smooth and strongly convex objectives.

entry.title: GraniKV: Asymmetric Granularity KV-Cache Paging for Multi-Agent Systems with Long Shared Prefix

author.name: Jinhyun Jeon, Sungjoo Yoo

entry.summary: GraniKV observes that multi-agent LLM workloads have a long shared prefix that wants contiguous storage and per-request suffixes that want fine-grained allocation, then serves each with a different paging granularity plus a per-step dispatcher choosing among backends. It reports gains at long shared prefix lengths in a production paged-serving engine.

entry.title: TinyCast: Probabilistic Zero-Shot Forecasting with Computed Periodicity

author.name: Armin Steinhauser

entry.summary: TinyCast is a zero-shot probabilistic time-series forecaster with under 150 thousand parameters that computes dominant periods with a parameter-free spectral detector, folds the context on their phase, and models the remainder with dilated convolutions and a quantile decoder. It claims the best size-versus-probabilistic-accuracy tradeoff among leaderboard entries declaring no test leakage.

entry.title: SAUL: Sharpness-Aware Augmented-Lagrangian Unlearning

author.name: Jaewan Choi, Junyoung Yang, Sangdon Park

entry.summary: SAUL casts LLM unlearning as constrained minimization, making forgetting an explicit constraint with a satisfaction criterion instead of an implicit optimization objective, and uses an augmented Lagrangian controller that can switch off forget-side updates once the constraint is met. Sharpness-aware updates aim to preserve general utility while erasing targeted knowledge.

entry.title: SCALE: State-Calibrated Latent Embeddings for JEPA Planning in the Right Geometry

author.name: Jiaming Hu, Yan Zheng, Tian Wang

entry.summary: SCALE examines why joint-embedding predictive world models plan differently depending on whether they inherit a pretrained feature space or learn one with anti-collapse regularization, showing the leading principal components of the two carry very different amounts of task-relevant state. Because Euclidean planning costs are dominated by high-variance directions, it proposes state-calibrated embeddings so planning happens in the right geometry.

entry.title: OceanDepths: A Global Dataset of Paired Subsurface and Surface Ocean Observations

author.name: Simon Donike, Ruben Cartuyvels, Antonino Ian Ferola, Elisa Carli, Diego Fernandez Prieto, Marie-Helene Rio

entry.summary: OceanDepths is presented as the first open, global, AI-ready dataset pairing satellite-derived sea surface temperature, salinity, and height fields with co-located in situ vertical depth profiles. It fills a gap left by model-reconstructed gridded products and single-variable or single-basin resources, at resolutions suitable for mesoscale dynamics.

entry.title: Evolving Executable Pipeline Programs for AutoML with Language Models

author.name: Sofoklis Kitharidis, Cor J. Veenman, Jan N. van Rijn, Thomas B\"ack, Niki van Stein

entry.summary: LACE searches over complete executable machine learning pipeline programs rather than a predefined operator space, maintaining a population of scikit-learn-compatible Python classes with an LLM acting as the evolutionary variation operator. Evaluation uses standardized OpenML tasks under a leakage-controlled protocol that hides dataset identity from the generator.

entry.title: Solvable Sokoban Without a Solver via Diffusion

author.name: Sina Baghal

entry.summary: Shows that a transformer-based discrete diffusion model trained only to fill in masked tiles of Sokoban puzzles, with no solver, reward, or solvability label, generates solvable puzzles about 77 percent of the time, and most failures become solvable by deleting a single wall. This is notable because deciding Sokoban solvability is PSPACE-complete and fragile to single-cell changes.

entry.title: Polaris: Learning to Generate Table Descriptions from Retrieval Feedback

author.name: Ting Cai, Tuan Minh Phan, AnHai Doan

entry.summary: Polaris trains an LLM to write table descriptions that maximize downstream retrieval effectiveness instead of fluency, generating multiple candidate descriptions per table, ranking them by BM25 retrieval performance, and fine-tuning on the resulting preference pairs with DPO. The key observation is that existing table retrieval benchmarks already contain the relevance supervision needed for this optimization.

entry.title: SpeechSense: A Paralinguistic-Focused Dataset for Fine-Grained Speech Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Shicheng Ma, Wenqian Cui, Irwin King

entry.summary: SpeechSense is a dataset for fine-grained speech sentiment analysis focused on paralinguistic cues, motivated by the fact that cascaded ASR-then-text pipelines discard prosody and tone and therefore misread acoustically ambiguous utterances. It also targets label-granularity mismatches in existing speech sentiment benchmarks.

entry.title: Grounding Healthcare LLMs in a Causal Knowledge Graph: Framework, Metrics, and a Cardiovascular Pilot

author.name: Ummara Mumtaz, Aimen Noor, Awais Ahmed

entry.summary: Proposes a graph-centered evaluation framework for healthcare LLMs that grades reasoning about interventions, mechanisms, harms, evidence, and uncertainty rather than single-answer accuracy, built on a causal knowledge graph whose assertions are provenance-preserving first-class nodes. Scenario-conditioned subgraph extraction and four controlled grounding conditions are stress-tested in a cardiovascular pilot.

entry.title: Reflex-Guard: A Low-Latency Guardrail for LLM Prompt Safety Using Dense Semantic Embeddings

author.name: Istiaque Ahmed, Afia Anjum Borsha, Ranat Das Prangon, Abu-fuad Ahmad, Thi Hong Tran

entry.summary: Reflex-Guard is a locally running prompt-safety guardrail built from jailbreak-aware preprocessing, compact sentence-transformer embeddings, and seven fast binary classifiers, targeting sub-100-millisecond latency. It is positioned against LLM-judge and cloud moderation APIs that add roughly 250 to 900 milliseconds per request and route user data to external endpoints.

entry.title: Rapid Debris-Volume Estimation from Post-Hurricane Aerial Imagery

author.name: Kooshan Amini, Jamie Ellen Padgett, Guha Balakrishnan

entry.summary: DebrisHeightNet estimates spatially explicit hurricane debris volume from a single pass of post-event aerial RGB imagery by training only a 1.08 million parameter head on top of two frozen foundation models, regressing height from a Depth Anything V2 backbone conditioned on debris segmentation from a CLIPSeg variant. It targets an operational problem where current parametric forecasts overestimate volume by 41 to 90 percent.

entry.title: PRISM: Precision and contact-rich Real-world Industrial Skill dataset with Multimodal sensing

author.name: Tengbo Yu, Jiahao Wu, Hanning Wang, Rui Chen, Chuanhou Liu, Chuang Sun, Hangxin Liu

entry.summary: PRISM is a large multimodal dataset of contact-rich industrial manipulation, covering more than 25 tasks such as connector plug and unplug and conveyor sorting, with over 5,000 teleoperated trajectories and 45 hours of synchronized vision, force or torque, and tactile recordings. It targets the gap left by existing robot datasets that emphasize short-horizon, low-contact pick-and-place. Data of this type is the main constraint on precision force-regulated robot learning.

entry.title: Cross-Model Memory Transfer via Target-Side Reader Adaptation

author.name: Mingyuan Li, Guangsheng Yu, Xu Wang, Shaoxiong Ji

entry.summary: The paper studies whether engram-style hashed external memory tables can be transplanted between different language model backbones, isolating whether the frozen memory contents or the small target-side reader module drives performance. It positions this hybrid between retrieval augmentation and parametric fine-tuning, where knowledge stays external, auditable, and updatable. Findings bear on modular knowledge editing and portable memory.

entry.title: Task Specialization Fine-Tuning for Contextual Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jianan Zhou, Jung-Hoon Cho, Tianyue Zhou, Han Zheng, Jie Zhang, Roy Dong, Yining Ma, Cathy Wu

entry.summary: The paper proposes pretraining one contextual RL policy for broad competence and then allocating a limited fine-tuning budget across task regions to create specialists, formalizing how much specialization each region should receive given heterogeneous marginal returns. This replaces training from scratch with either one multi-task policy or many independent policies. It gives a budget-allocation view of generalization across a continuous task space.

entry.title: When Agents Act on Web3: An Attack-Surface Survey of MCP, Skills, and Tool Calling

author.name: Rabimba Karanjai (Larry), Yang Lu (Larry), Nour Diallo (Larry), Wujie Xiong (Larry), Lei Xu (Larry), Weidong (Larry), Shi

entry.summary: A survey arguing that when agents act on public blockchains through Model Context Protocol tools and skills, four properties of the execution layer, namely irreversibility, signing authority, continuous autonomy, and sequence-level composition, qualitatively change the threat model relative to generic agent security. It reports that the share of deployed MCP tools that mutate external state rose from roughly a quarter to nearly two-thirds. It organizes a fragmented literature into a coherent attack-surface taxonomy.

entry.title: In Defense of OCTA: The Reconstruction-Utility Gap in OCT-to-OCTA Synthesis

author.name: Michael Chertok, Alon Tiosano, Orly Gal-Or, Lior Kramarski, Einav Baharav Shlezinger, Irit Bahar, Lior Wolf

entry.summary: Challenges the claim that OCT-to-OCTA image synthesis works, showing that high reconstruction scores hide a collapse in the clinically meaningful measurements: a frozen real-data segmenter probe finds fine capillary networks degrade about five times more than large vessels. The message is that reconstruction fidelity and diagnostic utility diverge in medical image synthesis.

entry.title: Routing Divergence Is Not Evidence of Behavioral Influence in Same-Weight MoE Self-Distillation

author.name: Cedric Caruzzo, Donggeun Yoo, Tae Soo Kim

entry.summary: Tests whether the fact that two mixture-of-experts forward passes can route the same token differently actually matters for same-weight self-distillation, using an exact blockwise decomposition that separates a routing term from a dense-like content term. Across seven open checkpoints the routing term contributes little to block output, so routing divergence alone is not evidence of behavioral influence.

entry.title: DeepOHeat-v2: Self-Improving Operator Learning for Fast and Trustworthy Thermal Optimization in 3D-IC Design

author.name: Xinling Yu, Yixing Li, Ziyue Liu, Xin Ai, Zhiyu Zeng, Hai Li, Zheng Zhang

entry.summary: DeepOHeat-v2 makes physics-only operator-learning surrogates work for high-contrast multi-die 3D integrated circuit thermal simulation, where discontinuous conductivities make continuous physics losses ill-defined and the discretized system is severely ill-conditioned. It switches to a discretized physics loss and addresses conditioning beyond first-order optimization for trustworthy design-space exploration.

entry.title: Koopman early warning signals for bifurcation and rate-induced tipping

author.name: Juan Nathaniel, Carla Roesch, Derek DeSantis, Parvathi Kooloth, Hang Fan, Valerio Lucarini, Anastasia Romanou, Pierre Gentine

entry.summary: The authors use Koopman operator theory and residual mode decomposition to build early warning indicators that work for both classical bifurcation tipping and rate-induced tipping, where transitions occur without local loss of stability. The framework extends to stochastic, nonautonomous systems by augmenting the observable space with control variables.

entry.title: Supervising the Path to Fine Scales: GalerkinFlow for Scientific-Field and Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Zikang Zhan

entry.summary: GalerkinFlow reframes super-resolution as supervising an entire coarse-to-fine reconstruction trajectory rather than only the final high-resolution output, predicting residual velocities at sampled intermediate states with a pseudo-endpoint anchor. The authors derive an exact time-weighted relationship between endpoint reconstruction loss and intermediate velocity loss, giving flow-matching-style supervision that is equation-agnostic across scientific fields and natural images.

entry.title: Towards Safer RAG: Only Agents Capable of System 2 Thinking may Access Untrusted Documents

author.name: Mehrdad Ghassabi

entry.summary: Proposes relaxing the strict isolation of the Cordon Principle in retrieval-augmented generation, which bars answer-synthesizing models from touching raw evidence, by allowing deliberative System-2-capable agents to read untrusted documents directly. The motivation is that models can detect misinformation in retrieved text yet still be influenced by it, while full isolation imposes heavy compute overhead.

entry.title: Preference Is Not Intervention: The Structure and Stability Boundaries of Reader-Specific Evidence Utility

author.name: Shi Zhou

entry.summary: Tests whether differences in how downstream reader models use retrieved evidence constitute stable, reusable model properties or merely input-local interactions, holding query, evidence, task, and intervention fixed across nine readers. Readers disagree on the sign of an evidence intervention in a third of jointly affected cases and reader-by-query interaction explains far more variance than a permutation null, but the paper separates which components of that heterogeneity actually persist across queries.

entry.title: PathoArgus: Advancing Evidence-Grounded Long-Context Visual Reasoning across Gigapixel Whole-Slide and Multi-Slide Case Contexts

author.name: Bowen Liu, Qixiang Zhang, Xiaomeng Li

entry.summary: PathoArgus-Bench evaluates whether pathology models actually use gigapixel slide evidence rather than exploiting linguistic priors, with over 22,000 questions from nearly 5,000 patients across fifteen cancer projects under a fixed reader budget. The protocol tests evidence availability, accessibility, use and responsiveness rather than only final answer accuracy.

entry.title: TINA+: Probing Residual Visual Knowledge in Unlearned Diffusion Models via Diffusion-Consistent Text-Free Inversion

author.name: Qianlong Xiang, Miao Zhang, Kun Wang, Haoyu Zhang, Junhui Hou, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: TINA+ probes whether concept erasure in text-to-image diffusion models truly removes visual knowledge, using diffusion-consistent text-free inversion to try reconstructing instances of an erased concept without going through the text pathway. It argues existing erasure methods and adversarial probes are too text-centric.

entry.title: Prism-GRPO: Faster VLA Policy Optimization via Splitting Same-outcome Groups

author.name: Zeyun Deng, Yuzhe Lu, Yawei Wang, Linbo Liu, Qing Ping, Han Ding, Guande Wu, Panpan Xu, Jun Huan

entry.summary: Prism-GRPO tackles a specific inefficiency in group-relative policy optimization for vision-language-action policies: under binary success rewards, groups where all rollouts succeed or all fail carry zero advantage and are discarded, wasting expensive robot rollouts early in training. The method adds a weighted trajectory-level execution-quality score that splits same-outcome groups into a quality spectrum, restoring gradient signal. This is a targeted fix for one of the main cost drivers in robotic RL fine-tuning.

entry.title: Feature Priming in Online Linear Regression: Sparse-Regret Lower Bounds and a Tight Univariate Rate

author.name: Huibo Xu, Shi Fu, Qixin Zhang, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: The authors resolve, negatively, the sparse-logarithmic form of a COLT 2023 open problem about whether feature-priming rules that reweight the design from past data can achieve sparsity-dependent online regret. They identify the obstruction as cheap nuisance interpolation causing the refit to underweight the truly predictive coordinate, and complement the lower bound with a tight univariate rate. Settling an open problem clarifies the limits of a natural family of methods.

entry.title: VERaiPHY -- Validation & Evaluation for Robust AI in PHYsics

author.name: Gaia Grosso, Ramon Winterhalder, Lydia Brenner, Louis Lyons, Tilman Plehn

entry.summary: VERaiPHY is the opening article of a PHYSTAT-affiliated series aiming to set statistical standards for developing, evaluating, and deploying machine learning in fundamental physics, covering validation, uncertainty quantification, and robustness. It lays out the shared probabilistic and statistical vocabulary for subsequent domain-specific articles. The effort responds to ML adoption in physics outpacing rigorous statistical practice.

entry.title: Benchmarking the Benchmarks: Evaluating Automated Safety Benchmarks for Small Language Models

author.name: Nyamtulla Shaik, Fengjun Li, Bo Luo

entry.summary: Evaluates whether five widely used safety and bias benchmark suites reliably measure small language models, running 26 open-source SLMs under a unified three-level judging rubric. Finds that pipelines designed for large models do not transfer dependably, raising concerns about safety claims for edge-deployed models.

entry.title: LiveHouse-TS: An Open-world Living Benchmark for Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Haomin Wen, Ziyu Zhou, Qingxiang Liu, Siru Zhong, Yuxuan Liang

entry.summary: LiveHouse-TS is a continuously updating benchmark that evaluates time series foundation models prequentially on genuinely future data instead of fixed historical test windows. It targets contamination and staleness in static forecasting evaluation and measures behavior under distribution shift and unexpected events.

entry.title: TileMix: Tile-Centric Mixed-Precision Attention for LLM Inference Acceleration

author.name: Hanzhi Zhang, Qiao Zhang, Qinglei Cao, Heng Fan, Yan Huang, Kewei Sha, Yunhe Feng

entry.summary: TileMix makes numeric precision a spatial routing decision inside fused dense attention, splitting the score matrix into hardware-aligned tiles and dispatching each tile group through FP16 or INT8 while sharing a softmax accumulator. It targets the compute and memory cost of long-context prefill.

entry.title: Evaluating the Diversity of AI-Generated Content with Diversity Profiles

author.name: Xiuyuan Hu, Xuege Hou, Guoqing Liu, Yang Zhao, Jieran Li, Dongbiao Sun, Jos\'e Miguel Hern\'andez-Lobato, Hao Zhang, Xue Liu

entry.summary: Argues that collapsing generative diversity into a single scalar is fundamentally under-specified, diagnosing existing metrics axiomatically and empirically before proposing diversity profiles as a richer alternative. Shows that different scalar metrics can rank the same sample sets contradictorily.

entry.title: Towards Zero-Shot Task Transfer with Neurosymbolic World Models

author.name: Isidoro Tamassia, Lennert De Smet, Giuseppe Marra

entry.summary: Proposes a world model in which reward prediction depends only on a structured symbolic subset of the latent state, decoupling observation reconstruction from reward modeling. This allows a learned model to adapt zero-shot to new reward functions without any further environment interaction.

entry.title: BEAR-Bench: A Bilingual Enterprise and Academic Reasoning Benchmark for Multimodal Models

author.name: Liubov Chubarova, Alexandra Kuleshova, Daniil Volkov, Kirill Sultanov, Alexey Zaytsev

entry.summary: BEAR-Bench is a 1000-question human-annotated benchmark testing multimodal models on reasoning over text-dense business and scientific documents in English and Russian. It targets the underrepresentation of non-English, non-Chinese professional document reasoning in existing evaluations.

entry.title: When Does the Best Sampling Temperature Rise with the Budget? Sufficient Conditions for Pass@k

author.name: Changsu Jeong (Independent Researcher)

entry.summary: The paper gives a population-level sufficient condition explaining why the temperature that maximizes pass@k tends to increase with sampling budget, even though for a single fixed task the optimal temperature does not depend on k. The condition is stated in terms of a monotonicity property of the conditional log-success response across a task distribution.

entry.title: PureTD: Reinforcement Learning for Backgammon Money Games with No Evaluation-time Search

author.name: Alexander L. Strehl

entry.summary: Revisits TD-Gammon by learning both checker play and doubling-cube decisions from scratch through self-play reinforcement learning with no hand-coded features and no search at evaluation time. The resulting search-free model is reported to be both faster and stronger than open-source engines running one-ply lookahead.

entry.title: Optimal Lower Bounds for Networked Information Aggregation

author.name: Ambar Pal

entry.summary: Establishes matching lower bounds for a recently studied networked information aggregation setting where learners arranged on a directed acyclic graph combine local features with their parents' predictions. The result shows the previously proven error rate for mean squared error cannot be improved.

entry.title: FluxBin: Flexible LUT-based Ultra-low-bit LLM Inference by Algorithm-Kernel Synergy

author.name: Qingyao Yang, Runming Yang, He Xiao, Wendong Xu, Junyu Chen, Haobo Liu, Chenchen Ding, Ruihan Hu, Yik-Chung Wu, Ngai Wong

entry.summary: FluxBin co-designs binary-basis post-training quantization with a lookup-table CUDA kernel so that ultra-low-bit LLM inference avoids floating-point arithmetic and runtime dequantization overheads. A decoupled row-column binary decomposition raises representational capacity while staying hardware friendly.

entry.title: Unifying Graph Neural Networks Through a Common Layer Equation

author.name: Sai Karthik Navuluru, Siddhartha Shankar Das, Bo Ni, Hongjie Chen, Yu Wang, Baris Coskunuzer, Nesreen K. Ahmed, Franck Dernoncourt, Mahantesh Halappanavar, Tyler Derr, Ryan A. Rossi, Lakshman Tamil

entry.summary: The authors propose a single layer equation with seven components that expresses many GNN families, factoring where information moves (propagation bank) from what moves (message maps), and show it covers message passing, attention, spectral filtering, global communication, relational channels, higher-order domains, and geometric messages. The unification is intended to expose shared computation and structural differences hidden by family-specific notation.

entry.title: A Privacy Study of Sparse Collaborative Inference

author.name: Maximilian Andreas Hoefler, Karsten Mueller, Wojciech Samek

entry.summary: This study tests the common intuition that sparsifying transmitted activations in split edge-server inference improves privacy, by separating the retained values from the sparsity pattern and reconstructing inputs from each component alone. It finds that sparsification does not deliver the assumed privacy benefit, since the position pattern itself leaks substantial input information.

entry.title: Q-based Variational Inverse Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ondrej Bajgar, Peter Tisnikar, Alessandro Abate, Konstantinos Gatsis, Maike Osborne

entry.summary: QVIRL is a Bayesian inverse reinforcement learning method that recovers a posterior over reward functions from expert demonstrations by primarily learning a variational distribution over optimal Q-values. Combining scalability with uncertainty quantification matters for safety-critical deployment and active preference learning.

entry.title: LLMs Can Predict Failure Risk, But Struggle to Predict Which Collaboration Protocol Pays Off: Cost-Aware Protocol Routing Across Reasoning Tasks

author.name: Chih-Hsuan Yang, Jingyan Jiang, Cheng-Hau Yang, Vikram Vasudevan, Huihuo Zheng, Venkatram Vishwanath, Rajeev Thakur

entry.summary: Every problem is solved under four fixed collaboration protocols, direct solving, iterative self-correction, planner-executor-reviewer, and multi-agent broadcast deliberation, over more than four thousand competition math problems plus science and biology robustness checks. Language models can predict whether they will fail but not which protocol will actually repay its extra cost, and both fixed policies and trained or frozen routers under-escalate.

entry.title: On Stopping Rules and Spatial Adaptation for CART

author.name: Zineng Xu, Yuchao Cai, Yan Shuo Tan

entry.summary: Provides theory for the often-ignored stopping rule in the CART regression tree algorithm, proving that with a minimum-impurity-decrease criterion and a suitable threshold, CART achieves pointwise adaptation to spatially heterogeneous and anisotropic smoothness. This closes a gap where Bayesian and empirical-risk-minimization trees were known to be spatially adaptive but greedy CART was not.

entry.title: Mint-Agent: Introducing Finance-Native Agentic Foundation Models

author.name: Agent Team, B. Zhang, Yaze Geng, Lei Tang, Yaoyang Yi, Zonghan Wu, Yifan Hu, Kun Wang, Qingsong Wen, Yilei Shao

entry.summary: Introduces a family of finance-specialized agentic models built on three pillars: a data engine constructing atomic financial capability tasks and long-horizon agentic trajectories from real sources, a harness for stable interaction with open-ended environments that maintains auditable evidence trails, and a training recipe combining supervised and reinforcement stages. Emphasis is on reliability of grounded operations and auditability of long-horizon research conclusions.

entry.title: TraceSQL: Traceable Answerability Estimation for Reference-Free Text-to-SQL Verification

author.name: Neelesh Kumar Shukla, Debasmita Panda, Srutanik Bhaduri, Aditya Banerjee, Viji Krishnamurthy

entry.summary: TraceSQL estimates whether a generated SQL query will actually answer the user question without access to gold queries or reference execution results, which is the realistic deployment condition. Unlike LLM-judge or reward-model approaches whose verdicts are opaque, it aims to expose traceable evidence for each verification decision.

entry.title: Calibrated Predictive Safety for Heterogeneous Robots: An Action-Conditioned JEPA Framework with Model-Based Safety Shields

author.name: Kaiming Zhong, Tianhua Liu, Yue Wang

entry.summary: The authors couple an action-conditioned Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture world model with an embodiment-specific model-based safety shield: a proposer generates candidate action chunks, the JEPA rolls each forward in frozen-encoder latent space to predict task progress and physical risk, and the shield enforces kinematic and geometric constraints before execution. The aim is calibrated pre-execution risk prediction across heterogeneous robots. It bridges generalist learned policies and classical guaranteed-safety planning.

entry.title: Scalix: Uncertainty-Aware Scale-Consistent Monocular SLAM

author.name: Sebastian Barbas Laina, Tianyi Zhang, Panagiotis Petropoulakis, Simon Schaefer, Simon Boche, Jaehyung Jung, Cedric Le Gentil, Stefan Leutenegger

entry.summary: Scalix is a real-time monocular SLAM system that resolves metric scale ambiguity by using learned geometric foundation model depth with explicit uncertainty handling to enforce scale consistency across frames. It targets cases where visual-inertial fusion fails, such as constant-velocity motion common in wheeled robots. The work integrates depth foundation models into a rigorous estimation backend rather than trusting their raw output.

entry.title: When Personalization Becomes Bias: Structural and Discursive Religious Framing in AI-Generated Financial Advice

author.name: Muhammad Salar Khan, Hamza Umer, Hasan Mahmud, Sandra Rothenberg

entry.summary: A mixed-methods audit of three commercial chat assistants across 432 simulated financial advisory conversations finds systematic differences in advice depending on the client's stated religious identity, spanning stock, housing, and insurance decisions. Only a small minority of cases were judged unbiased, and the authors trace both statistical and linguistic mechanisms of the disparity. It matters because personalization in regulated advisory settings can silently become discriminatory treatment.

entry.title: PXDepth: Pixel-Space Modeling for Structure Preserving Monocular Depth Estimation

author.name: Zhiyuan Yuan, Guanying Chen, Lingteng Qiu, Ruimao Zhang, Shuguang Cui, Xiaochun Cao

entry.summary: PXDepth separates global scene understanding from pixel-level prediction in monocular depth estimation, pairing a large-patch vision transformer for context with a pixel-space predictor built from context-modulated pixel transformer blocks that retain high resolution end to end. The design targets the loss of fine structures and object boundaries caused by coarse tokenization plus convolutional upsampling. Relevant to 3D perception and robotics pipelines.

entry.title: DEPT: Document Embedding Preservation Tuning for Unified Query Expansion and Retrieval

author.name: Jingyuan Wang, Richong Zhang, Zhijie Nie, Mingxin Li, Yanzhao Zhang

entry.summary: DEPT trains a single decoder-only LLM end to end to both expand underspecified queries and encode the expanded query and candidate documents, resolving the moving-target problem where retrieval updates simultaneously shift the document embeddings that serve as targets. Prior systems used prompted expansions or separately trained modules only loosely coupled to the retrieval loss. The unified objective aligns expansion directly with retrieval quality.

entry.title: Benchmarking Automated Security Patch Backporting: How Far Are We?

author.name: Jincheng Yang, Yulong Fu, Chengwei Liu, Lyuye Zhang, Fangyuan Zhang, Bingyang Ren, Yang Liu, Hui Li

entry.summary: The authors build a 1,234-case benchmark of security patch backporting spanning cross-version, cross-branch, and cross-repository scenarios, then re-evaluate five tools including program-analysis, LLM-prompting, and LLM-agent approaches under aligned conditions. Reported success rates above eighty percent on original in-distribution datasets do not generalize. Important reality check for automated N-day vulnerability mitigation.

entry.title: Interpretable Humans, Alien LLMs: Expert Analysis of Latent Structures in Assessment Responses

author.name: Alona Strugatski, Licol Zeinfeld, Jason Cooper, Shelley Rap, Gil Schwarts, Giora Alexandron

entry.summary: The authors run exploratory factor analysis separately on human and LLM responses to quantitative reasoning and chemistry assessments, then have subject-matter experts blindly interpret the resulting factor structures. Experts could ascribe pedagogical meaning to most human factors but not to the model-derived ones, challenging the assumption that human-designed tests measure comparable constructs in machines. It has direct implications for how benchmark scores are interpreted.

entry.title: Valid Per-Field Selective Risk Control for Document Extraction: Three Failure Modes, a Validity Ladder, and When Conditioning Pays

author.name: Bhaskar Gurram

entry.summary: Using nearly 14 thousand extracted fields from 800 receipts produced by an existing Claude Sonnet 5 pipeline, the paper diagnoses three ways naive per-field accept-or-review risk control breaks: document-level clustering, threshold refitting leakage, and degenerate tie masses. It then organizes fixes into a validity ladder with explicit guarantee tiers.

entry.title: Every Expert Counts: ExactMoE for Memory-Efficient W4A16 Inference

author.name: Amjad Saab

entry.summary: ExactMoE quantizes only routed experts to four bits in a kernel-native format, keeps them in pinned host memory, and streams them through a GPU slot cache with fused grouped kernels while leaving router, attention, and head in higher precision. Crucially it prunes no experts and leaves top-k routing unchanged, so behavior is preserved while memory footprint drops.

entry.title: A Pre-Specified Construction-Confirmation Test of Operation-Level Causal Transfer Across Finite Isomorphic Symbolic Domains

author.name: Xinyi Shan

entry.summary: Proposes a strict test for whether a model transfers an operation-level structure between isomorphic symbolic domains: estimate the hidden-state difference between two operations from source inputs and check whether adding it to a mapped recipient input steers the model toward the corresponding recipient answer. Wrong-operation, norm-matched random, and no-op controls plus a separate confirmation split guard against false positives.

entry.title: Beat the Counter First: A Baseline for Temporal-Graph Anomaly Detectors

author.name: Omair Shafi Ahmed, Zohair Shafi

entry.summary: The authors introduce SimpleCount, a parameter-free single-scalar-feature baseline for streaming edge-level graph anomaly detection, and show it matches or beats sophisticated memory-augmented temporal graph detectors on several public datasets. The message is that reported gains from architectural complexity in this subfield have not been rigorously isolated.

entry.title: LLM Safety Alignment in Low-Resource Languages: A Systematic Literature Review

author.name: Valdini Douglace Lemofouet, Blessing Ngozi Uzor, Paula Chikaodinaka Anyanwu, Danielle Blanche Kapsa, Sukairaj Hafiz Imam, P Sam Sahil, Abigail Oppong, Tassallah Abdullahi, Clemencia Siro, Idris Abdulmumin, Seid Muhie Yimam, Shamsuddeen Hassan Muhammad

entry.summary: A PRISMA-based systematic review of 50 studies on large language model safety alignment in low-resource and multilingual settings, organized around alignment methods, multilingual risks, evaluation benchmarks and cross-lingual transfer. It proposes a taxonomy of alignment approaches by adaptation mechanism and highlights persistent safety gaps outside high-resource languages.

entry.title: Training Leaves Traces: Centered Residual Signatures for Language Model Lineage Verification

author.name: Aman Singh Thakur, Rayan Khoury

entry.summary: The authors propose data-free white-box lineage verification, deciding from weights alone whether two checkpoints share ancestry, after removing the shared identity-aligned component that residual training induces in all compatible models. On residual-MLP and GPT-2 style benchmarks the calibrated symmetric score perfectly separates fine-tuned, LoRA-merged, pruned and quantized descendants from independent and distilled models.

entry.title: T-LLM Compiler: Trusted LLM-based Code Optimization and Verification Framework

author.name: Zahra Fazel, Sunanda Gamage, Shayan Shirahmad Gale Bagi, Amir H. Ashouri, Tomasz S. Czajkowski, Bryan Chan, Reza Azimi, Yaoqing Gao

entry.summary: The Trusted LLM Compiler couples language model code transformations with traditional compilers and formal verification tools so that proposed optimizations are checked for correctness rather than trusted. The authors report significant improvements in correctness of LLM-produced optimizations under this collaborative loop.

entry.title: Adding Voice Cloning to Text-to-Audio-Video Models with a Single Zero-Initialised Layer

author.name: Ivan Mikheev, Viacheslav Vasilev, Anna Dmitrienko, Alexey Letunovskiy, Ivan Kirillov, Kirill Chernyshev, Denis Dimitrov

entry.summary: Shows that a text-to-audio-video generation model can be converted into a voice-cloning model by adding a single zero-initialized linear layer to its audio backbone plus short fine-tuning, conditioning on a brief reference recording via prepended diffusion latents and a global speaker embedding. It is benchmarked against five text-to-speech cloning systems on 674 speaker-text pairs.

entry.title: Provenance, Not Behaviour: A Serialisation Artifact in Edge-IIoTset and a Leakage-Free Benchmark for Precision-Agriculture Intrusion Detection

author.name: Mostafa M. Galal

entry.summary: Demonstrates that near-perfect published intrusion-detection results on a widely used industrial IoT benchmark are largely an artifact: a placeholder string formatting difference between the normal and attack collection branches lets four categorical columns separate the classes with perfect accuracy, independent of any network behavior. The author proposes a leakage-free benchmark for precision-agriculture intrusion detection.

entry.title: The Null Token Knows: Reducing Message-Free Hallucination in ASR and NMT

author.name: Kirill Borodin, Vasiliy Kudryavtsev, Ivan Viakhirev, Grach Mkrtchian

entry.summary: Investigates whether the reserved end-of-sequence or null token in speech recognizers and translation models already carries a usable signal for abstaining when the input contains no recoverable message. The authors audit null-token scores and logit shifts across models including Whisper, finding a useful abstention signal that standard decoding fails to act on, with an inherent trade-off between suppressing fabrication and deleting valid content.

entry.title: An Investigation of the NeurIPS and ICML 2025 Position Tracks

author.name: Fan Yang, Wenkai Li, Jun Liu

entry.summary: Audits every publicly accessible submission to the NeurIPS and ICML 2025 Position Paper Tracks under a pre-specified rubric and compares the pattern to a reference class of historically agenda-shifting ML papers. Roughly three-quarters of audited submissions are reformist critique, leading to a recommendation that the tracks explicitly solicit direction-setting work alongside critique.

entry.title: If, Then, Otherwise: Diagnosing Conditional Branching in Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Seoyoung Lee, Neel P. Bhatt, Pranay Samineni, Cong Liu, S P Sharan, Timothy Barclay, Gregory M. Wagner, Daniel Milan, Sandeep Chinchali, Ufuk Topcu, Atlas Wang

entry.summary: CondVLN is a scene-graph-grounded benchmark that tests whether vision-language navigation agents can handle conditional instructions of the form if-condition-then-path-otherwise-other-path. It disentangles failures into perception, grounding, navigation and logical decision errors, which existing route-following benchmarks conflate.

entry.title: BrainNorm: A Foundation Model that knows Normal via Semantic Atlas Pretraining

author.name: Madhumitha Venkatesh, Shanawaj S Madarkar, Konda Reddy Mopuri

entry.summary: BrainNorm is a normative brain MRI foundation model trained with language-image contrastive pretraining on roughly 66,000 healthy structural scans, producing an atlas-parcel latent space with age-conditioned healthy trajectories. Deviation from these trajectories supports brain-age gap estimation and multi-disease classification across six external cohorts.

entry.title: Differentiable Voronoi Ray Tracing Beyond Rasterization Speeds

author.name: Bernardo Taveira, Carl Lindstr\"om, Joakim Johnander, Fredrik Kahl

entry.summary: VoroTracing analyzes what actually limits throughput in differentiable Voronoi ray tracing (traversal length, per-cell work, memory locality) and co-designs representation, optimization and GPU execution to reach speeds competitive with or exceeding rasterization. Ray-based rendering natively supports distortion, rolling shutter and depth-of-field effects that rasterizers need special extensions for.

entry.title: VLCP: Vision Language Control Policy Closed-Loop Code Replanning for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Dhia Naouali, Minghan Wu, Claudia Wong, Abhinav Puthran, Omar G. Younis

entry.summary: VLCP keeps a frontier vision-language model frozen and has it write a short Python control function as the robot policy, with no demonstrations or fine-tuning. Unlike prior closed-loop schemes that retry a fixed policy or switch subtasks, it periodically re-observes multi-view images and proprioception and rewrites the failing control code within the same episode. This targets code-level rather than action-level failure recovery for manipulation.

entry.title: Toward the Optimal Regret-Instability Trade-off in Multi-Armed Bandits

author.name: Kaifei Wang, Yinyu Ye, Han Zhong

entry.summary: This paper formalizes a trade-off in multi-armed bandits between worst-case regret and instability, defined as the largest standard deviation of a terminal arm pull count across runs, proving a finite-time lower bound on their product without the regularity assumptions of prior asymptotic work. It also introduces a tunable algorithm combining a running lower-envelope index with a decreasing pull schedule to navigate the trade-off. Reproducibility of allocations, not just average regret, is increasingly relevant for deployed adaptive experiments.

entry.title: Minimax Optimal Estimator and Improved Error Rate for the MLE in Logistic Regression with Gaussian Design

author.name: Junren Chen, Arya Mazumdar

entry.summary: The authors give the first minimax optimal estimator for the parameter vector in logistic regression with Gaussian design and improve the best known finite-sample error rate for the maximum likelihood estimator, both flowing from a minimax optimal estimator for the parameter norm. They establish a matching lower bound for norm estimation. This sharpens the theory of a workhorse statistical model in the high-signal regime.

entry.title: FedPref: Federated Preference Learning for Structured Radiology Report Extraction

author.name: Flint Xiaofeng Fan, Cheston Tan, Yew-Soon Ong, Roger Wattenhofer

entry.summary: FedPref lets hospitals train small Qwen3-8B adapters for structured radiology extraction by having frozen public models propose candidate JSON outputs that local annotators rank, sharing only model updates rather than patient data. A heterogeneous teacher pool prevents candidate collapse when one model repeats itself.

entry.title: Towards Better Agents for Multi-Turn User Interaction: The Next User Turn Is More Than Context

author.name: Yiwen Zhao, Zhihao Wen, Yuchen Mao, Mingxuan Jiang, Yihao Hu, Pan Wang, Xin Zhang, Wei Wu

entry.summary: FACA extracts credit signals from the next user turn, treating user reactions as noisy local evidence about the preceding agent segment, and adds a locally normalized reaction advantage to the terminal outcome advantage without needing a critic or extra rollouts. It targets the flat-credit problem in interactive GRPO for tool-using dialogue agents.

entry.title: GraphWake: Group Polarization via Memory-Mediated Polarization Cascade in LLM-Agent Communities

author.name: Haoran Bu, Zejian Chen, Litian Zhang, Xi Zhang

entry.summary: Defines a new attack on agent social platforms where an adversary exposes a few agents to stance-reinforcing arguments that persist in their memory and then propagate through public discussion, producing group polarization. Uses memory as the persistence channel and normal discourse as the propagation channel, avoiding prompt tampering or fake echo chambers.

entry.title: Auditing Self-Evolution in Financial Agents: Capability Gains, Security Drift, and Execution-Interface Mismatch

author.name: Jialong Li, Jialing Zhu

entry.summary: Audits three self-evolving agent memory and skill methods in a simulated e-banking environment, finding that benign utility rises while exposure to injected content and unauthorized financial state changes rise faster. Reports that overall attack success increases even when conditional success after exposure falls slightly.

entry.title: Position: Fairness Failure in Generative Models is an Evaluation Problem

author.name: Mariia Vladimirova, Jean-Yves Franceschi, Thibaut Issenhuth

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that persistent fairness failures in generative models are fundamentally caused by non-comparable, non-actionable evaluation practice rather than only by data or modeling choices. It catalogs recurring empirical and conceptual failure modes and proposes Fairness Cards as a minimal standardized reporting artifact for deployment decisions. Aimed at shifting the field from ad-hoc bias probes to reproducible measurement.

entry.title: Foundation Agents Meet Agentic Deep Research: Evidence-Grounded Clinical Code Forecasting

author.name: Junda Wang, Meysam Ghaffari, Akshat Choube, Mohsen Sharifi Renani, Hong Yu, Carlos Morato

entry.summary: ICD-Deepresearch composes structured EHR foundation models with language models, medical search, and ICD dictionaries in a deep-research style agentic workflow to forecast which diagnosis codes will appear at a patient's next encounter. The design compensates for the fact that no single source reveals the future code set by evaluating candidate transitions against linked clinical evidence. It shows agentic research loops applied to prospective clinical prediction.

entry.title: Encoded but Not Actionable: Auditing the Decode-Generate-Steer Gap in Frozen LLMs for Geometric Constraints

author.name: Man Liang, Xinzhao Cheng, Faizan Wajid

entry.summary: The authors probe six frozen decoder-only LLMs on parametric CAD geometry to separate what is linearly decodable from what actually drives generation and can be steered. They find pretraining improves decoding of local pairwise geometric relations while sketch-level constraint status remains weakly actionable, exposing a gap between encoded and usable knowledge.

entry.title: Policy-Invariant Reward Shaping from LLM Feedback: A Framework for Hybrid RL Agents

author.name: Christophe D. Hounwanou, John Emeka Eze, Ya\'e U. Gaba

entry.summary: The paper formalizes hybrid LLM-planner plus RL-controller systems as goal-augmented MDPs and proves that using a bounded LLM progress score as a potential function preserves the set of optimal policies even when the LLM scores are wrong. A small MDP experiment includes an adversarial potential scaled twenty times the base reward.

entry.title: One Score, Two Decisions: Selective Prediction on the Rare-Disease Tail

author.name: Zhaoyang Jiang, Zhizhong Fu, Yunsoo Kim, Zicheng Li, Xuanqi Peng, Fei Teng, Jiacong Mi, Honghan Wu

entry.summary: This paper shows that for rare-disease diagnosis, selective prediction over ranked outputs is bounded by ranking quality first: eight small open-weight LLMs reach at most 4.6 percent top-1 recall on ultra-rare diseases, so even perfect confidence ordering cannot reach 50 percent selective accuracy at 10 percent coverage. It argues for feasibility checks before deploying abstention thresholds.

entry.title: Generative Learning of Separatrices

author.name: Ellis R. Crabtree, Dimitris G. Giovanis, Anastasia Georgiou, George Datseris, Ioannis G. Kevrekidis

entry.summary: This work uses generative models to sample and reconstruct separatrices, the boundaries between basins of attraction in multistable dynamical systems, which are rarely visited by direct simulation. The method aims to work in higher dimensions and without requiring explicit knowledge of the governing equations.

entry.title: Lipschitz Bandits with Arbitrary Feedback Delays

author.name: Yuhao Liu, Yu Chen, Longbo Huang

entry.summary: Extends Lipschitz bandits over continuous action spaces to settings where reward feedback arrives after arbitrary delays, giving elimination-based and EXP3-based algorithms for stochastic and adversarial rewards. Regret bounds scale with a zooming dimension plus a square-root total-delay term.

entry.title: EMASAM: a Computationally Efficient Sharpness-Aware Minimization via EMA-Guided Perturbations

author.name: Tanapat Ratchatorn, Masayuki Tanaka

entry.summary: EMASAM removes the extra gradient computation that makes sharpness-aware minimization twice as expensive by defining the perturbation direction from the gap between current weights and their exponential moving average. This preserves much of the generalization benefit while approaching standard training cost.

entry.title: Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study

author.name: Fanqi Wang, Weisheng Tang, Hairong Qi

entry.summary: Studies how predictable short-horizon parameter updates are during training, using displacement, subspace-residual, and predictor-based probes with null-calibrated readouts on vision training and public Pythia pretraining checkpoints. It finds that normalization parameters and biases behave very differently from weight matrices in terms of temporal redundancy.

entry.title: SubZero+: Efficient Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-Tuning via Large Learning Rates

author.name: Ziming Yu, Shuyao Xiao, Xingyu Zhao, Sike Wang, Pan Zhou, Peiyu Zang, Xiangda Yan, Yongjie Yang, Jia Li

entry.summary: SubZero+ stabilizes zeroth-order fine-tuning of LLMs by combining multi-query gradient estimation inside layer-specific low-rank subspaces, a subspace Adam optimizer using in-subspace statistics, and a sign correction ensuring properly distributed random projections. This reduces the estimator variance that makes backprop-free tuning learning-rate sensitive.

entry.title: Second-Moment Memory in Coordinatewise Adam

author.name: Jeonseong Kim

entry.summary: Analyzes the optimization cost of Adam's exponential moving average of squared gradients, showing that long second-moment memory can suppress progress even with finite-variance gradients. It derives a directional bound scaling with the inverse square root of memory length and converts it into an average-stationarity lower bound on a smooth convex problem.

entry.title: Layers Matter: Why Continual Learning Regularization Should Be Layer-Adaptive

author.name: Brian B. Moser, Ahmed Anwar, Tobias Christian Nauen, Shishir Muralidhara, Federico Raue, Ren\'e Schuster, Stanislav Frolov, Andreas Dengel

entry.summary: Argues that continual learning regularizers like elastic weight consolidation should be layer-adaptive because diagonal Fisher importance misses the top-eigenvalue curvature that actually controls forgetting, and layer sensitivity spans orders of magnitude. Under a block-diagonal Hessian assumption the authors prove forgetting decomposes into per-layer terms weighted by each layer's top Hessian eigenvalue.

entry.title: Information Geometry of Message Passing

author.name: Mykola Lukashchuk, Kyrylo Yemets, Alex Ledbetter, \.{I}smail \c{S}en\"oz

entry.summary: The paper shows that the stationary condition of natural-gradient variational inference can be written as an edge-local rule on Forney-style factor graphs, where each edge parameter equals a sum of two projected belief-propagation messages. This yields natural-gradient message passing, allowing each edge to carry its own exponential family while remaining a local computation. It bridges information geometry and probabilistic graphical model inference in a way that could simplify hybrid inference engines.

entry.title: How Many Samples Are Needed to Determine Causal Direction? Sharp Minimax Bounds for Bivariate LiNGAM

author.name: Jikai Jin

entry.summary: Derives sharp minimax sample-complexity bounds for determining causal direction between two linearly related variables, quantifying how difficulty scales with the strength of the structural coefficient and the distance of the noise from Gaussianity. This puts precise numbers on when classical non-Gaussian identifiability becomes statistically hopeless.

entry.title: LaGSplat: Inferring Physics-Governed Interactive Simulation from Monocular Video Using Latent Lagrangian Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Louen Pottier

entry.summary: Infers interactive, physics-governed object dynamics from one or a few monocular videos by making a single low-dimensional latent state serve simultaneously as the generalized coordinate of a learned dissipative Lagrangian and as the conditioning variable of a Gaussian Splatting decoder. Because the splat primitives move with the object, user-applied forces in image space can be pulled back into the latent dynamics at inference, even though no forces were ever observed during training.

entry.title: Architecture-Dependent Causal Transfer of Activation States Across Large Language Models

author.name: Fernando Cardenas Piepereit

entry.summary: Tests whether internal activation states can be transferred causally between architecturally different open-weight LLMs via a learned projection, evaluated at three levels: representational similarity, cross-model retrieval from projected states, and end-to-end effects of injecting projected activations during generation. Alignment beats a random-initialization baseline and is best measured by rank-based metrics, but causal transfer turns out to depend heavily on architecture.

entry.title: Offline Reinforcement Learning for Hemodynamic Management of Sepsis in the ICU: a MIMIC-IV Study with Dual Off-Policy Evaluation

author.name: Marc P\'erez-Roig, David Fern\'andez-Narro, Carlos S\'aez

entry.summary: Learns offline RL policies for fluid and vasopressor dosing in sepsis from nearly 37,000 ICU stays, but centers the contribution on trustworthy evaluation: two complementary off-policy estimators plus reliability diagnostics and clinician-agreement analysis. The framing acknowledges that off-policy value estimates for clinical policies are often fragile and optimistic.

entry.title: MIRROR: Multimodal Intelligent Radiology Reasoning and Observation Reporter

author.name: Vignesh Nagarajan, Sriram Venkatapathy

entry.summary: MIRROR is a radiology reporting prototype that deliberately blinds the language layer to the image: a multi-label classifier plus Grad-CAM localizer produce labels, probabilities, and anatomical regions, and only those structured outputs feed the report writer. Because the text generator never sees pixels, it structurally cannot assert findings the classifier did not produce, making report findings auditable against the probability vector.

entry.title: Q-Interference: Memory-Efficient Phase-Aware Quantum-Inspired Attention

author.name: Emama Nahid, Tahmid Imtiaz Imu, Huayue Gu, Liran Ma, Zhipeng Cai, Honghui Xu

entry.summary: Q-Interference augments each query and key feature with an amplitude and a learned phase so attention scores can be constructive or destructive rather than only measuring similarity, in a fully classical quantum-inspired formulation. The paper addresses the memory blowup of the naive token-pair-feature interaction tensor to keep the mechanism practical for autoregressive language modeling.

entry.title: LIBERO-VIFO: Benchmarking the Capability and Safety of Visual Cue Following in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Zhengyan Qian, Rui Yan, Alex Jinpeng Wang, Jinhui Tang

entry.summary: LIBERO-VIFO benchmarks whether vision-language-action models follow authorized visual cues while ignoring unauthorized ones, defining eight cue families and four protocols that separate cue understanding from execution. Treating unauthorized cue following as a safety failure surfaces a visual prompt-injection style attack surface for robot policies. It moves evaluation beyond coarse task success.

entry.title: Runtime Governance for Agentic AI: Action-Boundary Control with Trusted Provenance and Fail-Closed Execution

author.name: Adam Mazzocchetti

entry.summary: Proposes Aegis, a runtime layer that treats agent tool calls as proposals judged by a trusted policy engine with server-side provenance, fail-closed defaults, and quorum-based authorization for high-risk actions. It reframes agent safety from text filtering to enforcing an execution boundary around side effects.

entry.title: A decodability criterion predicts when hidden-state selection beats majority voting in large language models

author.name: Zhixiang wang, Ziliang Hong, Ulas Bagci

entry.summary: Introduces CASE, a linear gate on answer-token hidden states that picks among sampled candidate answers, along with a decodability criterion predicting when this beats majority voting. The key insight is that voting fails precisely when sampled errors are correlated, and hidden-state probes can be trusted only under measurable conditions.

entry.title: Do LLMs Know a Good Hypothesis When They See One? Logit-Based Energy Scoring Outperforms Prompted LLM-as-Judge for Scientific Hypothesis Ranking

author.name: Swati Rajwal, Sanjay Das, Tirthankar Ghosal

entry.summary: Compares prompted LLM-as-judge ranking against a logit-based energy score derived from the model's intrinsic confidence for identifying the correct scientific hypothesis among distractors, across 1,323 papers in 12 disciplines. Intrinsic scoring roughly doubled top-1 hit rate over listwise prompting.

entry.title: Neuro-symbolic learning over OWL 2 DL via consequence-based compilation to differentiable circuits

author.name: Olga Mashkova, Asaad Mohammedsaleh, Fernando Zhapa-Camacho, Robert Hoehndorf

entry.summary: Baobab compiles a full SROIQ description-logic ontology with a finite ABox into a sentential decision diagram, saturating a propositional core and instantiating nominals, number restrictions, and role axioms over the active domain. This lets neurosymbolic learning preserve classical entailment beyond the usual restriction to the Horn EL fragment.

entry.title: Adaptive Policy Portfolios for Robust Markov Decision Processes

author.name: Kasper Engelen, Sebastian Junges, Guillermo A. P\'{e}rez, Marnix Suilen

entry.summary: Studies portfolios of memoryless randomized policies synthesized offline for robust MDPs, paired with a lightweight online selector that adapts once deployment reveals which environment is actual. Uses robust regret as the quality objective and provides complexity results relative to prior safe policy improvement work.

entry.title: Procedural Content Metageneration via Program Search and Continual Abstraction Discovery

author.name: Matthew Siper, Ahmed Khalifa, Julian Togelius

entry.summary: Evolves complete Python level generators for four games using LLM-driven mutation and crossover, and introduces continual abstraction discovery that extracts reusable primitives from high-fitness programs into a run-specific helper library. A 2x2 design with 160 runs shows the abstraction mechanism improves final best fitness in all eight comparisons.

entry.title: Authorization Before Context: A Model-Neutral Audience Boundary Against Cross-Audience Memory Leakage in Agentic Systems

author.name: Sibo Liu

entry.summary: The paper proposes enforcing an audience-membership check at the moment memories are assembled into an agent's prompt, so a fact learned in one social context cannot leak into a reply to a different audience. Each stored item carries the audience present at recording time, the current viewer set is read from channel metadata with a conservative public fallback, and admission requires an anti-monotone subset condition. It formalizes contextual integrity for personal agent memory in a model-agnostic way.

entry.title: Learning Where and What to Lift for Bi-planar X-ray-to-CT Reconstruction

author.name: Yifei Wu, Yicheng Wu, Qiang Ma, Qi Chen, Renyang Gu, Xinyu Liu, Yongsheng Pan, Yong Xia

entry.summary: LiftXR reconstructs CT volumes from only two X-ray views by interleaving explicit recovery of anatomical spatial layout with intensity estimation, on the premise that once regions are localized, predicting their attenuation values becomes far easier. It targets the severe ill-posedness of collapsing depth in sparse-view projection. Potentially reduces radiation dose and imaging cost.

entry.title: Beyond MSE: Rethinking the Evaluation Metric and Benchmarking for Irregular Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Rongwen Li, Haixin Xie, Xiao Wang, Changjian Chen

entry.summary: A companion evaluation paper showing that mean squared error in irregular time series forecasting is confounded by each sample's timestamp sampling distribution, producing biased rankings of models. The authors propose Continuous-time Squared Error, which uses importance weighting to remove that dependence, and prove bounds on its asymptotic estimation error relative to true continuous-time performance. It argues much prior benchmarking in this area is unreliable.

entry.title: SemComp-Bench: Benchmarking Semantic Task Completion in Video Generation

author.name: Keyu Tu, Zhuowei Chen, Mengqi Huang, Yuxin Wang, Jiahao Zhu, Zhendong Mao, Yongdong Zhang

entry.summary: SemComp-Bench defines an outcome-oriented video generation task where success requires achieving an intended end state and maintaining high-level semantic correspondence to a reference image, rather than showing complete intermediate steps or preserving appearance. It ships an evaluation dataset spanning six domains with reference images plus detailed and brief instructions. It shifts video generation evaluation toward task completion semantics.

entry.title: Coarse-to-Fine Multi-Resolution Diffusion Models for Trajectory Generation in Urban Systems

author.name: Wen Ye, Muyan Weng, Chuizheng Meng, Hao Niu, Yizhou Zhang, Yan Liu

entry.summary: MR-Traj generates synthetic human mobility trajectories with a multi-resolution diffusion model that composes coarse and fine spatial-temporal structure instead of only matching global distributions. The goal is privacy-preserving trajectory data whose utility holds up across resolutions used in real urban analyses.

entry.title: Metaplasticity as adaptive gradient preconditioning for incremental learning

author.name: Isabelle Aguilar, Zayn Andre Zainal, Omid Kavehei

entry.summary: SynGAP reinterprets synaptic metaplasticity as adaptive gradient preconditioning to give task-free continual learning without task labels or large replay buffers. It targets the stability-plasticity tradeoff in non-stationary streams with a biologically motivated optimizer-level mechanism.

entry.title: Randomly initialized autoencoders: fixed points and edge-of-chaos

author.name: Leonid Berlyand, Roman Sarapin, Yitzchak Shmalo, Victor Slavin, Sasha Sodin

entry.summary: This mathematical study characterizes autoencoders through their fixed points, analyzing existence, stability, and basins of attraction via contractivity, and links these properties to the edge-of-chaos initialization regime. It offers a dynamical-systems account of when randomly initialized autoencoders behave well.

entry.title: Training and Evaluating Ethical Reinforcement Learning Agents on Per-Episode Distributions

author.name: Prabhjyot Singh, Majid Ghasemi, Mark Crowley

entry.summary: The paper compares four ways to train ethically constrained RL agents in the Craftax survival benchmark, arguing that averaging rewards lets agents concentrate harm in a few episodes. It evaluates scalar penalties, multi-objective weight sweeps, adaptive Lagrangian constraints, and a non-compensatory per-episode utility under expected scalarized returns.

entry.title: Discrete Diffusion Language Models Are Training-Free Multi-Label Classifiers

author.name: Pawan Kumar

entry.summary: The paper uses masked discrete diffusion language models as training-free multi-label text classifiers by scoring yes-or-no questions at a single masked position, one label at a time. It documents a severe slot-position bias when all labels share one prompt and shows per-label scoring removes the asymmetry.

entry.title: Do Uncertainty Signals Help? A Systematic Study of Uncertainty-Aware Decoding with Rollback Mechanisms

author.name: Xianzong Wu, Xiaohong Li, Yuejun Guo, Xinyang Liu, Tianlin Li, Junjie Wang, Qiang Hu

entry.summary: The paper systematically studies uncertainty-aware rollback decoding for code generation, where uncertainty signals flag unreliable spans and generation restarts from an earlier valid prefix without retraining. It asks empirically how much value uncertainty signals actually add at inference time.

entry.title: Quantifying Depth Sufficiency in Residual Neural Networks: A First-Order Criterion

author.name: Zeyu Liu, Jinhao Zhang, Yunquan Zhang, Guangming Tan, Xiang Gao, Fangming Liu, Daning Cheng

entry.summary: This paper defines first-order residual depth saturation under a function-preserving residual-growth protocol and proves that adding depth has first-order value exactly when conditional activation gradients project nonzero onto some admissible residual tangent space. It gives a checkable criterion for whether a trained network is already deep enough.

entry.title: Does 1/2-Tsallis-INF Also Work Well for Best-Arm Identification?

author.name: Jingxin Zhan, Yuze Han, Zhihua Zhang

entry.summary: Analyzes whether the canonical best-of-both-worlds Tsallis-INF regret-minimization algorithm can also reliably identify the best arm, by bounding its failure probability when the empirical best arm is chosen from importance-weighted loss estimates. It probes the tension between regret minimization and pure exploration objectives.

entry.title: High-Dimensional Nonparametric Change-Point Detection via Low-Rank Degree-Three Density Projection

author.name: Guoqing Zhang, Zhaixin Chen

entry.summary: Proposes a nonparametric change-point detection method for high-dimensional data that captures shifts in third-order structure such as skewness and asymmetric interactions, which mean and covariance monitoring miss. It uses a symmetric order-three Legendre feature tensor that isometrically encodes the degree-three density projection while avoiding density estimation.

entry.title: UniFed-VLM: Federated Instruction Tuning for Vision-Language Models with Multiple Heterogeneity

author.name: Pengyu Wang, Baochen Xiong, Xiaoshan Yang, Yifan Xu, Zhang Qimeng, Haifeng Chen, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: UniFed-VLM tackles federated instruction tuning of vision-language models when clients differ simultaneously in tasks, modalities, and model architectures, a setting existing federated methods do not handle. It targets privacy-sensitive domains such as healthcare where centralizing multimodal data is not feasible.

entry.title: Guaranteed Adaptive Modality Acquisition: When the Policy Chooses Its Own Calibration Group

author.name: Melika Baghi

entry.summary: Analyzes conditional calibration when an adaptive policy decides which input modalities are ultimately acquired, so the grouping used for conditional guarantees is itself chosen by the policy rather than fixed in advance.
