author.name: Ahmed Nebli, Hadi Saadatdoorabi, Christopher Keibel, Kevin Yam

entry.summary: The paper changes the substrate of sequence models rather than the backbone, replacing real-valued hidden states and affine-softmax readouts with complex phase states and quadratic Born-rule scores. It reports that this quantum-inspired representation reduces the number of optimization steps needed.

entry.title: Do Geometry-Aware Positional Encodings Help Transformers in Spatial Imperfect-Information Games?

author.name: Wenji Fu

entry.summary: A careful four-level benchmark study asking whether geometry-aware positional encodings help Transformers track hidden entities in a hexagonal naval pursuit game, comparing against exact Bayesian belief targets and legacy opponents. Hex-aware rotary encodings reduce belief cross-entropy and improve imitation, with bootstrap confidence intervals reported.

entry.title: Beyond Field Accuracy: Two-Axis Diagnosis of Inverse-PINN Parameter Error

author.name: Yifan Zhang, Qian Tao

entry.summary: Shows that inverse physics-informed neural networks can reconstruct fields accurately while still returning wrong physical parameters, and proposes a two-axis post-training diagnostic separating finite-sample resolution from the signed parameter preference encoded by the learned residual landscape. Endpoint consistency checks test whether joint training actually delivers that preference.

entry.title: Breaking the Compression Barrier: Cross-Architecture Compression Boundary Learning via Reverse Regrowth

author.name: Zhaocen Liu, Satvik Praveen, Yi Sheng

entry.summary: BRIDGE reframes model compression as a boundary search: it first over-prunes a network into the collapse regime and then selectively regrows critical structure to recover accuracy, using a hierarchical regeneration strategy. The goal is to locate the true feasible compression limit rather than stopping at a conservative sparsity level.

entry.title: Efficient Coreset Selection via K-Nearest Neighbor Graphs

author.name: Yingfan Liu, Leiyu Zhang, Jiadong Xie, Mingzhe Wang, Jeffrey Xu Yu, Jiangtao Cui

entry.summary: KNNG-CS selects training coresets using a k-nearest-neighbor graph to estimate per-item importance from local neighborhood structure, avoiding the quadratic distance matrices or large item-cluster bound matrices required by gradient-approximation methods like CRAIG. It requires only linear storage and greedily picks representative nodes.

entry.title: Task-Anchored Representation Shaping for Pre-Trained Model-Based Continual Learning

author.name: Zhiming Xu, Huiyu Yi, Zhen-Hao Xie, Baile Xu, Furao Shen, Jian Zhao, Suorong Yang

entry.summary: TAILS is a lightweight module added on top of pre-trained-model-based continual learners that uses fixed task anchors as persistent references, reshaping latent representations so that inputs from unknown tasks can be resolved at inference time. It targets cross-task prediction, argued to be the main bottleneck once strong pre-trained features are available.

entry.title: Beyond $L_2$: Generalizing Abductive Latent Explanations to Diverse Prototype-Based Architectures

author.name: Jules Soria, Alban Grastien, Romain Xu-Darme, Julien Girard-Satabin, Zakaria Chihani, Daniela Cancila

entry.summary: This paper generalizes Abductive Latent Explanations, which give formally guaranteed explanations for prototype-based networks, beyond Euclidean latent spaces to spherical metrics, Gaussian densities, and dimensional projections. The extension is needed because modern interpretable-by-design architectures increasingly use non-Euclidean representations that current formal methods cannot handle.

entry.title: Cross-Modal Ultrasound-MRI Learning for Fetal Brain Ventricular Volumetry and Abnormality Screening

author.name: Yuhao Huang, Yuanji Zhang, Yuhuan Lu, Dong Ni, P. Ellen Grant, Davood Karimi

entry.summary: VIFBA learns from fetal brain ultrasound video to predict MRI-derived lateral ventricular volume, grade ventriculomegaly severity and flag other brain abnormalities, using a joint-embedding predictive objective over spatiotemporal tubes. It aims to transfer the reliability of volumetric MRI assessment into cheap, widely available ultrasound.

entry.title: A Unified Geometric Framework for Developmental Analysis of Spatial Transcriptomic Data

author.name: Mary Chriselda Antony Oliver, Kaitlyn Hohmeier, Tuyen Tran, Alejandra Castillo, Caroline Moosm\"uller, Shiying Li

entry.summary: The authors propose an optimal-transport-based geometric framework for spatial transcriptomics that aligns cell populations by the relational structure of gene expression networks rather than only distributions of cells in expression space, enabling reconstruction of developmental trajectories from destructive, unaligned snapshots. This targets the core measurement limitation of single-cell assays.

entry.title: Machine Learning Approaches to Decoding Topological Quantum Codes

author.name: Changwon Lee, Tak Hur, Jeongwoo Jae, Daniel K. Park

entry.summary: Reviews machine-learning approaches to decoding topological quantum error-correcting codes, framing decoding as a high-throughput spatiotemporal pattern-recognition problem over stabilizer measurements. It surveys accuracy, scalability, and real-time deployability constraints as code distances grow.

entry.title: Large Language Models as Implicit Sociological Models: Reconstructing Voting Behaviour from Sociodemographic Profiles

author.name: Roman Neruda, Martin Bako\v{s}, Josef \v{S}lerka, V\'it Tu\v{c}ek, Petra Vidnerov\'a, Gabriela Kadlecov\'a

entry.summary: Treats LLMs as implicit sociological models by conditioning them on synthetic demographic profiles, eliciting probabilistic turnout and party preference, and aggregating outputs into predicted election results. Validated on the 2021 Czech parliamentary election, the approach reportedly reproduces official outcomes with low mean error.

entry.title: Protein Structure Prediction: From Evolutionary Constraints to Generative Modeling

author.name: Wengan He, Yongsheng Luo, Lihong Jiang, Wenhui Xu, Yu Li

entry.summary: Reviews the methodological evolution of protein structure prediction from multiple-sequence-alignment-driven monomer folding toward generative modeling of complexes and heterogeneous molecular systems. It organizes progress along representations and data, modeling paradigms, and evaluation rather than by model or application.

entry.title: LiD-GLM: Lipschitz-constrained Deep Generalized Linear Models

author.name: Tom Splittgerber, Niklas Koenen, Marvin N. Wright, Werner Brannath

entry.summary: Proposes hybrid statistical-neural models that attach invertible residual networks to generalized linear models, using their Lipschitz constraints to bound how much the neural component can distort the interpretable linear structure. This targets the usual dilemma where structural constraints kill flexibility while weak constraints kill interpretability.

entry.title: zLend: A Dual-Scope Cash-Flow Reconstruction Framework for On-Chain Credit Underwriting

author.name: Girish G N, Ashutosh Sahoo, Akshay SP, Gurukiran S, Dhanashekar Kandaswamy

entry.summary: zLend is a deployed underwriting framework for decentralized lending that reconstructs a wallet's daily balance history from raw token transfers, computed twice per wallet, once over a stablecoin basket and once over all fungible tokens, to separate liquid spendable balance from total holdings. From these series it derives liquidity coverage and cash-flow features that serve as repayment-capacity signals in the absence of any credit bureau.

entry.title: HODAgent: Towards On-Demand, Responsive Humanoids for Physical World Human Interaction

author.name: Wang Warren Chen, Jiahao Zhang, Zhenjiang Li, Mingxu Wang, Lei Yi, Yuchen Kang, Shuo Sun, Ziping Chen, Jie Chen

entry.summary: HODAgent is a System-2 agent architecture for service humanoids, with a semi-duplex design combining an environment interactor, planner, executor, and hierarchical memory so the robot can accept new requests mid-motion, revise plans, and verify outcomes. It reports about 85 to 92 percent joint success across 164 interactive simulation cases under two VLM backbones, with a shared interface to a Unitree G1. It emphasizes responsiveness and task revision rather than one-shot instruction following.

entry.title: OVIP-SG: Open-Vocabulary Instance-Preserving Scene Graphs for Mapping and Retrieval of Small, Fine-Grained Objects

author.name: Tianjing Hao, Haiyu Lan, Angsong Li, Cheng Chen, Enyu Li, Jiarui Yang, Yuning Su, Peiwen Lin, Wang Chuang

entry.summary: OVIP-SG builds open-vocabulary 3D scene graphs that preserve instance identity, countering the tendency of vision-language detectors to fragment large surfaces and absorb small objects into neighbors. It adds functional scene partitioning and language-guided retrieval of small fine-grained objects, including the ability to conclude a queried object is absent. This supports more reliable open-world embodied search and mapping.

entry.title: Effector-Centric NMPC of Tiltable-Multirotors for Offset-Free Omnidirectional Aerial Manipulation

author.name: Jinjie Li, Yicheng Chen, Johannes K\"ubel, Haokun Liu, Junichiro Sugihara, Moju Zhao

entry.summary: This work analyzes tiltable multirotor design and proposes an end-effector-centric nonlinear model predictive control framework for omnidirectional aerial manipulation with offset-free tracking. It argues that a four-rotor tiltable configuration balances propeller sizing against hovering efficiency and that null-space redundancy is essential for passing through singular tilt configurations. The combination of design analysis and wrench-based control is the contribution.

entry.title: Whack-a-mole with a broken hammer: does a model internally track its automaton state?

author.name: star2vec

entry.summary: The author trains linear probes to test whether a small Qwen model internally tracks its state in a login-protocol deterministic finite automaton that is never written in the transcript, finding around 88 percent state decoding and strong evidence the model tracks event order rather than just event presence. However, the model cannot reliably count to three, conflating two failed attempts with a locked state, and drifts toward the locked belief as filler turns accumulate. Split-half probe experiments separate model encoding errors from probe guessing.

entry.title: StagedWorkspace: A Versioned Workspace for Knowledge-Work Agents

author.name: Yining Hua, Hongbin Na, Yifan Zhou, Akshay Kalose, Cyrus Ayubcha, Levi Lian

entry.summary: Proposes a versioned workspace contract for knowledge-work agents so that parsed views, native files, reviewed diffs, and submitted artifacts always refer to the same version of an evolving document set. Extends to agents the version and diff guarantees that coding agents get from repositories, covering PDFs, spreadsheets, slides, and notebooks.

entry.title: Delegation Asymmetry in Agentic Recommender Systems: Measuring Two-Sided Receptivity in Online Dating

author.name: Daria Leshchikova, Valentina V. Kuskova, Dmitry Zaytsev, Valerii Klimov

entry.summary: Surveys roughly 5,500 active dating-platform users across two studies to measure whether people accept both delegating conversations to an agent and receiving agent-mediated messages from others. A graded response measurement model shows willingness to send and willingness to receive are distinct constructs, revealing a delegation asymmetry.

entry.title: Expected free energy as an information constraint on the Bethe Lagrangian

author.name: Wouter M. Kouw

entry.summary: The paper reformulates active inference's expected free energy as a Bethe free energy subject to an information constraint requiring mutual information between future observations, states, and parameters to exceed the goal prior's entropy, restoring compatibility with message passing. This preserves epistemic exploration drive while making inference tractable on factor graphs. It is a theoretical contribution to the active inference literature.

entry.title: Nonadaptive Learning in Robust Nonlinear Output Regulation

author.name: Shimin Wang, Martin Guay, Richard D. Braatz

entry.summary: A control-theory paper presenting a nonadaptive output-feedback regulator for general nonlinear systems of arbitrarily high relative degree, combining an input-driven filter, a generic internal model, and recursive backstepping to recast regulation as robust input-to-state stabilization. It avoids linear parameterization assumptions and awkward Lyapunov constructions used by adaptive schemes. Theoretical advance for robust nonlinear control.

entry.title: Multi-turn Conversational AI from Text to Multimodal Interaction: Data, Models, Evaluation, and Open Challenges

author.name: Syeda Faiza Ahmed, Zien Sheikh Ali, Hunzalah Hassan Bhatti, Firoj Alam, Shammur Absar Chowdhury

entry.summary: A broad review of multi-turn conversational AI spanning text dialogue, speech-native and audio LLMs, omni-modal systems, and tool-augmented agents, organized around datasets, modeling paradigms, training, and evaluation. It stresses under-addressed challenges such as memory maintenance, interruption handling, topic switching, and cross-lingual and cross-cultural adaptation. A reference map for a fast-moving area.

entry.title: Command-Space Counterfactual Explanations for Pareto-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Joanikij Chulev, Hendrik Baier

entry.summary: Introduces counterfactual explanations in the return-command space of Pareto Conditioned Networks: given a state and a desired alternative action, it searches for the smallest change to the requested return vector that would flip the policy. Adversarial-attack machinery is repurposed as a black-box explanation search for multi-objective RL.

entry.title: PERO: Efficient Robust Post-Training Foundation Models for Encrypted Traffic Classification

author.name: Wumei Du, Jiarong Wen, Kaiyu Zhang, Zi Yang, Yiqin Lv, Longfei Zhang, Dong Liang, Zheng Xie

entry.summary: PERO post-trains an encrypted-traffic foundation model to be robust to rare high-loss errors such as missed malicious flows, arguing that standard empirical risk minimization ignores tail events and that direct conditional value-at-risk optimization is too expensive at scale. It proposes an efficient approximation for risk-sensitive post-training.

entry.title: Amortised Post-Hoc Explanation with Exact Preservation for Dynamic Graph Anomaly Detectors

author.name: Iyad Assaad Nekka, Hamida Seba, Walid Khaled Hidouci, Karima Amrouche

entry.summary: X-StrGNN wraps a frozen structural GNN anomaly detector for dynamic graphs with a post-hoc explanation layer producing both structural attributions over contextual interactions and temporal attributions over historical snapshots. It addresses the fact that the strongest benchmark detector previously emitted only a score with no attribution.

entry.title: Learning Auditable Classifier Models: Source-Disjoint Tree Ensembles

author.name: Srikumar Krishnamoorthy

entry.summary: RPTE learns tree ensembles under bounded feature budgets and source disjointness so that every prediction can be audited compactly, separating structure discovery from coefficient estimation unlike sequential boosting. It targets clinical and regulated tabular settings where full auditability is required.

entry.title: KOALA: Koopman Operator Learning for WiFi-Based Anticipatory Hum

author.name: Quang-Anh N. D., Duc Pham Minh, Thao Phuong Pham, Minh Anh Nguyen, Huan X. Nguyen, Tuan Dang

entry.summary: KOALA predicts future human motion directly from WiFi channel state information by lifting noisy CSI-derived pose sequences into a Koopman latent space where dynamics are linear, enabling multi-horizon forecasts as matrix-vector products without autoregressive rollout. This avoids the error compounding that plagues naive vision-style predictors on noisy sensing data.

entry.title: Structured Prediction for Scalable Spreadsheet Table Understanding: From Cell Types to Table Ranges (Extended Version)

author.name: Antoine Gauquier, Ioana Manolescu, Pierre Senellart

entry.summary: Presents a two-stage pipeline for extracting structure from spreadsheets: a gradient-boosted classifier with a pairwise conditional random field assigns roles to cells, and a deterministic algorithm then derives table bounding boxes from the predicted cell types. The emphasis is efficiency and scalability across heterogeneous layouts and file formats.

entry.title: Degradation-Aligned Self-Supervised Learning for State of Health Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries under Label Sparsity

author.name: Jiaqi Yao, Julia Kowal

entry.summary: Proposes a self-supervised pretraining scheme for lithium-ion battery state-of-health estimation, using a cycle-order ranking pretext task on unlabeled cycling data with a CNN-GRU backbone before fine-tuning on sparse labels. The degradation-aligned objective is designed to encode monotonic aging structure so downstream estimation stays robust when labels are scarce.

entry.title: Learning latent progression states from spatial heterogeneity in uterine histopathology

author.name: Qiming He, Yan Liu, Shuang Ge, Fan Yang, Yuxiang Wang, Ieng Man Zhang, Jing Yang, Zihao Jia, Ajin Hu, Yexing Zhang, Zixiu Song, Qiang Huang, Xiaoya Zhao, Zihan Wang, Xianjing Zheng, Yijun Zheng, Liling Lin, Shuxing Liu, Bin Bao, Yue Xie, Tian Guan, Yonghong He, Congrong Liu

entry.summary: SpaTIE is a uterus-specific computational pathology framework trained on over ten thousand whole-slide images that learns morphology-aware representations and organizes spatial heterogeneity into progression-associated tumor states. It is validated on public TCGA cohorts for diagnostic, molecular and survival prediction tasks.

entry.title: Primitive-Driven Compositional Forensic Visual Prompting for Open-World Face Anti-Spoofing

author.name: Fangling Jiang, Qi Li, Bing Liu, Weining Wang, Quilin Huang, Zhenan Sun, Ming-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: This paper tackles open-world face anti-spoofing by learning compositional visual prompts built from recurring low-level forensic primitives, on the hypothesis that unseen attacks are new combinations of familiar cues. It operates purely in visual feature space rather than relying on language or category semantics.

entry.title: GeoWeaver: Accurate Long-Sequence 3D Reconstruction via Hierarchical Geometric Assembly

author.name: Tinghao Jiang, Sheng Tang, Shengzhe Wei, Juntong Fang, Weiqi Zhang, Junsheng Zhou, Zesong Li

entry.summary: GeoWeaver scales feed-forward 3D reconstruction to long video sequences by predicting chunk-wise depth, confidence and camera parameters as adjustable priors and then applying test-time adaptation with global similarity-transform alignment and coarse-to-fine pose refinement. This targets the scale drift and misalignment that plague chunked processing.

entry.title: NGS-Marker: Robust Native Watermarking for 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Hao Qin, Yukai Sun, Luyuan Chen, Mengxu Lu, Feng Zhang, Ming Kong, Zhenhong Du, Qiang Zhu

entry.summary: NGS-Marker embeds watermarks natively into 3D Gaussian primitives rather than only into rendered images, using a jointly trained injector and decoder with gradient-based progressive injection for full-scene coverage. This makes ownership verification robust even when an adversary extracts only a subset of Gaussians.

entry.title: Magnitude-Direction Decoupling for Fast Video Generation with Flow Matching Models

author.name: Haonan Xu, Feiyang Chen, Songkui Chen, Hongpeng Pan, Zhefeng Wang, Xinyu Duan, Baoxing Huai, Yang Yang

entry.summary: The authors observe that lightweight surrogate models reliably reproduce the magnitude of a flow-matching video model's denoising output while cached features give reliable direction, and combine the two adaptively to accelerate sampling. This decoupling avoids the trajectory drift caused by naive caching or distillation substitution.

entry.title: PerFact: Perception-Derived Fact Prompting for 3D Brain MRI Report Generation

author.name: Jianyu Sun, Zhenxuan Zhang, Guang Yang, Peter J. Lally

entry.summary: PerFact studies 3D multi-sequence brain MRI report generation and finds that backbone choice and scale barely matter, while chest-radiograph-pretrained medical VLMs transfer poorly. Instead, quality is driven by injecting facts derived from upstream 3D segmentation and classification into the prompt.

entry.title: LinCa: Accelerating Diffusion Models via Learnable Decomposed Feature Caching

author.name: Jinshan Liu, Haoran Qin, Xiaobing Tu, Jiacheng Liu, Jiahui Hu, Zhengan Yan, Yukun Xie, Kerui Shen, Jinkui Ren, Yuqi Lin, Xiantao Zhang, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: LinCa accelerates diffusion sampling by using a lightweight invertible network to decompose cached features into sub-components with different temporal continuity, then applying different reuse or prediction strategies to each. This adapts to heterogeneous feature dynamics where uniform training-free caching degrades quality at high speedups.

entry.title: GS-Voxel: Fitting-Free Structured Latents for Large-Scale 3DGS Generation

author.name: Ming Qian, Zijian Wang, Minchao Sun, Jincheng Xiong, Hang Zhang, Mu Xu, Chi Wang, Baoquan Chen

entry.summary: GS-Voxel converts pre-optimized Gaussian splatting reconstructions into sparse active voxels without per-scene fitting, then encodes geometry and Gaussian attributes with a factorized VAE into structured sparse latents for generative modeling. It is evaluated on large-scale aerial 3D scene generation.

entry.title: Memory Tree Guided Key Frame Querying for Efficient 3D Question Answering

author.name: Hsiang-Wei Huang, Fu-Chen Chen, Li-Wu Tsao, Cheng-Han Lee, Che-Chun Su, Lu Xia, Ronghui Peng, Jenq-Neng Hwang, Min Sun, Cheng-Hao Kuo

entry.summary: This work replaces expensive per-query visual search over thousands of video frames with a reusable compact 3D memory tree built online from camera poses, which guides key frame retrieval for embodied 3D question answering. The reusable structure amortizes cost across multiple user queries.

entry.title: Deep Academic Survey: Stateful Agentic Closed-Loop Paradigm for Academic Survey Automation

author.name: Zhikai Xu, Zhucun Xue, Teng Hu, Yabiao Wang, Yong Liu, Jiangning Zhang

entry.summary: DAS is a stateful agentic framework for automatically writing publication-oriented academic surveys, separating reusable paper analysis from topic-specific manuscript construction through a shared revisable state and a continuously updated paper corpus. It coordinates literature organization, evidence-grounded drafting and manuscript validation in a closed loop.

entry.title: 3D Gaussian Accelerated Ray Tracing: Fast training through particle-based backward propagation

author.name: Laurent Vit, Oliver Batchelor, Richard Green

entry.summary: 3DGART identifies that the training bottleneck in Gaussian ray tracing is pixel-centric backward propagation, where many threads atomically accumulate gradients into shared primitive parameters, and restructures backpropagation around particles to remove contention. This makes ray-traced Gaussian representations, which natively support reflections and refractions, cheaper to train.

entry.title: Automating Parent Selection Configuration in Genetic Programming with Agentic AI

author.name: Jose Guadalupe Hernandez, Jui-Hsuan Chang, Anil Kumar Saini, Xi Li, Jason H. Moore

entry.summary: This study tests whether LLM agents with reasoning and retrieval augmentation can automatically identify and implement parent selection algorithms for genetic programming, using symbolic regression as a testbed and ablating four different LLMs. Agentic components strongly shape the kinds of algorithms produced, but downstream performance depends heavily on the underlying model.

entry.title: EATR-Stereo: Embodiment-Aware Routing of Paired Stereo Evidence for Humanoid Vision-Language-Action Control

author.name: Songwei Wu, Rui Zhao, Fan Yang, Zhongqiang Nie, Zhiduo Jiang, Wandong Sun, Yuwei Li, Yang Liu, Hong Liu

entry.summary: EATR-Stereo proposes an embodiment-aware token-routing interface for humanoid vision-language-action control with head-mounted stereo cameras, keeping the primary-view token pathway intact while adding cross-view auxiliary tokens queried from the second view. A body-segmented proprioceptive encoder modulates how much auxiliary information each token uses. The goal is exploiting stereo evidence without breaking compatibility with pretrained visual representations.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Sliding-Window Particle Filtering for Tactile-Only In-Hand 6-DoF Object Pose Refinement

author.name: Lingjun Shao, Ying Zhang, Xiangfei Li, Xiangyang Li, Huan Zhao, Zhenyu Wang, Han Ding

entry.summary: This paper (tactile-only in-hand pose refinement) proposes a physics-informed particle filter on SE(3) that updates belief over a grasped object's 6-DoF pose from sparse whole-hand taxel readings, with a likelihood combining signed-distance contact consistency, force-normal alignment, friction-cone feasibility, and zero-force negative evidence. A sliding window over recent tactile frames mitigates partial observability and symmetry ambiguity. It targets manipulation where vision is occluded or unavailable.

entry.title: Policy career planning in the age of imminent superintelligence

author.name: Peter Wildeford

entry.summary: The author argues that conventional career planning assumes the field you train for will still exist in recognizable form, an assumption he thinks breaks down in an AI midgame where policy windows shift within months, and offers guidance for policy careers under short timelines. He cites rapidly changing discourse following recent high-profile AI security incidents. It is strategic career and governance commentary.

entry.title: Synthesizing Feature Extractors: An Agentic Approach for Algorithm Selection

author.name: Hai Xia, Carlos Ans\'otegui, Stefan Szeider

entry.summary: Uses an LLM in a check, fix, and verify loop to synthesize executable Python feature extractors for constraint satisfaction instances, producing interpretable structural features such as graph density and constraint tightness. Removes the manual expertise bottleneck in algorithm selection portfolios.

entry.title: LLM-Only PDDL Domain Repair with Open-Weight Models

author.name: Nader Karimi Bavandpour, Pascal Bercher

entry.summary: Tests whether recent open-weight LLMs can repair faulty PDDL planning domains directly from positive and negative test plans, without symbolic tooling. Reports that a symbolic baseline reaches an F1 around 0.49 while the strongest open-weight model performs comparably or better on the repair task.

entry.title: Structure-Internalized Rule Language Model for Faithful Knowledge Graph Reasoning

author.name: Xingrui Zhuo, Jiapu Wang, Manzong Huang, Gongqing Wu, Xindong Wu

entry.summary: Tackles the mismatch between knowledge-graph structural context and an LLM's parametric knowledge, which the authors call reasoning evidence perception drift, by internalizing rules over graph structure into the language model. Aims to make KG reasoning both more accurate and more faithful to graph constraints.

entry.title: ARASH: Adaptive Retrieval And Shot Selection for Tabular Prediction

author.name: Samirasadat Jamalidinan, Yue Xu, Kazem Cheshmi

entry.summary: ARASH selects query-specific example rows to serve as in-context shots for tabular foundation models, avoiding the expense of retraining or fine-tuning models like TabPFN. It combines adaptive retrieval with shot selection to improve efficiency and accuracy on tabular prediction.

entry.title: EvoTS-Agent: A Self-Evolving LLM Agent for Financial Time Series Change Point Detection

author.name: Lei Jiang, Ye Wei, Xinyu Xi, Jordan Langham-Lopez, Yifan Bao, Raad Khraishi, Yihao Ang, Anthony K. H. Tung, Lukasz Szpruch, Hao Ni

entry.summary: EvoTS-Agent is a validation-guided self-evolving LLM agent that performs exploratory analysis of financial time series, initializes candidate change-point detectors, and evolves executable experiment trajectories through several operators. It replaces expert-driven algorithm and hyperparameter selection for non-stationary financial data.

entry.title: Communicating Credit Risk with Large Language Models: Evaluation of Explanations from Standard and Alternative Data-Based Models

author.name: Sahab Zandi, Noah Kostesku, Christophe Mues, Mar\'ia \'Oskarsd\'ottir, Cristi\'an Bravo

entry.summary: Using Freddie Mac loan-level data, the authors test whether LLMs can translate technical post-hoc explanation artifacts from XGBoost with SHAP and from graph neural network credit models into stakeholder-appropriate narratives that support compliant lending decisions. They compare pipelines built on standard tabular data versus alternative network data. It probes the communication layer between explainability tooling and regulated decision-making.

entry.title: Too Sure to Be Safe: Model Calibration for Reliable Log Anomaly Detection

author.name: Bin Li, Dongdong Wang, Siyang Lu

entry.summary: The authors show that language-model based log anomaly detectors are badly overconfident on wrong predictions under class imbalance, even when standard calibration metrics look acceptable. Their LoRD method adds lightweight post-hoc calibration using reconstruction error and distance signals to close this reliability gap.

entry.title: Why GPT-Style Models Do Not Directly Transfer to Symbolic Music: Compression in the Wrong Coordinate System

author.name: Yi Wang

entry.summary: This position and analysis paper argues that transplanting GPT-style tokenization to symbolic music fails because the benefit comes from compression in a well-chosen coordinate system, not from reusable chunks like chords or motifs. It proposes an effectiveness-versus-losslessness framing for choosing musical representations.

entry.title: BDIP-Net: Dual-Interaction Graph Learning for Property Prediction of Bilayer Materials

author.name: An Vuong, Chen Zhao, Jin Hu, Shui-Qing Yu, Xintao Wu

entry.summary: BDIP-Net predicts properties of stacked bilayer materials with a dual-interaction graph model that explicitly distinguishes strong intra-layer bonding from weak inter-layer van der Waals coupling, paired with a MatterSim-based structure generation workflow. This avoids costly DFT relaxation for candidate screening.

entry.title: Efficient Neural-Network-Based High-Resolution Radiative Transfer for CO___ Retrieval, and Application to Interferometric Sensing

author.name: Jordan Lontsi Tedongmo (CB), Yann Ferrec (CB, IFUMI), Laurence Croiz\'e (CB, IFUMI), Pablo Mus\'e (CB, IFUMI), Gabriele Facciolo (CB), Andr\'es Almansa (MAP5 - UMR 8145, IFUMI)

entry.summary: The authors replace expensive line-by-line radiative transfer simulations with a neural surrogate to enable high-resolution CO2 and CH4 retrieval for a low-cost satellite interferometer constellation. Speedups make full-physics retrieval feasible at higher revisit rates and spatial coverage.

entry.title: pico-type: A 1.5M-Parameter Byte-Level Multi-Head Content Classifier

author.name: Gautam Kishore

entry.summary: pico-type is a roughly 1.5 million parameter byte-level model that predicts seven content properties at once, including coarse type, modality, code and text language, MIME type, and secret-leak risk flags, directly from raw UTF-8 with no tokenizer. It targets extremely cheap, single-pass content triage.

entry.title: An automatic-differentiation framework for time-lapse electrical resistivity tomography inversion of hydrologic dynamics

author.name: Pu Yang, Zhengyang Fang, Yuxin Liu, Xuan Su, Deshan Feng, Hang Chen

entry.summary: AD-TLERT builds a GPU-accelerated, automatic-differentiation framework for time-lapse electrical resistivity tomography inversion, chaining parameterization, differentiable petrophysics, forward modeling, misfit, and regularization. Alternative inversion formulations can be swapped without deriving new gradients by hand.

entry.title: Probability-Preserving Transformer for the Time-Dependent Schr\"odinger Equation

author.name: Mushtaq Ali, Muzamil Tariq, Niaz Ali Khan

entry.summary: Presents a Transformer for the time-dependent Schrodinger equation that enforces probability conservation as an architectural hard constraint rather than a soft penalty, guaranteeing unitary time evolution. The authors report both physical exactness and lower computational cost than soft-constraint baselines.

entry.title: SAGA: Structure-Attended Generative Action Embedding Model that encodes Multi-Surface User Action Sequences

author.name: Tsz Fung Pang, Po Jen Chen, Nimish Ronghe, Farhad Farahani, Bo Zhang

entry.summary: SAGA is an industrial generative embedding model that unifies user actions across payments, peer-to-peer transfers, in-app engagement, email, and account activity by tokenizing each event into product, interaction, and surface fields. Field-level attention and per-field objectives produce a single user representation for downstream recommendation.

entry.title: AsyTO: Asymmetric Temporal Operator for Parameter-Efficient Multivariate Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Xiachong Lin, Du Yin, Hao Xue, Wen Hu, Imran Razzak, Arian Prabowo, Matthew Amos, Flora D. Salim

entry.summary: AsyTO argues the shared-versus-independent predictor dilemma in multivariate forecasting dissolves if one compresses the forecasting operator instead of the series, pairing a phase-locked seasonal component with a compact residual operator. Audits of per-variable linear history-to-future maps motivate the asymmetric design and yield parameter efficiency.

entry.title: Beyond Peak Backlog: Conditional Energy and Temporal Geometry in Capacity-Constrained Delayed Bandit Optimization

author.name: Anling Xiang, Yuwen Yang, Yang Shen

entry.summary: The paper studies bandit convex optimization when the learner can only track a bounded number of pending delayed feedback items and discarded feedback is lost forever, replacing dependence on peak backlog with a conditional-energy quantity. The resulting untuned learner achieves a sharper delay term under a hard-capacity contract.

entry.title: Localized TabICLv2: Scaling Tabular In-Context Learning through k-NN

author.name: Beimnet Bekele Guta

entry.summary: Localized TabICLv2 cuts the inference cost of full-context tabular in-context learning by retrieving only the k nearest training rows for each test point in the model's own row-representation space, with no architectural changes. Additional stage-level tuning is used to recover accuracy lost from the reduced context.

entry.title: BRAID: Learning Equilibrium Maps in Interdependent Security Games via Weight-Tied Iterative Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Elnaz Nowrouzi, Zhiqun Zuo, Xueru Zhang, Mohammad Mahdi Khalili

entry.summary: BRAID amortizes Nash equilibrium computation in networked interdependent security games by training a weight-tied iterative graph neural network to map game parameters directly to equilibrium effort profiles, replacing hundreds of best-response iterations with one forward pass up to 43 times faster. The architecture is derived from the fixed-point structure of the games, with aggregation chosen to match best-response form.

entry.title: Interpretable Cross-Lingual Alignment in Small Language Models: Probing Cultural and Pragmatic Reasoning in Japanese-English Bilingual LLMs

author.name: Florian Braun

entry.summary: The author introduces a minimal-pair benchmark isolating Japanese pragmatic phenomena such as honorifics, in-group versus out-group reference, context-sensitive politeness and zero anaphora, then uses linear probes and teacher-forced log-probability scoring to locate where a 1.5 billion parameter bilingual model represents these distinctions. The motivation is that standard Japanese benchmarks conflate lexical, syntactic and pragmatic competence.

entry.title: Developing an Offshore Machine Learning Surface Layer Scheme

author.name: Susan Dettling, Sue Ellen Haupt, Thomas Brummet, Patrick Hawbecker, Branko Kosovi\'c, David John Gagne

entry.summary: Neural networks and random forests are trained to replace empirically fitted surface-layer flux parameterizations for offshore conditions, using observations from an air-sea interaction tower, a research platform and a shipborne deployment, with vertical measurement differences supplied as gradients. Separate models are built for momentum and heat flux and tested for cross-site transfer.

entry.title: A Deep Learning Model for Spatially Clustered Data via Differentiable Cluster Assignment

author.name: Kexuan Li, Weidong Ma

entry.summary: This paper proposes nonparametric regression where the covariate-response relationship changes across an unknown spatial partition, learning both the partition and cluster-specific networks jointly via an annealed softmax relaxation of discrete assignments with graph-Laplacian and occupancy penalties. Theoretical results cover identifiability up to label permutation and partition error bounds under a margin condition.

entry.title: Fast Test-Time Refinement for Robust Learned Image Compression

author.name: Jiaming Liang, Chi-Man Pun, Weisi Lin

entry.summary: The paper studies test-time refinement as an adversarial defense for learned image compression, providing theoretical grounding for why it helps, reducing its prohibitive iteration cost, and extending evaluation to white-box settings and attacks beyond bounded-norm rate and untargeted distortion objectives. The motivation is that neural codecs cannot be trusted as standards while remaining adversarially fragile.

entry.title: Beyond Effective Sample Size: Effective Number of Proposals for Adaptive Importance Sampling

author.name: Ali Mousavi, Victor Elvira

entry.summary: The authors argue that effective sample size only reflects how concentrated importance weights are and says nothing about how proposal components are spread over the target, so several proposals covering the same region can look healthy. They introduce an effective number of proposals diagnostic for population-based adaptive importance sampling to capture proposal diversity.

entry.title: Memory-Bounded Continuation of Greedy Sampling for Continual Anomaly Detection

author.name: Yoon Gyo Jung, Jaewoo Park, Kuan-Chuan Peng, Seongdeok Bang, Octavia Camps

entry.summary: For continual anomaly detection with a fixed memory budget, the authors show that repeatedly applying greedy coreset selection to previously selected sets preserves representativeness surprisingly well, with quality degrading gradually despite discarding data at each step. This gives a constant-size alternative to unbounded coreset accumulation as tasks arrive.

entry.title: Convolution Smoothed Quantile Regression for XGBoost

author.name: Mandy Yao (University of Toronto), Meredith Franklin (University of Toronto)

entry.summary: QXGB adds a convolution-smoothed quantile loss to gradient boosting so that conditional quantiles can be estimated densely enough to build cumulative distribution functions, exceedance probabilities and tail estimates rather than only point predictions. It keeps the computational efficiency of extreme gradient boosting while characterizing rare and extreme outcomes.

entry.title: PWLR: Pairwise Witness Local Rejection for Boundary-Aware Out-of-Distribution Detection

author.name: Chengyao Jia, Ruixuan Wang

entry.summary: Improves out-of-distribution detection near class boundaries by having a multimodal LLM generate, offline, textual descriptions of local visual cues that distinguish one in-distribution class from a specific rival class, then screening those cues for reliability using only in-distribution data. At inference the method shortlists plausible classes and applies the pairwise local verifiers as boundary evidence.

entry.title: Collective Ranking of Environmental Signals through Gaussian Belief Propagation in a Patrolling Robot Swarm

author.name: Zachary R. Madin, Connor York, Jonathan Lawry, Edmund R. Hunt

entry.summary: The authors observe that a multi-robot patrol graph doubles as a factor graph and apply Gaussian Belief Propagation over it so a swarm can collectively rank all patrol locations by a measured continuous signal while still minimizing idleness. This generalizes best-of-n collective decision making to many options with continuous values. The dual interpretation of the patrol topology is the conceptual contribution.

entry.title: Structured Driving-State Narratives for Small Language Model-Based GNSS Spoofing Detection

author.name: Abyad Enan, Sagar Dasgupta, Mizanur Rahman, Mashrur Chowdhury

entry.summary: The authors convert vehicle state estimates derived independently from GNSS and from other onboard sensing into structured natural-language narratives, then use a small language model to detect and classify GNSS spoofing attacks on autonomous vehicles. Performance is compared against fine-tuned larger LLMs on identical data. It demonstrates a text-serialization approach to sensor-consistency anomaly detection on constrained hardware.

entry.title: Delta2Gamma: Band-Wise Adaptive Contrastive Learning of EEG for Alzheimer's Disease Detection

author.name: Chanwoo Park, Chanwoo Kim

entry.summary: Delta2Gamma is a self-supervised contrastive framework that splits EEG into the five canonical frequency bands, gives each band its own encoder, projection head, and adaptively predicted contrastive temperature, then learns representations from unlabeled recordings for Alzheimer's screening. The band-wise temperature adaptation accounts for differing signal quality across rhythms. It targets low-cost dementia screening where labels are scarce.

entry.title: DMT-Dens: Density-preserving manifold visualization for biological data

author.name: Ruizhe Wang, Yixuan Dong, Bolin Yang, Bingo Wing-Kuen Ling, Fuji Yang, Zelin Zang

entry.summary: DMT-Dens is a parametric manifold visualization method using a latent-token transformer encoder that explicitly preserves the apparent sampling density of high-dimensional biological data, optimizing correlation between neighborhood log-radius estimates in the original and embedded spaces. It targets misleading density distortions in single-cell embeddings that obscure rare or transitional cell states. Improves interpretability of standard exploratory plots.

entry.title: A Unified Mamba--MoE Surrogate for Closed-Loop Simulation and Measurement-Window Forecasting of Inverter Transients

author.name: Haoguang Wang, Huy Hoang Le, Akhila Kandivalasa, Christian Moya, Marcos Netto, Guang Lin

entry.summary: Builds a single Mamba state-space backbone with mixture-of-experts routing that handles both closed-loop simulation and windowed forecasting of power-inverter transients, replacing two separate specialist models. An adaptive conformal layer supplies calibrated prediction intervals for both tasks.

entry.title: SAPE: Sandwich Adapters for Parameter Efficiency in Large Language Model Fine-Tuning

author.name: Mohammad Aref Jafari-Raddani, Morteza Mohajjel Kafshdooz

entry.summary: SAPE is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning scheme that shares adapter weights in a sandwich topology motivated by the hierarchical structure of Transformer layers, rather than sharing uniformly or using dynamic masks. The goal is faster convergence without the overhead of dynamic sharing strategies.

entry.title: QSMP: finding representative time series subsequences through Quick Shift+Matrix Profile

author.name: Carlos H. Mendoza-Cardenas, Rogers F. Silva, Austin J. Brockmeier

entry.summary: QSMP finds representative waveform patterns in long time series by connecting the Quick Shift mode-seeking algorithm to the Matrix Profile similarity structure, clustering subsequences with better space complexity than prior state of the art. It supports summarization, visualization, and downstream classification or forecasting.

entry.title: Learning Stock Trading Policies via Barycenter-Based Adversarial Inverse Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Arishi Orra, Himanshu Choudhary, Manoj Thakur

entry.summary: BRaG aggregates multiple heterogeneous expert trading strategies into a stable pseudo-expert using a performance-weighted Wasserstein barycenter, then pretrains a policy by adversarial imitation before reinforcement fine-tuning. The aim is to avoid unstable exploration under noisy delayed financial rewards.

entry.title: CrevasseSeg: A Label-Efficient UAV Crevasse Segmentation Framework

author.name: Steven Wallace, William D. Harcourt, Richard Hann, Aiden Durrant, Somayajulu Sripada, Georgios Leontidis

entry.summary: CrevasseSeg provides a labeled and unlabeled UAV dataset over a Svalbard glacier terminus plus a benchmark of five self-supervised objectives across three segmentation architectures for label-efficient crevasse mapping. It targets a domain where expert pixel annotation is prohibitively expensive.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Auxiliary Task Discovery for Stable Reinforcement Learning in Stock Trading

author.name: Arishi Orra, Himanshu Choudhary, Manoj Thakur

entry.summary: Proposes automatically discovering auxiliary prediction tasks, formulated as General Value Functions, to stabilize representation learning for reinforcement learning trading agents instead of hand-designing targets and horizons. The motivation is that fixed auxiliary designs stop being appropriate as market regimes shift.

entry.title: Operator-Theoretic Generalization Bounds for Multitask Deep Learning

author.name: Mahdi Mohammadigohari, Thomas Borsani, Giuseppe Di Fatta

entry.summary: The authors derive generalization bounds for deep multi-output networks by treating layers as Koopman composition operators on vector-valued reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces, separating task-coupling effects from layerwise operator norms. A second analysis covers a one-dimensional Brownian and Cameron-Martin regime with exact derivative-norm characterizations.

entry.title: When Uncertainty Isn't Enough: An Empirical Study of Self-Correction in Code Generation

author.name: Pranav Rakasi, Maanas Lalwani, Arnav Srivastava, Arya Palanivel, Tinuade Adeleke, Ruizhe Li, Sean Wu

entry.summary: An empirical study of whether natural-language uncertainty estimators transfer to code generation, comparing token entropy, verbalized confidence, probability-of-true, entropy ensembles and semantic entropy probes on HumanEval and BigCodeBench with small code models. Multi-sample probability-of-true correlates best with correctness while other signals are weak, and gating self-correction on uncertainty gives limited gains.

entry.title: FedPA-LoRA: Product-Aligned Framework for Mitigating Aggregation and Initialization Errors in Heterogeneous Federated LoRA

author.name: Juseok Jeon, Ramy E. Ali, Doyun Kwon, Myungbeom Her, Jinhwi Kim, Jinhyun So

entry.summary: Proposes a federated fine-tuning method for low-rank adapters that reconciles two competing strategies: averaging the low-rank factors directly versus reconstructing their product. The authors keep local factors persistent across rounds while aligning them to the aggregated product, with convergence proofs for both equal and unequal client ranks.

entry.title: Temporal Logic Guided Universal Task Representations for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Hao Zhang, Zhangli Zhou, Zhen Kan

entry.summary: Proposes a temporal-logic-inspired task representation module that can be plugged into any RL algorithm, avoiding reliance on gradient signals from the policy learner to shape the representation. The goal is task encodings that generalize across diverse task specifications rather than being tuned to one environment.

entry.title: Turning spectra into images improves plant trait retrieval with 2D-CNNs

author.name: Javier Lopatin, Teja Kattenborn, Eya Cherif, Sebasti\'an Moreno

entry.summary: Tests whether reshaping one-dimensional hyperspectral plant reflectance spectra into two-dimensional images helps CNNs predict plant functional traits, comparing nine transformations with EfficientNet-B0 on a nearly 8,000-spectrum benchmark. The simplest option, directly reshaping the spectrum into a grid, worked best and beat published 1D CNN baselines on the same split.

entry.title: From Entity Mentions to Tone: An LLM-Based Pipeline for Media Bias Analysis

author.name: Klesti Hoxha, Olti Qirici

entry.summary: Describes an LLM pipeline for media bias analysis that clusters articles into topics and events, annotates named entities and sentiment, and compares outlets by person mentions, tone, and coverage patterns. Applied to over 8,000 Albanian news articles, it shows moderate agreement with GDELT annotations and compares two prompt variants with different sentiment-validation strictness.

entry.title: Multi-Observer Vehicle Localization Case Study with Roadside Radar and Connected Vehicle Sensing

author.name: Aleksi Pippuri, Nilusha Jayawickrama, Risto Ojala

entry.summary: A real-world case study fusing object-level detections from a static roadside radar with those from a LiDAR-equipped connected vehicle to localize vehicles at an urban intersection, validated against an instrumented reference vehicle in Helsinki. It provides field evidence on decision-level fusion between infrastructure and vehicle observers in mixed traffic.

entry.title: SPVC: Structured and Panoptic Video Fixing for Cross-Dataset Driving Scene Rendering

author.name: Gen Li, Shu Han, Yun Xi Qiao, Hua Chen, Xuyang Dai, Bohan Li, Hao Zhao, Chaojian Li

entry.summary: SPVC is a video repair framework for driving scene rendering that uses explicit structured conditions such as camera pose and 3D boxes plus panoptic cues to fix blur, flicker and foreground-background misalignment in Gaussian-splatting renders under extrapolated trajectories. It targets cross-dataset generalization for autonomous driving simulation.

entry.title: SpurCon: Weighted Supervised Contrastive Learning for Mitigating Spurious Cues in Medical Imaging

author.name: Shenhav Nadir, Meir Yossef Levi, Eyal Gofer, Guy Gilboa

entry.summary: SpurCon is a weighted supervised contrastive learning framework that both identifies dataset-specific spurious cues, such as devices or treatment artifacts correlated with pathology, and reduces model reliance on them. The goal is improved worst-group performance on small or imbalanced medical datasets.

entry.title: Denoised Variance-Based Pruning with Optimal Brain Bias Compensation

author.name: Geon Tack Lee, Jaegul Choo, Kang Eun Jeon

entry.summary: This paper improves variance-based structural pruning of vision transformers by denoising finite-sample activation covariance estimates and replacing bias-only correction with an optimal-brain-style compensation that accounts for reconstruction error. The aim is strong accuracy retention without expensive retraining.

entry.title: Cross-Domain Generalization in Machine Unlearning via Label-Conditioned Energy Magnitude Regularization

author.name: Syed Ali Ahmed (National University of Computer and Emerging Sciences, Karachi, Pakistan), Syed Bilal Ahsan (National University of Computer and Emerging Sciences, Karachi, Pakistan), Muhammad Zaigham Zaheer (Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence, Abu Dhabi, UAE)

entry.summary: This work studies collateral effects of machine unlearning using a label-conditioned energy-based model where per-class energies make forgetting effects directly observable, forgetting a class by raising its energy while anchoring retained classes. A similarity-weighted propagation term extends forgetting to semantically related retained samples.

entry.title: AViTS: Adaptive Spatiotemporal Token Selection for Efficient Dynamic-Resolution Generation

author.name: Haoran Qin, Zhengan Yan, Shikang Zheng, Xiaobing Tu, Jiacheng Liu, Yuqi Lin, Chang Zou, JinShan Liu, Peiliang Cai, Xiantao Zhang, Jinkui Ren, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: AViTS reduces diffusion transformer cost by selectively upsampling only important latent tokens at resolution transitions, scoring spatial importance via latent-text attention and temporal importance via representation dynamics across steps. Uniform upsampling wastes compute and can harm fine detail.

entry.title: Reconfiguration-Complete Motion Primitives with Constructive Planning for Deformable Planar Modular Robots

author.name: Jie Gu, Tingting Wang, Hongrun Gao, Yirun Sun, Zhihao Xia, Chunxu Tian, Dan Zhang

entry.summary: This paper introduces a square-cell abstraction that maps deformable rhombus modules of a planar modular robot onto grid cells with two interpretable primitives, pivoting and shearing. It proves constructively that any non-straight edge-connected configuration with at least seven modules can be canonicalized into a staircase, implying mutual reconfigurability, and derives a planner from the proof. The completeness guarantee is the main contribution.

entry.title: Stability Control for Real World Testing in Autonomous Racing

author.name: Phillip Pitschi, Simon Sagmeister, Frederik Werner, Markus Lienkamp, Boris Lohmann

entry.summary: The paper presents a stability safeguarding stack for driverless autonomous racing, combining electronic stability control, slip control, and a countersteer system to keep the vehicle controllable when motion controllers that assume stable dynamics would fail. It is validated on real vehicles operating at the limits of handling without a safety driver. The focus is safe real-world experimentation at high speed.

entry.title: ClawGym II: Exploring Black-Box RL on Agent Harness

author.name: Huatong Song, Fei Bai, Ming Yang, Renyuan Li, Jia Deng, Jujie He, Zhange Zhang, Daixuan Cheng, Yan Xing, Qi Yun, Xuxing Chen, Danyang Li, Feng Chang, Chuan Hao, Ran Tao, Jian Yang, Bryan Dai, Wayne Xin Zhao, Mingjie Tang, Ji-Rong Wen

entry.summary: Already covered in yesterday's Research roundup, ClawGym II presents a black-box reinforcement learning framework that trains general agents through complex, opaque agent harnesses rather than reimplementing simplified environments. It combines sandboxed concurrent rollouts with a serving proxy at the model boundary that intercepts trajectories, decoupling policy optimization from harness internals so long-horizon agentic RL becomes stable and scalable.

entry.title: Explicit State Elicitation Is Not Enough: A Controlled Audit of Memory-Policy Classification

author.name: Yihang Chen, Pin Qian, Su Wang, Chong Peng, Huan Xu, Shuaiting Li, Yiqi Sun

entry.summary: Audits whether prompting an agent to emit an explicit memory-policy state (use, ignore, update, or query) actually improves decisions, and shows apparent gains on a synthetic set vanished under controlled counterfactuals. Diagnostics revealed lexical shortcuts and missing standalone cases in the original development data.

entry.title: Task-Aware Harness Provisioning for LLM Agents in Mission-Critical Infrastructure Operations

author.name: Liangtao Lin, Qingang Zhang, Zhaomeng Zhu, Tianwei Zhang, Yonggang Wen

entry.summary: Frames the choice of agent harness configuration as a matching problem between what a mission-critical infrastructure task mathematically requires and what tools and information a harness provides. Argues that giving every task the maximal harness wastes resources and proposes ranked, task-aware provisioning.

entry.title: Accuracy and Robustness of Model Cascades Under Data Perturbations

author.name: Pallavi Mitra, Jai Kushwaha, Felix Biessmann

entry.summary: Examines whether confidence-based model cascades, which route easy inputs to a small model and defer hard ones to a large model, remain reliable when inputs are corrupted or sequentially perturbed. Finds that degradations shift confidence and therefore distort deferral behavior in image classification cascades.

entry.title: Intent-Driven Dynamic Chunking: Segmenting Documents to Reflect Predicted Information Needs

author.name: Christos Koutsiaris

entry.summary: Intent-Driven Dynamic Chunking uses an LLM to predict likely user queries for a document and then applies dynamic programming to find a globally optimal segmentation aligned to those predicted information needs. It targets the mismatch where fixed-length or coherence-based chunking splits answers or bundles noise.

entry.title: Early Cycle Charge Trajectory Generative Prediction and Full Life Cycle Health Management of Iron-Chromium Flow Batteries Based on FlowBD-E1

author.name: Suyang Zhuang, Zekun Jiang, Tianhang Zhou

entry.summary: FlowBD-E1 forecasts the full charge voltage and current trajectory of an industrial 33 kW iron-chromium redox flow battery from early cycles, rather than compressing aging into a single state-of-health scalar. This supports earlier detection of degradation mechanisms specific to flow batteries.

entry.title: ARGUS: Attention-Guided Transformers for Scalable Person Identification Using Wi-Fi Telemetry

author.name: Nayan Sanjay Bhatia, Pranay Kocheta, Yuhan Li, Katia Obraczka

entry.summary: Argus identifies individuals passively from commodity Wi-Fi channel state information by converting short CSI spans into compact statistical maps read as tokens by a small decoder-only transformer. It is evaluated on 154 subjects without requiring wearables or prescribed gait motions.

entry.title: GATTA: Graph Active Learning with Test-Time Augmentation

author.name: Zsombor B\'anfi, Andr\'as G\'ezsi, Andr\'as Formanek

entry.summary: GATTA brings test-time augmentation to graph neural networks for active learning, aggregating predictions across augmented views and filtering out views whose predictions are inconsistent, to obtain better uncertainty estimates for sample acquisition. It is evaluated across several graph datasets, GNN architectures, and acquisition strategies.

entry.title: Global Federated Learning Strategies for Building Efficient Personalized Models

author.name: Seongyoon Kim

entry.summary: A dissertation-style synthesis of federated learning strategies that jointly improve global and personalized accuracy under client heterogeneity, arguing that feature-vector collapse rather than classifier drift is the primary bottleneck as heterogeneity grows. It proposes methods to preserve global knowledge during local adaptation.

entry.title: Structuring Semantic Embeddings for Principle Evaluation: A Prototype-Guided Contrastive Learning Approach

author.name: Che Shen, Junwei Su, Lingpeng Kong, Chuan Wu

entry.summary: PGCL adds a prototype-anchored attention and supervised contrastive regularization module on top of frozen text embeddings so that semantically similar but task-distinct examples separate cleanly. It is evaluated on post-hoc evaluation proxies such as toxicity detection, emotion categorization, and ordinal rating.

entry.title: Sequential Multimodal Evidence Optimization for Product Media Ranking in E-Commerce

author.name: Prasenjit Dey, Frank McIntyre, Arnab Sinha

entry.summary: SMEO orders heterogeneous product media such as images, videos, and 3D renders by learning a trajectory utility model that estimates how a consumed prefix of media helps a shopper reach a purchase decision, rather than optimizing myopic clicks. A second stage uses that utility to sequence assets cooperatively.

entry.title: Group ICA 2.0: Closing the Gap Between Subjects and Group Latent Decomposition with Copula-Linked Group ICA (CoLiG-ICA)

author.name: Oktay Agcaoglu

entry.summary: CoLiG-ICA extends group independent component analysis for fMRI so that template-linked, cohort-only, and subject-only brain networks are estimated jointly, using copula dependence modeling plus deep-learning optimization. It targets the loss of individual-specific networks in conventional group ICA for clinical neuroimaging.

entry.title: Multi-Feature Riemannian Hypergraph for Online Test-Time Adaptation of Motor Imagery Brain-Computer Interface

author.name: Siqi Li (Peking University, Chinese Institute for Brain Research, Beijing), Zhi Li (NeuCyber Neurotech), Tong Liu (NeuCyber Neurotech), Shuai Zhang (NeuCyber Neurotech), Yanfei Jia (Beijing Medical University), Zhiqiang Yi (Beijing Medical University), Jue Xie (NeuCyber Neurotech), Ni Ji (Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College, Chinese Institute for Brain Research, Beijing)

entry.summary: MRieHy combines Riemannian alignment of covariance matrices across recording days with hypergraph modeling of higher-order sample relationships to enable online test-time adaptation for motor imagery brain-computer interfaces. It targets the cross-day transferability and online operation gaps in clinical BCI decoding.

entry.title: Rotation-Invariant Multi-IMU Activity Recognition under Independent Per-Location Orientation Shifts

author.name: Seungyeol Baek, Yoonbyung Chai, Yonghyeon Lee, Sungjoon Choi, Sungho Suh

entry.summary: Proposes a human activity recognition framework that is structurally invariant to independent rotation offsets at each body-worn IMU location, which is what happens when users reattach sensors themselves between sessions. Unlike rotation augmentation or calibration pipelines, invariance is built into the model rather than learned from sampled transformations.

entry.title: Representation Is Not Enough: Body-Localized Thermal Evidence for Contactless Stress and Craving Sensing in Opioid Use Disorder

author.name: Sachin Deb, Harshit Sharma, Asif Salekin

entry.summary: Presents a weakly supervised architecture for contactless stress and craving detection from thermal video in opioid use disorder, preserving evidence localized to specific body regions, time windows, and encoder representations until the final decision. The authors fuse frozen foundation-model encoders at the embedding level and give theory for why localized fusion beats concatenation or prediction averaging.

entry.title: Predicting, Evaluating, and Explaining Top Misinformation Spreaders via Archetypal User Behavior

author.name: Enrico Verdolotti, Luca Luceri, Silvia Giordano

entry.summary: Identifies and ranks the users most responsible for misinformation diffusion by characterizing three non-exclusive behavioral archetypes, amplifiers, super-spreaders, and coordinated accounts, and predicting who will occupy those roles. The aim is proactive, explainable intervention targeting rather than post hoc content moderation.

entry.title: LLMs for Zero-Shot Threat Detection via Structured Risk Indicators

author.name: Abdullah Alghamdi, Siamak Layeghy, Marius Portmann

entry.summary: Builds a two-stage LLM framework for zero-shot insider threat and advanced persistent threat detection that represents user activity as chronological timelines, retrieves each user's historical behavior as context, generates interpretable structured risk indicators, and only then classifies across temporal sequences. It is evaluated on standard insider threat and attack-provenance benchmarks.

entry.title: CAS-FD: Contact-Aware Temporal Sampling for Single-View Foul vs Dive Recognition

author.name: Md. Jahidul Islam, Mahfujul Alam, Md. Nazmul Islam Seyam, Md. Tamim Hossain

entry.summary: Introduces a balanced 600-clip single-view football dataset for distinguishing genuine fouls from simulated dives and shows that concentrating temporal sampling around the moment of physical contact substantially improves recognition. The contact-aware approach reaches 86 percent accuracy, roughly 12 points above contact-unaware sampling, with the gap widening on unseen data.

entry.title: Language models suffer from a curse of ambiguity

author.name: Nicolas Zucchet, Hyun Dong Lee, Scott Linderman

entry.summary: Already covered in yesterday's Research roundup, Identifies a systematic learning pathology the authors call a curse of ambiguity: the more entropic or ambiguous a next-token distribution is, the harder it is for a neural network to fit accurately, requiring more capacity, larger embeddings, more optimization steps, and amplifying sampling noise. The claim is supported by theoretical analysis plus empirical validation, with implications for self-improvement pipelines that depend on sampling fidelity.

entry.title: The Price of Thinking: Reasoning Effort as a Model-Specific API Contract

author.name: Yeabin Moon

entry.summary: A registered paired experiment measuring what buyers actually pay when specifying a high reasoning-effort setting versus omitting it, using Sonnet 5 on AIME 2026 items. Explicit high effort cost about one cent more per call with an accuracy difference that was not statistically distinguishable from zero.

entry.title: SkillEffect: Checked Lowering for Memory-Bounded Agent Tools

author.name: Yinuo Wang, Yiyu Shi

entry.summary: SkillEffect is a runtime that verifies an agent-generated program can be lowered into a memory-bounded streaming implementation before granting execution authority, using independent reconstruction from the submitted code and immutable input. It targets the failure mode where semantically correct agent code loads an entire input and exhausts tool memory.

entry.title: SAGE: Self-Evolving Storyboard Skills via Attribution-Guided Rule Evolution

author.name: Maolin Ran, Xiaoyang Lu, Jiaqi Liu, Jian Wang, Weiwen Liu, Jianghao Lin, Yong Yu, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: SAGE automates storyboard generation for short-form drama by evolving explicit directing rules, attributing outcome quality back to the rules responsible, and selecting only relevant knowledge for injection into limited context. It addresses knowledge acquisition, refinement, and injection as three distinct bottlenecks.

entry.title: Graph Surgery and the Do-Operator: A Precise Correspondence for Acyclic Structural Causal Models

author.name: Satpreet Makhija

entry.summary: Proves an exact correspondence between graph surgery and mechanism replacement for the do-operator in deterministic acyclic structural causal models, showing that the dependency graph of intervened mechanisms equals the surgically modified graph. Makes rigorous an equivalence usually stated informally.

entry.title: Structural Plan-to-Model Conversion with Deterministic Geometry and Guarded Agentic Vision-Language Refinement

author.name: Mohammad Talebi-Kalaleh, Qipei Mei

entry.summary: This framework converts structural framing plan PDFs into editable finite-element model drafts by combining a deterministic primitive-extraction and scale-estimation stage with a guarded agentic vision-language refinement layer, avoiding any task-specific detector training. It claims to be the first application of agentic VLMs directly to structural drawings rather than to text or model data. It shows how guardrailed VLM agents can replace bespoke detectors in engineering document workflows.

entry.title: From Student Risk Prediction to SC2R: Semantics-Constrained Counterfactual Recourse for Educational Decision Support

author.name: Ngoc Luyen Le, Marie-H\'el\`ene Abel, Bertrand Laforge

entry.summary: SC2R turns student risk prediction into actionable intervention plans by generating counterfactual recourse over discrete action variables with integer programming, then encoding plans in a lightweight RDF vocabulary validated by SHACL shapes that enforce timing, budget, immutability, and availability constraints. It is evaluated offline on the OULAD dataset at two decision horizons. Bridges prediction and feasible institutional action.

entry.title: MotoSafety: Edge-AI with Learned Temporal Importance for Two-Wheeler Collision Risk Assessment Under Time Pressure

author.name: Sumit S. Shevtekar, Chandresh K. Maurya, Gourab Sil, Subasish Das

entry.summary: MotoSafety introduces a dataset of over 129,000 labeled multivariate time-series sequences from 153 simulator rides by 51 participants under varying time pressure, capturing 64 features covering vehicle dynamics, control inputs, proximity, and violations, plus an edge-deployable model using learned temporal importance. It reports high accuracy and low latency versus ten baselines including TimesNet. It targets motorcycle rider safety in low- and middle-income countries.

entry.title: Comparative Study of Out-of-the-Box Technology for Automatic Target Detection and Recognition

author.name: Alma M. Liezenga, Lotte Nijskens, Henrik R. Baumann, Stefan Becker, Simon Bensberg, Niccol\`o Camarlinghi, H{\aa}vard R. Eiring, Alexander W. Johnsgaard, Tanel Liiv, Giuseppe Martino, Matteo Marturini, Matthias Rapp, Jan Erik van Woerden, Alexander Wolpert, Hugo J. Kuijf

entry.summary: A multi-national team benchmarks off-the-shelf detectors, including six YOLO variants and two DETR variants, on a newly collected military-vehicle dataset to see whether civilian pretraining transfers to defense target recognition. The study documents how far public models get without military training data.

entry.title: Collective Counterfactual Planning: Coordination, Consent, and Verification under Representational Constraints

author.name: Chainarong Amornbunchornvej

entry.summary: Collective Counterfactual Planning formalizes team problem solving where each agent only perceives, conceives, consents, and verifies through its own projection of a shared task space. Four gating conditions determine when a group can both reach and legitimately certify a conjunctive goal.

entry.title: Against Political Polarization: A Unified Framework for Tracing Evolving Political Ideologies on Social Media

author.name: Yijie Xu, Chao Wang, Hui Xiong

entry.summary: TSN4PI combines LLM-based ideology detection with style transfer and unsupervised domain adaptation, plus temporal graph neural networks, to trace how individual political ideologies evolve on social media. It aims to handle noisy, largely non-political content and avoid costly manual labeling.

entry.title: FedImp: Enhancing Federated Learning Convergence with Impurity-Based Weighting

author.name: Hai Anh Tran, Cuong Ta, Truong X. Tran

entry.summary: FedImp weights client contributions in federated averaging by an impurity-based measure of the informational content of each device's local data, aiming to speed convergence under non-IID conditions. Experiments on EMNIST and CIFAR-10 report substantial reductions in communication rounds.

entry.title: A Reproducibility Study of Partial Residual Ablations in Pre-LN Transformers

author.name: Pratikkumar Babariya

entry.summary: A reproducibility study selectively removes attention or feed-forward residual connections in Pre-LN GPT-style transformers at 10M and 124M scale. Removing the attention residual collapses performance to the no-residual floor, while removing the feed-forward residual shows a reproducible partial recovery.

entry.title: A Novel Fourier Feature Network for Solving Partial Differential Equations

author.name: Qihong Yang, Zhijie Su, Yangtao Deng, Qiaolin He

entry.summary: Fourier Feature Networks use a single hidden layer of sine and cosine features whose output coefficients are fit by least squares, in the spirit of extreme learning machines but without input affine transformations. The paper evaluates their representational capacity for solving partial differential equations to high precision.

entry.title: Real-Time State-of-Health Estimation and Online Degradation Prognosis from Partial Battery Discharge Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Bego\~na Ispizua, Serio Gil-L\'opez, Leire Arrizabalaga, Ibai La\~na

entry.summary: The paper estimates lithium-ion battery state of health from partial discharge curves taken over arbitrary voltage ranges using a physics-informed neural network, reporting mean absolute percentage error below four percent. It adds a real-time degradation-trend estimator for online prognosis.

entry.title: M-LINKX: Multiview Graph Learning for Brain Cognitive Disease Detection

author.name: An Phan, Yufei Jin, Xingquan Zhu

entry.summary: M-LINKX classifies dementia-related conditions from EEG segments using a multi-view graph learning approach that combines within-channel signal information and cross-channel interactions. It targets the noise, non-stationarity, and subject variability that make EEG-based dementia detection difficult.

entry.title: A Physiology-Informed Digital Twin Framework for Simulating Liver Health Progression

author.name: Sumaiya Afroz Mila, Sandip Ray

entry.summary: HEPATWIN is a mechanistic digital twin of the liver that simulates metabolic, bilirubin, bile, and detoxification processes to produce longitudinal biomarker trajectories under patient-specific diet and activity inputs. A stage-transition mechanism keeps simulated progression consistent with clinical disease staging.

entry.title: Quantum Models with Multi-Stage Training for Compositional Concept Generalization

author.name: Mina Abbaszadeh, Matilda Karabina Moore, Mehrnoosh Sadrzadeh, Martha Lewis

entry.summary: Applies compositional distributional semantics with tensors and variational quantum circuits to compositional concept generalization, training object representations first from single-object image-caption pairs and then freezing them while learning relational components. The staged design enforces factorization between nouns and relations at the circuit level.

entry.title: Retrieval-guided Twin Fusion with Similarity-aware Contrast for Molecule-Text Alignment

author.name: Shunshun Gu, Shengqi Qiu, Hang Zhou, Xiao Luo

entry.summary: RISEN aligns molecules and text by constructing latent twin molecules for substructures and applying similarity-aware contrastive objectives to capture fine-grained substructure-text correspondence. It targets molecule search and property prediction downstream tasks.

entry.title: RetroMPA: A Molecular Property-Aware Auxiliary Framework for Enhancing Retrosynthesis Prediction

author.name: Mianzhi Liu, Fan Xiao, Zhiliang Yu, Huayang Huang, Yuke Li, Yi Yang, Wenbo Liu, Yu Wu

entry.summary: RetroMPA is a model-agnostic post-hoc module that injects molecular property knowledge to rerank and recalibrate the candidate reactants produced by existing retrosynthesis predictors. It functions as a plug-in chemical filter rather than a standalone sequence generator.

entry.title: A Tree-Structured Approach for Phishing Template and Attacker Attribution Analysis

author.name: Unai Agirre, Imanol Jerico, Felipe Casta\~no, Andrea Venturi, Francesco Zola

entry.summary: This work builds tree-structured representations of phishing webpage DOMs to cluster pages by structural reuse, enabling attribution of pages to shared phishing kits and templates rather than classifying individual instances. The goal is to detect coordinated campaigns that surface-level features and blocklists miss.

entry.title: Reference-free logged energy-oracle recovery for neural approximations of symmetric coercive variational problems: conforming Riesz reconstruction and archive-level selection

author.name: Karim Bounja, Lahcen Laayouni, Boujemaa Achchab, Abdeljalil Sakat

entry.summary: For neural approximations of symmetric coercive variational problems, this paper proposes a reference-free rule for selecting among training checkpoints by minimizing a computable conforming Riesz monitor, since true energy errors are unavailable without the exact solution. The monitor is an unconditional lower bound converging monotonically to the logged energy error, with hierarchical enrichment giving an upper estimate.

entry.title: Variational Outlier-Robust Gaussian Process Regression with Generative Modeling

author.name: Arslan Majal, Aamir Hussain Chughtai

entry.summary: This paper makes Gaussian process regression robust to outliers by introducing a generative model of observation-specific contamination and inferring latent contamination indicators plus GP hyperparameters with a variational generalized EM procedure. Experiments across contamination settings show competitive or better accuracy than robust GP baselines.

entry.title: Hoeffding adaptive splitting trees for data stream classification with concept drift and ensemble learning

author.name: Daniel Nowak Assis, Jean Paul Barddal, Fabr\'icio Enembreck

entry.summary: The authors show that adaptive-splitting decision trees, which split in response to detected performance degradation, fail to generate enough diversity when used as ensemble base learners on drifting data streams. They propose Hoeffding Adaptive Splitting Trees that combine Hoeffding-bound and adaptive triggers to restore ensemble diversity.

entry.title: When to Communicate: Belief Distributions and KL Divergence for Principled Gating in Multi-Agent RL

author.name: Teoman Kaman

entry.summary: This paper replaces high-variance REINFORCE-learned binary communication gates in multi-agent RL with a rule that triggers communication only when the KL divergence between agents' learned belief distributions over a latent world state exceeds a threshold. The result is intended to be more stable and more interpretable gating.

entry.title: Longitudinal and Graph-Augmented Prediction of Adolescent Substance Use Onset in the ABCD Study

author.name: Yixuan He, Jinni Su, Yun Kang

entry.summary: Using roughly 11,860 participants from the ABCD study, this paper compares cross-sectional, longitudinal, and graph-based models for predicting onset of adolescent alcohol and marijuana use, including temporal graph convolutional networks built on family, school, and feature-similarity graphs. Longitudinal models such as temporal gradient boosting consistently outperform baseline-only models.

entry.title: PandasCorpus: A Resource of Real-World Pandas Workflows and Usage Patterns

author.name: Syrym Abdikhan, Mazhar Hameed

entry.summary: PandasCorpus is a large mined dataset of roughly 139 thousand Jupyter notebooks from about 100 thousand GitHub repositories capturing over four million Pandas API calls, characterizing how data-analysis workflows are actually composed in practice. It fills a gap in empirical understanding of real-world data science code.

entry.title: CFR without Unbiasedness: Deterministic Guarantees for Persistent Public-Chance Schedules

author.name: Jiaxing Guo, Lei Ye

entry.summary: The paper analyzes counterfactual regret minimization when only part of a public chance node is evaluated per update in a fixed without-replacement order, which makes feedback conditionally biased because earlier batches shape later profiles. It proves a deterministic target-transfer theorem bounding full-cut exploitability by regret on delivered feedback plus a public-debit coupling term.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Adaptation of Medical Vision Foundation Models for High-Frequency Micro-Ultrasound Prostate Segmentation

author.name: Ayusha Abbas, Saram Abbas, Kabita Adhikari

entry.summary: The paper builds a zero-shot prostate segmentation pipeline for high-frequency micro-ultrasound by adapting a medical segmentation foundation model with no task-specific training data, addressing the speckle and boundary ambiguity of 29 MHz imaging. It is positioned as the first such pipeline for this emerging modality where inter-clinician outlines differ by over ten percent in area.

entry.title: Uncovering Hidden Leptonic Correlations with Flow Matching and Autoencoders

author.name: Haruto Kitagawa, Satsuki Nishimura, Hajime Otsuka
