entry.summary: Flow matching is used as a generative sampler to find many Yukawa matrix and Majorana mass configurations consistent with measured neutrino mass splittings and mixing angles in the Type-I seesaw model, and an autoencoder then compresses these solutions to expose latent structure. The analysis surfaces new nonlinear relations among neutrino masses and CP phases.

entry.title: Sufficient Dimesion Reduction via Generalized Stein's Lemma

author.name: Ye Tian

entry.summary: The paper develops sufficient dimension reduction for multivariate responses using a generalized Stein identity, avoiding the distributional assumptions and matrix inversions of inverse regression, the slice sparsity of its multi-response extensions, the cost of forward smoothing and the data hunger of deep approaches. The aim is estimating the central subspace with limited samples.

entry.title: BrainLinear: A Linear Model for Brain Network Analysis in Sparse Tangent Subspaces

author.name: Sijing Wu, Dongyuan Li, Miaoting Huang, Weiwei Ye, Ying Zhang, Feng Xia, Renhe Jiang

entry.summary: BrainLinear questions whether graph neural networks and transformers over full functional connectivity matrices are necessary, proposing instead a lightweight geometry-aware linear model operating in sparse tangent subspaces of the connectivity manifold. The claim is that identifying a small set of disease-relevant connections suffices while improving interpretability and cost.

entry.title: Prediction Inference of Time Series with Standard ReLU Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Kejin Wu

entry.summary: The paper builds prediction intervals for time series forecasts made with standard ReLU deep networks that account for both future randomness and estimation variability from finite training data. The proposed pertinent prediction interval aims to give asymptotically valid uncertainty quantification where prior deep forecasting work focused only on point accuracy.

entry.title: When Is Shallow Enough? Adaptive Split Federated Learning with Client-Specific Sufficiency Estimation

author.name: Wenhao Yuan, Chenchen Lin, Wenhao Hu, Jian Chen, Jinfeng Xu, Shujie Li, Edith Cheuk Han Ngai

entry.summary: Argues that in split federated learning the cut point between client and server should adapt per client rather than being fixed, because clients differ in data distribution and representation learning progress. The method uses private prompt tokens to estimate when a client's shallow layers are already sufficient and adjusts the split accordingly.

entry.title: Asymptotics-guided learning and symbolic regression for dispersive resonances

author.name: Konstantinos Alexopoulos, Josselin Garnier

entry.summary: Uses asymptotic analysis of subwavelength expansions not merely as a baseline approximation but as a design principle for the feature space of a learned correction model predicting resonances in dispersive media. Symbolic regression then distills the learned residual into compact closed-form formulas.

entry.title: RadioVIL: Anomaly-Aware Diffusion Models for Radio Map Inpainting and Zero-Shot Vehicle Localization

author.name: Ruixin Zhao, Xiucheng Wang, Qiming Zhang, Nan Cheng, Ruijin Sun, Conghao Zhou

entry.summary: Reframes radio-map completion for 6G sensing as a prior-guided physical inverse problem rather than image inpainting, arguing that standard deep completion over-smooths and erases the high-frequency scattering signatures of hidden vehicles. A denoising diffusion model learns structural priors, enabling both accurate map reconstruction and zero-shot localization of vehicles.

entry.title: Self-Routed Tensor Adapters for Parameter-Efficient Universal Visual Adaptation

author.name: Suraj Yadav

entry.summary: Proposes a compact parameter-efficient adaptation module for frozen visual foundation models in which each input is projected into a low-rank space that also determines its own routing, avoiding both fixed single-subspace adapters and mixture-of-experts adapters that need external routers and large expert banks. The target is multi-domain visual adaptation without fragmenting knowledge into per-domain modules.

entry.title: Environment-Invariant Subspace Learning for Generalizable Deepfake Detection

author.name: Shenghao Chen, Hao Jia, Chen Li, Chunjie Ma, Zan Gao, Shengyong Chen

entry.summary: EISL improves deepfake detection generalization by disentangling foundation-model features into orthogonal forgery-relevant and environment-related subspaces, removing spurious correlations between manipulation cues and lighting or style. This targets cross-distribution failure, the main bottleneck in deployed detectors.

entry.title: Beyond Instrument Motion: Recognizing Tissue Tension Toward Surgical Skill Assessment

author.name: Marko Haralovi, Zhiqi Miao, Alexander Machiel Bont, Jiapan Guo, Frans van Workum, Estefania Talavera

entry.summary: The paper introduces tissue tension recognition as a new surgical video understanding task and releases SurgTension, an expert-annotated dataset for laparoscopic and robot-assisted rectal cancer surgery. Tissue handling quality is a key skill indicator that instrument-motion-based methods do not capture.

entry.title: Jetson-ORB-SLAM3: Accuracy-Preserving GPU Implementation for Edge Computing Devices

author.name: Rajat Roy, Aditya Arun Kumar Yadav, Hardik Jain

entry.summary: The authors port the ORB front end of ORB-SLAM3 to the GPU of an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano while reproducing the reference CPU detector almost exactly, reporting about 95 percent exact keypoint agreement and near-perfect descriptor bit agreement, and make CNN-based loop closure edge-viable through TensorRT. Mapping and optimization stay on the CPU to match each workload to the right processor. This gives speedups without the trajectory drift that earlier approximate GPU ports introduced.

entry.title: Modified Bryson-Frazier Smoothing and Hyperparameter Learning for Temporal Gaussian Process Regression

author.name: Tom Colemont, Brecht Evens, Tjonnie G. F. Li, Frederik De Ceuster

entry.summary: The authors revisit the modified Bryson-Frazier smoother as a replacement for the Rauch-Tung-Striebel smoother in state-space Gaussian process regression, showing it recovers identical posteriors while avoiding inversion of possibly ill-conditioned predicted covariance matrices and reducing compute and memory. They also address hyperparameter learning in this formulation. It improves numerical robustness of linear-time temporal GP inference.

entry.title: From Abductive Explanations to Global Logical Rules for Node Classification in SGCs

author.name: Bryan Lima Cavalcante, Thiago Alves Rocha

entry.summary: This work extracts global logical rules explaining node classification in Simple Graph Convolution networks by first computing minimal abductive explanations per node, which strips node-specific redundancy before rule aggregation. It is positioned as an improvement over subgraph-collection approaches such as LogicXGNN. The result is more general and compact symbolic descriptions of GNN behavior.

entry.title: Maximum Tsallis Entropy Distributions for Robust and Efficient Sparse Learning from Correlated Data

author.name: Kai Yang, Masoud Asgharian, Celia M. T. Greenwood

entry.summary: The authors replace Gaussian assumptions in sparse learning with q-Gaussian distributions derived from Tsallis entropy maximization, re-deriving the multivariate density for correlated observations and building robust sparse estimators suited to heterogeneous biostatistical data such as genetic and longitudinal studies. The goal is outlier robustness without sacrificing sparsity. Statistical methodology with biomedical applications.

entry.title: Adaptive surrogate modeling for high-dimensional spatio-temporal output

author.name: Berkcan Kapusuzoglu, Shunsaku Matsumoto, Yoshitomo Miyagi, Daigo Watanabe, Sankaran Mahadevan

entry.summary: An adaptive surrogate modeling method for multi-physics simulations with extremely high-dimensional spatio-temporal outputs, which first reduces the output to a latent space and then fits and adaptively refines a surrogate there for use in uncertainty quantification and optimization. It targets settings where each physics-based run is prohibitively expensive. Standard but useful engineering-simulation machinery.

entry.title: Integrating Novelty and Surprise for Experience Prioritization and Exploration in Image-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Hoda Yamani, Henry Williams, Bruce A. MacDonald

entry.summary: NSPER integrates novelty and surprise signals into prioritized experience replay for image-based reinforcement learning, so the same intrinsic quantities that drive exploration also determine which stored transitions get replayed. The paper argues the interaction between replay prioritization and intrinsic motivation has been under-explored. Aims at sample efficiency in high-dimensional visual control.

entry.title: CoAL-RAG: A Complexity-Aware Legal Retrieval-Augmented Generation Method

author.name: Jin Su, Zhuofeng Zhao, Huanhuan Wang, Hao Chen

entry.summary: CoAL-RAG routes legal consultation queries to different retrieval strategies based on estimated question complexity, quantified from logical structure and from disagreement between semantic and keyword retrieval. This avoids over-reasoning on simple questions while improving interpretability on complex ones. Targets the quality-versus-cost tradeoff in high-risk legal advice.

entry.title: Training with synthetic data for drone detection in thermal imagery

author.name: Tanel Liiv, Sander Soodla, Nzamba Bignoumba, Alma M. Liezenga, Toomas Pruuden

entry.summary: This study evaluates a synthetic-first training strategy for detecting drones in medium and long-wave infrared imagery, where annotated real data is scarce and thermal contrast is weak. Synthetic scenes support initial representation learning, but small amounts of real in-domain infrared data are still needed, and dataset alignment matters more than model size. Practical guidance for defense and counter-UAS perception.

entry.title: Feasible and Novel Synthetic Population Generation with Tabular and Sequential Travel Attributes

author.name: Farbod Abbasi, Zachary Patterson, Bilal Farooq

entry.summary: Presents a two-stage regularized generative framework that produces synthetic populations combining static socio-demographic attributes with sequential trip-chain behavior for travel demand modeling. Added loss terms push the generator to cover valid but unsampled attribute combinations while avoiding structurally impossible ones.

entry.title: NPU Offloading of a Frozen Visual Encoder for Robot Policy Training

author.name: Hyojun Yun, Seungjae Won, Hyungpil Moon

entry.summary: The paper asks whether offloading the forward pass of a frozen visual encoder in robot policy training to a low-power neural accelerator reduces total energy despite transfer overhead and longer wall-clock time. An asynchronous GPU-plus-NPU pipeline runs the encoder in eight-bit integer precision on a commercial NPU while the action module trains in full precision on GPU, with policy performance also measured.

entry.title: Functional anatomy of Pythia-Herwig differences with Kolmogorov-Arnold networks

author.name: Arghya Chattopadhyay

entry.summary: Uses additive Kolmogorov-Arnold networks to decompose where two widely used high-energy physics event generators disagree, tracking the same hard dijet events through shower-only, hadronized, and full-generator stages. The goal is to attribute global classifier-level disagreement to specific observable-level structures and see whether they persist across simulation stages.

entry.title: AISA: AI Safety Assistant Framework for Continuous Improvement of Highway Construction

author.name: Mason Smetana, Trevor Neece, Lev Khazanovich

entry.summary: Presents a framework using locally hosted LLMs to classify and quality-score unstructured highway construction incident narratives and retrieve relevant historical accidents, imagery, and industry documents for daily safety planning. Neural probes are trained to support deterministic local inference as a foundation for later agentic applications.

entry.title: Key-Frame Reasoning with SAM3: Third Place Solution for the MeViS-Text Track of the 8th LSVOS Challenge

author.name: Ce Bian, Xusheng He, Jinrong Zhang, Canyang Wu, Xianjing Han, Jianlong Wu

entry.summary: A competition report describing a training-free two-stage pipeline for language-guided video object segmentation: an existing multimodal model (Gemini-3.1 Pro, available since February 2026) decomposes an event-level description into instance targets and picks key frames, then SAM3 produces seed masks that are propagated bidirectionally through the video. It placed third in the MeViS-Text track of the LSVOS challenge.

entry.title: Scanline-Aware Animatable Gaussian Avatars from Rolling-Shutter Videos

author.name: Youxiang Wang

entry.summary: This work points out that animatable Gaussian avatar reconstruction assumes global shutter, while rolling-shutter cameras expose rows at different times so each scanline observes a different body pose. The proposed scanline-aware formulation models per-row readout timing across a multi-camera rig to remove baked-in shear and wobble artifacts.

entry.title: Noisy group neurons with synchronous resetting for high-performance spiking neural networks

author.name: Yajie Zhai, Yanmei Kang, Meng Li, Zigang Huang

entry.summary: The paper introduces a noisy group neuron model for spiking networks that adds population-level synchronous resetting and stochasticity, trained via mean-field-based backpropagation to reduce spatiotemporal information loss and gradient mismatch. Results are demonstrated on standard image classification benchmarks.

entry.title: Looking Beyond the Scale: Do Surgical Skill Models Learn Transferable Representations Across Assessment Rubrics?

author.name: Hanna Hoffmann, Felix von Bechtolsheim, Stefanie Speidel, Rebecca Hisey

entry.summary: This study asks whether vision-based surgical skill assessment models learn transferable notions of proficiency or merely dataset-specific visual patterns, testing end-to-end training, sharpness-aware minimization and self-supervised or contrastive pretraining across two rubrics and datasets. Each method is used as a targeted diagnostic rather than a performance claim.

entry.title: Evaluation of AI-based Visual Crack Detection in Steel Bridges Using Probability of Detection

author.name: Andrii Kompanets, Finn Michael Sherry, Remco Duits, Davide Leonetti, H. H. Snijder

entry.summary: The paper evaluates AI-based crack detection on steel bridges using probability-of-detection curves, the standard reliability framework in structural engineering, instead of intersection-over-union or mean average precision. This makes computer vision results interpretable and comparable within established inspection practice.

entry.title: Improving Complex Moir\'e Removal with Generative Supervision

author.name: Xinyang Gu, Zhilu Zhang, Honglei Xu, Yanting Mei, Yukang Ding, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: A generative data engine synthesizes realistic paired training data for removing complex, large-scale multicolored moire patterns of the kind seen in photographs of displays and web-sourced images. This addresses the scarcity of clean counterparts for real-world degraded images.

entry.title: CFB-GBM v2.0: An Augmented Longitudinal Dataset for Multi-Modal Glioblastoma Segmentation, Radiomics, and RANO Progression Tracking

author.name: Alexandre G. Leclercq, No\'emie N. Moreau, Hugo Audebert, Andros Nassar, Thomas Cochin, Thomas Leleu, Lo\"ic Le Henaff, Alexis Desmonts, Yoann Poirier, Aur\'elie Dubru, Laura Guillemette, Pascal Lecoeur, K\'evin Lemasson, Cyril Jaudet, S\'ebastien Bougleux, Romain H\'erault, Carole Brunaud, Samuel Valable, Dinu Stefan, Charlotte Raboutet, Alain Batalla, Jo\"elle Lacroix, Roman Rouzier, Aur\'elien Corroyer-Dulmont

entry.summary: CFB-GBM v2.0 extends a longitudinal glioblastoma imaging dataset of 264 patients with near-complete tumor volume delineations at all three timepoints, plus clinical and treatment metadata. It is intended to support reproducible work on segmentation, radiomics and response or progression tracking.

entry.title: Repetition as Reinforcement: Enhancing Sample Efficiency via Instant Episode Repetition in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Hoda Yamani, Yuning Xing, Koen van Rijnsoever, Bruce A. MacDonald, Henry Williams

entry.summary: Instant Episode Repetition improves reinforcement learning sample efficiency by immediately repeating the action sequence of a high-reward episode for several subsequent episodes, thereby shaping data collection rather than only reusing stored transitions as in experience replay or self-imitation. The mechanism is simple, biologically motivated, and easy to bolt onto existing agents. It is evaluated in robotic control settings.

entry.title: Equilibrium Forcing: Adaptive Video Generation Without Noise Conditioning

author.name: Hansen Jin Lillemark, Alex Rojas, Zachary Novack, Runqian Wang, Yilun Du, Yian Ma, Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick, Rose Yu

entry.summary: Already covered in yesterday's Research roundup, Equilibrium Forcing trains autoregressive video diffusion models without conditioning on the noise level, decoupling learning of the denoising field from the sampling schedule so that inference can adapt to feedback from the partially generated sample. The authors report improved quality and temporal consistency on hard autoregressive video benchmarks plus analysis of why noise-unconditional training works.

entry.title: SignalReasoner: Assessing the Upper Bound of 3B Models for Signal Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Guozheng Sun

entry.summary: A technical report exploring how far reinforcement fine-tuning and distilled chain-of-thought SFT can push a 3B base model on graduate-level wireless signal mathematics from a specialized benchmark. Compares direct RL with verifiable rewards against SFT followed by RL.

entry.title: D$^2$ACCI: A Dual-Loop Diagnostic Protocol for Evidence-Preserving Agent Memory

author.name: Xule Liu, Yijun Liu, Chao Li, Shao Kun

entry.summary: Proposes a dual-loop diagnostic protocol for persistent agent memory that localizes which pipeline stage, from ingestion to generation, caused a failure, using paired statistical comparisons, protected-slice monitoring, and stage-level traces. Aims to replace aggregate end-to-end scores that reveal that an error occurred but not why.

entry.title: CARA: Cognitive Adaptive Recommendation Agent

author.name: Weijun Gao, Jinyang Dong, Chuanru Ren, Hengxiao Li

entry.summary: CARA is an LLM agent framework for recommendation that explicitly models a fast affective preference channel and a slow deliberative evaluation channel before producing a decision, rather than relying on end-to-end generation or loose agent workflows. The cognitive decomposition is intended to make preference processing explicit and auditable. It contributes to the growing line of agentic recommender designs.

entry.title: Dual Co-Train: Cross-Dataset Ultrasound Tongue Segmentation Under Extreme Data Scarcity

author.name: Alisher Myrgyyassov, Zhen Song, Bruce Xiao Wang, Yu Sun, Min Ney Wong, Yihao Zhou, Yongping Zheng

entry.summary: A source-free domain adaptation pipeline adapts an ultrasound tongue segmentation model from a checkpoint trained on only five labeled images to an unlabeled target domain. It combines pseudo-label refinement, contour-based quality filtering, and a segmentation-guided conditional GAN for target-style synthetic pairs.

entry.title: ER-KANs: Efficient and Robust Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Data-Scarce Scientific Machine Learning

author.name: Harshil Lodhiya

entry.summary: ER-KANs argue that the Kolmogorov-Arnold Network literature has been benchmarked mostly on clean data, hiding large robustness differences: a Chebyshev variant degrades over ten times under moderate input noise versus 1.4 times for the proposed model. The design uses shared Gaussian radial basis functions per layer plus curriculum noise injection.

entry.title: Can Neural Networks Learn by Experimenting on Themselves? Self-Interventional Learning from Functional Consequences to Predictive Self-Knowledge

author.name: Micha{\l} Tomaszewski

entry.summary: Self-Interventional Learning has a neural system perturb its own internal structure, observe the functional consequences, and learn a predictive self-model that generalizes to unexecuted interventions. In a synthetic system with known construction, it recovered critical structure, redundancy, and replaceability but not synergy, with held-out error dropping as intervention budget grew.

entry.title: Detecting Money Laundering in Rwandan Mobile Money: A Machine Learning Framework

author.name: Emmanuel Nahimana, Ya\'e Ulrich Gaba

entry.summary: Builds and evaluates a transaction monitoring framework for mobile money anti-money-laundering in Rwanda under extreme class imbalance, delayed labels, and limited investigator capacity, using a large synthetic transaction dataset. It explicitly aligns the modeling objective with regulatory alert-review constraints.

entry.title: RagGAD: Rationale-Aware Conditional Gaussian Mixture Normalizing Flow for Unsupervised Graph Anomaly Detection

author.name: Junxin Lu, Jing Zhao, Shiliang Sun

entry.summary: RagGAD performs unsupervised graph anomaly detection using a conditional Gaussian mixture normalizing flow conditioned on disentangled rationales, separating stable structure from spurious affinities. It aims to reduce reliance on the homophily assumption that limits many existing detectors.

entry.title: FETERS: Few-Shot Early Time-Series Classification via Effective Ratio Selection

author.name: Chen-An Tai, Yujia Wu, Vincent S. Tseng

entry.summary: FETERS tackles early time-series classification with very few labels by choosing a dataset-level stopping ratio through class-wise leave-one-out evaluation on the support set instead of learning a per-sample stopping module. A penalty-based reward function balances earliness against accuracy.

entry.title: TRACE-CASH: Trial-History-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Configuration Exploration in Time-Series CASH

author.name: Yu-Han Huang, Yujia Wu, Vincent S. Tseng

entry.summary: TRACE-CASH applies trial-history-conditioned reinforcement learning to combined algorithm selection and hyperparameter optimization for time-series forecasting, using grouped actor-critic candidate generation plus fixed rules for coverage, exploitation, and stall-triggered exploration. It also aims to provide a shared evaluation protocol for time-series CASH comparisons.

entry.title: Deep Analog: Open-Set Film Emulation with Reference-Conditioned 3D LUTs

author.name: Yitong Mu

entry.summary: The paper treats reference-conditioned film emulation as predicting a 3D color lookup table and shows that the common practice of blending a fixed bank of LUTs is a gated mixture of experts that collapses onto one expert when trained end-to-end. Adding an entropy load-balancing term restores expert utilization and recovers around one decibel of PSNR, while arguing that any fixed LUT basis is fundamentally closed-set.

entry.title: Uncertainty Identifies Difficult Samples Across Methods: A Multi-Task Study on a Heterogeneous Skin Lesion Dataset

author.name: Leon Koole, Jiapan Guo, Matias Valdenegro-Toro

entry.summary: Five uncertainty quantification methods are compared on a pooled skin lesion dataset with a shared backbone and two heads for malignancy and five-class diagnosis, evaluated on calibration, uncertainty decomposition and risk-coverage. Difficulty rankings are largely method-agnostic, with per-sample entropy correlations from 0.54 to 0.91, so the choice of method matters more for calibration than for identifying hard cases.

entry.title: Identifying parameter couplings and uncertainties of mixed-noise stochastic systems via full-covariance Gaussian mixture network

author.name: Xiaolong Wang, Xiangwen Hao, Jing Feng, Yuanyuan Liu, Yong Xu

entry.summary: PENN-GMD maps partially observed trajectories of stochastic systems driven by mixed noise to a full-covariance Gaussian mixture over parameters, trained by maximizing likelihood through a surjective parameterization that hard-encodes mixture constraints. The full covariances expose parameter couplings and multimodal likelihood structure that point estimates and diagonal uncertainties hide.

entry.title: A Counterexample to the Tang Zhang Schatten Norm Conjecture and Sharp Positive Results

author.name: Zijian Zeng, Houde Liu, Kurunathan Ratnavelu

entry.summary: Disproves a conjectured sharp constant relating the Schatten norm of a sum of matrices to the norm of the sum of their absolute values, using explicit rank-one 2x2 counterexamples at p equal to three halves. The authors also prove the conjecture does hold for rank-at-most-one families when p is at least two, and classify equality cases.

entry.title: Adaptive Heterogeneous Compression for Resource-Efficient Federated Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Chenwang Liu, Yijun Liu, Chang Liu, Xu Zhang, Pengchao Han

entry.summary: Proposes letting each client in a federated knowledge distillation setup choose its own gradient compression strategy based on its model architecture and resource budget, rather than applying one uniform compression scheme across clients. The aim is to cut communication overhead at the network edge while preserving distillation quality.

entry.title: Continuous Quantum Feedback Control via Kraus-Parameterized Belief Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Priyanshi Singh, Krishna Bhatia

entry.summary: Combines a recurrent encoder constrained to a Stiefel manifold, which guarantees physically valid density-matrix estimates, with a PPO policy that maps those belief states to continuous control actions for a continuously monitored qubit. Embedding quantum state geometry into the learning loop yields stable feedback control with high belief fidelity.

entry.title: Domain-Agnostic Neural Topic Modeling with Contextual Token-Level Semantic Graph Representation

author.name: Seung-Won Seo, Won Ik Cho, Yongmin Yoo

entry.summary: Argues that neural topic models lose interpretability on specialized corpora because domain-specific terms collapse into an indistinguishable region of the pretrained embedding space, and that neither retraining, word-level graph enrichment, nor parameter-efficient fine-tuning fixes this geometry. The proposed remedy is a learnable graph layer over token-level embeddings that builds corpus-specific semantic structure on top of a frozen encoder.

entry.title: The politics of postmortem privacy

author.name: Mauricio Figueroa

entry.summary: A legal and conceptual analysis of postmortem privacy, arguing that the concept is internally unstable across its scope, its justificatory foundations, and its uneven treatment across jurisdictions. The paper frames these tensions collectively as the politics of postmortem privacy.

entry.title: Nonlocal Transition Kernel for Efficient Learning of Restricted Boltzmann Machines

author.name: Kaiji Sekimoto, Muneki Yasuda

entry.summary: The authors propose a nonlocal Markov chain transition kernel for training restricted Boltzmann machines, aiming to escape the poor mixing of blocked Gibbs sampling when the energy landscape has high barriers, while avoiding the multi-step traversal that deep tempering requires. Better sampling directly translates into better gradient estimates and learning. The contribution is an improved sampler for a classical energy-based model.

entry.title: Memory Is Communication: The Frontier Between Remembering and Signaling

author.name: Yashar Talebirad, Eden Redman, Ali Parsaee, Osmar R. Zaiane

entry.summary: Formalizes the tradeoff a bounded agent faces between retaining its own history and requesting information from peers, defining an efficient boundary between memory rate and message rate at a fixed performance level. It hypothesizes that agents with more useful history need proportionally less peer communication.

entry.title: Can Large Language Models Explain Flight Safety Events? A Prior-Guided Semantic LLM-based Approach

author.name: Lu Xu, Xu Li, Linjiang Zheng, Fan Li, Riquan Zhang, Jiaxing Shang

entry.summary: FlightLLM uses prior-guided semantic prompting to make LLMs explain flight safety events in terms of pilot control behavior rather than opaque feature importance scores. Addresses modality mismatch, weak classification, scarce fine-tuning data, and missing domain knowledge in aviation safety analysis.

entry.title: Graphectory Viewer: A Tool for Process-Centric Analysis of Agentic Software Trajectories

author.name: Charlie Jyu, Shuyang Liu, Reyhaneh Jabbarvand

entry.summary: Graphectory Viewer is a web tool that converts raw software-agent execution traces from multiple frameworks into phase-aware graphs, with node-level inspection of thoughts, actions, and observations plus Sankey summaries of problem-solving phase transitions. It supports search and filtering across large trajectory collections. It targets the growing need to debug and compare coding-agent behavior.

entry.title: Analysis of Types of Inquiries in Student-AI Interaction: A case study of two CS2 tasks

author.name: Matin Amoozadeh, Amin Alipour

entry.summary: The paper classifies 830 student-AI interactions from two CS2 programming tasks into 18 question types using a few-shot classifier, tracking how inquiry patterns evolve during problem solving. It offers empirical grounding for how learners actually query generative AI tutors.

entry.title: Paired Exact-Reset Evaluation of a Prediction-Derived Medium-to-Full World-Model Cascade

author.name: Malo de Pastor

entry.summary: This work proposes a paired exact-reset audit protocol to decide when routing from a cheaper medium world-model predictor to a frozen full predictor actually reduces task loss enough to pay for the extra compute. It is evaluated on a PushT manipulation bank with identical reset states for all candidate actions.

entry.title: LLM-based Framework for Generating and Verifying Parallel DEVS Statecharts

author.name: Vamsi Krishna Vasa, Hessam S. Sarjoughian, Edward J. Yellig

entry.summary: An agentic LLM pipeline that drafts and then verifies Parallel DEVS statecharts for discrete-event simulation models, using generated facts from a system description plus a controlled-correction loop to catch logical inconsistencies. It targets the modeling bottleneck in simulation engineering.

entry.title: Multi-Granularity Sentiment Integration for LLM-Based Multimodal Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Shanshan Lin, Yuesheng Wu, Chao Chen, Yizhe Yang, Zhihao Chen, Zexian Yang, Xiangwen Liao

entry.summary: MGSI encodes audio and visual streams at short, medium, and long temporal granularities before fusing them with an LLM, arguing that shallow projection or coarse pooling destroys fine-grained affective cues. It targets multimodal sentiment polarity and intensity prediction.

entry.title: Transfer Learning of Keystroke Dynamics for Cross-Device User Authentication

author.name: Nuwan Kaluarachchi, Sevvandi Kandanaarachchi, Kristen Moore, Arathi Arakala, Conrad Sanderson

entry.summary: This paper adapts keystroke-dynamics authentication models learned on one device to a second device with a different form factor using inductive transfer learning, then combines adapted and native data. It addresses the typing-pattern distribution drift that breaks single-device behavioral biometrics.

entry.title: Learning Generalizable Reconstruction of High-Dimensional Neural Dynamics

author.name: Anima Kujur, Zahra Monfared

entry.summary: PCA-DMD reconstructs long multichannel local field potential recordings by windowing signals, projecting into a compact PCA space, learning linear Koopman dynamics there, and reassembling with overlap-add. It reports better distributional fidelity than several dynamic mode decomposition variants and strong zero-shot cross-subject generalization on hippocampal data.

entry.title: Data-Efficient and Interpretable Classification of Circulating Tumor Cell Phenotypes in Microfluidic Devices via Deep Learning

author.name: Serena Su, Yifan Wang, Senwei Liang

entry.summary: This work classifies circulating tumor cell phenotypes from the kinematic trajectories they trace through label-free microfluidic obstacle courses, an inverse problem made analytically intractable by nonlinear fluid-structure interaction. The approach targets data efficiency and physical interpretability given limited trajectory data.

entry.title: Auxiliary uncertainty signals for LLM-assisted systematic review screening: a benchmark across eight Cohen drug-class reviews

author.name: Arya Rahgozar, Pouria Mortezaagha

entry.summary: This benchmark tests whether an auxiliary BERT plus graph convolutional classifier can supply calibrated uncertainty signals that make LLM title-abstract screening for systematic reviews more efficient, across eight drug-class review datasets with repeated cross-validation. It compares five prompt-delivery strategies to find the best benefit-to-cost ratio.

entry.title: Anatomy of a Quantized Agent: VRAM Stability and Forecasting in Code-Synthesis Agentic Workloads

author.name: Anubhab Banerjee

entry.summary: This measurement study tests whether closed-form models decomposing peak GPU memory into weights, key-value cache and activations can forecast memory use for a coding agent that synthesizes CUDA kernels, across four backbones, four-bit quantization and nearly two thousand trajectories on one accelerator. Analytical models are accurate once two empirical constants, loaded weight memory and a fixed activation overhead, are supplied.

entry.title: Maintaining IoT Device Identification under Concept Drift via Budget-Aware Traffic Labeling

author.name: Shayan Azizi, Norihiro Okui, Masataka Nakahara, Ayumu Kubota, Gustavo Batista, Hassan Habibi Gharakaheili

entry.summary: Studies how to keep IoT device-type classifiers accurate as network behavior drifts, arguing that the decision of how much traffic to label should be separated from which instances to label. Drift-detector-only selection misses parts of the emerging behavior space, so the authors combine it with uniform sampling under a labeling budget.

entry.title: Learning Varying Physical Therapist-Patient Interactions for Robot-mediated Upper Limb Task-Specific Training

author.name: Jia Quan Loh (Human Robotics Laboratory, Department of Mechanical Engineering, The University of Melbourne), Vincent Crocher (Human Robotics Laboratory, Department of Mechanical Engineering, The University of Melbourne), Marlena Klaic (Melbourne School of Health Sciences, The University of Melbourne), Denny Oetomo (Human Robotics Laboratory, Department of Mechanical Engineering, The University of Melbourne), Ying Tan (Human Robotics Laboratory, Department of Mechanical Engineering, The University of Melbourne)

entry.summary: Develops a learning-from-demonstration framework so rehabilitation robots can reproduce the personalized physical interaction patterns of a human therapist across varying practice conditions during upper-limb task-specific training. The premise is that generic robot assistance has failed to beat conventional therapy partly because it does not capture therapist-patient interaction and practice variability.

entry.title: GOD: Enhancing Generalization via Deep Grafting for Sequential Recommendation

author.name: WooJoo Kim, JunYoung Kim, JaeHyung Lim, HwanJo Yu

entry.summary: Proposes a component-level distillation method for sequential recommenders in which selected frozen teacher components are grafted into the student, so that the source of weak generalization can be isolated to embeddings, encoding, or co-adaptation to sparse histories. This contrasts with standard distillation that matches outputs or representations after running teacher and student independently.

entry.title: TokenSTFormer: A Tokenized Spatial-temporal Attention Model for Holistic Motion Analysis in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis Screening

author.name: Dong Chen, Kenneth M. C. Cheung

entry.summary: Releases a dataset of over 1,500 gait video clips paired with X-ray records for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis screening and introduces a spatial-temporal attention model that tokenizes motion semantics, reporting accuracy around 0.79 and beating a vanilla vision transformer encoder. The goal is scalable screening that does not depend on subjective expert interpretation.

entry.title: Convolution-Free Holistic Multivariance Decomposition Layer for Efficient Hyperspectral Image Classification Tensor Networks

author.name: S\"uha Tuna, \"Ulker Ba\c{s}ar

entry.summary: Introduces an end-to-end differentiable tensor decomposition layer for hyperspectral image classification that explicitly separates independent single-mode variation from cooperative higher-order interactions using learnable matrix-valued supports. It avoids convolutions and is trained jointly with the downstream classifier.

entry.title: Automating Learner Assessment: Benchmarking Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models for EEG-Based Familiarity Prediction

author.name: Isuru Nanayakkara, Thilina Halloluwa

entry.summary: Benchmarks fifteen classical ML and deep learning models on EEG data from 23 participants to predict whether a learner finds faces or math equations familiar. The main contribution is methodological: standard stratified cross-validation inflates F1 up to about 0.985 because of temporal leakage across adjacent EEG windows, so the reported ceiling is an artifact rather than genuine generalization.

entry.title: AerialYield-B2D: A Greenhouse Blueberry Dataset with Five-Stage Ripeness Masks and Fruit Counts

author.name: Iyyakutti Iyappan Ganapathi, Afeefa Azam, Muhammad Owais, Irfan Hussain, Yusra Abdulrahman

entry.summary: Releases AerialYield-B2D, a greenhouse blueberry dataset with 514 RGB images and over 30,000 annotated berry instances labeled across five ripeness stages, including class-specific and overall masks, semantic label maps, count tables, provenance hashes, and recommended splits. It targets the scarcity of dense ripeness-stage annotations for agricultural vision.

entry.title: QuantumNovelty: A Skill-Orchestrating Language Agent for Referee-Style Review and Patentability Screening of Quantum Papers and Patents

author.name: Shlomo Kashani

entry.summary: An open-source skill-orchestrating agent that both produces quantum-computing artifacts and reviews them through simulated referee and patent-examiner panels, constrained by deterministic gates including strict Pareto domination, numerical recomputation from stored artifacts, and cross-vendor consensus checks. The gates are designed to restrict rather than generate the claims allowed to survive.

entry.title: YILDIZ-VPR: A Novel Dataset with Dense Coverage Under Diverse Environmental Conditions for Visual Place Recognition

author.name: Serdar Yildiz, Abbas Memi\c{s}, Song\"ul Varli

entry.summary: YILDIZ-VPR is a new visual place recognition dataset collected by repeated pedestrian-level walking traversals of a university campus with a GoPro across times of day, seasons, and weather. It emphasizes dense coverage from human viewpoints, which existing vehicle-centric datasets lack. Useful for benchmarking condition-invariant localization.

entry.title: tinyDSM: A Framework for Skill Modeling and Development for Resource-Constrained Millirobots

author.name: Markus D. Kobelrausch, Michael Miedler, Axel Jantsch

entry.summary: tinyDSM is a developmental skill-modeling framework for centimeter-scale robots that pairs reinforcement learning with intrinsic motivation and fitness-based assessment, deliberately encoding minimal prior knowledge so the system discovers its own embodiment-specific dependencies over its lifetime. It emphasizes open-ended skill growth under severe compute and energy constraints. Relevant to embodied developmental learning on microcontrollers.

entry.title: p-Spin Glass Network Efficient Single-Batch Continual Learning

author.name: Vladimer Khasia

entry.summary: The p-Spin Glass Network is a physics-inspired sequence architecture claiming native ternary quantization for eight-fold parameter compression, bounded activation memory via exact implicit gradients, transformer-matching performance with eight times fewer training sequences, and single-batch continual learning stability. It targets memory and sample efficiency barriers simultaneously.

entry.title: NRCD: An Open Database of Collegiate Running with Unified Performance Standardization

author.name: Jonathan A. Karr Jr., Ryan M. Fryer, Ben Darden, Nicholas Pell, Kayla Ambrose, Evan Hall, Ramzi K. Bualuan, Nitesh V. Chawla

entry.summary: The National Running Club Database releases nearly 129 thousand approved collegiate running performances from about 29 thousand athletes across 1336 meets spanning 2004 to 2026, with unified performance standardization. It removes the bulk-download and gender-skew limitations of prior small-scale sports datasets.

entry.title: Shape Operator PCA: Curvature-Aware Projections for Geometric Machine Learning

author.name: Alexandre L. M. Levada

entry.summary: SHOPCA regularizes the PCA covariance matrix with an averaged local shape operator so principal directions favor both high variance and informative curvature of the data manifold, with a single mixing coefficient interpolating between classical PCA and a curvature-driven embedding. It targets unsupervised metric learning and dimensionality reduction.

entry.title: Fiber Fingerprints of Hidden Learning-State Dynamics

author.name: Qinyou Wang

entry.summary: This paper formalizes the idea that two learning systems can look identical under all present behavioral measurements yet respond differently to future training, using a construct called fiber fingerprints built from prefix-compatible probes and a Nerode-style minimal sufficient representation. It decomposes future-learning response into visible, mode-reuse, and irreducibly new components.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Noise2Noise-Enhanced Denoising for Continuous-Scan Air-Plasma THz Spectroscopy

author.name: Adam Umra, Oways Alsoloh, Oliver Nagy, Aydin Sezgin, Clara Saraceno

entry.summary: Trains a compact one-dimensional residual U-Net to denoise terahertz time-domain spectroscopy traces, comparing supervision against long-average references with a self-supervised strategy that maps one noisy trace to another. The payoff is recovering usable waveforms from a single delay sweep instead of averaging many, which directly cuts measurement time.

entry.title: Data-Driven Reconstruction of Spatially Resolved Electron and Ion Energy Distributions from Macroscopic Plasma Quantities with Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Libin Varghese, Kaushik Prajapati, Bhaskar Chaudhury

entry.summary: Asks whether non-invasively measurable macroscopic plasma observables contain enough information to reconstruct spatially resolved electron and ion energy distribution functions, and trains deep networks to solve this inverse problem. Success would replace invasive or shape-assuming diagnostics with inference from routine measurements.

entry.title: TF-CADE: Foreground-Concentrated Text-Video Alignment for Zero-Shot Temporal Action Detection

author.name: Yearang Lee, Ho-Joong Kim, Seong-Whan Lee

entry.summary: TF-CADE improves zero-shot temporal action detection by aggregating action-concentrated video segments into foreground representations before aligning them with class text embeddings, reducing text-irrelevant predictions on unseen action categories. The method emphasizes semantic distinction between action classes.

entry.title: How smoothing the affinity matrix affects neighborhood preservation in t-SNE

author.name: Shirin Mohebi, Guillaume Bied, Jefrey Lijffijt

entry.summary: This analysis introduces a row-wise power transform on the t-SNE affinity matrix that sharpens or smooths pairwise similarity distributions while preserving sparsity and rank order, and shows it is equivalent to rescaling Gaussian bandwidths. The study quantifies how this affects neighborhood preservation at different scales.

entry.title: Communication Reduction via Semantic-Based Encoding in DMPC Using LSTMs

author.name: Torben Schiz, Pedro H. J. Nardelli, Henrik Ebel

entry.summary: This paper reduces the communication load of distributed model predictive control by inserting LSTM encoder-decoder networks that compress each agent's message and reconstruct it at the receiver, a form of semantic compression. Experiments with mobile robot formations show acceptable control performance retained under bandwidth conditions that would break full-message exchange. It links learned compression to distributed optimization for multi-robot control.

entry.title: GPT-2's IOI behavior is defined where the paper's algorithm isn't

author.name: Zach Allen

entry.summary: This post points out that the widely cited indirect object identification circuit account leaves undefined what should happen when the indirect object token itself is duplicated, yet the model still performs correctly, and asks the community how to interpret and follow up on this. It is a probe of the completeness of a canonical mechanistic interpretability result. The value lies in stress-testing an oft-reused benchmark explanation.

entry.title: What If AI Carried Her Imagination? Black Girls as Creators in an AI Storytelling Weekend Program

author.name: Chun Li, Lauren Brown, Hubert Asare, Shawna Patterson, Dennis Henderson, Ericka Roland, tara Nkrumah, Angela E. B. Stewart

entry.summary: Reports on a seven-weekend AI storytelling program for Black girls aged 10 to 12, grounded in Afrofuturism and Black feminist thought, in which participants built counter-narratives while learning prompt engineering and bias critique. Analyzes learner artifacts to document emerging AI literacies and identity-rooted creative work.

entry.title: ComNetX: Local Hierarchical Adaptation for Dynamic Community Detection

author.name: Aleksandr Konovalov, Anna Uporova, Alexander Drobyshev, Iaroslav Egorov, Grigoriy Bokov

entry.summary: ComNetX provides solver-agnostic local updates for dynamic community detection by maintaining a multi-level community state and expanding only the affected region rather than recomputing entire snapshots. It aims to preserve mature static solver semantics while avoiding repeated processing of unchanged graph areas.

entry.title: The Acknowledgment Point Is the System: Durable Policy-Decision Receipts for AI Audit Evidence

author.name: Neeraj Kumar Singh Beshane

entry.summary: A systems prototype that binds every deterministic AI policy decision to its exact policy source, commits a privacy-minimizing record at a caller-chosen durability boundary, and returns a signed receipt stating whether the write completed, with chained Merkle attestations for post-restart verification. It argues that audit evidence is only meaningful if durability and trust boundaries are explicit. Relevant to emerging AI compliance and audit requirements.

entry.title: iFuzz-Meta: An Interpretable Fuzzy Learning Framework Bridging Top-Down and Bottom-Up Knowledge Integration

author.name: Xiaowei Jiang, Daniel Leong, Beining Cao, Nan Zhou, Yingtao Ren, Yu-Cheng Chang, Thomas Do, Chin-Teng Lin

entry.summary: iFuzz-Meta embeds interpretable fuzzy rules, each corresponding to a semantic and spatial prototype in the original feature space, inside a neural architecture, and uses meta-learning to study how those rules reorganize across tasks. The aim is transparent inference alongside modern adaptation.

entry.title: Population Structure Analysis of an Inbred Population using Quantitative Shape Phenotyping from Stereo Retinal Photographs

author.name: Li Tang, Michael D Abramoff

entry.summary: Analyzes the population structure of an inbred island community by reconstructing three-dimensional optic nerve head shape from stereo fundus photographs and learning hierarchical shape features with a neural network. Selected features distinguish descendants of a historical founder population from other residents.

entry.title: ReliaGate: Reliability Routing for Low-Stakes Wearable Stress Prediction

author.name: Jaden Moon, Yu Wu, Arvind Pillai, Andrew Campbell

entry.summary: ReliaGate studies whether a wearable stress classifier should show or withhold a fixed prediction, framing this as post-hoc reliability routing rather than label correction. It combines confidence, signal quality, agreement, and atypicality cues into a correctness score and evaluates across four wearable datasets with subject-disjoint folds.

entry.title: SoftModel: A Neural Model That Grows Its Own Topology -- Governed Structural Growth for Continual In-Service Learning

author.name: Zhoumin Xie

entry.summary: SoftModel takes total plasticity as an axiom, treating network topology itself as a learnable degree of freedom, and defines an algebra of structural growth operators covering width, hierarchy, composition, input interface, cycles, and attention heads for lifelong in-service learning. Stability is meant to come from governance of growth rather than freezing.

entry.title: One Residual with Three Reuses: A Wristband Front End for Gesture Sensing

author.name: Sam Rifaki

entry.summary: This design study builds an always-on wristband sensing front end that shares one on-chip residual generator across classifier wake-up gating, radar-versus-IMU sensor routing, and Kalman filter measurement reweighting, fitting into a coin-cell power budget on a commodity edge microcontroller. Reported footprints are tens of kilobytes of program memory and around 110K multiply-accumulates per frame.

entry.title: The Ethical Decision Head: Operationalizing Normative Ethics in Autonomous Vehicles via Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback

author.name: Thomas Mbrice, Ammar Ali, Sami Mian, Khai Hern Low, Eric Chen, Arshia Aghajani, Wolf Sch\"afer, Amin Shirangi

entry.summary: The Ethical Decision Head encodes normative ethical principles as a differentiable reward signal so a policy-gradient agent learns morally-aligned driving behavior in CARLA-aligned scenarios, instantiating utilitarian and Kantian frameworks for comparison. It aims at the moral dimension of Level 4 and 5 autonomous vehicle decision systems.

entry.title: Prompting is not enough: supervised baselines and leakage control for measuring shared decision-making with LLMs in pediatric encounters

author.name: Bernardo Modenesi, Jody Lin, Kimberly Kaphingst, Angela Zhu, Maya Wheeler, Peilu Zhang, Angela Fagerlin

entry.summary: Using 21 recorded pediatric surgical consultations with expert-coded shared decision-making behaviors, the study compares zero-shot prompting of a mid-size open model against a supervised classifier over frozen sentence embeddings under patient-grouped nested evaluation. The conclusion is that prompting alone is insufficient and supervision plus leakage control adds substantial value.

entry.title: Distinguishing AI-Generated Music from Edited Audio as a Hard-Negative Robustness Task

author.name: Alexandru-Stefan Morosanu, Valerian Cecan, Stefan-Daniel Achirei, Laura Erhan

entry.summary: The paper reframes AI-generated music detection as a hard-negative robustness task by training and evaluating detectors to separate AI-generated tracks from merely edited human recordings that have been remixed, re-encoded or pitch-shifted from the same anchor songs. The dataset is compiled from YouTube with original tracks used only as references.

entry.title: Integrating Persuasion Theory into the Epidemiological Modelling of Health Misinformation Spread on Social Media

author.name: Mkululi Sikosana, Sean Maudsley-Barton, Oluwaseun Ajao

entry.summary: Extends the classic epidemic SIR model to six compartments capturing the misinformation lifecycle, then modulates transmission rates using psychological signals drawn from persuasion theory such as sentiment, engagement, and cognitive effort. The result is a hybrid behavioral-epidemiological simulator for health misinformation spread.

entry.title: Coded Hankel Polynomial Chaos: Spectral Identification of Dominant Polynomial-Chaos Modes

author.name: Zhiliang Deng, Xiaomei Yang

entry.summary: Reformulates identification of dominant polynomial-chaos expansion modes as a spectral problem, converting expansion coefficients into a generating polynomial whose evaluation along a geometric phase orbit yields a finite exponential sum with low-rank Hankel structure. Root-of-unity labels from coordinate phase shifts then recover the full multi-indices.

entry.title: Digital Twin Degradation: Detecting Cyber Physical Attacks via Temporal Inconsistencies

author.name: Konstantinos E. Kampourakis, Vasileios Gkioulos, Sokratis Katsikas

entry.summary: Proposes detecting cyber-physical attacks by monitoring temporal consistency between a physical system and its digital twin, training a predictor only on normal behavior and flagging divergences that may indicate manipulation, delay, or sensor degradation. The key premise is that digital twin fidelity cannot be assumed in adversarial settings.

entry.title: POI Recommendation with LLM-Augmented Multi-Graph Learning and Contrastive Alignment

author.name: Burak Tamer, Wolfram H\"opken, Zehui Wang

entry.summary: Extends a graph-based point-of-interest recommender with two auxiliary item-item graphs to address cold start: a semantic graph from embeddings of LLM-generated photo summaries and keywords, and a geographic graph from great-circle distances between businesses. Item representations propagate across all graphs with contrastive alignment.

entry.title: Where A Small Language Model Helps in Invoice Categorisation, Understood Through Embedding Geometry

author.name: Emma Ceccherini, Daniel Lawson, Anjulika Salhan

entry.summary: This applied study examines where a small in-house language model helps for assigning invoices to general ledger codes, analyzing the pretrained embedding geometry of a sentence transformer and a compact encoder model to explain when classification succeeds. The motivation is cost, confidentiality, and interpretability advantages of small models over frontier APIs for financial back-office work. The embedding-geometry lens gives some diagnostic insight rather than just accuracy numbers.

entry.title: Spatially explicit feature importance for building height estimation using research-access high-resolution SAR and optical sensors

author.name: Guilherme Iablonovski, Pierre-Louis Frison, Tatiana Silva da Silva

entry.summary: This study estimates per-building heights in a large Brazilian city using research-license TerraSAR-X StripMap and PlanetScope imagery alongside Sentinel-1, and analyzes feature importance spatially rather than globally. The motivation is material stock accounting and post-disaster damage assessment in regions lacking LiDAR or affordable very high resolution imagery. The spatially explicit interpretability angle is the methodological twist.

entry.title: AI Sandbagging (w/ Inspect)

author.name: Leo H

entry.summary: A sprint project replicating prior work on sandbagging, the strategic underperformance of models on capability evaluations, using the Inspect evaluation framework on frontier models. The author frames the incentive problem by analogy to automotive emissions defeat devices. Replication of evaluation-gaming results is useful infrastructure work for governance-relevant testing.

entry.title: Validated Adaptation for Aerial Crowd Monitoring at Mass Gathering Scale: A Deployment Protocol, a Severity Law, and a Diagnostic for Label-Free Drone Crowd Counting, Toward the FIFA World Cup 2034 (Saudi Arabia)

author.name: AlAnoud AllGhayth, AlJawharh AlOtaibi, Jude AlSubaie

entry.summary: Studies label-free domain adaptation for drone-based crowd counting at mass-gathering scale, reporting recovery of 31 to 49 percent of shift-induced error across corruption types and severities across 525 controlled runs. Also proposes a severity scaling law and a safety-interlock evaluation for early crush warning.

entry.title: Education-centered critical policy analysis of AI: Ghana's AI strategy as a case

author.name: Matthew Nyaaba, Vida Awinime Bugri, Eric Kojo Majialuwe, Bismark Nyaaba Akanzire, Ibrahim Nantomah, Felicia Boateng, Patrick Kyeremeh, Benjamin Quarshie, Ellen Kwarteng, Macharious Nabang

entry.summary: The paper builds an education-centered framework with six components and applies it to Ghana's national AI strategy for 2025 to 2035, examining teacher agency, curriculum, language and culture, and learner protection. It concludes the strategy is ambitious but under-specifies pedagogy and implementation governance. Useful for understanding how Global South AI policy treats education as more than workforce supply.

entry.title: MoFE: A Novel Mixture-of-Experts Framework with Fourier Neural Operators for Cryptocurrency Forecasting

author.name: Bowen Liu, Mingming Sun

entry.summary: MoFE combines Fourier neural operators with a mixture-of-experts architecture for cryptocurrency price forecasting, framing volatility as a superposition of multi-frequency components tied to network growth, mining costs, and halving cycles. The stated aim is to reduce the phase-lag artifacts that plague deep forecasters on non-stationary financial series. Architecture-level idea applied to a notoriously difficult prediction target.

entry.title: Iterative Grasp Pose Refinement: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for 2D Vision

author.name: Amir Arsalan Nematollahi, Shayan Ahmadi, Mehdi Tale Masouleh, Ahmad Kalhor

entry.summary: A deep Q-network iteratively refines initial geometric grasp candidates using keypoint-based object representations from 2D overhead images, converting previously failed grasps into successful ones on 300 Dex-Net objects with a simulated UR5. The reported success rate on formerly ungraspable objects is complete in simulation. Compact representation-plus-RL approach to grasp correction.

entry.title: GADR: Gathering Architecture Decision Records from Meeting Transcriptions

author.name: Lucas Daniel Costa da Silva, Kiev Gama

entry.summary: GADR is a multi-agent self-correcting workflow that extracts architectural decisions from raw, noisy meeting transcripts and drafts records in the standard Nygard format, targeting the realistic case where decisions are implicit and tangled with off-topic talk. A feasibility study used five real project meetings, four senior architect reviewers, and fifteen student evaluators. Addresses documentation debt in software teams.

entry.title: Ring-based Spatial Transformer: Learning Non-linear Spatial Interactions between Building Distribution and Pedestrian Flow

author.name: Shun Nakayama, Takahiro Kanamori, Wanglin Yan

entry.summary: A ring-based spatial transformer treats concentric 100-meter buffers around Tokyo rail stations as tokens and uses self-attention to learn how building uses at different distances jointly generate pedestrian flow. It outperforms geographically weighted regression across 30 trials, with SHAP indicating mid-to-outer rings dominate.

entry.title: 6G Native AI and Channel Foundation Models

author.name: Shugong Xu, Jun Jiang, Yuan Gao

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that AI in 6G should be co-designed into the wireless stack rather than bolted on, and that task-specific supervised models are inadequate because they need labels and generalize poorly across propagation environments. It proposes channel foundation models as the technical basis for native AI in future radio systems.

entry.title: On Cross-Validation for Hyperparameter Optimization of Deep Learning Image Classifiers

author.name: Ljubomir Buturovic (East Palo Alto, United States)

entry.summary: A controlled comparison of three hyperparameter-optimization validation protocols, fixed holdout, reshuffled holdout and five-fold cross-validation, measured by how closely the winning configuration's validation AUROC matches its test AUROC. Everything else in the pipeline is held constant across three public image datasets spanning small and larger sample regimes.

entry.title: An Adaptive Gradient Clipping and Noise Injection Mechanism for Differentially Private Federated Learning

author.name: Wenjing Wei, Alla Jammine, Farid Nait-Abdesselam

entry.summary: This method sets per-layer, per-round gradient clipping thresholds in differentially private federated learning from the median of each client's per-sample gradient norms, so noise is calibrated to evolving gradient scales instead of one static bound. It is combined with secure aggregation to preserve privacy during averaging.

entry.title: The Physical Cutoff Does Not Restore Homogenization: Phase-Dependent Burning in the Strain G-Equation

author.name: Michele Caprio

entry.summary: A mathematical paper disproving a conjecture that the physically motivated positive-part strain G-equation admits an effective burning velocity in two-dimensional cellular flows, showing instead phase-dependent burning where an order-one value gap persists between nearby points at every positive time. This means the rescaled solutions have no locally uniformly convergent subsequence, so homogenization fails.

entry.title: BERTopic-Virality Prioritisation: A Scalable Framework for Thematic and Comparative Analysis of COVID-19 and Monkeypox Misinformation on Twitter

author.name: Mkululi Sikosana, Sean Maudsley-Barton, Oluwaseun Ajao

entry.summary: Builds a topic-modeling pipeline that ranks topics not only by semantic coherence but also by how fast they are spreading, combined with a two-stage misinformation detector that fuses a supervised classifier with public-health knowledge-base verification. It is applied comparatively to COVID-19 and monkeypox Twitter data.

entry.title: Ask to Be Sure: Informative Interactions for Confident Multi-Turn LLM Recommendation

author.name: Cedar Site Bai, Duanshun Li, Zhenyu Liao, Sheikh Sarwar, Huiyuan Chen, Yuan Chen, Changhe Yuan, Haiyang Zhang, Qilin Qi

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.15949v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled their use as conversational recommender systems (CRS), demonstrating strong recommendati...

entry.title: Language Has Two Parameters: Narrative-Induced Semantic Plasticity and Phase-Sensitive Interpretation

author.name: Hollis Robbins (University of Utah)

entry.summary: A theoretical humanities argument that language carries a second parameter beyond co-occurrence amplitude, called phase, which governs how coactivated meanings combine and can invert a meaning's contribution while it remains present. The claim is that corpus averaging over speakers deletes history-indexed phase, so embeddings and attention weights can only recover the population marginal.

entry.title: MS-MFAD : Multimodal large language models for Face Anti-spoofing Detection

author.name: Xiaoyong Yu, Rongzhen Li, Shuming Shi, Xinge You

entry.summary: MS-MFAD adapts multimodal LLMs to face anti-spoofing by anchoring fine-grained pixel evidence to semantic descriptions, producing auditable reasoning rather than opaque binary decisions, and introduces a semantic-level annotation benchmark. The goal is better generalization across both generative and physical presentation attacks.

entry.title: TEAMS: Text-prompted spatiotEmporal dual-heAd Mamba Snake

author.name: Ruicheng Zhang, Jianhui Lei, Kaiwen Shen, Haowei Guo, Jun Zhou, Bin Chen, Mengtang Li, Shen Zhao, Shuo Li

entry.summary: TEAMS is a text-prompted contour-based instance segmentation framework that combines a spatiotemporal snake evolution strategy with dual-head Mamba state-space modules to handle complex organ morphology and fix detection errors. It targets medical image segmentation where pixel-wise masks show cavities and jagged boundaries.

entry.title: GSToken: Geometry-Structured Gaussian Tokens for Compact 3D Medical Image Representation

author.name: Xiaoduo Li, Quan Gu

entry.summary: GSToken represents 3D medical volumes as geometry-structured Gaussian tokens so that compressed tokens explicitly carry lesion shape and spatial extent, unlike fixed patch or attention-pooled tokens. The paper also argues for disentangling tokenizer information retention from decoder capacity when evaluating compression schemes.

entry.title: S$^3$AM: A Single-Stream SAM with Reliability-Calibrated Frequency Adapter for Multi-modal Salient Object Detection

author.name: Ruichao Hou, Boyue Xu, Tongwei Ren, Dongming Zhou, Gangshan Wu, Jinde Cao

entry.summary: S3AM adapts a promptable segmentation foundation model to multi-modal salient object detection with a single-stream encoder plus a reliability-calibrated frequency adapter, avoiding duplicated backbones while controlling how noisy auxiliary high-frequency cues are injected. The design cuts computation relative to dual-stream approaches.

entry.title: NeuroPath: Brain-Inspired Dual-Pathway Graph Convolutional Networks for Skeleton-Based Action Recognition

author.name: Kanglei Zhou, Ruizhi Cai, Hubert P. H. Shum, Frederick W. B. Li, Xiaohui Liang

entry.summary: NeuroPath proposes a dual-pathway graph convolutional architecture for skeleton-based action recognition, inspired by ventral and dorsal visual streams, that models structural and motion cues separately before combining them. The design is motivated by observed performance imbalance across skeletal modalities.

entry.title: Leveraging existing sparse point annotations for benthic imagery dense segmentation

author.name: Cesar Borja, Breck A. McCollum, Jarret E. Byrnes, Kenneth Sebens, Ana C. Murillo

entry.summary: This work turns legacy sparse expert point labels from historical underwater surveys into visual prompts for segmentation foundation models, producing dense benthic segmentation without new expert annotation. It targets scalable marine ecosystem monitoring.

entry.title: CoinVE-200K: A Large-Scale High-Quality Dataset for Compositional Instruction-Guided Video Editing

author.name: Fuchen Long, Cong Wang, Zitao Gao, Wenhao Zhong, Yu Cheng, Xiaolu Hou, Yan Li, Xiao Cao, Xinlong Sun, Xi Chen, Yu Liu

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.17566v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quality and diversity of instruction-based video editing datasets are steadily improving, yet existing datasets mainly focus on single editing oper...

entry.title: MaLViL: Multi-axis Low-rank Vision-LSTM for Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Afshin Bozorgpour, Sina Ghorbani Kolahi, Moein Heidari, Ilker Hacihaliloglu, Dorit Merhof

entry.summary: MaLViL extends Vision-LSTM sequence modeling beyond the bottleneck to full decoder resolutions for medical segmentation using bidirectional low-rank recurrence, scale-aware serialization that preserves cross-axis adjacency, and a mixer fusing horizontal and vertical scan paths. The design keeps global context affordable while retaining fine anatomical detail.

entry.title: Monitoring Pasture Restoration from Satellite Image Time Series: Caveats and Opportunities

author.name: Linnea Sartorius, Isak Randahl, Delia Fano Yela, Georg Andersson, Sadegh Jamali, Aleksis Pirinen

entry.summary: This work asks whether grassland restoration status can be classified directly from satellite image time series, and reports that weather, acquisition conditions and processing artifacts make genuine restoration signals hard to separate from irrelevant temporal variation. It documents caveats alongside opportunities for scalable ecological monitoring.

entry.title: Vision-Language Models for Analog Gauge Reading: An Empirical Study of Specialization, Transfer and Reliability

author.name: Abdul Mueez, Aaditya Baranwal, Junior Chaj-Mejia, Guneet Bhatia, Jason T. Voelker, Shruti Vyas

entry.summary: An empirical study of whether a general-purpose vision-language model can read analog gauges directly, comparing zero-shot prompting, in-context learning and quantized low-rank fine-tuning of a 7B open model across synthetic, video-derived and proprietary industrial datasets. It measures specialization, transfer, robustness and reliability rather than accuracy alone.

entry.title: SFMformer: A Spatial-Frequency Modulation Transformer for Lightweight Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Chih-Hsiang Yang, Chia-Min Lin, Ching-Yu Tsai, Yung-Che Wang, Jen-Shiun Chiang

entry.summary: SFMformer argues that sparse attention creates two separable quality targets, token selection and feature aggregation, and inserts spatial-frequency modulation modules before and after attention to improve each. The target application is lightweight image super-resolution.

entry.title: Optimize Your Sampling: Tuned Diffusion Sampling with Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Travis Zhang, Christian Belardi, Justin Lovelace, Jin Peng Zhou, Saebyeol Shin, Carla P. Gomes, Kilian Q. Weinberger

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.18040v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sampling from a diffusion model typically requires many forward passes through a large neural network, making generation computationally expensive. W...

entry.title: Robust Brachiation on a Life-Sized Dual-Arm Robot Using Waypoint-Guided Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ayumu Iwata, Kento Kawaharazuka, Keita Yoneda, Takahiro Hattori, Kei Okada

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.17320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Brachiation is a form of locomotion in which primates move primarily using their arms, enabling traversal in environments without footholds. However, t...

entry.title: Force-Based Offset Estimation for Keyed Peg-in-Hole Assembly Using Local Gaussian Process Regression

author.name: Chandra Yuvesh Aubeeluck, Abilash Philip Madavath, Augustin Raju, Nicolas Pyschny, Felix Hackel\"oer, Florian Zwanzig

entry.summary: This work estimates residual misalignment in keyed peg-in-hole assembly directly from wrist force and torque signals, using a hybrid nearest-neighbor and Gaussian process regressor with separate models routed by contact regime, distinguishing hard collision from guided chamfer insertion. It sits within a perception, validation, insertion pipeline with monocular visual pre-checks. The target application is high-precision industrial assembly under grasp uncertainty.

entry.title: Diagonal Multi-omics Integration of Heterogenous Datasets

author.name: Maksim V. Kukushkin, Mikhail S. Arbatskiy, Dmitriy E. Balandin, Alexey V. Churov

entry.summary: The paper develops methods for diagonal integration of heterogeneous multi-omics datasets, formulating the problem as extremal trace optimization for a coupled Laplacian on a Stiefel-manifold-like set in complex Euclidean space and deriving a gradient ascent procedure with functional-analytic justification. It also proposes a heterogeneity measure based on the distance between maximizing and minimizing points. The contribution is largely mathematical.

entry.title: Regularization of Statistical Inverse Problems on Non-Reflexive Banach Spaces

author.name: Darrel K Joseph, M P Rajan

entry.summary: The paper studies regularized stable approximation for statistical inverse problems where the operator domain is a non-reflexive Banach space and the observations are finitely many i.i.d. noisy samples of a function on a metric space. It provides convergence and regularization results in this harder functional-analytic setting. The contribution is purely mathematical inverse-problem theory framed for statistical learning.

entry.title: Toward Personal Intelligence Through Cooperative Observation

author.name: Yashar Talebirad, Osman Jime, Ali Parsaee, Eden Redman, Yongbin Kim, Osmar R. Zaiane

entry.summary: A position paper framing personal AI as bounded by what users allow it to observe, and arguing that observation is a cooperative loop where useful behavior earns broader access while failures cause users to revoke it. Emphasizes selection and compression under an observation bottleneck.

entry.title: AI, Brain Death Detection, and Islamic Law

author.name: Muhammad Aurangzeb Ahmad

entry.summary: Examines how machine learning systems that detect covert consciousness in brain-injured patients interact with Islamic legal concepts of evidentiary proof, epistemic certainty, and mandated agnosticism about the soul. Maps the technical literature onto brain-death jurisprudence and identifies unresolved challenges.

entry.title: In-Context Learning to Assess Built Environment Impacts on Perceived Neighborhood Walkability Among Mobility-impaired Older Adults

author.name: Houhao Liang, Kresimir Friganovic, Joanne Kua, Noor Hafizah Ismail, Su Su, Bryan Yijia Tan, Navrag B. Singh, Panos Mavros

entry.summary: The study applies the tabular foundation model TabPFN via in-context learning to a 257-person survey of mobility-impaired older adults, predicting perceived neighborhood walkability from built-environment features. Macro F1 reaches about 55 percent on a three-way classification.

entry.title: Quantifying the Gap Between Laboratory Battery Test Patterns and Field Duty Profiles

author.name: Chunyang Zhao, Chresten Tr{\ae}holt

entry.summary: This paper quantifies the mismatch between laboratory battery test protocols and real field duty profiles across six evidence sources using usage frequency, intensity, C-rate, and a duty-structure index. It finds lab cycling patterns can be several times more structured than real electric-vehicle traces, undermining transfer of lab-derived degradation models.

entry.title: Time-Aware Validation of Machine Learning Fuel Consumption Models: Evidence from 1\,Hz Operational Data, CCGS \textit{Sir Wilfrid Laurier}

author.name: Samarasimha Reddy Chittamuru, Ayhan Akinturk, Allison Kennedy, Joshua Barnes, Matthew Hamilton

entry.summary: Using 1 Hz operational data from a Canadian Coast Guard vessel, this paper shows that random train-test splits on high-frequency ship fuel consumption records leak temporal information and produce optimistic accuracy that does not survive time-series and blocked cross-validation. It advocates time-aware validation for deployment-realistic evaluation.

entry.title: STAR-FL: Secure Federated Learning with Spatial-Temporal Analysis and Robust Aggregation

author.name: Nawrin Tabassum, Yanzhao Wu

entry.summary: STAR-FL defends federated vision models against targeted data poisoning by clustering client updates over both space and time to flag malicious contributors, then damping the learning rate during aggregation to limit residual damage. It targets the twin problems of detecting bad updates and neutralizing those that slip through.

entry.title: Distribution-free false-alarm calibration and chance-corrected spatial evaluation for industrial anomaly detection

author.name: Jie Deng

entry.summary: For industrial visual inspection, this work replaces AUROC and raw mask overlap with a distribution-free upper tolerance threshold that pins the false-alarm rate and a paired-minus-crossed spatial test that credits a detector only for overlap exceeding chance from recurrent defect locations and mask geometry. Three detectors are evaluated on point-defect images across several modalities.

entry.title: Decentralized Federated Learning for Heterogeneous Multi-Task Semantic Communication

author.name: Lin Yin, Tiejun Lv, Weicai Li, Xi Yu, Xiaoyu He

entry.summary: The paper identifies negative transfer and overconsensus bias when topology-agnostic decentralized federated averaging is applied to heterogeneous multi-task semantic communication networks. It proposes policy-driven multi-path routing that separates task-specific from shared features at each node plus a task-affinity-calibrated column-stochastic consensus matrix for aggregation.

entry.title: FedADB: Class Anchor-Driven Dual-Branch Federated Learning for Mitigating Forgetting

author.name: Zhenyan Liu, Hua Zhang, Haoran Gao, Qi Li, Hongliang Zhu, Huiyu Zhou, Zongliang Shen, Yanxin Xu, Jiahui Wang

entry.summary: FedADB tackles forgetting of global knowledge during local federated training under multimodal client heterogeneity by using class anchors and a dual-branch design instead of global alignment strategies that suppress local optimization or proxy datasets that add overhead. The aim is to balance class-wise global consistency with local adaptation, especially for classes missing from a client.

entry.title: A Scalable Pipeline for LLM-Teacher Distillation Labeling: Work-Stealing Job Scheduling and Memory-Aware GPU Concurrency

author.name: Ravi Satya Durga Prasad Yenugula

entry.summary: Describes an infrastructure recipe for large-scale LLM-teacher labeling that combines a work-stealing queue design with exactly-once task claims via atomic compare-and-set on a single SQLite file, plus memory-aware GPU concurrency. It also frames the question of how much label quality a teacher model buys per dollar.

entry.title: Misaligned Incentives in Pause Scenarios

author.name: Michael Soareverix

entry.summary: A discussion write-up in which the author, previously a pause advocate, reports becoming more wary of pausing after conversation with a researcher, reasoning about how a pause following a major security incident could create misaligned incentives among labs and states. It references a sharp shift in community sentiment after a widely discussed model-security incident. The value is in surfacing second-order effects of pause policies.

entry.title: Demo: Real-time Generative Multicasting with On-Device Intent-aware Semantic Decomposition

author.name: Xinkai Liu, Mahdi Boloursaz Mashhadi, Yi Ma, Rahim Tafazolli

entry.summary: A demonstration system for semantic multicasting where a transmitter sends a segmentation-derived semantic map to all receivers and only the sub-signals each user cares about, letting a generative model locally synthesize the rest. The authors also derive rate-distortion-perception tradeoff curves for the mixed reconstruct-plus-synthesize regime.

entry.title: Phase-Aware CNN for Real-Time 5G/6G Channel Estimation with Hardware-in-the-loop Validation

author.name: Javad Zolfaghari-Bengar, Rakibul Rony, Elisa Gomez-de-Lope, Alejandro Villena-Rodriguez, Abhinav Mahadevan, Nicolas Kourtellis

entry.summary: A convolutional network estimates both magnitude and phase of the wireless channel from pilot symbols, explicitly handling phase wrap-around discontinuities that trip up prior deep estimators. Evaluation uses emulated data from an end-to-end O-RAN testbed with hardware in the loop rather than pure simulation.

entry.title: Beyond Binary Priorities: Multi-Tier SLA Scheduling for Large Language Model Serving

author.name: Anders Vestrum, Arya Raeesi, Hanna Roed

entry.summary: Extends an existing migration-capable multi-instance LLM inference scheduler beyond its two-level priority model to support an arbitrary number of service-level tiers, then evaluates the effect under several workload regimes. The motivation is that production deployments span latency-critical API traffic through background batch jobs.

entry.title: Continuity-Driven Representation Learning for Industrial Defect Detection

author.name: Minjong Kim, Hyun Jun Kim, Jeongrae Kim, Heeseung Shin, Changwon Lim
