entry.summary: LongDocBench targets document-level structure recovery in long visual documents, specifically reconstructing cross-page table-of-contents hierarchies and identifying typed one-to-many links from tables and figures to their captions, notes, and sources. These tasks are only partially covered by existing page-level parsing benchmarks.

entry.title: Constraint-Aware Synthetic Tabular Data Generation via Inter-Column Constraint Discovery with LLM Agents

author.name: Jianxing Zhao, Mao Guan, Dongyu Liu

entry.summary: Uses LLM agents to discover inter-column constraints in tabular data across three families, namely equations, linear inequalities, and logical dependencies, representing each as a machine-executable hypothesis validated against the full table. A generator-agnostic postprocessor then repairs synthetic data that is statistically faithful but semantically invalid, using counterexample-guided revision.

entry.title: ACTS-SQL: Agentic and Critic-Oriented Tree-Structured SQL Correctness with Large Language Models

author.name: Xinmei Huang, Jie Song, Peng Li, Fuxin Jiang, Jing Zhang, Tieying Zhang, Jianjun Chen, Chenming Liu, Tao Yang, Maoyin Liu, Wenda Li, Hong Chen, Cuiping Li

entry.summary: ACTS-SQL is a training-free framework that treats SQL error correction as plan-guided tree search with backtracking and critic feedback, instead of a single linear repair chain. Maintaining multiple correction strategies reduces error propagation from early mistakes in industrial text-to-SQL pipelines.

entry.title: The Benchmark Trap: Structures of Power and Injustice in AI Evaluations

author.name: Jason Branford, Angelie Kraft

entry.summary: Argues that AI benchmarks are power-laden socio-technical artifacts whose leaderboard rewards concentrate prestige and influence in well-resourced industry labs, and analyzes this through Iris Marion Young's theories of oppression and structural injustice. It maps current benchmarking practice onto specific forms of structural harm.

entry.title: When Entropy Is Not Enough: Reclaiming Lost Semantics in LLM Output Length Prediction

author.name: Feiyang Ren, Shengtao Wen, Lingbing Guo, Yu Tian, Yuanning Cui, Xiang Chen

entry.summary: Improves prediction of how long an LLM's output will be, arguing that token-entropy signals used by prior schedulers ignore semantic content and misweight informative tokens. The proposed entropy-and-semantics predictor supports length-aware batching and scheduling, which matters most for long-context reasoning and RL rollout serving.

entry.title: VARM-Bench: Benchmarking Verifiable Structured Reasoning in Chinese Abusive Speech Moderation

author.name: Mingyu Yuan, Shengtao Wen, Lingbing Guo, Zhen Bi, Xiang Chen

entry.summary: VARM-Bench evaluates whether a moderation model's stated rationale is verifiable, requiring Chinese abusive-speech judgments to be anchored in six explicit fields such as target, target type, explicitness, author stance, harm label and fine-grained category. A deterministic protocol checks field correctness rather than relying on free-text rationale grading.

entry.title: Argumentation for Common Ground: Finding Zones of Possible Agreement between Individuals in Conflict

author.name: Elisa Cavatorta, Antonio Rago

entry.summary: Uses quantitative bipolar argumentation frameworks to model each side's reasoning about peace-agreement clauses and merges these frameworks to identify mutually acceptable agreements, that is a zone of possible agreement. Offers negotiators a computational way to locate common ground under contested narratives.

entry.title: Protein Structure Prediction: From Evolutionary Constraints to Generative Modeling

author.name: Wengan He, Yongsheng Luo, Lihong Jiang, Wenhui Xu, Yu Li

entry.summary: A review tracing protein structure prediction from alignment-driven monomer folding toward generative modeling of complexes and heterogeneous molecular systems, organized around representations, data, and methodological evolution. It complements existing surveys by focusing on how methods themselves changed rather than on applications. Useful orientation for researchers entering structural biology modeling.

entry.title: AeroCopilotBench: A Two-Tier Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Agents as Aviation Copilots in an Interactive Virtual Cockpit Environment

author.name: Yuchen Yuan, Zhenghuang Wu, Yuangan Li, Liang Ma, Ke Li

entry.summary: AeroCopilotBench pairs an interactive virtual cockpit environment with a two-tier evaluation: 1,200 aviation knowledge questions and 73 emergency or abnormal procedure tasks derived from pilot operating handbooks and made executable in simulation. It moves aviation LLM evaluation from static knowledge toward procedural execution and safety compliance. The environment is reproducible for agent testing.

entry.title: Offline Reinforcement Learning for Hemodynamic Management of Sepsis in the ICU: a MIMIC-IV Study with Dual Off-Policy Evaluation

author.name: Marc P\'erez-Roig, David Fern\'andez-Narro, Carlos S\'aez

entry.summary: Using nearly 37,000 septic ICU stays from a public critical care database, the authors learn fluid and vasopressor dosing policies offline and evaluate them with dual off-policy estimators plus reliability diagnostics and clinician-agreement analyses. The emphasis is on making value estimates trustworthy rather than on beating clinicians. It responds to known optimism bias in earlier sepsis RL work.

entry.title: DeepInsight II: One Trace from Benchmark to Robot

author.name: Siyi Li, Yuchen Kang, Wuliang Wang, Zhengjie Zhang, Jiangpin Liu, Jianhao Yao, Jie Chen

entry.summary: DeepInsight II extends a unified evaluation substrate across the physical AI stack from foundation models down to navigation, manipulation, and whole-body control, and adds physical execution that the first report lacked. It keeps the task, resource, and result abstractions fixed while quantifying the embodied layers. The aim is standardized evaluation where deployment risk is highest.

entry.title: Calibrated Trust, Not Sharper Prediction: An Empirical Test of Uncertainty Fusion

author.name: Surya Saka

entry.summary: Testing whether stacking uncertainty machinery such as belief propagation, sequential Bayesian updating, evidence combination, and conformal prediction improves legal case-outcome prediction on one thousand European Court of Human Rights cases, the study compares raw frontier models against the same models routed through the fusion pipeline and a term-frequency baseline. It uses existing models (Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5, both available for months before this work) as per-fact evidence estimators. The conclusion is that fusion improves calibration rather than discrimination.

entry.title: Local AI pre-screening for human triple-blind peer review in health sciences

author.name: Rodrigo Martins Boos

entry.summary: Motivated by evidence that a large fraction of reviews at recent major conferences are AI-generated and by documented risks like hallucinated citations and hidden prompt-injection text planted in manuscripts, this paper proposes a locally hosted triple-blind multi-model pre-screening framework for health sciences peer review. The design keeps data local and uses multiple models to reduce single-model idiosyncrasy. It targets disclosed, controlled AI assistance instead of undisclosed use.

entry.title: Inference-Time Mitigation of Adversarial Political Bias in Large Language Models

author.name: Tejaswi V. Panchagnula, Bruce Coburn, Bryce J. Dietrich, Robert X. Browning, Edward J. Delp, Fengqing Zhu

entry.summary: This paper targets political bias as a safety-relevant harm that current alignment methods do not explicitly address, showing that instruction tuning can be exploited via adversarial prompt injection and proposing inference-time mitigation strategies including chain-of-thought based interventions. The setting is information retrieval and summarization where non-partisanship matters. It argues for treating partisan output as an alignment failure.

entry.title: Do Uncertainty Signals Help? A Systematic Study of Uncertainty-Aware Decoding with Rollback Mechanisms

author.name: Xianzong Wu, Xiaohong Li, Yuejun Guo, Xinyang Liu, Tianlin Li, Junjie Wang, Qiang Hu

entry.summary: A systematic study of whether token-level uncertainty signals can improve LLM code generation via rollback decoding, where unreliable spans are detected at inference and generation restarts from an earlier valid prefix. The work evaluates the framework without retraining, probing how far confidence estimates can substitute for extra training signal.

entry.title: Handoff-H1: An Orchestrated Vision-Agent System for Material Quantity Takeoff from Construction Blueprints

author.name: Bruno Chicelli, Henrique Alves, Rodrigo Anselmo, Joshua Weinberg, Felipe Lemos, Jan Baryla

entry.summary: Handoff-H1 is a production-oriented vision-agent system that converts architectural blueprint sets into material quantity takeoffs, combining purpose-built CV primitive extractors, tool-using agents with counting and detection tools, and a persistent hierarchical project representation grounded in construction knowledge. It is evaluated on a new benchmark of ten real residential blueprint sets with expert takeoffs.

entry.title: Max-Q Selective Imitation for Human-in-the-Loop Online Robot Learning

author.name: Zihang Wang, Yishan Wang

entry.summary: Presents a human-in-the-loop online RL method combining a Monte Carlo chunk-level critic that credits human intervention trajectories directly rather than diluting them through current-policy bootstrapping, with an actor update that imitates whichever of the policy action or buffer action has higher Q. The winner-take-all rule automatically switches between imitating the human and improving beyond them.

entry.title: An Evaluation Framework for National AI Regulation

author.name: Kaushik Sanjay Prabhakar, Tarun Adarsh R S, Amal Dhivyan Gregory, Sreeparvathy Sajeev, Utkarsh Tomar, Avyay M Casheekar

entry.summary: Builds a comparative framework for scoring national AI policy portfolios on documented design and implementation readiness, covering major jurisdictions plus the EU as a supranational comparator. Crucially it evaluates versioned bundles of binding and nonbinding instruments rather than a single flagship law.

entry.title: ETHOS: Towards a Modular Ethics Framework for Clinical Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Rakesh Sharma, Sydney Pugh, Cameron Beeche, Pankhuri Singhal, Rachel Wu, Margaret Eby, Jeffrey Duda, James Gee, Kyra O'Brien, Hersh Sagreiya, Marina Serper, Victoria Gershuni, Angela Bradbury, Anurag Verma, Eric Eaton, Kevin B. Johnson, Walter Witschey

entry.summary: Proposes a modular ethics and oversight architecture for clinical multi-agent LLM systems, translating high-level healthcare AI principles from bodies such as the WHO into hierarchical, implementable oversight components. The author list spans a large clinical and computer science collaboration.

entry.title: From Sequence to Structure: Relational Uncertainty Propagation for LLM Agents

author.name: Zhengzhao Ma. Boxi Cao, Yaojie Lu, Hongyu Lin, Xianpei Han, Le Sun

entry.summary: Argues that token-level or per-step confidence misses how agent errors accumulate, and models an execution history as a directed graph over reasoning states and tool interactions to propagate uncertainty at the trajectory level. The goal is to catch failures whose causes originated many steps before the final answer.

entry.title: STAIR: Semantic-Temporal Automaton for Interpretable Reasoning in Temporal Question Answering

author.name: Xinlong Dai, Jinchuan Zhang, Lei Gao, Xinzhe Hu, Yuefeng He, Hui Gao

entry.summary: STAIR separates semantic parsing from temporal computation in temporal question answering: an answer-free LLM adapter converts complex questions into normalized temporal intents, and a deterministic automaton performs exact interval and ordering inference. The design makes temporal decisions verifiable rather than probabilistic.

entry.title: VCE-Skill: Enhancing Skill Self-Evolution with Version-Change Experience

author.name: Jianming Chen, Xuanbin Ye, Yawen Wang, Junjie Wang, Qing Wang, Fanjiang XU

entry.summary: VCE-Skill improves agent skill self-evolution by mining public skill version histories for reusable evolution priors and adaptively fusing them with proposals derived from the agent's own execution trajectories. A pilot study motivates this by showing the two knowledge sources are complementary.

entry.title: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection for Image Dataset Quality Assurance in Multi-Center Breast MRI

author.name: Chiara Tappermann, Steffen Renisch, Lars Ole Schwen, Hans Meine, Horst K. Hahn, Eike Petersen

entry.summary: This study applies unsupervised anomaly and out-of-distribution detection as automated dataset quality assurance for multi-center dynamic contrast-enhanced breast MRI, building a controlled benchmark of 17 realistic anomaly types drawn from six public datasets, including protocol violations, processing errors, and wrong anatomical regions. It also proposes a perception-based taxonomy enabling fine-grained analysis of detector failure modes.

entry.title: PIKFNO: An Interpretable Neural Operator Based on Physics Informed Kernel Function

author.name: Yuan Guo, Hanshu Chen, Zhuojia Fu

entry.summary: PIKFNO embeds physics-informed kernel functions derived from the governing equations into a neural operator, constraining the trunk network so its structure aligns with kernel expansions used in meshless collocation methods rather than implicitly learning basis functions as DeepONet does. Two construction strategies are offered, one data-learned and one analytically derived.

entry.title: RouteTS: Frequency-Time Routing for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Gaofeng Lin, Lei Duan

entry.summary: RouteTS argues that the optimal computational domain for time series is a property of the data rather than the model, routing dominant frequency components to a complex-valued linear predictor while sending residual non-stationary components to time-domain processing. This targets the complementary failures of periodic misalignment and over-smoothed transients.

entry.title: p-Spin Glass Network Efficient Single-Batch Continual Learning

author.name: Vladimer Khasia

entry.summary: Introduces a p-spin glass network architecture claiming ternary quantization for eightfold parameter compression, exact implicit gradients that bound activation memory, transformer-matching asymptotic quality with eightfold fewer training sequences, and stability under single-batch continual updates. The framing is that large-batch stochastic optimization and heavy memory footprints block sample-efficient continual learning.

entry.title: A Unified Mamba--MoE Surrogate for Closed-Loop Simulation and Measurement-Window Forecasting of Inverter Transients

author.name: Haoguang Wang, Huy Hoang Le, Akhila Kandivalasa, Christian Moya, Marcos Netto, Guang Lin

entry.summary: Builds a single Mamba backbone with mixture-of-experts routing that serves both closed-loop simulation and measurement-window forecasting of inverter transients, replacing two specialist surrogates, with an adaptive conformal layer supplying prediction intervals for both tasks. Task conditioning and expert routing let one model handle two distinct prediction forms.

entry.title: Global Federated Learning Strategies for Building Efficient Personalized Models

author.name: Seongyoon Kim

entry.summary: A dissertation on federated learning strategies for personalized models, arguing that under increasing data heterogeneity the collapse of feature representations is a more fundamental bottleneck than classifier weight divergence, and proposing methods to preserve global knowledge during local adaptation. It covers both global training strategy and local personalization stages.

entry.title: Probability-Preserving Transformer for the Time-Dependent Schr\"odinger Equation

author.name: Mushtaq Ali, Muzamil Tariq, Niaz Ali Khan

entry.summary: Introduces a transformer for the time-dependent Schrodinger equation that enforces probability conservation as a hard architectural constraint, intrinsically guaranteeing unitarity across temporal evolution rather than penalizing violations softly. The authors report both exact conservation and better computational behavior than soft-constraint baselines.

entry.title: Guaranteed Adaptive Modality Acquisition: When the Policy Chooses Its Own Calibration Group

author.name: Melika Baghi

entry.summary: Studies conformal-style conditional guarantees when an adaptive policy itself decides which modalities are eventually observed, breaking the usual assumption that grouping is independent of the calibration sample. Provides two finite-sample constructions and a counterexample showing naive approaches fail.

entry.title: Benchmarking Quantum Machine Learning for Power-System Attack Detection: Evaluation Choices Decide the Outcome Before the Models Do

author.name: Md Rezwanul Islam

entry.summary: Benchmarks quantum kernel and variational classifiers against tuned classical models for power-system cyberattack detection under white-box, transfer, black-box, and poisoning attacks. The headline result is methodological: eight evaluation and tuning choices each flipped conclusions, with file-level versus row-level splits causing the largest swing.

entry.title: A Pre-Specified Construction-Confirmation Test of Operation-Level Causal Transfer Across Finite Isomorphic Symbolic Domains

author.name: Xinyi Shan

entry.summary: Tests whether a frozen Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct model carries operation-level structure across isomorphic symbolic domains by estimating per-input hidden-state differences between two operations and adding them to mapped recipient inputs, with wrong-operation, norm-matched random, and no-op controls. Uses a pre-registered construction versus confirmation split.

entry.title: Deploying Frontier Agentic Technology in MOOSEnger, a Multiphysics-Capable AI Assistant

author.name: Zaid Abulawi, Mengnan Li, Guillaume Giudicelli, Yang Liu, Cody Permann

entry.summary: Extends MOOSEnger, a domain-specific agent for the MOOSE multiphysics finite-element framework, with a harness for locally hosted models that retrieves repository knowledge, validates generated inputs by executing the simulator, and stores lessons from failures. Aims to lower the expertise barrier for scientific simulation.

entry.title: Towards Reasonable Molecular Structure Elucidation from Infrared Spectroscopy with Chemical Feedback

author.name: Yusen Tan, Hongyu Zhan, Hai-tao Yu, Changxi Chi, Wenjie Du, Jun Xia

entry.summary: Proposes preference-style training with chemical feedback so that molecular structures predicted from infrared spectra actually satisfy the input molecular formula and reproduce the observed spectrum. Addresses the common failure of top-ranked candidates being chemically inconsistent.

entry.title: REFLEX: Reflexive Equilibrium Fixed-point Learning for Endogenous eXchanges

author.name: Vignesh Nagarajan, Shriraghav Ashok

entry.summary: REFLEX studies feedback loops when bond dealers retrain quoting models on the trades their own quotes attract, grounding abstract performative-prediction stability conditions in concrete market microstructure. It asks not only whether a quoting model performs well but whether the market it induces remains stable as the model learns.

entry.title: The Trade-off Between Covariate Dependence and Latent Structure in Representation Learning

author.name: Ma{\l}gorzata {\L}az\k{e}cka, Ewa Szczurek

entry.summary: Presents a unified supervised framework linking latent-dimension-to-covariate dependence with constraints on latent structure, and proves an inherent trade-off: under correlated covariates one cannot simultaneously enforce latent independence and one-to-one covariate alignment. Clarifies why disentanglement objectives conflict in practice.

entry.title: Localized TabICLv2: Scaling Tabular In-Context Learning through k-NN

author.name: Beimnet Bekele Guta

entry.summary: Reduces the inference cost of the TabICLv2 tabular in-context learner by retrieving only the k nearest training rows per test point in the model's own row-representation space, instead of attending over the full training context. Requires no architectural changes and recovers accuracy with additional stage-level adjustments.

entry.title: Pallas: A Proactive KV Cache Migration Framework for LLM Inference in AI-RAN

author.name: Tianhang Ding, Jianchun Liu, Hongli Xu

entry.summary: Pallas proactively migrates LLM KV cache state to a predicted target base station before a cellular handover occurs, avoiding the choice between persistent inter-token latency (keeping state at the source) and long service interruption (recovering state after handover). Targets LLM serving embedded in AI-RAN mobile infrastructure.

entry.title: Koopman early warning signals for bifurcation and rate-induced tipping

author.name: Juan Nathaniel, Carla Roesch, Derek DeSantis, Parvathi Kooloth, Hang Fan, Valerio Lucarini, Anastasia Romanou, Pierre Gentine

entry.summary: Uses Koopman operator theory and residual Koopman mode decomposition to build early warning indicators that cover not only classical bifurcation-induced tipping detectable via critical slowing down but also rate-induced tipping, where transitions occur without local loss of stability. Extends the residual measure to nonautonomous control settings with time-varying forcing under stochasticity.

entry.title: IP Protection in the Era of Visual Generative AI: A Survey

author.name: Zhuan Shi, Shunchang Liu, Alireza Dehghanpour Farashah, Qian Yang, Han Yu, Cao Yang, Chaochao Chen, Yuping Yan, Yaochu Jin, Golnoosh Farnadi, Lingjuan Lyu

entry.summary: A survey of intellectual property protection techniques for visual generative models, proposing a two-axis taxonomy whose primary axis groups methods by control logic into information exposure control, generative behavior constraint, and attribution plus accountability. Covers risks from unauthorized training, reproduction, extraction, misuse, and redistribution of data and model assets.

entry.title: NeuRoute: Logit-Guided Neural Routing for Billion-Scale Vector Search with Sub-Hour Index Construction

author.name: Xingqiao Wang, Zi Wang, Xiaowei Xu

entry.summary: NeuRoute is a learned hashing index for billion-scale approximate nearest neighbor search that trains a lightweight encoder with a selective similarity-preserving objective to produce balanced short binary addresses used for routing, then clusters within buckets in the encoder's low-dimensional space. At query time it treats encoder logit deviations as an uncertainty signal for adaptive routing, and it claims sub-hour index construction where global clustering or graph building would dominate cost.

entry.title: Large Language Models as Implicit Sociological Models: Reconstructing Voting Behaviour from Sociodemographic Profiles

author.name: Roman Neruda, Martin Bako\v{s}, Josef \v{S}lerka, V\'it Tu\v{c}ek, Petra Vidnerov\'a, Gabriela Kadlecov\'a

entry.summary: Proposes treating LLMs as implicit sociological models by conditioning them on demographic profiles, eliciting turnout and party preference probabilities, and aggregating via soft voting to reconstruct aggregate election results. Validated against the 2021 Czech parliamentary election with reportedly low aggregate error.

entry.title: Correlation Clustering with Random Partial Information

author.name: Rajath Rao K. N., Jens Schl\"oter, Sami Davies, Amira Ouchene, Yasamin Nazari

entry.summary: Studies correlation clustering on graphs formed by randomly deleting edges from a complete signed graph, asking whether such incomplete instances escape the logarithmic and square-root approximation barriers of general graphs. Provides guarantees approaching the complete-graph regime for both min-disagreement and min-max objectives.

entry.title: BCMT: Blockwise Causal Memory Transformer

author.name: Rachid Arezki

entry.summary: Introduces a long-context architecture that applies dense causal attention only within local blocks while each block emits an adaptive summary aggregated through an exponential causal memory that is injected back into token representations. This decouples local token interaction from global context propagation without explicit global attention.

entry.title: Geometric Filtering of LLM-Generated Samples for Few-Shot Text Classification

author.name: Benjam\'in Schindler, Gonzalo A. Ruz

entry.summary: Filters LLM-generated synthetic training examples by their Euclidean distance to real class examples in sentence-embedding space, converting filter scores into soft training weights. Evaluated over thousands of configurations, it beats classical oversampling and other augmentation baselines for few-shot text classification.

entry.title: Split the Labor: Separating Evidence Interpretation from Decision Aggregation

author.name: Zhelun Wu

entry.summary: Argues that systems aggregating evidence from many sources should separate per-source interpretation from decision aggregation, and proposes a fixed four-field evidence tuple as the interface. It identifies a failure mode where thresholding unnormalized summed weights drifts with the number of sources.

entry.title: Do CNNs Internally Represent Real and Fake Images Differently? A Hidden-Layer Analysis

author.name: Moumita Sen Sarma, Pascal Hitzler, Eugene Y. Vasserman

entry.summary: Tests whether CNNs internally encode real and synthetic images differently by comparing dense-layer activations for real scenes and semantically matched generated counterparts, with neurosymbolic labeling of individual neurons. The goal is a mechanistic account of what deepfake detectors are actually keying on.

entry.title: SOS! : A Streamlined Object-Conditional Transformer for Model-free Segmentation

author.name: Jiaqi Hu, Junwen Huang, Hongli Xu, Peter KT Yu, Nassir Navab, Benjamin Busam, Slobodan Ilic

entry.summary: SOS segments unseen target objects by conditioning a transformer on a single reference image, removing the usual dependence on 3D CAD models and multi-stage pipelines built around foundation segmentation masks. This targets robotic manipulation, where class-agnostic masks must be matched to a specific object of interest.

entry.title: CBX-Bench: A Human-Aligned MLLM Council for Benchmarking Concept Bottleneck Model Explanations

author.name: Yusuf Meric Karadag, Gulay Oklan, Seref Baris Cagliyan, Umut Ozdemir, Emre Akbas

entry.summary: CBX-Bench uses a council of multimodal LLMs to score the quality of concept bottleneck model explanations, validated against human judgments, providing a quantitative alternative to evaluating interpretable models only by downstream accuracy. It addresses the absence of ground-truth concept annotations and consensus concept vocabularies.

entry.title: ConceptFormer: Learning Adaptive Latent Concepts for Query-Document Alignment in Visual Document Retrieval

author.name: Peng Chunyi, Xu Zhipeng, Yan Yukun, Liu Zhenghao, Yu Shi, Mei Sen, Sun Yubo, Zhang Yongheng, Zhou Jie, Gu Yu, Yu Ge, Sun Maosong

entry.summary: ConceptFormer learns continuous, query-conditioned latent concepts as evidence representations for visual document retrieval, replacing supervision proxies based on textual descriptions or cropped visual regions. It targets multimodal retrieval-augmented generation where relevant evidence is spread across text, layout, charts and visual structure.

entry.title: RoofGS: Roofline-Guided End-to-End Acceleration of 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Yang Luo, Yan Gong, Yongsheng Gao, Jie Zhao

entry.summary: RoofGS accelerates 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering by first characterizing stage-wise hardware bottlenecks with roofline analysis, finding the front end memory-bound and rasterization instruction-bound. It then applies bottleneck-specific optimizations including a 32-bit resolution-adaptive quantized sorting key and a range-aware bit-level fast exponential approximation.

entry.title: SafeGesture: Evaluating Fine-Grained Hand Gesture Understanding in Vision-Language Models through Scenario-Conditioned Safety Interpretation

author.name: Taegang Kim, Saleh Afroogh, Junfeng Jiao

entry.summary: SafeGesture pairs six hand gestures with eight operational scenarios to test whether vision-language models can infer scenario-appropriate safety actions, evaluating several open-weight models plus GPT-4o over 4,800 items. It documents a large perception-reasoning gap, with GPT-4o recognizing gestures at 98 percent accuracy but choosing safe actions only about 53 percent of the time.

entry.title: Joint Flow Matching Enables Continuous Dose-Conditioned Cell Morphing

author.name: Lea Bogensperger, Manuela Merlo, Martin Baumgartner, Michael Krauthammer, Bernard Ciraulo

entry.summary: Introduces a joint flow matching formulation with dual timesteps that models cell image latents and drug concentration together, enabling continuous dose-conditioned prediction of cellular morphology changes. Invertibility also lets the model estimate concentration from observed morphology, and the latent space exhibits monotonic dose-response geometry.

entry.title: Automatic Cephalometric Landmark Localization on CBCT-Derived Digitally Reconstructed Radiographs for Skeletal Malocclusion Classification

author.name: Benjamin Hou, Konstantinia Almpani, Janice S. Lee, Zhiyong Lu

entry.summary: CephViT is a Vision Transformer for automated cephalometric landmark detection on 2D lateral radiographs, additionally validated on digitally reconstructed radiographs derived from 3D CBCT scans for skeletal malocclusion classification. It reports sub-1.3 mm mean radial error and 92 percent detection within 3 mm.

entry.title: Ultra: Unsupervised Cross-Task Optimization for Reliable Restoration Segmentation Collaboration under Adverse Weather

author.name: Shiqin Wang, Zhiqian Li, Haoyuan Du, Junming Chen, Jiayuan Li, Tianrun Xu, Haoyang Chen

entry.summary: Ultra tackles unsupervised domain adaptation for semantic segmentation in adverse weather by questioning the assumption that image restoration and segmentation always help each other. It recasts cross-task interaction as direction selection under uncertainty with causal effect estimation to avoid hallucination-driven error propagation.

entry.title: Modular Cognitive Architecture Emerges in Large Language Models

author.name: Pengrui Han, Jacob Andreas, Evelina Fedorenko, Andrea Gregor de Varda

entry.summary: Already covered in yesterday's Research section, Using circuit analyses over 46 tasks spanning language, formal reasoning, social reasoning, and physical reasoning, the authors find that LLMs spontaneously develop functionally specialized, partly dissociable subnetworks resembling the modular organization of the human brain. This suggests modularity may be a convergent property of intelligent systems rather than a biological accident.

entry.title: TwinGridShield: Consequence-Aware Runtime Authorization for LLM Grid-Agent Actions

author.name: Md Fazley Rafy

entry.summary: TwinGridShield is a model-independent authorization layer that simulates each LLM-proposed power grid command in a deterministic network twin before execution, checking connectivity, branch-flow, generator and load-shedding invariants and logging decisions in a hash chain. Demonstrated on an IEEE 14-bus study of switching, redispatch and load-shedding actions.

entry.title: OTel: Building Domain-Specialized Telecom LLM Foundations for Intelligent Networks

author.name: Farbod Tavakkoli, Roderic Paulk, Jorden Terrazas, Kenneth Church, Mark Austin, Louis Powell, Gregory Diamos, Lina Bariah, Syed Ali Raza Zaidi, Maryam Hafeez, Ali Maatouk, Imtiaz Karim

entry.summary: Reorganizes reported text-to-SQL results along an inference-autonomy axis from constrained decoding to fully agentic and reasoning-internalized generation, with provenance for each reported number, plus a Spider case study using 8B open backbones against stronger baselines. Finds Spider gains transfer unevenly to harder benchmarks and that autonomy buys robustness at a cost.

entry.title: NumerosityVLM: A Cognitively Inspired Benchmark for Interpreting Numerosity Representations in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yiming Fu, Fangjun Li, Xiujin Liu, Ruidong Ma, Hang Yu, Zhichen Lu, Kanwei He, Alessandro Di Nuovo, Angelo Cangelosi, Zhegong Shangguan

entry.summary: Introduces a controlled synthetic benchmark of nearly eleven thousand images that separates numerosity from confounds like object size, arrangement, texture, shape, and color, then evaluates seven vision-language models zero-shot. Analysis attributes most performance variance to architecture and reveals systematic failures in a capacity that appears in preverbal human infants.

entry.title: Algorithm-Architecture Co-Design for Efficient VLA Inference via Speculative Inference and Verification

author.name: Chunyu Qi, Zhuoran Song, Jian Weng, Haozhe Jiang, Xueyuan Liu, Naifeng Jing, Guanghui He, Xiaoyao Liang, Haibing Guan

entry.summary: Exploits the observation that robot rollouts alternate between active phases needing precise control and inactive phases where actions matter little, scheduling long speculative action predictions during inactive states and verification during active ones. The scheduling policy is paired with accelerator-level co-design for embodied inference.

entry.title: Beyond Single Object: Learning 3D Relations with Large Language Models

author.name: Kohsuke Ide, Ryousuke Yamada, Yue Qiu, Xianzheng Ma, Yoshihiro Fukuhara, Hirokatsu Kataoka, Yutaka Satoh

entry.summary: Targets the inability of 3D language models to compare multiple objects, contributing an instruction dataset for fine-grained multi-object comparison, a patch-interaction transformer that models both inter- and intra-object structure, and two application benchmarks on shape mating and change captioning. Existing 3D language models and 2D vision-language models perform poorly on these tasks.

entry.title: Walk Before You Run: The Importance of Data Exploration for Data Analysis Agents

author.name: Yike Yuan, Virum Ranka, Tina Lasisi, Lin Ma

entry.summary: Points out that LLM data-analysis agents are graded on final answers while the prerequisite step of understanding a messy workbook, including recovering logical tables, column semantics, keys, and quality issues, is left implicit. The paper argues for evaluating this exploration phase explicitly to close the gap with downstream task success.

entry.title: LLMs for Zero-Shot Threat Detection via Structured Risk Indicators

author.name: Abdullah Alghamdi, Siamak Layeghy, Marius Portmann

entry.summary: A two-stage LLM framework for zero-shot insider threat and advanced persistent threat detection that models user activity as timelines, retrieves per-user historical context, and first emits structured interpretable risk indicators before classifying temporal sequences. Evaluated on CERT insider threat and a domain-specific APT benchmark.

entry.title: Supervising the Path to Fine Scales: GalerkinFlow for Scientific-Field and Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Zikang Zhan

entry.summary: GalerkinFlow supervises super-resolution along an entire coarse-to-fine reconstruction path rather than only at the final output, predicting residual velocity at random intermediate states with a coarse-anchored pseudo-endpoint. The authors relate the pseudo-endpoint reconstruction loss exactly to the intermediate velocity loss through a time-dependent weight, making every intermediate state a supervisable target.

entry.title: IterCOMP: Reasoning-aware Adaptive Prompt Compression for Multi-hop Question Answering

author.name: JungMin Yun, YoungBin Kim

entry.summary: IterCOMP is a training-free prompt compression framework that decomposes retrieved documents into evidence segments, checks whether the question is answerable, and generates targeted follow-up questions to iteratively pull in missing evidence. It targets multi-hop QA where single-pass compressors drop interdependent reasoning steps.

entry.title: The conditional superiority of fast silicon sampling

author.name: Nickolas Hock Yuen Lam, Ji Xuan Voo, Xiangyu Ma

entry.summary: Compares fast and slow modes of LLM-based silicon sampling against a nationally representative Singaporean survey, finding that fast modes can be conditionally superior while both understate opinion variance and distort the latent structure behind human opinions. Concludes that silicon sampling remains an early-stage method to be used cautiously.

entry.title: DCA-MoE: Spatially Adaptive Cross-Layer Fusion and Density-Routed Experts for Crowd Counting

author.name: Hao Wang

entry.summary: A crowd counting model that makes feature fusion and receptive field selection content-dependent, using position-wise fusion weights over frozen DINOv3 features and a density-routed mixture of local, mid-range, and large-context experts. It targets severe scale and occlusion variation across image regions.

entry.title: Counterfactual Sensitivity Is Not Repairability: Auditing Replay Probes for Video Evidence

author.name: Rama AlHamidi, Rasul Khanbayov, Erchin Serpedin, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: CARVE is a black-box faithfulness probe for tool-using video agents that destroys the semantic content of retrieved frames and compares answer changes against a sham replay running the same pipeline on the same frames. Across repeated runs the destroy condition flips answers about 29 percentage points more often than sham, but per-question stability is low, leading the authors to argue counterfactual sensitivity does not imply repairability.

entry.title: Sterilizable Scene Graph Generation for Operating Rooms

author.name: Nick Lemke, Ssharvien Kumar Sivakumar, Antoine P. Sanner, John Kalkhof, Henry John Krumb, Ghazal Ghazaei, Anirban Mukhopadhyay

entry.summary: SG-NCA builds surgical scene graph generation on neural cellular automata, claimed as the first NCA framework able to learn structured relational representations, so it can run on tiny fanless hardware suitable for sterile operating rooms. Motivation includes hygiene constraints, latency and keeping patient data on device.

entry.title: Modality-Invariant Coarse-to-Fine Retinal Image Registration

author.name: Bo Wen, Nehal Nailesh Mehta, Melanie Tran, Dirk-Uwe Bartsch, William Freeman, Truong Nguyen

entry.summary: A two-stage retinal image registration framework aims to be modality-invariant, first matching sparse features derived from a universal vessel segmentation and then refining alignment. This removes the usual restriction to one modality or one fixed cross-modal pair.

entry.title: Readiness Barrier Functions: Forward-Invariant Control Authority for Overactuated Multirotor Allocation

author.name: Giuseppe Silano

entry.summary: Treats control authority of an overactuated multirotor as a quantity to be kept forward-invariant using a control barrier function on the log-determinant of a drag-aware actuator authority metric, enforced by a quadratic program in the allocation null space. This reconciles jumpy readiness-maximizing allocation with smooth but uncertified effort-minimizing allocation.

entry.title: Throwing a Tight Spiral American Football by a Humanoid Robot

author.name: Zaid Mahboob, Bowen Weng

entry.summary: Demonstrates a humanoid robot throwing an American football with a stabilizing spiral, which requires explicit control over spin injection at release rather than only linear release velocity. The work coordinates high-DoF whole-body motion to hit a target coupled linear and angular momentum at detachment.

entry.title: Position: Want Better ML Reviews? Stop Asking Nicely and Start Incentivizing with a Credit System

author.name: Shaochen Zhong

entry.summary: A position paper contending that fragmented jurisdiction-specific AI laws are insufficient and that governance needs ISO-style interoperability protocols enabling standardized, machine-readable risk communication across borders. It draws an analogy to how GDPR was operationalized through technical standards such as ISO 27001.

entry.title: SKILL: Self-correcting Knowledge-guided Iterative Large Language Model Agent for Logic Optimization

author.name: Rui Yang

entry.summary: SKILL couples three specialized LLMs for planning, detailed reasoning, and analysis with a PPO agent to automate logic synthesis optimization, addressing sparse rewards and poor sample efficiency in EDA flows. The multi-agent controller iteratively self-corrects synthesis recipes using domain knowledge.

entry.title: A Human-Centred Approach to Benchmarking LLMs for Parenting Advice

author.name: Yunke Zhao, Isobel Voysey, Alastair van Heerden, Rob Hughes, Jun Zhao

entry.summary: Evaluates 15 LLMs across 100 parenting scenarios in English and Chinese using a multi-dimensional rubric authored by parenting experts and an LLM judge. Findings include that aggregate scores mask item-level weaknesses, that models implicitly promote different parenting styles, and that language shifts responses.

entry.title: Cross-Domain Industrial Fault Detection by Causal Mechanism Monitoring

author.name: Dhiraj Neupane, Mohamed Reda Bouadjenek, Richard Dazeley, Sunil Aryal

entry.summary: CMR-Mamba trains per-domain state-space encoders on healthy industrial sensor data and regularizes them with a causal cross-modal predictor so the learned manifold reflects normal cause-to-effect coupling between sensor groups. Anomalies are scored by nearest-neighbor distance, targeting coupling faults that leave individual sensor marginals looking normal.

entry.title: LLM-Based Hierarchical Coordinated Control with Continuation-Aware Policy Learning

author.name: Changhong He, Jinda Gao, Xinkuan Liu, Le Zhang, Xizi Luo, Yu Mei

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchy where an LLM coordinates interacting units in a complex engineering system using heterogeneous operational context, while conventional controllers or optimizers produce constraint-satisfying low-level actions. A continuation-aware variant of group-relative policy optimization scores coordination decisions by how the system evolves in subsequent control intervals rather than only by immediate outcome.

entry.title: A concentration result for multilayer feedforward neural networks

author.name: Vera Koponen

entry.summary: Proves a concentration result for fixed-depth feedforward networks whose input width grows: if the layer-to-layer weight distributions converge to a fixed continuous profile and inputs are i.i.d. with a continuous density, the output concentrates around a single value. Formalizes when wide random networks become effectively deterministic.

entry.title: From Generalist to Specialist: A Context-Fusion Framework for Endoscopic Polyp Reporting with a Frozen VLM

author.name: Ruijie Yang, Yan Zhu, Peiyao Fu, Siyuan Li, Te Luo, Zhihua Wang, Quanlin Li, Pinghong Zhou, Xian Yang, Shuo Wang

entry.summary: Specializes a frozen general-purpose vision-language model for endoscopic polyp reporting using implicit instruction context and explicit transduction context from specialist modules, without touching model weights. This preserves the pretrained model's general abilities and unified interface while injecting quantitative sizing and standardized classification knowledge.

entry.title: Rotation-Invariant Multi-IMU Activity Recognition under Independent Per-Location Orientation Shifts

author.name: Seungyeol Baek, Yoonbyung Chai, Yonghyeon Lee, Sungjoon Choi, Sungho Suh

entry.summary: TRI-HAR makes multi-sensor human activity recognition structurally invariant to independent orientation offsets at each body location, which arise whenever users reattach wearable sensors between sessions. It avoids reliance on rotation augmentation or calibration pipelines that assume reference frames or explicit procedures.

entry.title: Intent-Driven Situation Tracking for User-Centric Multi-Turn Agents

author.name: Meiling Tao, Yiling Tao, Peng Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free situation-state layer for multi-turn agents that parses tool outputs into provenance-aware entities and attributes, tracks evolving user intents, and explicitly separates grounded facts from task-state judgments. This spares the model from re-inferring constraints and dependencies from raw dialogue history.

entry.title: Large language models as synthetic clinical experts to inform longitudinal rare-disease modeling

author.name: Clemens Sch\"achter, Astrid Pechmann, Janbernd Kirschner, Jan Hasenauer, Harald Binder

entry.summary: The authors query LLMs offline on textual descriptions of patient visits to obtain expert-like judgments, then use those judgments to supervise a variational autoencoder that learns low-dimensional latent summaries of longitudinal rare-disease observations. This substitutes for scarce expert elicitation time in a data-poor setting. It is a concrete pattern for injecting model-derived domain knowledge into statistical model fitting.

entry.title: CUBICS: Situation-aware performance estimation for safety-relevant ML components

author.name: Benjamin Herd, Jessica Kelly, Mario Trapp

entry.summary: CUBICS replaces the usual single-global-failure-probability Bernoulli model used in Bayesian field-data safety arguments with situation-aware performance estimation, recognizing that machine learning component performance depends strongly on operating context. It supports proven-in-use arguments built from shadow-mode or safety-envelope monitoring. The target is certifiable safety cases for learned components.

entry.title: Hypergraph-based Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Incremental Refinement

author.name: Shenao Chen, Yidan Xu, Xiangmin Han, Rundong Xue, Duanpo Wu, Yuhan Gao, Chenggang Yan, Yue Gao

entry.summary: Hyper-M2RAG replaces binary graph edges with hypergraph structures to capture higher-order relations among charts, scattered text, and underlying numbers in multimodal documents, and adds incremental refinement instead of full-page reconstruction. The design targets both expressiveness and computational redundancy in long-document retrieval. It aims to reduce contextual noise while improving cross-modal alignment.

entry.title: Efficient Block-Layer Parallel Inference for Vision-Language-Action on Hybrid Architectures

author.name: Haibo HU, Lianming Huang, Qiao Li, Nan Guan, Chun Jason Xue

entry.summary: The paper proposes block-layer parallel inference that splits vision-language-action computation across underused CPU capacity and the contended GPU on legacy vehicle platforms, motivated by the fact that absorbing planning functions into a unified model concentrates demand on the GPU. The aim is to meet real-time latency budgets without new hardware. It is a deployment-oriented scheduling contribution.

entry.title: SMOPD: Selective Token-Entropy Masking for Dirty-History Multi-Turn On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Chenyang Jiang, Changhan Huang

entry.summary: SMOPD stabilizes multi-turn on-policy self-distillation when the student conditions on its own earlier mistakes, by dropping the lowest-entropy 20 percent of token positions from the distillation loss. It is a loss-only change with no extra parameters and no inference cost, targeting token-level uncertainty rather than trajectory-level rewards.

entry.title: Identifying Harm in Personalized, Generative AI Systems Requires User-Centered Auditing at the Interaction Level

author.name: Hannah Cha

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that standard harm audits fail for personalized generative systems because harms emerge from evolving individual interaction histories rather than static, group-level definitions. It names three flawed presuppositions in current auditing paradigms and calls for user-centered auditing at the interaction level.

entry.title: Cross-Modal Ultrasound-MRI Learning for Fetal Brain Ventricular Volumetry and Abnormality Screening

author.name: Yuhao Huang, Yuanji Zhang, Yuhuan Lu, Dong Ni, P. Ellen Grant, Davood Karimi

entry.summary: VIFBA predicts MRI-derived lateral ventricular volume from fetal brain ultrasound video, classifies ventriculomegaly severity, and flags other abnormalities, using a JEPA-inspired tube latent prediction objective. The goal is to bring MRI-grade volumetric assessment to cheaper, more accessible ultrasound screening.

entry.title: NARRATE: A Multimodal Real-World Australian Driving Dataset for Human-Centred Explanations in Automated Driving

author.name: Ashkan Yousefi Zadeh, Zishuo Zhu, Xiaomeng Li, Andry Rakotonirainy, Sebastien Glaser, Ronald Schroeter, Patricia Delhomme, Zahra Mehraban

entry.summary: NARRATE is a real-world Australian driving dataset of 2,050 events from 35 experienced drivers, pairing synchronized video, localization, motion, and LiDAR with explanations elicited from the driver performing the action rather than written by observers afterwards. It supports research on human-centered explanations for automated driving.

entry.title: Hierarchical Agentic Incident Response with Digital-Twin-Validated Attack Inference

author.name: Yiran Gao, Juntao Chen, Tao Li

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical incident response framework where a fine-tuned LLM infers multi-stage attack progression from alerts and measurements, a rollout planner selects recovery actions, and an emulated network digital twin validates the proposed commands before execution. The digital twin is intended to catch hallucinated attack hypotheses and unsafe remediation.

entry.title: Low-Rank Dynamics-Effective Latent Carriers for Counterfactual Rollout in Learned World Models

author.name: Yang Liu, Yuming Chen

entry.summary: Investigates whether a small, directly addressable edit to a recurrent world model's 192-dimensional hidden state can place it on an intended counterfactual trajectory that it then continues autonomously. The authors learn low-rank carriers from factual-to-counterfactual hidden differences in a controlled two-object collision environment.

entry.title: FinFraudBench: A Heterogeneous Graph Benchmark for Financial Fraud Detection

author.name: Yixuan Chen, Hongyu Zhan, Jie Sheng, Weiyu Han, Shuai Chen, Tianyi Zhang, Xiao Tan, Jun Xia

entry.summary: FinFraudBench provides a heterogeneous graph benchmark for financial fraud detection that preserves multiple entity types such as customers, cards, merchants, categories, and locations rather than collapsing them into homogeneous or single-node-type graphs. It aims to align academic evaluation with the relational structure of real financial systems.

entry.title: VTInstructor: Visual Trajectory Prompting for Navigation Instruction Generation in Continuous Environments

author.name: Haolin Yang, Yuxing Long, Zihan Yang, Hao Dong

entry.summary: Introduces the first framework for generating natural-language navigation instructions from continuous egocentric RGB streams, rather than from discrete panoramic viewpoint graphs. It converts implicit trajectory geometry into explicit visual prompts by selecting keyframes and overlaying path, turn, and goal cues for a vision-language model.

entry.title: PhaseLoRA: Control-Regime-Conditioned Low-Rank Adaptation for Continuous-Action Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Yufei Guo, Yinan Wu, Haoran Duan, Guiguang Ding, Jungong Han

entry.summary: Argues that adapters for vision-language-action policies apply the same update throughout a manipulation rollout even though approach, contact, grasp, transport, and placement need different behavior. PhaseLoRA conditions the low-rank update on weakly supervised descriptors of fine-control tendency and event intensity so adaptation varies by control phase.

entry.title: Ask to Be Sure: Informative Interactions for Confident Multi-Turn LLM Recommendation

author.name: Cedar Site Bai, Duanshun Li, Zhenyu Liao, Sheikh Sarwar, Huiyuan Chen, Yuan Chen, Changhe Yuan, Haiyang Zhang, Qilin Qi

entry.summary: Proposes rewarding a conversational recommender for the amount of uncertainty it actually removes, measured as entropy reduction over candidate recommendations, instead of relying on templated interaction policies or another model judging interactivity. This gives a ground-truth-free signal for learning what to ask next.

entry.title: AsyTO: Asymmetric Temporal Operator for Parameter-Efficient Multivariate Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Xiachong Lin, Du Yin, Hao Xue, Wen Hu, Imran Razzak, Arian Prabowo, Matthew Amos, Flora D. Salim

entry.summary: AsyTO reframes multivariate time-series forecasting as compressing the forecasting operator rather than the series, pairing a phase-locked seasonal component with a compact residual operator per variable. This aims to escape the trade-off between one shared temporal predictor and expensive per-variable predictors.

entry.title: Securing AI-Generated Code: A Just-in-Time Vulnerability Detection and Remediation Pipeline

author.name: Mikhail Surikov

entry.summary: This pipeline generates Python from security-focused prompts, scans it in parallel with CodeQL, Bandit, and an independent validator LLM, enriches findings with MITRE ATT&CK techniques and CWE examples, generates fixes, then rescans to verify remediation. It measures whether threat-context enrichment improves automated repair of vulnerable AI-generated code.

entry.title: HarmTrace: Anchor-Calibrated Decoupled Optimization for Fine-Grained Target Identification in Harmful Memes

author.name: Yujia Li, Yiqun Zhang, Zihan Cheng, Yijie Huang, Tenglong Ye, Zihan Wang, Xiaocui Yang, Shi Feng, Yifei Zhang, Daling Wang

entry.summary: HarmTrace extends harmful meme detection beyond binary classification to fine-grained target identification, predicting target category, target entity, the textual mention, and the visual region for harmful memes. The authors unify several public datasets into Meme3W with human-verified annotations and propose a joint record accuracy metric plus anchor-calibrated decoupled optimization.

entry.title: Orbit-Planner: Towards Latent World Models for On-Orbit Obstacle Avoidance of Satellite Agents

author.name: Zhijian Li, Chao Ren, Peijin Wang, Xian Sun

entry.summary: Orbit-Planner is a two-stage latent world model for satellite on-orbit obstacle avoidance that learns action-conditioned spacecraft dynamics, rolls out futures in latent space, and uses a physics probe to decode physical state changes from imagined trajectories. It aims to replace planners that depend on predefined maps and fixed environmental assumptions.

entry.title: UniTAC: Universal Task-Aware Compression via Weighted Distortion Measures

author.name: Homa Esfahanizadeh, Matin Mortaheb, Jinfeng Du, Harish Viswanathan

entry.summary: UniTAC is a single learned image codec that can be retargeted at runtime from task-agnostic to task-specialized compression by conditioning encoder and decoder on a per-component importance vector, for example derived from gradient attribution of any downstream model. This avoids training or shipping a separate codec per downstream task in bandwidth-constrained physical AI systems.

entry.title: Topological Attribution Distance (TAD): Revealing Segment-Level RAG Influence on LLM Output Geometry for Incident Log Analysis

author.name: Reza Fayyazi, Michael Zuzak, Shanchieh Jay Yang

entry.summary: Topological Attribution Distance measures how individual retrieved segments shift the geometry of an LLM's output representations, providing segment-level evidence attribution and provenance for RAG-based incident log analysis in security operations. The aim is to let analysts trace which piece of retrieved data drove an agent's conclusion.

entry.title: Efficient Neural-Network-Based High-Resolution Radiative Transfer for CO___ Retrieval, and Application to Interferometric Sensing

author.name: Jordan Lontsi Tedongmo (CB), Yann Ferrec (CB, IFUMI), Laurence Croiz\'e (CB, IFUMI), Pablo Mus\'e (CB, IFUMI), Gabriele Facciolo (CB), Andr\'es Almansa (MAP5 - UMR 8145, IFUMI)

entry.summary: Replaces expensive line-by-line high-resolution radiative transfer simulations with a neural surrogate for CO2 and methane retrieval, applied to the NanoCarb imaging interferometer within a low-cost satellite constellation concept. The aim is to make full-physics retrieval tractable at high revisit rates and spatial coverage.

entry.title: An automatic-differentiation framework for time-lapse electrical resistivity tomography inversion of hydrologic dynamics

author.name: Pu Yang, Zhengyang Fang, Yuxin Liu, Xuan Su, Deshan Feng, Hang Chen

entry.summary: AD-TLERT builds a unified GPU-accelerated automatic-differentiation framework for time-lapse electrical resistivity tomography inversion, integrating parameterization, differentiable petrophysics, forward modeling, misfit, and regularization into one differentiable chain. This removes the need to hand-derive new gradients whenever any component of the inversion formulation changes.

entry.title: M-LINKX: Multiview Graph Learning for Brain Cognitive Disease Detection

author.name: An Phan, Yufei Jin, Xingquan Zhu

entry.summary: M-LINKX applies multi-view graph learning to segmented EEG for classifying Alzheimer disease, mild cognitive impairment, and frontotemporal dementia, modeling both within-channel signal information and inter-channel interactions. The approach targets the noise, non-stationarity, and subject variability of EEG recordings.

entry.title: Can Neural Networks Learn by Experimenting on Themselves? Self-Interventional Learning from Functional Consequences to Predictive Self-Knowledge

author.name: Micha{\l} Tomaszewski

entry.summary: Self-Interventional Learning has a network perturb its own functional structure, observe consequences, and fit a predictive self-model that generalizes to unexecuted interventions and then guides later structural actions. On a synthetic system with known construction it recovers criticality, redundancy, and replaceability but not synergy, with held-out prediction error falling as intervention budget grows.

entry.title: LLM-based Framework for Generating and Verifying Parallel DEVS Statecharts

author.name: Vamsi Krishna Vasa, Hessam S. Sarjoughian, Edward J. Yellig

entry.summary: Presents an agentic LLM framework that generates and verifies parallel discrete event system specification statecharts from natural-language system descriptions, first extracting plausible facts and then applying a controlled-correction mechanism to catch logical and behavioral inconsistencies. The aim is to assist human modelers in producing verifiable simulation models.

entry.title: Detecting Money Laundering in Rwandan Mobile Money: A Machine Learning Framework

author.name: Emmanuel Nahimana, Ya\'e Ulrich Gaba

entry.summary: Builds and evaluates a transaction-monitoring framework for anti-money-laundering in Rwandan mobile money, explicitly designed around roughly 0.1 percent positive prevalence, scarce and delayed labels, and bounded investigator capacity, using a synthetic dataset of about 9.5 million transactions. The framing aligns detection metrics with regulatory workflow constraints rather than raw classification accuracy.

entry.title: TransfHAR: Self-Supervised Wrist Representations for On-Demand Activity Recognition

author.name: Aidan Bradshaw, Riku Arakawa, Xin Liu, Karan Ahuja

entry.summary: TransfHAR pretrains self-supervised representations on unlabeled coarse wrist IMU activity and shows the learned motion priors transfer to fine-grained manipulative and gestural actions never seen in pretraining, deployed as a real-time smartwatch app. Targets on-demand activity recognition without per-task labeling.

entry.title: A Banach-Space Theory of Markovian Halpern Iteration for Non-Expansive Maps

author.name: Ege C. Kaya, Arda Fazla, M. Berk Sahin, Abolfazl Hashemi

entry.summary: Analyzes Halpern iteration for fixed points of non-expansive operators when samples come from a continuing Markov chain, then introduces a variance-reduced PAGE-Halpern method analyzed via the Poisson equation. Improves sample complexity from roughly epsilon to the minus five to epsilon to the minus three in Hilbert spaces and extends the construction to finite-dimensional Banach spaces.

entry.title: AdROD: HyperNetwork-based Adversarially Robust Object Detection for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yuting Wu, Dongfang Guo, Xiangzhong Luo, Qun Song, Rui Tan

entry.summary: AdROD defends camera-based object detectors in autonomous driving using low-rank hypernetworks that generate a fresh detector per frame, so attackers cannot pin down the deployed model, plus a functional-diversity mechanism for ensemble robustness. Claims a large parameter-footprint reduction versus standard hypernetworks.

entry.title: Beyond Peak Backlog: Conditional Energy and Temporal Geometry in Capacity-Constrained Delayed Bandit Optimization

author.name: Anling Xiang, Yuwen Yang, Yang Shen

entry.summary: Analyzes bandit convex optimization when the learner can track only a bounded number of pending feedback items and discarded feedback is permanently lost, replacing peak-backlog dependence with a conditional-energy quantity. Yields an untuned learner with sharper delay scaling under a hard-capacity contract.

entry.title: Beyond $L_2$: Generalizing Abductive Latent Explanations to Diverse Prototype-Based Architectures

author.name: Jules Soria, Alban Grastien, Romain Xu-Darme, Julien Girard-Satabin, Zakaria Chihani, Daniela Cancila

entry.summary: Generalizes Abductive Latent Explanations, which give formally guaranteed explanations for prototype-based networks, beyond Euclidean latent spaces to spherical metrics, Gaussian densities, and projection-based representations. Closes a compatibility gap with modern prototype architectures.

entry.title: Beyond Boundary Noise: Aggregated Aleatoric Uncertainty Fails to Capture Presence Ambiguity in 3D Lung Nodule Segmentation

author.name: Simon Baur, Arne Schernich, Ekin B\"oke, Wojciech Samek, Jackie Ma

entry.summary: Systematically tests whether entropy-based aleatoric uncertainty in 3D lung nodule segmentation captures the clinically decisive question of whether a lesion is present at all, across four architectures with Monte Carlo dropout and deep ensembles on LIDC-IDRI plus external LNDb validation. Finds that aggregated entropy largely reflects boundary noise and fails to signal case-level presence disagreement.

entry.title: What Makes a Good Layer? Assessing the Layer-Wise Intrinsic Properties of Music Foundation Models

author.name: Angelos-Nikolaos Kanatas, Yuexuan Kong, Pablo Alonso-Jim\'enez, Xavier Serra, Dmitry Bogdanov

entry.summary: Systematically analyzes layer-wise representation quality across twelve music foundation models spanning masked, autoregressive, and contrastive pretraining, characterizing hidden states with intrinsic geometric and transformation-based metrics. Correlates label-free representation-quality measures with downstream performance to replace heuristic layer picking with principled selection.

entry.title: When do machine-learned exchange-correlation improvements inherit into density-functional tight binding?

author.name: Can Polat, Mustafa Kurban, Erchin Serpedin, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: Asks whether improvements from machine-learned exchange-correlation functionals carry over when used as parents for density-functional tight binding parameterizations, and finds they do not, defining a transfer ratio and observing coherently negative anti-transfer across four covalent semiconductors. Attributes the failure to a representational mismatch, since modern functionals are orbital-dependent generalized Kohn-Sham operators while the parameterization channel assumes a multiplicative potential.

entry.title: SkillComposer: Learning Reusable Skills for Natural-Language Robot Programming

author.name: John Woods, Hasti Seifi

entry.summary: SkillComposer is an interactive natural-language robot programming system for simulation in which an LLM iteratively generates and revises programs against execution tests, and successful programs feed an online library-learning algorithm that compresses recurring function sequences into reusable abstractions. The goal is to handle multi-step tasks where direct LLM code generation typically fails.

entry.title: Global Simulation-Guided Dynamic Operator Scheduling for Efficient Multi-Tenant Model Serving

author.name: Weinan Liu, Zeyuan Ding, Dian Ding, Chengcheng Wan, Lu Tang, Guangtao Xue, Jiwu Shu, Yiming Zhang

entry.summary: SliceScheduler performs operator-level scheduling for multi-tenant model serving to reclaim short-lived idle slices inside containers that coarse container-granularity reallocation cannot exploit under service-level agreements. Its core abstraction is a global mapping graph capturing operator dependencies, tensor state, and cluster-wide execution dynamics, enabling simulation-guided what-if reasoning before committing scheduling decisions.

entry.title: Representation Is Not Enough: Body-Localized Thermal Evidence for Contactless Stress and Craving Sensing in Opioid Use Disorder

author.name: Sachin Deb, Harshit Sharma, Asif Salekin

entry.summary: Presents a weakly supervised architecture that fuses frozen foundation-model encoders while preserving body-region and temporal localization, so a clip-level stress or craving label can be traced to the thermal evidence that produced it. Applied to contactless monitoring in opioid use disorder.

entry.title: RadioVIL: Anomaly-Aware Diffusion Models for Radio Map Inpainting and Zero-Shot Vehicle Localization

author.name: Ruixin Zhao, Xiucheng Wang, Qiming Zhang, Nan Cheng, Ruijin Sun, Conghao Zhou

entry.summary: RadioVIL reframes radio map completion as a prior-guided physical inverse problem, first training a diffusion model on structural radio-map priors and then using anomaly awareness to preserve high-frequency scattering signatures for zero-shot localization of hidden vehicles. Targets 6G integrated sensing and communication use cases.

entry.title: Hide&Seek: Learning to Explain in an End-to-End Differentiable Network

author.name: Tal Ellinson, Hadi Mohasel Afshar, Sally Cripps

entry.summary: Hide&Seek trains a feature selector and predictor jointly under a single end-to-end differentiable objective for instance-wise feature selection, avoiding the information leakage and non-differentiability problems of earlier selector-predictor methods. Intended for interpreting individual predictions of black-box models.

entry.title: BM25-Augmented Many-Shot Translation for Low-Resource North-Eastern Indian Languages

author.name: Aashish Dhawan, Christopher Driggers-Ellis, Dzmitry Kasinets, Christan Grant, Daisy Zhe Wang

entry.summary: A WMT26 shared-task submission that translates between English and eleven North-Eastern Indian languages using BM25 retrieval of similar parallel examples as many-shot context for a general-purpose Gemini model, with no fine-tuning. Reports a grid search over retrieval and exemplar counts across all 22 directions.

entry.title: Beam-Wise Statistical Background Subtraction for Static Roadside LiDAR: A Cross-Sensor Benchmark Study

author.name: Alexander Baumann, Marcel Vosshans, Thao Dang

entry.summary: Benchmarks per-beam statistical background subtraction strategies for statically mounted roadside LiDAR across different sensors, and releases a new highway scene dataset for reproducible evaluation. It fills a gap in cross-sensor evaluation for infrastructure perception preprocessing.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Topologically Invariant Manifold Learning for Railway Image Quality Assessment

author.name: Tingqiong Cui, Yibu Yang, Yang Li, Jiahao Fu, Xiaoliu Luo, Xu Wang, Mengzhu Wang, Siyuan Liu, Guanghui Huang

entry.summary: A fully self-supervised blind image quality assessment method that builds a quality reference by exploiting monotonic degradation of information density under repeated random cropping, avoiding synthetic distortions and human labels. It is validated on railway inspection imagery.

entry.title: JoLT: Joint Latent Trajectories for Context-Guided High-Resolution Tiled Generation

author.name: Mathis Koroglu, Guillaume Jeanneret, Hugo Caselles-Dupr\'e, Matthieu Cord, Arnaud Dapogny

entry.summary: JoLT generates high-resolution images by jointly denoising a low-resolution and a high-resolution latent in two interconnected streams, with the low-resolution branch governing layout and the high-resolution branch adding detail. This replaces the usual sequential generate-then-upsample cascade for dense high-resolution synthesis.

entry.title: Efficient Audio-Visual Generation via Synchrony-Aware Cross-Modal Sparse Attention

author.name: Shengchuan Gao, Teng Hu, Bohao Feng, Luchen Li, Wenqiang Wang, Hongqian Deng, Ran Yi

entry.summary: Proposes a synchronization-aware acceleration framework for joint audio-video diffusion generation, arguing that generic sparsification, quantization and caching tricks break cross-modal alignment when applied naively. Cross-modal sparse attention is designed to preserve audio-video synchrony while cutting repeated attention cost over denoising steps.

entry.title: AlloEgo-VLM: Disambiguating Allocentric and Egocentric Reference Frames in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Kuan-Lin Chen, Tzu-Ti Wei, Chao-Chi Liao, Yu-Chee Tseng, Jen-Jee Chen

entry.summary: AlloEgo-VLM studies how vision-language models fail when spatial language omits the reference frame, producing inconsistent answers depending on whether an allocentric or egocentric perspective is assumed. The authors build a dataset of image, query and view-specific answer triplets to make models disambiguate reference frames explicitly.

entry.title: Towards Zero-Shot Domain Generalization for ID Cards Presentation Attack Detection

author.name: Mario Nieto-Hidalgo, Juan M. Espin, Juan E. Tapia

entry.summary: This paper builds a presentation attack detector for national ID cards that generalizes to unseen countries using a prototypical-network head over an EfficientNet backbone, needing only four genuine samples per class. Episodic training varies the card domain while fixing attack classes so the model learns transferable attack cues, reaching roughly 9 percent equal error rate.

entry.title: Some Modifications to Our End-to-End UAV Planner

author.name: Junjie Lu, Bailing Tian

entry.summary: A short technical report describing modifications to the YOPO one-stage UAV planner, including a two-piece MINCO trajectory parameterization for better smoothness and lifting multi-modal prediction to span distinct homotopy classes. The changes address pathologies of soft-constrained learned planning where safety competes with smoothness and goal costs.

entry.title: FollowUpBot: An LLM-Based Conversational Robot for Automatic Postoperative Follow-up

author.name: Chen Chen, Jianing Yin, Jiannong Cao, Zhiyuan Wen, Mingjin Zhang, Weixun Gao, Xiang Wang, Haihua Shu

entry.summary: FollowUpBot is a mobile robot with an on-device LLM that navigates hospital wards and conducts adaptive face-to-face postoperative follow-up conversations, then structures the results into documentation. Edge deployment is motivated by patient privacy concerns with cloud-based automated calling systems.

entry.title:
Value Alignment Is a Pseudo Concept.
A translation; humanity is not a single subject, and alignment is not one-way.

author.name: Davidmanheim

entry.summary: A translated Chinese essay arguing that value alignment is an ill-posed concept because humanity is not a single unified subject with coherent values and because alignment should not be conceived as a one-way imposition. The translator flags partial disagreement while noting the value of surfacing perspectives from outside the Anglophone alignment discourse.

entry.title: The canonical facets of multi-separator polytopes

author.name: Bjoern Andres, Silvia Di Gregorio, Jannik Irmai, Lucas Fabian Naumann, Shengxian Zhao

entry.summary: Provides the first polyhedral analysis of the graph multi-separator problem used as an alternative to lifted multicut for image segmentation, characterizing all facets induced by the natural integer program inequalities via efficiently checkable graph conditions. Strengthens the inequalities and gives a totally dual integral description in a special case.

entry.title: TeachMateGPT: A Multi-Agent Knowledge-Grounded Framework for Pedagogical Assessment Generation from Science Curriculum Materials

author.name: Fatema Tuj Johora Faria, Mukaffi Bin Moin, M. F. Mridha, Jubayer Al Mahmud

entry.summary: CLAIR-Fin decomposes cross-modal financial questions into atomic claims tracked in a typed ledger, conditions evidence trust on claim type rather than treating all modalities equally, and verifies grounding at the hand-off between drafting and adversarial review. Uses nine agents to catch inter-agent errors before the final answer is written.

entry.title: ArtLang: Structured Language-to-Kinematics Grounding for Articulated 3D Actuation

author.name: Sylvia Yuan, Dan Wang, Ravi Ramamoorthi, Xinrui Cui

entry.summary: ArtLang lets users control reconstructed articulated 3D assets with open-vocabulary language by representing each asset as a semantic-kinematic articulation graph and parsing commands into a typed directive graph of referring expressions, actions and magnitudes. Uncertain parts can remain unnamed, and actuation is solved as a global graph-constrained optimization.

entry.title: CLARA: Clip-Level Multimodal Alignment with VLM-Derived Rationales for Hateful Video Detection

author.name: Yuchen Zhang, Shuang Dai, Zeyu Fu, Yunfei Long, Ravi Shekhar, Haralambos Mouratidis

entry.summary: CLARA detects hateful video by aligning speech, audio and visual cues at the clip level and incorporating rationales derived from vision-language models, rather than relying on a single video-level representation. The design targets hateful signals that are brief, implicit and temporally dependent.

entry.title: SCOUT: Semantic Concept Discovery for Open-Vocabulary Editing of face Recognition Templates

author.name: Leon Todorov, Peter Rot, Peter Peer, Vitomir \v{S}truc, Klemen Grm

entry.summary: SCOUT discovers and directly manipulates open-vocabulary semantic concepts inside face recognition template space, without manual neuron inspection or predefined attribute lists. It shows that compact identity embeddings encode editable semantic appearance information, which has clear privacy and template-protection implications.

entry.title: GUIDER: Evaluating Goal-Free Human Intent Inference for Teleoperated Manipulation on Real-Robot Data

author.name: Nicholas Kenny, Cesar Alan Contreras, Basile Ouedraogo, Rustam Stolkin, Manolis Chiou, Maria Kyrarini

entry.summary: This paper evaluates GUIDER, a goal-free probabilistic framework for inferring human intent during teleoperated manipulation, on real robot-arm data from tea-making and medicine-fetching scenarios. Added components include online probability updates, workspace limits, support-plane filtering, and a grasp-feasibility mode, with intent correctly bracketed in all 20 tested steps.

entry.title: Design Optimization for Large High-Force Soft Robot Manipulators Under Gravitational Loads

author.name: Isara Cholaseuk, Penelope Llibre, Alexa Kyriacou, Audrey Wang, Akua K. Dickson, Ran Jing, Juan C. Pacheco Garcia, Andrew P. Sabelhaus

entry.summary: Develops a geometry optimization method for large pneumatic soft robot limbs that maximizes blocking force under an anti-buckling constraint while supporting their own weight, with an explicit closed-form solution under stated assumptions. Three fabricated geometries validate the predictions.

entry.title: Position: Certified Correctness in Neural Constraint Reasoning Requires Symbolic Integration

author.name: Shufeng Kong, Xiaochuan Zhang, Caihua Liu

entry.summary: Argues that neural constraint solvers systematically violate hard constraints under distribution shift even when confident, and that symbolic verification should be integrated whenever checking is cheap relative to solving. Sudoku serves as the representative NP-complete testbed given its polynomial-time verification and exponential search.

entry.title: TAHB: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Text-Attributed Hypergraph Learning

author.name: David Yoon Suk Kang, JungHyun Kim, Juhyun Jeon, Sang-Wook Kim

entry.summary: Releases the first public benchmark pairing hypergraph structure with raw textual node and edge attributes, containing ten real-world datasets from e-commerce, academic, movie, and political networks. It enables systematic study of how pretrained and large language models combine with higher-order graph learning.

entry.title: GraphLoom: Reliability-Calibrated Graph Evidence Routing for Multimodal KG-RAG

author.name: Zafar Ali, Asad Khan, Aalia Malik, Pavlos Kefalas

entry.summary: GraphLoom builds an instance-level multimodal knowledge graph from grounded scene descriptions, extracted triples, and external commonsense, then performs reliability-calibrated subgraph retrieval with bounded expansion instead of dumping all retrieved evidence into the generator. The goal is compact, faithful evidence that supports multi-hop reasoning without unsupported generation.

entry.title: ReasonCast: Agentic Demand Forecasting with Selective Semantic Reasoning

author.name: Ziyue Yang, Chaolin Xu, Yijing Wang, Tiankai Gu, Hui Yang, Yanhong Lin, Kaiyuan Liu, Fei Xiao

entry.summary: ReasonCast has an agent inspect event context, a text-free baseline forecast and its uncertainty, then emit explicit structured interventions (such as level shifts around promotions or holidays) rather than fusing text embeddings uniformly with time series. The aim is selective, interpretable semantic adjustment of demand forecasts.

entry.title: Grounding Healthcare LLMs in a Causal Knowledge Graph: Framework, Metrics, and a Cardiovascular Pilot

author.name: Ummara Mumtaz, Aimen Noor, Awais Ahmed

entry.summary: Proposes evaluating healthcare LLMs against a provenance-preserving causal knowledge graph in which assertions are first-class nodes, extracting scenario-relevant subgraphs and varying how much grounding the model receives. A cardiovascular pilot tests reasoning about interventions, mechanisms, harms and uncertainty rather than single-answer accuracy.

entry.title: Invariant Pretraining for Robust Code Representations

author.name: Yifeng He, Yundi Xu, Christopher Castro Gaw Gonzalo, Zili Wang, Hao Chen

entry.summary: Documents how encoder-based code models degrade when programs are rewritten into semantically equivalent but syntactically different forms, then shows a lightweight continued-pretraining recipe using semantics-preserving transformations that recovers much of the lost robustness. Evaluation spans four encoders, two tasks, and four datasets.

entry.title: EgoGazeLite: On-Device Egocentric Gaze Prediction for Token-Efficient Multimodal LLM Video Input

author.name: Matteo Stoiber, Niels Buus Lassen

entry.summary: Replaces dedicated eye-tracking hardware with an on-device gaze predictor so that egocentric video can be cropped around the likely fixation point before being sent to a multimodal LLM, cutting visual token counts roughly tenfold. The work analyzes the joint accuracy and latency constraints needed to preserve downstream description quality.

entry.title: Temporal Graph Prototype-conditioned Conformal Prediction for Fraud Detection
