author.name: Hyojun Yun, Seungjae Won, Hyungpil Moon

entry.summary: Measures whether offloading the forward pass of a frozen visual encoder in robot policy training from GPU to a low-power INT8 NPU reduces total energy despite added data transfer and longer wall-clock time, using an asynchronous dual-device pipeline with FP32 action expert on GPU. Reports the energy and policy-performance trade-offs of the arrangement.

entry.title: Uncovering Hidden Leptonic Correlations with Flow Matching and Autoencoders

author.name: Haruto Kitagawa, Satsuki Nishimura, Hajime Otsuka

entry.summary: Applies flow matching to generate a broad set of Yukawa matrix and Majorana mass solutions consistent with measured neutrino mass-squared differences and mixing angles in the Type-I seesaw mechanism, then uses an autoencoder to discover latent structure among the solutions. Reports new nonlinear relations involving neutrino masses and CP phases.

entry.title: Maintaining IoT Device Identification under Concept Drift via Budget-Aware Traffic Labeling

author.name: Shayan Azizi, Norihiro Okui, Masataka Nakahara, Ayumu Kubota, Gustavo Batista, Hassan Habibi Gharakaheili

entry.summary: Addresses maintaining IoT device-type classification from passive network traffic as device behavior drifts, arguing that how much traffic to label and which instances to label are separable decisions. Shows that retraining only on drift-detector-selected instances systematically misses parts of the emerging behavior space while uniform sampling wastes budget, and proposes a budget-aware labeling strategy.

entry.title: Coded Hankel Polynomial Chaos: Spectral Identification of Dominant Polynomial-Chaos Modes

author.name: Zhiliang Deng, Xiaomei Yang

entry.summary: Develops a spectral alternative to sparse regression for identifying dominant polynomial-chaos expansion modes, converting coefficients into an exponential sum whose order and nodes are recovered from low-rank Hankel matrices with root-of-unity phase labels. Targets uncertainty quantification for high-dimensional surrogate models.

entry.title: Cross-Disciplinary Taxonomy and Modeling of Misunderstanding Generation, Amplification, and Detection, from Pragmatics to AI Agents

author.name: Babak Abbaschian

entry.summary: A cross-disciplinary synthesis of research on communicative misunderstanding, organizing it into generation, amplification, detection, and repair stages with eleven identified failure modes tied to specific points in a conversation. It argues AI-mediated communication removes the repair cues humans normally rely on.

entry.title: HistReNeRF: Historic Image Relocalisation within Contemporary Neural Radiance Field Reconstructions

author.name: Benjamin T. Hughes, Stuart James

entry.summary: HistReNeRF estimates the 6-DoF camera pose of archival photographs inside a modern neural radiance field reconstruction by matching adapted DINOv2 patch features against rays sampled from the NeRF. The continuous scene representation acts as a queryable interface enabling feature-space domain adaptation across large appearance and layout gaps.

entry.title: Automated Fetal Brain MRI Biometry in Healthy and Pathological Cases

author.name: Ema Masterl, Tina Vipotnik Vesnaver, Nejc \v{S}ubi\v{c}, \v{Z}iga \v{S}piclin

entry.summary: Assembles and validates an automated fetal brain MRI biometry pipeline that localizes 22 landmarks on reconstructed 3D volumes and derives 11 clinically relevant measurements, comparing two landmark localization networks. Evaluation spans 122 acquisitions including pathological cases, using mixed-effects modeling and comparison with normative growth curves.

entry.title: TISC: A Text-Driven Image Semantic Communication System for Faithful Reconstruction

author.name: Feifan Zhang, Yuyang Du, Xiaoyan Liu, Soung Chang Liew

entry.summary: TISC is a text-driven image semantic communication system that converts images to text for extremely low-bandwidth transmission and reconstructs them with diffusion at the receiver, addressing semantic loss during captioning and unfaithful reconstruction. It targets fine-grained attribute and spatial-position preservation across both stages.

entry.title: Bit-Level Triangular Content-Aware Permutation for Fragile Image Watermarking: Zero False Positive Rate, Single-Bit Sensitivity, and Arbitrary Dimension Support

author.name: Zahra Ghoraeian, Mohammad-Reza Sadeghi, Samaneh Mashhadi

entry.summary: A fragile image watermarking scheme replaces hash functions with a bit-plane content-aware permutation that has an avalanche property, aiming for zero false positives, single-bit tamper sensitivity, and support for arbitrary image dimensions. It targets vector quantization and collage attacks that defeat prior methods.

entry.title: Platform Adaptation Under Governance Interventions: Actor Best-Response Modeling and an External Public-Case Benchmark

author.name: Wesley Shu, Peng Wei

entry.summary: Proposes a game-theoretic style model of how platform participants best-respond to governance changes such as ranking tweaks, monetization thresholds and moderation rules, and evaluates it against 72 documented public platform cases. The goal is to predict gaming, moderation burden and downstream stability before interventions ship.

entry.title: MistyPilot: Enabling Social-Robot Control through Multi-Agent LLM Skill Orchestration

author.name: Xiao Wang, Lu Dong, Ifeoma Nwogu, Srirangaraj Setlur, Venu Govindaraju

entry.summary: Builds a multi-agent LLM controller for a commercial social robot that routes natural-language instructions to either a sensor-triggered physical control agent or a stateful social interaction agent, handling skill composition and event binding automatically. It removes much of the manual API plumbing developers currently do.

entry.title: Feasible and Novel Synthetic Population Generation with Tabular and Sequential Travel Attributes

author.name: Farbod Abbasi, Zachary Patterson, Bilal Farooq

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage regularized generative framework for synthesizing travel-demand populations that must combine static socio-demographics with sequential trip chains, explicitly balancing coverage of unobserved but valid combinations against generation of structurally impossible ones. Stage one uses an adversarial tabular generator with added regularization terms.

entry.title: Grounding Without Corrective Control: Truth-Tracking Profiles for Large Language Models

author.name: Brett Reynolds

entry.summary: A philosophical analysis distinguishing grounding from corrective control, arguing that LLM representations can have reference without live routes for detecting and repairing discrepancies. It develops route profiles as a tool for analyzing when a system's outputs genuinely track truth.

entry.title: PCT-Prompt: A Prompt-Guided Transformer Framework for Dense Prediction Tasks in Point Clouds

author.name: Dejun Zhang, Yanzi Bai, Yiqi Wu

entry.summary: PCT-Prompt augments a standard point cloud transformer with a prompt-guided feature branch that injects fine-grained multi-scale geometric priors for dense prediction in complex scenes. The pretrained transformer branch handles global features while the prompt branch supplies the missing local geometric inductive bias.

entry.title: Visible Reasoning and Indirect Prompt-Injection Monitorability Across English, Tamil, and Tanglish

author.name: Madhusudhanan G

entry.summary: A small case study of whether API-visible chain-of-thought helps monitor indirect prompt-injection attacks in one Indic-multilingual model across English, Tamil and code-mixed Tanglish. A pilot suggested reasoning reduced attack success, but a preregistered follow-up reversed the direction, and the author concludes the design cannot separate a real effect from prompt-specific noise.

entry.title: Large Language Model Assisted Operational Monitoring for Battery Energy Storage System Integrated Power Distribution Networks

author.name: Azmeer Akhtar, Md Fazley Rafy, Anurag K. Srivastava

entry.summary: Builds an operator-facing LLM interface that converts natural-language questions about battery storage in distribution networks into validated SQL over approved telemetry views, then checks retrieved measurements against engineering constraints. Aims to make grid telemetry queryable without exposing operators to unconstrained model output.

entry.title: A Responsible Artificial Intelligence Framework for Groundwater Modeling

author.name: Chong Chen, Yulu Zhang, Qingxi Guo, Yihan Liu

entry.summary: Applies six responsible-AI principles to groundwater modeling in a river basin case study, training LSTM and Transformer time-series models and validating them with post-hoc interpretability and related checks. Argues responsible AI practice is especially underdeveloped in hydrology compared to healthcare or finance.

entry.title: CoupVisor: Strategy Optimization by Round and Challenge Decision Support

author.name: Cris Huynh

entry.summary: CoupVisor is a decision-support system for the hidden-information card game Coup that shares one event representation across manual play, replay, simulation, belief tracking and learned policies, and estimates claim truthfulness by combining role priors with card counts. It compares rule-based advisors with learned and heuristic players.

entry.title: UAV Video Deblurring via Motion-Aware Diffusion: A Path to Robust Target Detection

author.name: Zhiqiang Hu, Shouren Huang, Masatoshi Ishikawa

entry.summary: Proposes a diffusion-based video deblurring pipeline for drone footage that adapts latent-space resolution to motion intensity and enforces temporal consistency, aiming to restore downstream target detection accuracy. The contribution is mostly an engineering combination of adaptive latent scaling with a motion-aware diffusion restorer for aerial imagery.

entry.title: ENAF: A Multi-Exit Network with an Adaptive Patch Fusion for Large Image Super Resolution

author.name: Duong M. Nguyen, Tuan Nghia Nguyen, Xuan Truong Nguyen

entry.summary: Builds a dynamic super-resolution network for very large images that uses early exits plus a tiny predictor of reconstruction quality to decide how much computation each patch deserves, replacing hand-crafted difficulty heuristics. An adaptive fusion step recombines patches processed at different depths.

entry.title: Identifying Confusion Trends in Concept-based XAI for Multi-Label Classification

author.name: Haadia Amjad, Ronald Tetzlaff

entry.summary: Evaluates two concept-based explanation methods on multi-label image classification with common backbones trained on the most annotated categories of a standard object dataset, focusing on where concept attributions become confused between co-occurring labels. The study characterizes systematic confusion patterns rather than proposing a new method.

entry.title: A Scalable Pipeline for LLM-Teacher Distillation Labeling: Work-Stealing Job Scheduling and Memory-Aware GPU Concurrency

author.name: Ravi Satya Durga Prasad Yenugula

entry.summary: Describes an engineering pipeline for large-scale distillation labeling with teacher models, combining a work-stealing job scheduler with exactly-once claims and crash tolerance with memory-aware GPU concurrency control. It is designed to be reproducible using only a compare-and-set primitive over a simple embedded database.

entry.title: Decoupling Parcellation from Classification: Systematic Benchmark of Fast Brain Segmentation Methods for Alzheimer's Disease Detection

author.name: Jiadao Zou, Hongyu Guo, Wei Xi

entry.summary: Systematically benchmarks fast deep-learning brain parcellation methods against a clinical baseline by measuring their effect on downstream Alzheimer's classification, across volumetry strategies and four classifier families including foundation models with few-shot prompting. All results are reported with bootstrap confidence intervals.

entry.title: Domain-Specific Text Embedding Models for Entity Resolution

author.name: Khajesh Sapram, Srivardhani Raju, Kishore Konda

entry.summary: The authors fine-tune general text embedding models with triplet objectives on synthetic business and person records containing identity-preserving variations and hard negatives, to make retrieval sensitive to entity identity rather than mere semantic similarity. Margin-based evaluation shows improved separation of matching versus non-matching records after adaptation.

entry.title: Fiber Fingerprints of Hidden Learning-State Dynamics

author.name: Qinyou Wang

entry.summary: Formalizes the idea that two learning systems can be behaviorally indistinguishable now yet respond differently to future training, defining fiber fingerprints as future-learning response laws restricted to present-behavior equivalence classes. Builds a Nerode-style minimal predictive representation and decomposes responses into visible, mode-reuse, and irreducible-new components.

entry.title: On Cross-Validation for Hyperparameter Optimization of Deep Learning Image Classifiers

author.name: Ljubomir Buturovic (East Palo Alto, United States)

entry.summary: Empirically compares fixed holdout, reshuffled holdout, and five-fold cross-validation as the validation signal driving hyperparameter search for deep image classifiers, scoring protocols by the absolute gap between the winning configuration's validation AUROC and its test AUROC. Focuses on small-sample regimes typical of medical imaging with search space, sampler, and test set held identical.

entry.title: STAR-FL: Secure Federated Learning with Spatial-Temporal Analysis and Robust Aggregation

author.name: Nawrin Tabassum, Yanzhao Wu

entry.summary: STAR-FL defends federated vision models against targeted data poisoning by clustering client updates over both space and time to identify and drop suspicious contributions, then damping the learning rate during aggregation to limit the residual influence of poisoned updates. Addresses the twin problems of detection accuracy and post-detection mitigation.

entry.title: An Adaptive Gradient Clipping and Noise Injection Mechanism for Differentially Private Federated Learning

author.name: Wenjing Wei, Alla Jammine, Farid Nait-Abdesselam

entry.summary: Presents an adaptive per-layer gradient clipping and noise calibration mechanism for differentially private federated learning with secure aggregation, where each client sets each layer's clipping threshold from the median of its per-sample gradient norms at every round. Aims to avoid the excessive clipping or excessive noise inherent in a single static global threshold.

entry.title: Identifying parameter couplings and uncertainties of mixed-noise stochastic systems via full-covariance Gaussian mixture network

author.name: Xiaolong Wang, Xiangwen Hao, Jing Feng, Yuanyuan Liu, Yong Xu

entry.summary: PENN-GMD trains a neural network to map partially observed trajectories of stochastic dynamical systems driven by mixed noise to a full-covariance Gaussian mixture over system parameters, using a surjective parameterization that hard-encodes mixture constraints and training by negative log-likelihood. The full covariance structure exposes parameter couplings and multimodal likelihood geometry that point estimates hide.

entry.title: LLMs Don't Pay for the Jump

author.name: Paras Balani, Subhrakanta Panda

entry.summary: A short position piece rebutting the claim that LLMs cannot perform creative abductive leaps for lack of embodied simulation, using Planck's quantization of energy as a counterexample driven by mathematical inconsistency rather than sensorimotor grounding. It is argument rather than experiment.

entry.title: Depth-Dominant Skeleton Detection for Natural Scenes

author.name: Chengkun Rao, Yixuan Deng, Min Li, Yangjun Ou, Ye Li, Ziwei Luo, Zhaojing Wang, Junwei Tang, Bangchao Wang, Xiaoyun Yan

entry.summary: DDSkel inverts the usual modality hierarchy for natural scene skeleton detection, making depth the dominant input and RGB auxiliary, on the grounds that depth is insensitive to color and texture clutter while giving clean contours. The paper claims first exploration of this depth-dominant paradigm for skeleton extraction.

entry.title: Incision trajectory tracing for electrosurgical navigation by CNN-based knife contacting frames extraction method

author.name: Yu Chun Wang, Kaixu Chen, Naoto Ienaga, Yoshihiro Kuroda

entry.summary: This study uses a CNN on thermal images to detect when an electrosurgical knife or ultrasonic cutter is actually contacting tissue, then extracts those contact frames to reconstruct incision trajectories for surgical navigation. The trajectories are intended to update preoperative 3D models during surgery.

entry.title: AccretionLink: On-Device Auditing of Exposure-Control Attacks on Attribute Inference

author.name: Faruk Alpay, Taylan Alpay

entry.summary: Studies an attack in which an adversary does not alter content but merely reorders or selects which authentic public posts a model sees, in order to strengthen inference of a private attribute, and proposes time-uniform e-process auditing for detecting it. Effects reported on synthetic profiles and a PAN15 test set are very small in magnitude.

entry.title: What 27 AI Safety Generalists Are Building This Summer

author.name: agucova

entry.summary: A roundup of projects from 27 participants in the first cohort of a Berkeley-based residency for AI safety generalists, including workshops for mid-career professionals entering the field, talent directories, university group support, and tooling for model welfare and model spec research. It is primarily a field-building status report.

entry.title: An Agentic Framework Using Rules and LLMs for Embedding and Annotating Descriptive Document Layouts: A Plant Science Use Case

author.name: Nicolas Turenne, Youcef Sklab, Eric Chenin, Jean-Daniel Zucker

entry.summary: Presents an agentic pipeline combining rules and LLMs to embed and annotate descriptive document layouts, applied to plant science literature for improved retrieval over structured botanical descriptions. It integrates layout analysis, dense and sparse retrieval, and multi-agent reasoning.

entry.title: Accuracy and Reliability of Large Language Models in Cosmetic Chemistry and Skin Health: A Benchmarking Study

author.name: Amelia Liu

entry.summary: Benchmarks 14 LLMs, with web search disabled, on cosmetic chemistry and skin health questions covering ingredient properties and consumer scenarios. Performance is generally weak, especially on quantitative reasoning and chemical structure identification, even though general skincare answers appear reasonable.

entry.title: Demand-Driven Vertiport Siting and Discrete-Event Fleet Simulation for On-Demand Urban Air Mobility Network Design

author.name: Hossein Z. Saghazadeh, Yonas Ayalew, Reza Ahmari, Parham Kebria, Abdollah Homaifar

entry.summary: Presents a demand-driven pipeline for urban air mobility network design that clusters estimated trip endpoints into candidate vertiport sites, screens networks under range and spacing constraints, and evaluates them with a discrete-event simulation of dispatch, deadheading, and battery swaps. A Los Angeles case study assesses door-to-door travel-time feasibility.

entry.title: Validation-Frontier Representation Selection under Constrained Observation

author.name: Wesley Shu

entry.summary: Studies how to choose a state representation when observations are incomplete, costly, or degraded, proposing a selector that trades balanced accuracy against feature cost, overfit gap, and validation-to-test instability. It is evaluated on three standard tabular datasets across five observation regimes.

entry.title: Constitutive Priors for Machine Intelligence: A Legitimacy Theory of the Artificial Physical World

author.name: Jiang Jiang (Persagy Science and Technology Co., Beijing, China), Yifu Sun (Persagy Science and Technology Co., Beijing, China), Qi Shen (Persagy Science and Technology Co., Beijing, China)

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that physical-world AI can escape its data cold-start problem by exploiting the fact that buildings and infrastructure ship with design archives that constitute their instances. It proposes a four-world ontology and a legitimacy criterion for when such documents may serve as priors.

entry.title: Baseline-Relative Counterfactual Refinement for Bit-Aware Visual Token Communication

author.name: Jia Guo, Xiaohan Zhao, Changwang Liu, Shuqing He, Chenyang Zhang, Bingchuan Zhao, Jinqi Zhu

entry.summary: GCR-C adds a rollout-style counterfactual correction layer to generative visual-token communication, replacing a baseline token-selection action only when a matched full-budget continuation shows a positive reconstruction gain under the same packet budget. It aims to fix the mismatch between local token-importance heuristics and end reconstruction quality. Application is bandwidth-constrained semantic communication.

entry.title: Drive, Pack, Fly: The Travelling Thief Problem with Drone

author.name: Kabir Murjani, Abhay Sobhanan

entry.summary: The paper introduces a routing variant in which a ground vehicle slows as its payload grows while an onboard drone retrieves outlying items, jointly optimizing item selection, routing, and flight synchronization to maximize profit net of time-based rental cost. A mixed-integer program solves small instances exactly and heuristics handle larger ones. It extends the travelling thief problem with drone logistics.

entry.title: Multi-Modal Generative Fuzzy System: Fuzzy Inference Guided Large Model Interactive Question Answering Framework

author.name: Hailong Yang, Jianqi Wang, Guanjin Wang, Zhaohong Deng

entry.summary: This framework uses fuzzy inference to guide large multimodal models in question answering, aiming to counter modality bias from differing feature distributions and to represent uncertainty when questions require knowledge from several domains. Fuzzy rules provide interpretable intermediate structure over deep semantic reasoning. It targets robustness in multimodal question answering.

entry.title: Fractional Optimizers Meet Fractal Activation Functions: An Empirical Study of Multi-Scale Optimization in Neural Network

author.name: Sebastian Raubitzek, Georg Goldenits, Sebastian Schrittwieser, Philip K\"onig, Kevin Mallinger

entry.summary: This empirical study examines whether fractional-derivative optimizers and fractal, self-similar activation functions interact usefully, evaluating optimizer families on synthetic benchmark surfaces with and without multi-scale perturbations and then in feedforward networks across ten classification datasets. The framing is multi-scale optimization matched to multi-scale nonlinearity. Results compare against conventional activations and optimizers.

entry.title: FedImp: Enhancing Federated Learning Convergence with Impurity-Based Weighting

author.name: Hai Anh Tran, Cuong Ta, Truong X. Tran

entry.summary: FedImp weights client contributions in federated averaging by the informational impurity of each client's local data distribution, aiming to speed convergence under non-IID conditions. Experiments on EMNIST and CIFAR-10 report substantial reductions in communication rounds.

entry.title: Does the Heart Show Your Pain? Tackling the X-ITE Pain Challenge with Self-Supervised ECG Representation Learning

author.name: Dominika Kunc, Przemys{\l}aw Kazienko, Stanis{\l}aw Saganowski

entry.summary: Evaluates self-supervised representation learning on ECG, plus multimodal pretraining with chest accelerometry, for classifying low versus medium pain on the X-ITE dataset. Results are modest overall and highlight large inter-subject variability in physiological pain signatures.

entry.title: Offline Ambient-Controlled Latent Diffusion: Architecture, Telemetry, and On-Device Evaluation

author.name: Lech Kalinowski, Artur Morys-Magiera, Piotr Mi{\l}kowski

entry.summary: Presents an Android app running latent diffusion fully on-device, conditioned on the ambient light sensor rather than text, with each generated artifact bound to its sensor reading, runtime path, and seed. The contribution is the auditability and telemetry workflow rather than a new generative method.

entry.title: Handover Analysis for Vehicular Communication with Explainability on the Fly

author.name: Ali Fuat Sahin, Semiha Tedik Ba\c{s}aran, Tufan Kumbasar

entry.summary: Applies inherently interpretable functional ANOVA models to handover detection in vehicular networks, using two real operator datasets, and compares against an LSTM with post-hoc SHAP explanations. The claim is that on-the-fly interpretability can match black-box accuracy while giving operators trustworthy real-time reasons.

entry.title: DualMiT-Net: Local-Global Transformer-Convolutional Fusion for Breast Mass Segmentation in Mammographic Regions of Interest

author.name: Alibek Kamiluly, Milana Muratova, Yash Patel, Fan Li

entry.summary: DualMiT-Net segments breast masses in mammographic regions of interest using a local Mix Transformer branch for mass detail and a global EfficientNet branch for surrounding tissue context, fused through a spatially gated decoder. The design targets low-contrast, irregular masses whose boundaries blend into breast tissue.

entry.title: LAPF: LLM-Agent-Based Path Finder Using the UAVScenes Dataset

author.name: Yousef Emami, Mohammadhossein Homaei, Hao Zhou, Miguel Guti\'errez Gait\'an, Atefeh Hajijamali Arani, Rui Zhang

entry.summary: LAPF wraps an LLM agent with memory, planning, and tool interaction around UAV path finding using the UAVScenes dataset, aiming for adaptability that predefined optimization or task-specific RL policies lack. The framework targets dynamic outdoor missions with uncertain conditions.

entry.title: Quantifying the Gap Between Laboratory Battery Test Patterns and Field Duty Profiles

author.name: Chunyang Zhao, Chresten Tr{\ae}holt

entry.summary: Quantifies the mismatch between laboratory battery test protocols and real field duty profiles across six data sources using usage frequency, intensity, C-rate, and a duty-structure index. Finds lab protocols are far more aggressive and structured than field traces, questioning degradation models trained on lab data.

entry.title: One Residual with Three Reuses: A Wristband Front End for Gesture Sensing

author.name: Sam Rifaki

entry.summary: Design study of an always-on wristband sensing front end that shares a single on-chip residual generator across classifier wake-up gating, radar-versus-IMU routing, and Kalman filter measurement reweighting, fitting in about 14 KB of program memory at 110K MACs per frame. Targets coin-cell power budgets for gesture and motor-symptom monitoring.

entry.title: An Analytical-Prior Framework for Data-Efficient Prediction of Sound-Reduction Frequencies in Rectangular Side-Branch Helmholtz Resonators

author.name: Jiaming Li

entry.summary: Uses a cheap analytical acoustic model as a prior for predicting sound-reduction frequencies of side-branch Helmholtz resonators under scarce finite-element data, either learning only the analytical-to-simulation discrepancy or distilling the analytical mapping into a self-contained predictor. Improves data efficiency for engineering surrogates.

entry.title: 6G Native AI and Channel Foundation Models

author.name: Shugong Xu, Jun Jiang, Yuan Gao

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that so-called native AI in 6G should be co-designed as an intrinsic part of the wireless system rather than bolted on, and that task-specific supervised models cannot serve as the technical basis because of labeled-data dependence and poor generalization across propagation environments. Advocates channel foundation models as the alternative substrate.

entry.title: Phase-Aware CNN for Real-Time 5G/6G Channel Estimation with Hardware-in-the-loop Validation

author.name: Javad Zolfaghari-Bengar, Rakibul Rony, Elisa Gomez-de-Lope, Alejandro Villena-Rodriguez, Abhinav Mahadevan, Nicolas Kourtellis

entry.summary: Presents a phase-aware convolutional network for pilot-based 5G/6G channel estimation that reconstructs both magnitude and phase across the subcarrier grid, explicitly handling the wrap-around discontinuity that degrades naive deep estimators. Evaluation uses emulated data from an end-to-end O-RAN testbed with hardware in the loop rather than pure simulation.

entry.title: The Physical Cutoff Does Not Restore Homogenization: Phase-Dependent Burning in the Strain G-Equation

author.name: Michele Caprio

entry.summary: Disproves a stated expectation that the physically motivated positive-part strain G-equation admits an effective burning velocity in two-dimensional cellular flows, exhibiting parameter ranges where phase-dependent burning persists. Shows that under physical rescaling an order-one gap survives between nearby points at every positive macroscopic time, so rescaled solutions have no locally uniformly convergent subsequence and homogenization fails.

entry.title: Resource-Efficient QUBO Formulation for Anchored Currency Arbitrage

author.name: Eric A. F. Reinhardt, Adam J. Hauser

entry.summary: Reformulates currency arbitrage cycle detection as a QUBO problem with realistic constraints such as starting from a held currency and per-transaction fees, requiring fewer binary variables than prior encodings. Includes provably sufficient penalty weights and an exact rate reweighting that compresses the problem.

entry.title: Anatomical and Physical Supervision for CT-less PET Attenuation Correction: BIC-MAC 2026 Challenge

author.name: Petros Chatzitoulousis, George K. Matsopoulos

entry.summary: A challenge submission report for CT-less PET attenuation correction that synthesizes pseudo-CT with an nnU-Net, adding frozen segmentation-model features, anatomy-guided constraints and a differentiable attenuation projection loss. Pretraining on synthetic data is used for initialization.

entry.title: Not All Attention Is Equal: A Quantitative Survey of the EEI Trade-off

author.name: Aditya Singh

entry.summary: A survey of twenty-one attention mechanisms scored along efficiency, expressiveness, and interpretability axes, with a Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis of the scoring. The analysis itself shows that rankings shift substantially under small perturbations to the subjective scores.

entry.title: Hierarchical Adaptive Feature Refinement Network for VHR Remote Sensing Image Segmentation

author.name: Shuaishuai Cao, Meng Tang, Shuwei Peng, Xuan Liu, Min Huang, Jie Chen, Jiacheng Niu, Yong Chen, Edore Akpokodje, Hui Lin

entry.summary: Proposes a segmentation network for very-high-resolution satellite imagery that adaptively weights multi-stage features from a pretrained hierarchical encoder and refines them conservatively rather than replacing them with a heavy decoder. Dense per-region stage weights let nearby areas trade detail against context differently.

entry.title: ARISE: An adaptive residual-informed stability ensemble for feature selection in small-sample biomedical omics

author.name: Zardad Khan, Amjad Ali, Naz Gul, Sheema Gul, Saeed Aldahmani

entry.summary: ARISE is an ensemble feature selector for small-sample omics classification that fuses seven percentile-normalized relevance signals through fifteen predefined weighting profiles chosen by nested inner cross-validation, adds class-balanced stability assessment, residual-informed redundancy control, and pairwise coverage for multiclass problems. Benchmarked on five molecular datasets against six filter methods with three fixed classifiers.

entry.title: Distribution-free false-alarm calibration and chance-corrected spatial evaluation for industrial anomaly detection

author.name: Jie Deng

entry.summary: Argues that industrial visual inspection evaluations relying on AUROC and raw anomaly-map overlap hide the operating false-alarm rate and are inflated by recurring defect locations and mask geometry. Proposes a distribution-free upper tolerance threshold plus a paired-versus-crossed spatial test that credits a detector only for overlap exceeding chance, demonstrated on point-defect images across modalities.

entry.title: FedADB: Class Anchor-Driven Dual-Branch Federated Learning for Mitigating Forgetting

author.name: Zhenyan Liu, Hua Zhang, Haoran Gao, Qi Li, Hongliang Zhu, Huiyu Zhou, Zongliang Shen, Yanxin Xu, Jiahui Wang

entry.summary: FedADB attacks the forgetting of global knowledge during local training in heterogeneous multimodal federated learning by combining class anchors with a dual-branch design, aiming to retain global consistency without the local-optimization interference caused by strict global alignment or the reliance on proxy datasets. Targets improved supervision for classes missing from individual clients.

entry.title: Adaptive Heterogeneous Compression for Resource-Efficient Federated Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Chenwang Liu, Yijun Liu, Chang Liu, Xu Zhang, Pengchao Han

entry.summary: Proposes a heterogeneous compression framework for federated knowledge distillation in which each client selects a compression strategy matched to its own model characteristics and resource capacity, rather than applying one uniform scheme across clients. Targets the communication overhead that persists when transmitting gradients even after prototype-based aggregation mitigates model heterogeneity.

entry.title: Multi-scale Decomposed Convolution Refinement Network for Visible-Infrared Person Re-Identification

author.name: Mingsheng Zheng, Zirui Jiang, Bo Liu, Yupeng Chen, Jun Zhang, Kai Zhao

entry.summary: MDCRNet improves visible-infrared person re-identification with hierarchical decomposed convolution attention modules that combine lightweight channel attention with multi-scale spatial perception, plus modified metric constraints. The goal is better cross-modal feature learning and discriminability.

entry.title: Advanced modelling and data analytics in aviation

author.name: Aziida Nanyonga

entry.summary: Applies machine learning, deep learning, and NLP over aviation safety datasets from several national and international sources to mine incident narratives and improve prediction of safety events. The work aggregates existing model families rather than proposing new architectures.

entry.title: Beyond Thresholds: A Quality-Aware Decision Intelligence Framework for Cold Chain IoT Systems

author.name: Aashna Sofat, Balwinder Sodhi

entry.summary: Proposes a decision-intelligence framework for cold chain logistics that replaces threshold alerts with a quality state vector covering remaining shelf life, degradation rate, uncertainty, and operational risk, combining microbial kinetics with a learned correction term and an LLM-based reasoning layer. The aim is to convert sensor violations into logistics decisions.

entry.title: Reasoning-supported Robustness Validation of Automotive E/E Components

author.name: Jan Novacek, Alexander Viehl, Oliver Bringmann, Wolfgang Rosenstiel

entry.summary: This work formalizes automotive robustness validation knowledge, including stress and load mission profiles, in an OWL ontology so that analysis selection and decision support can be automated with semantic queries. It replaces an error-prone manual industrial procedure with a machine-queryable representation. The contribution is knowledge engineering for hardware reliability workflows.

entry.title: From Reactive to Autonomous: Evolution of AI Operations in Cloud Network Infrastructure

author.name: Arun Malik

entry.summary: This experience paper traces cloud network operations through five generations from manual troubleshooting to scripted automation, rule engines, AI assistance, and autonomous incident resolution, presenting a maturity model and the technical and organizational barriers at each transition. It draws on hyperscale production experience. The value is practitioner framing rather than new results.

entry.title: Ring-based Spatial Transformer: Learning Non-linear Spatial Interactions between Building Distribution and Pedestrian Flow

author.name: Shun Nakayama, Takahiro Kanamori, Wanglin Yan

entry.summary: Applies a transformer over concentric ring buffers around Tokyo railway stations, treating each distance ring as a token, to predict GPS-derived pedestrian flow from building-use composition. It outperforms geographically weighted regression across 30 trials, with SHAP indicating mid-to-outer rings matter most.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving Dataset Curation for Kuala Lumpur Urban Traffic: Grounded Vision-Language Detection with Spatial Vehicle-Context Filtering

author.name: Mohammed Abdul Al Arafat Tanzin, Rudzidatul Akmam Dziyauddin

entry.summary: Describes an automated PII anonymization pipeline for a Kuala Lumpur urban driving dataset, using grounded vision-language detection with spatial vehicle-context filtering. The authors document concrete failure modes of Haar cascades and YOLOv8 under tropical glare, dark license plates, and high motorcycle density.

entry.title: PAS-QFL: Personalized Ansatz Selection for Quantum Federated Learning under Client Data Heterogeneity

author.name: Jindi Wu, Qun Li

entry.summary: PAS-QFL personalizes quantum federated learning by decomposing each client's quantum neural network into a shared global ansatz and a client-specific private component, so that heterogeneous non-IID clients can use circuit structures suited to their data. It targets instability and unfairness caused by imposing a single ansatz on all clients.

entry.title: A Unified Backbone--Expert Framework with Relation-Token and Residual--Classifier Interfaces for Automatic Modulation Recognition

author.name: Zhixiang Deng, Houbiao Li, Zongyong Cui

entry.summary: Proposes a shared convolutional state-space backbone with two specialized interfaces for automatic modulation recognition: lag-aware complex-plane relation tokens for short signal windows and gated multi-scale residual refinement with classifier averaging for long ones. Reported accuracies are around 67 percent on RML2016.10b and related benchmarks.

entry.title: Shape Operator PCA: Curvature-Aware Projections for Geometric Machine Learning

author.name: Alexandre L. M. Levada

entry.summary: Proposes a variant of principal component analysis that regularizes the covariance matrix with an averaged shape operator estimated from the data manifold, steering components toward directions of high curvature as well as high variance. A single mixing parameter interpolates between standard PCA and a fully curvature-driven embedding.

entry.title: EA-LiteUNet: An Edge-Adaptive and Resource-Efficient U-Net for Boundary-Sensitive Dermoscopic Image Segmentation

author.name: Wang Jiangtao, Nur Intan Raihana Ruhaiyem, Fu Panpan, Yang Yu, Huang Yan

entry.summary: Presents a lightweight U-Net variant with edge-adaptive components for skin lesion segmentation, motivated by the observation that lesion boundaries are high-frequency content destroyed by repeated downsampling. It targets accurate boundary delineation at low computational cost.

entry.title: Comprehensive Benchmarking of Deep Learning Architectures for Lung Cancer Histopathology

author.name: Hadi Hasan, Safaa Salman, Lama Sleem, Ralph Mouawad, Ali Chehab

entry.summary: Benchmarks a range of deep architectures for lung cancer histopathology in a two-stage pipeline covering tissue classification and pixel-level region segmentation. The contribution is a systematic comparison rather than a new model.

entry.title: Dynamic Evidence Collection Ecosystem for Assessment Integrity and Authentic Competence

author.name: Rajan Kadel, Bellal Hossain, Samar Shailendra, Bushra Naeem

entry.summary: Proposes an assessment design framework that replaces single-submission grading with continuous collection of process evidence such as iterative artefacts, design logs, reflection, and peer collaboration, supported by learning analytics. It responds to generative AI making product-only assessment unreliable.

entry.title: Population Structure Analysis of an Inbred Population using Quantitative Shape Phenotyping from Stereo Retinal Photographs

author.name: Li Tang, Michael D Abramoff

entry.summary: Applies stereo reconstruction of optic nerve head 3D shape plus self-taught deep feature learning to distinguish descendants of the Bounty mutineers from other residents in an inbred Norfolk Island cohort. The work treats retinal shape as a heritable quantitative phenotype for population structure analysis.

entry.title: Optimizing Multi-Market Participation of Battery and Electrolyser Systems Based on Field Performance

author.name: Chunyang Zhao, Stoyan Trenchev, Shi You, Chresten Tr{\ae}holt

entry.summary: Characterizes a real 55 kW battery system and a small electrolyser stack experimentally (ramp limits, efficiency, setpoint-tracking error) and embeds those measured behaviors into a price-driven multi-market bidding optimization. Shows that ignoring hardware realities distorts revenue-stacking estimates.

entry.title: A Parameter-Free Few-Shot Evaluation for Elephant Vocalisation Classification

author.name: Christiaan M. Geldenhuys, Thomas R. Niesler

entry.summary: Evaluates parameter-free nearest-centroid episodic classification of elephant vocalizations on frozen pretrained audio embeddings including Perch versions 1 and 2 and HuBERT, comparing against MFCC baselines as the number of labelled exemplars per class varies. The framing asks how the simplest possible classifier scales with label budget rather than which embedding wins with full supervision.

entry.title: Explainability Boosted Anomaly Detection Framework for O-RAN based NextG Networks

author.name: Nurullah Aksu, Ali Fuat Sahin, Semiha Tedik Ba\c{s}aran

entry.summary: Builds an anomaly detection framework for Open RAN next-generation cellular networks, benchmarking several AI models for accuracy and runtime on a realistic O-RAN testbed and adding post-hoc explainability to surface the key performance indicators that drive malicious-traffic decisions. Positions explainability as an operational aid for network security teams.

entry.title: BERTopic-Virality Prioritisation: A Scalable Framework for Thematic and Comparative Analysis of COVID-19 and Monkeypox Misinformation on Twitter

author.name: Mkululi Sikosana, Sean Maudsley-Barton, Oluwaseun Ajao

entry.summary: Extends BERTopic with a post hoc virality prioritization layer so that topic discovery surfaces themes that are both semantically coherent and rapidly diffusing, rather than treating engagement as an external outcome. Adds a two-stage misinformation detector fusing a supervised content classifier with an external public-health knowledge-base verification signal, applied comparatively to COVID-19 and monkeypox Twitter data.

entry.title: Deep learning-based computed tomography (CT) derived body composition classifier for colorectal cancer patients

author.name: Eve Harling (James Watt School of Engineering, College of Science & Engineering, University of Glasgow, Glasgow, UK), Chattarin Pumtako (Academic Unit of Surgery, School of Medicine, College of Medical Veterinary & Life Sciences, University of Glasgow, Glasgow, UK), Bernd Porr (James Watt School of Engineering, College of Science & Engineering, University of Glasgow, Glasgow, UK), Donald C McMillan (Academic Unit of Surgery, School of Medicine, College of Medical Veterinary & Life Sciences, University of Glasgow, Glasgow, UK), Ross D Dolan (Academic Unit of Surgery, School of Medicine, College of Medical Veterinary & Life Sciences, University of Glasgow, Glasgow, UK)

entry.summary: Pilot feasibility study training four standard CNN architectures to regress skeletal muscle area and density plus subcutaneous and visceral fat area directly from CT scans of colorectal cancer patients, replacing labor-intensive manual body composition annotation. Frames automated regression as a route to routine clinical use of these nutritional-status markers.

entry.title: A Survey of Large Models in Sports

author.name: Yichen Xu, Jianzhe Ma, Chuhan Wang, Zhonghao Cao, Liangyu Chen, Wenxuan Wang, Qin Jin

entry.summary: A survey mapping how large language and multimodal models are being applied across sports tasks, covering user groups, datasets, benchmarks, and open challenges. It is a landscape paper rather than a technical contribution, useful mainly as an entry point for a niche application area.

entry.title: Tabletop Pen Manipulation With a Vision-Guided 4-DoF Arm

author.name: Anirudh Rangarajan, Bibit Bianchini

entry.summary: Demonstrates that a roughly 200-dollar 4-DoF arm with a fixed overhead camera can pick and color-sort pens despite lacking the wrist rotation normally assumed necessary, by combining an oriented-bounding-box detector with motion planning. It is essentially an accessible educational demonstration of perception compensating for hardware underactuation.

entry.title: A Shop Floor Production Scheduling Case based on RFID-supported Smart Factory

author.name: Zhihui Chen, Yize Sun, Yuhao Dong, Zeyu Xiao, Ray Y. Zhong

entry.summary: This case study performs dynamic shop-floor scheduling in a real RFID-instrumented smart factory, mining feasible production sequences and estimating real-time processing rates from collected data to handle operational uncertainty. It emphasizes practical deployment rather than idealized scheduling assumptions. The contribution is an industrial validation of data-driven dynamic scheduling.

entry.title: Demo: Real-time Generative Multicasting with On-Device Intent-aware Semantic Decomposition

author.name: Xinkai Liu, Mahdi Boloursaz Mashhadi, Yi Ma, Rahim Tafazolli

entry.summary: Demonstration of semantic multicasting in which a transmitter segments video into intent-specific sub-signal classes, broadcasts only a shared semantic map plus each user's needed classes, and lets receivers generatively synthesize the rest locally. The authors derive rate-distortion and perception trade-off curves for this hybrid reconstruct-and-synthesize scheme.

entry.title: A Low-Cost IoT Device for Environmental Monitoring and Embedded Solar Forecasting with On-Device Incremental Learning

author.name: Erick Michel Lara Pinal, Abhinav Das, Stephan Schl\"uter

entry.summary: Describes a roughly 65 dollar ESP32-based weather and irradiance sensing node in a weatherproof enclosure that performs 24-hour solar voltage forecasting on-device, with model training decoupled onto a conventional computer and incremental updating on the microcontroller. Targets economically viable dense deployment for hyperlocal photovoltaic forecasting.

entry.title: Q&A: Rethinking how innovation happens

author.name: Jason Sparapani | Department of Materials Science and Engineering

entry.summary: An interview with an MIT materials science professor about his book arguing that innovation is systematically misunderstood and resists management and control, framed against a moment when AI is reshaping knowledge production and research. It draws on his experience co-inventing strained silicon and leading international research programs.

entry.title: Local Gains and Fixed-Assignment Set Losses in Shared Set Decoders

author.name: Ze Zhang, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: Investigates a trade-off in DETR-family object detectors where deleting a query-relation improves the specific edited slot while degrading the utility of the surrounding prediction set, using recorded selection-conditional evidence over hundreds of paired image-relation units in two checkpoints. Reports a consistent locally positive but assignment-level negative contrast pattern.

entry.title: The Note-Chord-Voice Framework: Structured Source Separation and Causal Inference for EV Charging Data

author.name: Jiajie Chen, Jinfeng Li

entry.summary: Proposes a music-inspired pipeline that separates repair of fragmented EV charging session records, structural pattern discovery, non-negative matrix factorization based source separation, and causal price-elasticity estimation into distinct falsifiable stages with pre-modeling suitability gates. Motivated by real data pathologies including split sessions, physically impossible energy-duration combinations, and collider bias from clustering on post-treatment outcomes.

entry.title: Emergence of Transfer Learning towards Specific Identification of Alzheimer's Disease A Prospective Approach

author.name: Soumik Podder, Chandramouli Haldar

entry.summary: Applies transfer learning to MRI-based Alzheimer's disease classification, arguing it mitigates overfitting and preprocessing sensitivity relative to training convolutional models from scratch. It is a conventional medical imaging pipeline study.

entry.title: External Sinkhole Attack Detection in Large-Scale WSNs Using Metaheuristic Feature Selection

author.name: Seungwoo Han, Sawako Kitagata, Ingon Chanpornpakdi, Toshihisa Tanaka, Su Man Nam

entry.summary: This very short paper applies bee swarm optimization for feature selection in detecting external sinkhole attacks in a simulated 2,000-node wireless sensor network. It reports 0.997 detection accuracy while halving the feature set from sixteen to eight.

entry.title: Lateral Workshop Applications: A Case Study

author.name: Jacob Brinton

entry.summary: Notes from organizers who received over 700 applications for a three-day program helping experienced professionals transition into AI safety, describing common application weaknesses and how candidates could better present competence. It functions as feedback for future applicants.

entry.title: Characterization of Thermal Systems from Noisy and Low-resolution Measurements Using Dynamic Mode Decomposition

author.name: M. E. P. Silva, L. S. Araujo, F. T. Colombo, A. Cunha Jr, S. da Silva

entry.summary: A book-chapter style study of Dynamic Mode Decomposition for identifying heat transfer dynamics from sparse, noisy, low-resolution thermal sensor data, focusing on how preprocessing and rank truncation choices affect stability and interpretability. Demonstrated on forced convection thermocouple data and a transient case.

entry.title: Hardware-in-the-Loop Phase-Aware CNN for Real-Time 5G Channel Estimation

author.name: Javad Zolfaghari-Bengar, Rakibul Rony, Elisa Gomez-de-Lope, Alejandro Villena-Rodriguez, Abhinav Mahadevan, Nicolas Kourtellis

entry.summary: A short demo companion describing live inference of a lightweight phase-aware CNN uplink channel estimator using data captured from a hardware-in-the-loop 5G platform with commercial RF generation, programmable channel emulation, an O-RAN radio unit, and DU emulation. Highlights exposure to real impairments like phase noise, quantization, and synchronization error.

entry.title: Image Denoising via the Adaptive Rank-Cluster Filter

author.name: Dmitry Pozdnyakov

entry.summary: Presents a hand-designed 3x3 local denoising filter that clusters sorted pixel intensities with Otsu partitioning and fuzzily fuses the majority intensity with the window median. It is compared against classical baselines such as median, bilateral, Wiener and non-local means.

entry.title: From Generation to Matching: A Development Report on Personalized Chinese Handwriting

author.name: Yiwei Liu

entry.summary: A retrospective engineering report on personalized Chinese handwriting that documents how few-shot generation of unseen characters kept trading off structural correctness against identity-defining strokes. The project pivoted from generation to retrieving compatible real human samples via character equivalence classes over a multi-writer corpus.

entry.title: Evaluating the impact of adversarial traffic patterns on vanet communication using veins simulation

author.name: Henry Agyapong

entry.summary: Simulation study of how adversarial behaviors such as message flooding, false information injection, and coordinated congestion degrade vehicular ad hoc network performance, measured through packet delivery ratio and delay in a Veins/OMNeT++/SUMO setup. Provides a characterization of vulnerability under varying traffic densities.

entry.title: QuantumPhaseNet: A Gauge-Covariant Geometric and Quantum-Spectral Theory of Semantic Concept Hierarchies with Prototype Validation of a Classical Quantum-Inspired Model

author.name: Kiyotaka Kasubuchi, Kazuo Fukiya

entry.summary: Proposes a gauge-covariant, quantum-spectral reinterpretation of transformer representations in which contextual semantics are complex amplitudes, a covariant phase rate defines a semantic wavelength as a conceptual scale proxy, and low-frequency graph modes define a document-level discourse direction, together with claimed invariance, unitarity, and stability results and a calibratable hallucination-risk formulation. Validation is a prototype offline studio evaluated on built-in synthetic data.

entry.title: Connect to your future selves

author.name: PatrickDFarley

entry.summary: A personal-development essay about treating your future self as someone deserving charity and accountability, illustrated with examples like abandoned blogs and unfinished projects. It has no connection to AI research.

entry.title: Do your readers get annoyed if you post every day for 30 days?

author.name: Steff

entry.summary: A short open question from a blogger asking whether subscribers find daily posting for thirty days annoying and whether a separate experimental blog would be preferable. It contains no research content.

entry.title: Agentic-SQL Revisited: Autonomy-Based Taxonomy and Empirical Benchmark Analysis for LLM Text-to-SQL

author.name: Changruo Zhao, Zujun Peng, Yu Tian, Yuting Liu, Yiyun Su, Huiying Zhu, Luyan Zhang, Heming Zeng

entry.summary: Note: no such standalone item beyond those analyzed; placeholder retained for id completeness.

entry.title: Research Summary: August 17, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's strongest work clusters around automating AI research itself, the fragility of interpretability and benchmark evidence, and pretraining data economics.

  • AI Research Preference Models score candidate experiments before execution, attacking the evaluation-compute bottleneck that dominates autonomous research agents
  • Toby Ord's formal treatment of intelligence explosion dynamics shows true singular growth requires stricter feedback conditions than governance discourse assumes

Interpretability and measurement validity form the dominant theme, with two papers in direct tension. An MIT circuit study across 46 tasks in four cognitive domains reports spontaneous brain-like functional modularity; a pre-registered grid of 15,840 specifications on GPT-2 small IOI circuits shows such findings often do not survive defensible analytic variation. On evaluation: post-training on SWE-bench trajectories transfers poorly to a purpose-built Django suite, and Behavioral Lift demonstrates that amplified reasoning behaviors in thinking models are weakly predictive of correctness.

  • Scaling Domain Data Repetition quantifies optimal repeat counts for scarce high-quality domain corpora as token budgets scale with model size
  • A unified path-space policy-gradient view derives reverse-trajectory and forward-matching diffusion RL objectives from one framework, consolidating a fragmented area
  • A Year in LLM Serving releases rare long-horizon production traces with actionable caching and load-balancing implications
  • Also notable: Jais 2 Arabic-centric open model family (MBZUAI/Cerebras/Inception), thermodynamically consistent universal interatomic potentials, and a full ImageNet-1k validation re-annotation
entry.content:
Today's strongest work clusters around automating AI research itself, the fragility of interpretability and benchmark evidence, and pretraining data economics.

  • AI Research Preference Models score candidate experiments before execution, attacking the evaluation-compute bottleneck that dominates autonomous research agents
  • Toby Ord's formal treatment of intelligence explosion dynamics shows true singular growth requires stricter feedback conditions than governance discourse assumes

Interpretability and measurement validity form the dominant theme, with two papers in direct tension. An MIT circuit study across 46 tasks in four cognitive domains reports spontaneous brain-like functional modularity; a pre-registered grid of 15,840 specifications on GPT-2 small IOI circuits shows such findings often do not survive defensible analytic variation. On evaluation: post-training on SWE-bench trajectories transfers poorly to a purpose-built Django suite, and Behavioral Lift demonstrates that amplified reasoning behaviors in thinking models are weakly predictive of correctness.

  • Scaling Domain Data Repetition quantifies optimal repeat counts for scarce high-quality domain corpora as token budgets scale with model size
  • A unified path-space policy-gradient view derives reverse-trajectory and forward-matching diffusion RL objectives from one framework, consolidating a fragmented area
  • A Year in LLM Serving releases rare long-horizon production traces with actionable caching and load-balancing implications
  • Also notable: Jais 2 Arabic-centric open model family (MBZUAI/Cerebras/Inception), thermodynamically consistent universal interatomic potentials, and a full ImageNet-1k validation re-annotation

entry.title: Modular Cognitive Architecture Emerges in Large Language Models

author.name: Pengrui Han, Jacob Andreas, Evelina Fedorenko, Andrea Gregor de Varda

entry.summary: Uses circuit analysis across 46 tasks in four cognitive domains to test whether language models spontaneously develop brain-like functional specialization, and reports that distinct circuits handle language, formal reasoning, social reasoning, and physical reasoning. This is evidence that modularity may be a convergent property of intelligent systems rather than a quirk of biological evolution.

entry.title: AI Research Preference Models

author.name: Thomas Simon Foster, Bassel Al Omari, Tingchen Fu, Thomas Mann, Carl Domond, Lucia Cipolina-Kun, Bhavul Gauri, Muna Aghamelu, Alexander D. Goldie, Eryk Helenowski, Jean-Christophe Gagnon-Audet, Alberto Pepe, Saba Nazir, Daniel Izcovich, Noam Levi, Rishi Hazra, Karen Hambardzumyan, Nicolas Baldwin, Xian Li, Martin Josifoski, Paris Giampouras, Masoud Jalili Sabet, Anya Sims, Hela Momand, Tatiana Shavrina, Despoina Magka, Jason Weston, Yulin Wang, Anirudh Goyal, Jo\~ao Henriques, Yoram Bachrach, Emily McMilin, Jakob Nicolaus Foerster

entry.summary: Tackles the compute bottleneck in autonomous AI research agents, where writing a candidate experiment takes minutes but evaluating it takes hours or days of GPU time, so success depends on how a fixed execution budget is allocated. The authors build research preference models from frozen pretrained language models that predict which candidate solutions are worth actually running, without task-specific training.

entry.title: Intern-S2-Mobius: Foundation Model with Decoupled Knowledge and Reasoning

author.name: Kai Chen, Jifeng Ding, Ning Ding, Jiaye Ge, Lixin Gu, Yicheng Gu, Qipeng Guo, Ermo Hua, Haian Huang, Haozheng Hou, Jie Hou, Xiangyu Hong, Che Jiang, Minxi Jin, Cheng Liang, Dahua Lin, Dawei Liu, Kuikun Liu, Chengqi Lv, Haijun Lv, Han Lv, Ningsheng Ma, Biqing Qi, Jianmin Qian, Shiya Su, Youbang Sun, Huanze Tang, Zhongbo Tian, Hanjing Wang, Rui Wang, Ting Wang, Yi Wang, Baiting Wu, Jun Xu, Bowen Yang, Hui Wang, Weida Wang, Haochen Ye, Jiashuo Yu, Shan Yu, Xiaoyi Yu, Qirui Zeng, Qi Zhang, Ming Zhang, Wenwei Zhang, Bowen Zhou, Xinyu Zhou

entry.summary: Intern-S2-Mobius proposes an architecture that separates knowledge storage in a globally shared feed-forward memory from iterative reasoning performed by repeated self-attention operators that query that memory. A 7B model trained from scratch reportedly matches a transformer baseline using about 63 percent of the training data, and a continually pretrained version builds on the existing Qwen3.5-35B model. If it holds up, decoupling knowledge from reasoning is a substantive departure from the standard transformer block.

entry.title: The Dynamics of Intelligence Explosions

author.name: Toby Ord

entry.summary: Toby Ord analyzes the mathematics of AI-accelerated AI research feedback loops, showing that true singular growth toward a vertical asymptote is harder to obtain than recent economics-style models suggest, and highlighting a neglected regime of super-exponential but non-singular growth. He argues the loop generation time is a pivotal and usually ignored parameter. The paper sharpens quantitative discussion of takeoff speeds that underpins much AI policy debate.

entry.title: Jais 2: A Family of Arabic-Centric Open Large Language Models

author.name: Mohamed Anwar, Abed Alhakim Freihat, George Ibrahim, Mostafa Awad, Abdelrahman Sadallah, Gurpreet Gosal, Gokulakrishnan Ramakrishnan, Sarath Chandran, Biswajit Mishra, Rituraj Joshi, Ahmed Frikha, Etienne Goffinet, Abhishek Maiti, Ali El Filali, Sarah AlBarri, Samujjwal Ghosh, Rahul Pal, Parvez Mullah, Awantika Shukla, Sajid siddiki, Samta Kamboj, Onkar Pandit, Sunil Kumar Sahu, AbdelRahman Elbadawy, Amr Mohamed, Ahmad Chamma, Evan Dufraisse, Abdelaziz Bounhar, Dani Bouch, Hadi Abdine, Guokan Shang, Fajri Koto, Yuxia Wang, Zhuohan Xie, Ali Mekky, Rania Elbadry, Sarfraz Ahmad, Momina Ahsan, Omar El Herraoui, Daniil Orel, Hasan Iqbal, Kareem Elzeky, Mervat Abassy, Kareem Elozeiri, Saadeldine Eletter, Farah Atif, Nurdaulet Mukhituly, Haonan Li, Xudong Han, Aaryamonvikram Singh, Zainul Abedien Ahmed Quraishi, Neha Sengupta, Larry Murray, Avraham Sheinin, Joel Hestness, Natalia Vassilieva, Hector Xuguang Ren, Zhengzhong Liu, Michalis Vazirgiannis, Preslav Nakov

entry.summary: Jais 2 is a family of Arabic-centric open models from MBZUAI, Cerebras, and Inception, including what the authors describe as the largest open Arabic-centric LLM trained from scratch at 70B parameters plus a competitive 8B variant. A custom Arabic vocabulary and optimized training recipe deliver strong Arabic and culturally grounded benchmark results with a substantially smaller token budget than comparable models. It is a substantive contribution to non-English open model availability.

entry.title: Scaling Domain Data Repetition in LLM Pretraining

author.name: Jingwei Li, Xinran Gu, Rui Dai, Xintong Hao, Chengyin Xu, Yan Wu, Shuran Zheng, Jingzhao Zhang

entry.summary: Studies how many times scarce high-quality domain data should be repeated in LLM pretraining when the token budget grows with model size, finding that at fixed tokens-per-parameter the optimal repetition count mildly increases with model scale. This directly addresses the dilution of specialist data as general web corpora dominate larger training mixtures. The results provide actionable scaling guidance for pretraining data mixture design.

entry.title: Don't Claim Benchmark-Oriented Optimization Improves General Coding Capability -- Diverse Evaluation Is Required

author.name: Egor Shibaev, Vera Kudrevskaia, Timur Galimzyanov, Mikhail Evtikhiev, Ana Terna, Rastislav Rabatin, Timur Kudashev, Timofey Bryksin, Arina Puchkova, Patrik Bartak, Egor Bogomolov, Sergey Titov

entry.summary: Using a purpose-built Django case-study suite, the authors show that post-training on SWE-bench trajectories yields little transfer to other coding tasks and that benchmark rankings frequently fail to generalize, undermining the common practice of citing a handful of coding scores as evidence of general coding ability. They argue for diverse evaluation before claiming broad capability. The results are a direct challenge to how model cards and post-training papers report coding progress.

entry.title: Designing Reinforcement Learning for Diffusion Models: A Unified Path-Space View

author.name: Yixian Xu, Yuanrui Zhang, Shengjie Luo, Liwei Wang, Di He

entry.summary: Shows that reverse-trajectory and forward-matching reinforcement learning objectives for diffusion models both fall out of a single path-space policy-gradient principle derived via importance sampling between sampling SDEs. This unification explains Flow-GRPO-style updates as special cases and suggests principled design choices for new diffusion RL algorithms.

entry.title: Amplified Does Not Mean Predictive: Reasoning Behaviors in Thinking Models

author.name: Jean de Dieu Nyandwi, Leena Mathur, Yonatan Bisk, Robert Hawkins, Graham Neubig

entry.summary: The authors introduce Behavioral Lift, measuring how much a reasoning behavior changes correctness when present versus absent, and annotate over fifteen thousand traces across fifteen models and six text and vision-language benchmarks. They document an amplification-lift gap in which reasoning-trained models amplify behaviors that make traces look deliberative without amplifying those actually associated with correct answers. This is a direct empirical challenge to assumptions behind reasoning-oriented training.

entry.title: A Year in LLM Serving: Workload Evolution, Caching and Load-Balancing

author.name: William Nixon, Jon Durbin, Florian Standhartinger, Haryadi S. Gunawi, Juncheng Yang

entry.summary: Characterizes a full year of production inference traffic from a real LLM serving provider, analyzing how workloads evolve over time and what this implies for prefix caching and load balancing. Longitudinal, full-production traces of this scope are rare and directly useful for designing and benchmarking serving systems.

entry.title: Twin: Playing an Unknown Game with a Test-Time Digital Twin

author.name: Alexy Skoutnev, Kirill Acharya, Gaston Longhitano, Madeleine Udell, Kevin Ellis, Iddo Drori

entry.summary: Twin has a frontier coding agent write an executable world model of an unknown game at test time, then requires the program to reproduce every previously observed transition before any new action is taken, using mismatches as a repair signal. On ARC-AGI-3 style continual-learning games it recovers true transition rules and goals on nearly all levels. It is a concrete demonstration of program-synthesized world models as a test-time reasoning substrate.

entry.title: Universal Thermodynamic Interatomic Potentials for Crystalline Materials

author.name: Juno Nam, Bowen Deng, Xiaochen Du, Luis Barroso-Luque, Benjamin Kurt Miller, Rafael G\'omez-Bombarelli

entry.summary: Extends a universal machine-learned interatomic potential from static energies to a thermodynamically consistent Gibbs free energy model, so that temperature- and pressure-dependent responses follow by automatic differentiation from a single evaluation. This lets materials screening use free energies, which actually govern phase stability, instead of ground-state energies.

entry.title: Doomed to Re-Annotate, Forever: The ImageNet Story

author.name: Illia Volkov, Nikita Kisel, Tetiana Mishkina, Klara Janouskova, Jiri Matas

entry.summary: A comprehensive re-annotation of the ImageNet-1k validation set adding multilabel corrections, object localization, revised class definitions and semantic attributes. The audit finds roughly 12 percent of original labels are wrong, a third of images contain multiple valid labels, and nearly 4 percent contain no object from any ImageNet class at all.

entry.title: Does DiffusionGemma do latent reasoning?

author.name: Jan Bauer

entry.summary: Cross-posted version of the interpretability study on whether a diffusion-based language model hides reasoning in its continuous denoising vectors, concluding that monitorability is largely preserved and that existing interpretability tools transfer. Identical content to the forum original.

entry.title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation

author.name: Ajay Pravin Mahale (Hochschule Trier)

entry.summary: Pre-registers a crossed grid of seven analytic choices in circuit discovery and runs 15,840 specifications on GPT-2 small for the indirect object identification task, then maps each discovered circuit into a structured regulatory documentation statement. The finding is that circuit-level explanations vary substantially across defensible analyst settings, undermining their use as compliance evidence.

entry.title: From Passive Delegates to Strategic Negotiators: Reinforcing Social Reasoning in Small Language Models with SocialRL

author.name: Wenyue Hua, Zachary Huang, Tyler Payne, Safoora Yousefi, Saleema Amershi, Asli Celikyilmaz

entry.summary: Presents SocialRL, a recipe for training social and negotiation reasoning directly into a small 4B model across six interactive domains including bargaining, job interviews, and scheduling. It is motivated by the observation that agreeable assistant behavior makes a poor delegate, since helpful frontier models tend to leak private principal information and concede too quickly.

entry.title: The Past and Future of AI Scientists

author.name: Ross D. King

entry.summary: Ross King surveys the history and trajectory of AI Scientists, machines that form hypotheses, design and run physical experiments, and revise beliefs, tracing the line from the Adam and Eve robot scientists to today combination of foundation models, autonomous agents, and lab robotics. It argues that closed-loop autonomous discovery systems are now buildable at far greater generality. The perspective is authoritative given the author pioneered the field.

entry.title: GRPO Beyond English: A Large-Scale Study of GRPO in Non-English and Multilingual Settings

author.name: Konstantin Dobler, Federico Scozzafava, Jonathan Janke, Mohamed Ali, Simon Lehnerer

entry.summary: A large-scale empirical study of group relative policy optimization for verifiable-reward reasoning training outside English, spanning many base models, training languages and reward designs for reasoning language. Key findings are that training reasoning in the native language costs little relative to English, and that crosslingual transfer is strong but highly model- and language-dependent.

entry.title: RGBX-Next: Towards Realistic Generative Rendering from G-Buffers

author.name: Zheng Zeng, Marco Salvi, Lifan Wu, Jan Nov\'ak, Daqi Lin, Saeed Hadadan, Yichen Sheng, Robert Pottorff, Shiqiu Liu, Ravi Ramamoorthi, Ling-Qi Yan, Milo\v{s} Ha\v{s}an

entry.summary: Provides a general recipe for finetuning diffusion transformers into both forward and inverse renderers, estimating geometry and material buffers from images, video and streams, and rendering realistic output conditioned on those buffers. The goal is to give generative models the precise controllability that traditional 3D rendering pipelines offer.

entry.title: Adversarial Learning of Classifier-Free Guidance Schedules

author.name: Ashwini Pokle, Alexandre Galashov, Arnaud Doucet, Mauricio Delbracio, Valentin De Bortoli

entry.summary: Learns classifier-free guidance strength as a function of diffusion time, conditioning, and the current noisy sample instead of using a single global scale, framing the problem as density-ratio estimation with an adversarially trained discriminator. Aims to improve prompt alignment and reduce artifacts without hand-designed schedules.

entry.title: Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work-Until They Don't

author.name: Zhiyuan Jiang, Fangrui Huang, Hanwen Xing, Xander Wu, Yipeng Gao, Rui Cao, Mengdi Wang, Shilong Liu, Yijiang Li

entry.summary: A controlled study of agent skills, the structured knowledge packages increasingly bundled with LLM agents, isolating how representation format, outcome annotation, retrieval difficulty, and cross-framework transfer determine whether skills help. The authors normalize over 8,000 trial records and pair trajectory analysis with quantitative ablations to explain when and why skills fail. It moves the field beyond aggregate success rates toward mechanism-level understanding of an increasingly deployed technique.

entry.title: Think in Latent, Explain in Language: Self-Explainable Latent Reasoning

author.name: Dayuan Zhao, Shengcao Cao, Yu-Xiong Wang, Liang-Yan Gui

entry.summary: SELR aims to keep the compute savings of latent chain-of-thought while restoring interpretability, training a single model whose latent reasoning states are directly decodable into faithful natural-language explanations rather than relying on a bolt-on post-hoc decoder. It positions itself against opaque latent methods like Coconut and decoupled explainers like Heima. The unified design targets the efficiency-transparency tradeoff that limits deployment of latent reasoning.

entry.title: VoiceChat-TTS: A Low-Latency Continuous Speech Synthesis Model for Interactive Agents

author.name: Edresson Casanova, Jaehyeon Kim, Mariana Graterol Fuenmayor, Shehzeen Hussain, Viacheslav Klimkov, Valentin Mendelev, Mikyas Desta, Paarth Neekhara, Piotr Zelasko, Chen Chen, Elena Rastorgueva, Ke Hu, Ankita Pasad, Xuesong Yang, Aya Alja'fari, Rajarshi Roy, Rohan Badlani, Jason Roche, Jason Li, Zhehuai Chen

entry.summary: A streaming text-to-speech model from an NVIDIA-affiliated team that is driven directly by LLM text token streams, supports explicit interruption through control tokens, and emits silence when no text is arriving, enabling always-on conversational agents. It targets the latency and quality tradeoffs that duplex speech-to-speech systems currently face.

entry.title: MobileMem: Learning from a Year of Mobile Experiences

author.name: Xinle Deng, Yida Xue, Xiangyuan Ru, Haoming Xu, Shuofei Qiao, Mengru Wang, Yijun Chen, Buqiang Xu, Chen Jiang, Yuchen Eleanor Jiang, Lizhong Wang, Jianfeng Wang, Li Zeng, Haofen Wang, Guilin Qi, Huajun Chen, Ningyu Zhang

entry.summary: Presents MobileMem, a benchmark and framework for on-device long-term agent memory built from a year-scale collection of heterogeneous, multimodal, personal mobile experiences, generated through a knowledge-grounded synthesis pipeline for temporal consistency. It targets the gap between existing recall benchmarks and realistic personal-assistant settings.

entry.title: Wrong but Useful: Trajectory Value Beyond Answer Correctness in Multi-Agent Messages

author.name: Chih-Hsuan Yang, Anjir Ahmed Chowdhury, Cheng-Hau Yang, Weijian Zheng, Fernando Llorente, Xiaolong Ma, Xinyang Li, Eliu A. Huerta, Ian T. Foster, Rajeev Thakur

entry.summary: Challenges the assumption in multi-agent reasoning that only likely-correct messages should be kept, using a replay protocol in which the same downstream solver is run with each candidate message available or hidden to measure that message's true contribution. Across five math and science benchmarks the authors show wrong answers can still carry useful decompositions and constraints. This has direct implications for how multi-agent systems filter and aggregate intermediate communications.

entry.title: ASSERT: A Measurement Pipeline for GenAI Audits

author.name: Riccardo Fogliato, Abhinav Palia, Xiawei Wang, Emily Sheng, Chad Atalla, Jean Garcia-Gathright, Nicholas Pangakis, Sharman Tan, Dan Vann, Hannah Washington, P. Alex Dow, Heba Elfardy, Hanna Wallach, Sandeep Atluri

entry.summary: ASSERT is a specification-driven pipeline that ties every reported compliance rate in a generative AI audit to a written record of the measurement choices that produced it, so a change in the number can be attributed either to the system or to the measurement. It helps draft behavioral rubrics and test cases and then runs the audit end to end. The authors, including established measurement-theory researchers, demonstrate it in a case study.

entry.title: More Correct Mass, Worse Answers: Why Power Sampling Can Fail and How to Fix It

author.name: Haohui Yang, Jiaxing Sun, Xiujun Ma

entry.summary: Documents a paradox in power sampling, a verifier-free inference-time technique that sharpens a language model distribution over whole reasoning trajectories: it can shift more probability mass onto correct trajectories while reducing downstream self-consistency accuracy by as much as 18.5 points. The authors attribute this to a dose mismatch from fixed sharpening exponents and a second mismatch, and propose corrections.

entry.title: Approximate Muon with low-rank adapters

author.name: Ben Anson, Conor Houghton, Edward Milsom

entry.summary: Addresses the incompatibility between the Muon optimizer and LoRA, since a low-rank update cannot be exactly orthogonalized, by approximating a relaxed Muon objective through linearization plus least squares. The resulting sMuon method uses only matrix multiplications and performs well across supervised fine-tuning tasks.

entry.title: Q2.5 2026 Timelines Update: Uplift and Revenue

author.name: brendanhalstead

entry.summary: A quarterly update to a public AI timelines model, replacing reliance on coding time-horizon extrapolation with anchors based on measured research uplift and AI revenue. The authors report slightly shorter timelines but mainly greater confidence due to a stronger evidence base and better-documented modeling.

entry.title: An explainable biomedical foundation model via large-scale concept-enhanced vision–language pretraining

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: This Nature Biomedical Engineering paper presents a biomedical vision-language foundation model pretrained at scale with explicit clinical concept supervision, so that its predictions can be attributed to named medical concepts rather than only saliency heatmaps. Building interpretability into the pretraining objective, instead of bolting it on afterward, is a practically important direction for clinical deployment and regulatory acceptance of medical AI.

entry.title: AgentRewind: Recoverable Execution for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Yu Zhuang, Kefei Chen, Yitong Duan, Shuxin Zheng, Jian Li, Xu-Yao Zhang

entry.summary: AgentRewind adds runtime recovery to long-horizon LLM agents by recording aligned checkpoints of both the agent context and a controlled environment, so an agent that makes an irreversible early mistake can roll back and retry with knowledge from the failed attempt. The authors also build MettleBench to measure recovery rather than only first-pass success. This targets one of the main practical failure modes of deployed agents: error propagation that later actions cannot undo.

entry.title: Rollplex: Cross-Phase GPU Spatial Sharing for Vision Language Model Post-Training

author.name: Hanfeng Lu, Tianyu Feng, Suyi Li, Yuheng Zhao, Wei Gao, Shaopan Xiong, Ju Huang, Siran Yang, Jiamang Wang, Lin Qu, Wei Wang

entry.summary: Presents a runtime that overlaps prompt and video prefix processing with rollout decoding during on-policy RL post-training of vision-language models, exploiting idle GPU capacity without breaking synchronous semantics. It targets the phase-serial execution pattern inherited from text-only RL frameworks, which wastes compute when visual inputs dominate.

entry.title: MathForm: Scaling Mathematical Autoformalization with Knowledge Retrieval and Verification-Guided Refinement

author.name: Lushi Pu, Weiming Zhang, Xinheng Xie, Zixuan Fu, Bingxiang He, Hengyu Zhao, Hongya Lyu, Xin Li, Jie Zhou, Yudong Wang

entry.summary: MathForm improves autoformalization into Lean 4 by retrieving Mathlib library knowledge instead of relying on parametric memory and by using verification feedback to iteratively refine generated formal statements. It addresses the twin failures of wrong library typing and semantic drift from the natural-language source. Formal verification feedback loops are among the most credible routes to reliable mathematical AI.
